展开英文原题摘要与原文链接
ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Metabolic reprogramming of myeloid‑derived suppressor cells (MDSCs) plays a role in immunotherapy resistance in colorectal cancer (CRC). This metabolic reprogramming appears to be coordinated by oncogenic mutations (such as adenomatous polyposis coli, KRAS and TP53) through a proposed self‑reinforcing 'mutation‑metabolism‑suppression' axis. In the present review, four core metabolic pillars sustaining MDSC pathogenicity and the epimetabolic regulation that durably locks them into a suppressive state were examined. Furthermore, two emerging dimensions were highlighted: The spatial metabolic antagonism through which MDSCs may construct a metabolically hostile zone to limit the functional activity of tertiary lymphoid structures, and the remote manipulation of MDSC function by gut and intratumoral microbiota‑derived metabolites. To transcend the limitations of non‑specific myeloid depletion, immunometabolic rehabilitation is proposed as a potentially transformative framework targeting intrinsic metabolic vulnerabilities to functionally reprogram MDSCs from an immunosuppressive to a homeostatic or immunostimulatory phenotype. By integrating emerging spatial omics for precise target validation, artificial intelligence‑guided rational drug design and microbiome modulation, this paradigm provides a strategic roadmap for next‑generation precision immunotherapy, aiming to achieve durable responses across both microsatellite stable and microsatellite instability‑high CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The present study investigated the relationship between phospholipase D2 (PLD2) and hypoxia‑induced chemoresistance in colorectal cancer (CRC) and elucidated its regulatory mechanisms. The present study demonstrated that increased PLD2 was associated with poor prognosis and chemoresistance in CRC via The University of Alabama at Birmingham cancer data analysis portal and Kaplan‑Meier plotter databases and 5‑fluorouracil (5‑Fu)‑resistant CRC tissues. The protein expression of PLD2, hypoxia‑inducible factor 1 alpha (HIF‑1α), multidrug resistance‑associated protein 2 (MRP2), LC3‑II/I, and Beclin‑1 was markedly upregulated under hypoxia in SW620 and SW480 cells in a time‑dependent manner. Next, SW620 and SW480 cells were transduced with recombinant replication‑deficient adenoviral vectors encoding PLD2‑targeting short hairpin (sh)RNA (Ad‑sh‑PLD2) or PLD2 overexpression (oe) constructs (Ad‑oe‑PLD2), followed by treatment with 5‑Fu, rapamycin (Rapa), or 3‑methyladenine (3‑MA), either alone or in combination.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Gastrointestinal (GI) cancers, including colorectal and pancreatic cancers, remain among the most lethal cancers worldwide. These tumors often exhibit resistance to immune checkpoint inhibitors, largely due to microsatellite stability and a profoundly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). While chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy has demonstrated curative potential in hematological cancers, its translation to solid tumors has been limited by challenges such as antigen heterogeneity, physical barriers to infiltration, and TME-mediated immunosuppression. Gene-editing technologies, including CRISPR-Cas9, have catalyzed the development of next-generation cellular immunotherapies. By precisely modifying T cells, natural killer (NK) cells, and mesenchymal stem/stromal cells (MSCs), it is possible to enhance their functionality, persistence, and safety. This review highlights the clinical progress of gene-edited cell therapies and specifically explores the synergistic "one-two punch" potential of engineered MSCs as TME remodeling platforms. By acting as localized delivery vehicles for cytokines or prodrug-activating enzymes, MSCs can modulate TME, thereby facilitating the infiltration and sustained cytotoxic activity of CAR T or CAR NK cells. Finally, we address critical translational challenges and propose future directions that integrate multi-omics to identify novel therapeutic agents for cellular immunotherapy in GI oncology.

展开英文原题摘要与原文链接
ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Liquid biopsies provide a source of biomolecules that allow tumor characterization. Increasing evidence shows that the tumor microenvironment (TME) plays a central role in behavior of colon cancer. This study assessed which proteins in the circulation correlate with tumor stromal content through analysis of serum and corresponding tissue samples from patients with colon cancer. A broad set of circulating proteins is quantified, ranging from common apolipoproteins, transport and complement factors, to key factors from interconnected stromal pathways such as coagulation and acute phase inflammation. The cohort consisted of 97 patients with colon cancer and 50 control individuals who all underwent colonoscopy. Targeted mass spectrometry was applied to quantify 156 serum proteins via their surrogate peptides and corresponding internal standards. Matching solid tumor tissue slides from all 97 patients were used to determine the Tumor-Stroma Ratio (TSR). Serum protein levels were compared between stroma-high and stroma-low tumors, resulting in a subset of discriminating proteins. Composite protein scores were evaluated in multivariable Cox models. Four serum proteins differed significantly between stroma-high and stroma-low tumors, all showing elevated levels in stroma-high patients, including complement-related proteins (C2, factor B, and C1r subcomponent-like protein) and the coagulation-related vitamin K-dependent protein S. This resulted in a composite Stromal Protein Score that may capture TME-driven variations. The Stromal Protein Score was significantly different between stroma-high and stroma-low patients (adjusted p < 0.001). Our data indicate that stroma-high tumors are associated with systemic alterations in complement and coagulation-related proteins. The results encourage further development of liquid biopsy-based protein profiling approaches, aiming for clinical implementation as a non-invasive strategy for TME-informed risk stratification and treatment monitoring in colon cancer.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The present study aimed to assess the utilization of biomarker testing, including companion diagnostics and comprehensive genomic profiling (CGP), in Japan and to highlight the value of large-scale real-world database analysis in precision oncology. Claims data from the Medical Data Vision Co., Ltd. database, covering ~40 million patients across 26% of advanced treatment hospitals in Japan, were retrospectively analyzed. Biomarker tests for five genomic biomarkers (BRAF, BRCA1/2, KRAS/NRAS, homologous recombination deficiency and microsatellite instability (MSI)) were evaluated in patients with a confirmed diagnosis of one of 11 common cancer types, a cancer of unknown primary origin (CUP) or a rare cancer, who underwent at least one biomarker test between December 2018 and March 2022. A total of 41,191 biomarker tests were recorded in 28,382 patients, with test volumes increasing markedly between 2018 and 2021. MSI testing was the most common (70.1% of patients), followed by RASKET-B for KRAS/NRAS (25.5%) and BRAF (23.9%). Patients with colorectal cancer frequently underwent multiple tests (42.8%) and distinct testing sequences were observed in gynecological cancer. CGP was more commonly performed on tissue-based samples than through liquid biopsy, particularly in rare cancer (38.5%) and CUP (11.4%). Notably, ~40% of patients received a new treatment after CGP, whereas only 1.7% initiated indicated therapy after MSI testing. The mean time to subsequent treatment initiation from the index date was 70.4 days. In conclusion, the present nationwide real-world study provides an early comprehensive overview of the prevalence and trends of biomarker testing in Japan, and reveals a gap between testing and treatment implementation. Although testing is increasing, its effective clinical use remains limited. Large-scale database analyses may help identify barriers and support strategies to improve the integration of biomarker testing into treatment decision-making, ultimately advancing precision oncology.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Prostate cancer screening guidelines emphasize shared decision-making, yet these decisions are shaped by structural contexts. While racial and ethnic disparities in outcomes are well-documented, the socioeconomic and pre-diagnostic health pathways driving these differences in later life remain unclear. This study utilized structural equation modeling (SEM) to evaluate whether socioeconomic status (SES) and pre-diagnostic health profiles mediate the relationship between race/ethnicity and clinical severity at prostate cancer diagnosis. We analyzed 5,438 men aged 55 to 74 years diagnosed with prostate cancer in the Prostate, Lung, Colorectal and Ovarian (PLCO) Cancer Screening Trial. Parallel mediation SEM with weighted least squares estimation examined two pathways linking race/ethnicity to latent clinical severity (prostate-specific antigen (PSA), Gleason score, and stage): SES pathway and a pre-diagnostic health profile pathway (PSA screening history, comorbidity, and family history). The baseline latent severity model demonstrated acceptable fit (CFI = 0.872, TLI = 0.872, RMSEA = 0.034, SRMR = 0.027). Neither SES nor the measured pre-diagnostic health profile meaningfully mediated racial/ethnic differences in clinical severity. Compared with White men, total effects on latent clinical severity were significant only for AsAm men (0.465, 95% CI: 0.256 to 0.642). Predicted latent severity was highest among Asian men (1.659), followed by Black (1.155) and Hispanic (1.076). These findings suggest that unmeasured mechanisms remain poorly understood in explaining racial and ethnic disparities in prostate cancer severity. Future studies incorporating richer social determinants measures and greater inclusion of underrepresented racial and ethnic groups may clarify pathways underlying these disparities.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Most patients with colorectal cancer (CRC) and peritoneal metastases (PM) face a dismal prognosis. Cytoreductive surgery and hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy (CRS-HIPEC) is a curative-intent treatment for patients with limited disease. This study assessed long-term survival and recurrence patterns. A consecutive cohort of patients with CRC-PM treated with CRS-HIPEC. Patients with complete macroscopic cytoreduction were eligible. Main outcomes were overall survival (OS), disease-free survival (DFS), peritoneal recurrence-free survival (PRFS) and recurrence patterns. In total, 440 patients were evaluated over a median follow-up of 35.2 months (IQR 25.3-68.7). Induction systemic therapy was administered to 43.1% of patients. Median DFS was 9.7 months (95% CI 8.3-11.1), and median OS was 50.2 months (95% CI 44.3-56.2). Independent prognostic factors for decreased OS were Peritoneal Cancer Index (PCI) > 10, positive lymph node status (N-stage), ASA score > 2, and right-sided primary tumors. During follow-up, 71.4% of patients developed recurrent disease in the peritoneum (54.8%), lungs (22.9%), and liver (19.1%). Independent prognostic factors for decreased PRFS were lymph node metastases and higher PCI scores. Neither induction therapy nor HIPEC regimen was correlated with PRFS. Early metachronous presentation of peritoneal metastasis, also emerged as a significant adverse factor for OS, DFS and PRFS. Patients undergoing complete CRS-HIPEC achieved a favorable median OS exceeding 50 months, with approximately 30% of individuals exhibiting long-term survival indicative of cure. However, early recurrence remains a major problem and is in need for further research to improve CRS-HIPEC regimens.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) ranks among the leading malignancies worldwide in both incidence and mortality, and its treatment continues to face major challenges such as chemoresistance and tumor metastasis. This study aims to investigate the potential therapeutic value and underlying mechanisms of the multikinase inhibitor Rigosertib (Rig) in CRC. Our findings demonstrate that Rig markedly suppresses the proliferation, migration, and invasion of CRC cells while inducing apoptosis. Transcriptomic analyses suggest that ferroptosis may be involved in Rig's antitumor activity. Subsequent experiments confirm that Rig induces typical features of ferroptosis. Mechanistically, Rig exerts its effects through a dual regulatory mechanism. On one hand, it upregulates Keap1 expression, thereby suppressing the Nrf2/SLC7A11 signaling pathway and weakening the cellular antioxidant defense. On the other hand, Rig enhances autophagic flux, promoting the autophagy-lysosome-dependent degradation of GPX4, a key regulator of ferroptosis. Notably, both the Nrf2 pathway agonist KI696 and the autophagy inhibitor 3-methyladenine partially reverse Rig-induced ferroptosis, while GPX4 overexpression markedly attenuates Rig's cytotoxicity, confirming the crucial roles of these pathways in its mechanism of action. Moreover, Rig exhibits a pronounced synergistic antitumor effect with 5-fluorouracil in vitro. In xenograft mouse models, Rig treatment effectively suppresses tumor growth without causing significant systemic toxicity. This study, for the first time, reveals that Rig induces ferroptosis through dual mechanisms involving coordinated regulation of the Keap1/Nrf2/SLC7A11 axis and autophagy-dependent degradation of GPX4. These findings provide a novel theoretical foundation and a promising therapeutic strategy for colorectal cancer treatment.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
To better understand real-world practices on HER2 testing and guide practices for selecting patients for HER2-targeted therapy in non-breast/non-gastroesophageal (GE) solid tumors, we assessed 241 non-breast/non-GE solid tumors undergoing HER2 IHC at our institution between April 2024 and June 2025. Among 22 tumor types evaluated, endometrial (29.5%), colorectal (22.8%), and urothelial (10.4%) carcinomas were the most common. Among tumor types with ≥6 cases, urothelial carcinoma (UC) showed the highest HER2 positivity rate (32%, 8/25), while small bowel carcinoma had the highest HER2 alteration rate (50%, 3/6). Twenty-three HER2 positive tumors (9.5%) were identified, including 17 IHC 3+ (7.1%), five IHC 2+/FISH amplified and one IHC 2+/NGS amplified. The positive predictive value (PPV) of HER2 IHC using gastric criteria for ERBB2 amplification was 50% overall, 100% in non-UCs and 14.3% in UCs, respectively. Nine of 19 (47%) eligible patients received trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd), and seven (78%) experienced stable disease or no radiologically detectable tumor during a median follow-up of 21 months. Fourteen cases (6.9%) were interpreted using criteria that did not align with the recommendations, and 51 (25.1%) lacked gastric criteria results for T-DXd eligibility. Our findings support continued education on HER2 testing and interpretation in non-breast/GE solid tumors to optimize selection for HER2-targeted therapy. HER2 alterations across 10 tumor types suggest therapeutic opportunities, whereas the low prevalence of HER2 positivity in other tumor types underscores further evaluation of the utility of routine upfront HER2 IHC. Additionally, the lower PPV of HER2 IHC for ERBB2 amplification in UCs warrants further investigation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Chemoresistance is the innate or acquired ability of cancer cells to evade the cytotoxic effects of chemotherapeutic agents. This hypothesis-generating study presents a systematic comparative analysis of public transcriptomic datasets associated with acquired chemoresistance to major drugs including doxorubicin, cisplatin, and gemcitabine. The aim was to identify recurrent drug-specific gene expression patterns in drug-resistant cancer cells relative to their drug-sensitive parental cells. Publicly available microarray datasets of breast, ovarian, neuroblastoma, bladder, and gallbladder chemoresistant cell lines were retrieved from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database. Differential expression analysis using R/Bioconductor revealed distinct and overlapping signatures of chemoresistance across different cancer types. In doxorubicin-resistant breast cancer, recurrently dysregulated genes included IL-18, CD44, FN1, EGFR, and the histones H2BC10 and H2BC7. Neuroblastoma and ovarian cancer cell datasets shared Differentially Expressed Genes (DEGs) including ABCB1, RUNDC3B, CROT, and TP53TG1. TMEM47 was the only common DEG among all three (breast cancer, neuroblastoma, and ovarian cancer) doxorubicin-resistant datasets, although with tissue-dependent regulation. Gemcitabine resistance signatures in bladder and gallbladder cells include EPCAM, AGR2, NRP2, FGF1, CTH, TENM2, and the long non-coding RNAs APCDD1L-DT and LINC01234. Combined gemcitabine/5-FU resistance revealed common patterns of resistance in gallbladder and colon cancer cell lines. In cisplatin-resistant ovarian cancer cells, LAMA2 and SOX8 were differentially expressed with a consistent direction of change in all datasets in which they were measured. These recurrent associations do not establish causality; rather, they prioritize candidate genes for functional validation in future studies of chemoresistance.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Celastrol (Cel) is a potent natural anti-inflammatory agent whose clinical utility is severely limited by its poor aqueous solubility and negligible oral bioavailability. Herein, we report a surfactant-free oil-in-water Pickering emulsion (C-PE/Cel) stabilized by composite particles of acid-hydrolyzed corn starch and chitosan for oral Cel delivery and gut-brain axis-mediated neuroinflammatory therapy. Controlled sulfuric acid hydrolysis for 6 days was used to tune starch surface amphiphilicity for effective interfacial anchoring, while electrostatic chitosan coating at 1.0 wt% reversed the particle zeta potential from negative to positive, thereby enhancing intestinal retention. C-PE/Cel exhibited high encapsulation efficiency and good colloidal stability at 25 °C for at least 55 days when prepared at an optimized water-to-oil ratio of 3:1. In vitro, C-PE/Cel demonstrated enhanced cellular uptake by Caco-2 human colorectal adenocarcinoma cell monolayers and superior suppression of lipopolysaccharide-induced oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction in the RAW 264.7 mouse monocyte-macrophage cell line. In a chronic LPS-induced murine neuroinflammation model, oral administration of C-PE/Cel restored intestinal barrier integrity by upregulating zonula occludens-1 protein expression and reshaping the gut microbiota by enriching beneficial taxa (e.g., Lachnospiraceae_NK4A136_group and Odoribacter) while reducing potentially pathogenic Ruminococcaceae. Furthermore, integrated 16S ribosomal ribonucleic acid and brain transcriptomic analyses revealed that the therapeutic effects were mediated via the gut-brain axis, involving the downregulation of immunoglobulin-related genes and the upregulation of fatty acid β-oxidation markers. This study established a simple, green, polysaccharide-based Pickering emulsion platform for the oral delivery of hydrophobic therapeutics targeting central nervous system disorders.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
To synthesise evidence informing risk-adapted treatment and organ preservation in locally advanced rectal cancer. This narrative review used targeted English-language searches of PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library through 31 March 2026, supplemented by targeted source verification in September 2026. Magnetic resonance imaging, mismatch repair status, recurrence risk, and patient preferences inform treatment selection. Total neoadjuvant therapy is established for higher-risk mismatch repair-proficient/microsatellite-stable disease. Chemoradiation followed by consolidation chemotherapy can improve organ-preservation probability compared with induction sequencing, without a demonstrated disease-free survival advantage. Selected lower-risk surgical candidates may receive chemotherapy with selective chemoradiation. Both short-course radiotherapy and long-course chemoradiation remain evidence-based options; the long-term locoregional failure signal in RAPIDO cannot be attributed to fractionation alone. Watch-and-wait requires multimodal confirmation of clinical complete response, intensive surveillance, and access to salvage surgery; oncological equivalence to immediate resection is unproven. Prospective dostarlimab data support non-operative management in selected mismatch repair-deficient rectal cancers, while long-term durability requires further evaluation. Management should integrate tumour anatomy, biology, treatment response, and patient priorities. Organ preservation requires careful selection and structured follow-up, with treatment intensity individualised rather than applied uniformly.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer patients frequently report unmet information across physical, psychological, and social domains. Technology offers a promising solution for delivering tailored support. This qualitative study aims to identify and explore the information needs of colorectal cancer patients from diagnosis through surveillance and to understand their preferred digital delivery methods for clinical and supportive content. It represents the initial phase of a broader project to co-design a digital platform to support colorectal cancer patients. A qualitative research design with purposive sample of newly diagnosed colorectal cancer patients and colorectal cancer survivors attending outpatient review between May and August 2024. Open-ended interviews were audio recorded, transcribed verbatim and analysed thematically. The study was reported following the COREQ checklist. 21 participants were initially recruited with one participant withdrawing prior to the interview. Participants (n = 20) identified as predominantly female (n = 11) compared to male (n = 9) with a mean age of 62 years (range 36-82). Most participants were in surveillance stage (n = 16). Participants identified their level of digital literacy as competent (n = 14). However, 12 cited inadequate proficiency with digital technology requiring additional assistance. Two key themes reflected the procedural information needs throughout the cancer journey and factors that either eased or complicated the experience and were identified: Information and Digital Platform, each with corresponding subthemes. Findings emphasise a hybrid system of information is advocated by CRC patients. The ability to access information varies and is dependent on personal preferences and stages of the cancer journey and via different information platforms. Whilst written and verbal information were preferred pathways, digital platforms offered others autonomy and accessibility to information when required.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Chemotherapy-associated steatohepatitis (CASH) increases the risk of postoperative liver failure and mortality in patients undergoing liver surgery. However, non-invasive diagnosis remains an unmet need. Radiomics has potential for characterizing liver parenchyma. This study evaluated the performance of a virtual liver biopsy for CASH prediction, comparing it with whole-liver radiomic analysis. Two retrospective series of patients undergoing hepatectomy for colorectal liver metastases were analyzed: the public "Colorectal-Liver-Metastases" dataset (training and internal validation) and a monocenter series from Humanitas Research Hospital (external validation). Inclusion criteria were preoperative chemotherapy (≥ 2 months) and post-chemotherapy CT (thickness ≤ 5 mm). IBSI-compliant radiomic features were extracted from whole-liver parenchyma and from a virtual biopsy (manually segmented 2-mL cylinder of non-tumoral liver parenchyma). Estimated liver volume (eLV) was computed using three orthogonal diameters. Four XGBoost models were developed (70/30 split, 5-fold cross-validation): clinical; clinical + VB-radiomics (ViB); clinical + VB-radiomics + eLV (ViBE+); clinical + whole-liver radiomics (WholeLiver). One hundred eighty patients were included: 105 internal (63 males, mean age 58.9 years, 38% CASH+) and 75 external (44 males, mean age 62.4 years, 19% CASH+). WholeLiver and ViBE+ models achieved excellent and comparable performance in internal validation (WholeLiver: AUC = 0.857 (95% BS-CI: 0.676-0.954), accuracy = 0.774 (95% BS-CI: 0.613-0.903); ViBE + : AUC = 0.831 (95% BS-CI: 0.549-0.956), accuracy = 0.839 (95% BS-CI: 0.710-0.935); p = 0.814), outperforming ViB model (AUC = 0.724 (95% BS-CI: 0.483-0.896), accuracy = 0.774 (95% BS-CI: 0.613-0.903)). SHAP analysis confirmed liver volume metrics as key predictors. In external validation, the ViBE+ model achieved AUC = 0.745 (95% BS-CI: 0.604-0.886) and accuracy = 0.680 (95% BS-CI: 0.562-0.783). Virtual biopsy provides a reproducible, non-invasive radiomic sampling strategy for CASH prediction. Combined with liver volume metrics, it achieves performance comparable to whole-liver analysis, supporting its potential clinical application. Question Despite its association with postoperative morbidity, the non-invasive preoperative assessment of CASH remains challenging in patients undergoing liver surgery. Findings Radiomic analysis based on a virtual liver biopsy, combined with volumetric measurements, showed excellent performance in predicting CASH, comparable to whole-liver analysis, with liver volume emerging as a key predictor. Critical Relevance Statement A standardized virtual biopsy-based radiomic analysis represents a promising non-invasive approach for evaluating liver parenchymal injury, as demonstrated in preoperative assessment of CASH and identification of high-risk surgical patients.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Rolling circle amplification (RCA) is a simple and efficient isothermal enzymatic reaction. However, its linear amplification kinetics and unsatisfactory multiplex detection capability severely limit further improvements in detection sensitivity and application flexibility. In this work, we developed a lambda exonuclease-assisted probe signal amplification strategy termed LEPA, integrated with endonuclease-mediated exponential RCA for the sensitive detection of target nucleic acids. This system enables precise target recognition through ligase and padlock probes, which, in turn, initiate cascaded RCA for efficient signal amplification. Through a cyclic "binding-cleavage-dissociation" process between E-probes and amplification products, the system achieves dual signal amplification and single-nucleotide resolution. The LEPA-RCA system demonstrates exceptional detection sensitivity and specificity, allowing precise discrimination of alleles with a mutation frequency as low as 0.1% and supporting multiplex intracellular RNA detection. In clinical validation, this method effectively distinguished the expression levels of serum miR-16-5p and miR-92a-3p between healthy individuals and colorectal cancer (CRC) patients, showing high consistency with RT-qPCR results. Moreover, it achieved excellent diagnostic performance (AUC = 0.85). With a modular design, the LEPA-RCA system serves as a robust platform for high-precision multiplex nucleic acid detection in complex biological matrices, showing great potential for clinical translation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
High-temperature requirement protease A3 (HtrA3) has been implicated in the progression of various carcinomas through tissue-specific mechanisms; however, its precise role in colorectal cancer (CRC) remains unclear. We initially identified the upregulation of HtrA3 in CRC tissues through Isobaric Tags for Relative and Absolute Quantitation (iTRAQ) proteomics, which was consistent with the analysis of the CPTAC dataset. Our research further confirmed that HtrA3 is significantly upregulated in CRC tissues and associated with reduced overall survival. Functional assays showed that HtrA3 overexpression enhanced CRC cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, while HtrA3 knockdown yielded opposite effects. In HtrA3-overexpressing HCT116 cells, increased phosphorylation of PI3K, AKT, and FOXO1 was observed, which was reduced upon treatment with the PI3K inhibitor LY294002. Conversely, in HtrA3-knockdown SW480 cells, these phosphorylation levels declined but were restored with the PI3K activator 740Y-P. In vivo, HtrA3 overexpression accelerated xenograft tumor growth. These findings suggest that HtrA3 promotes CRC cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, potentially involving PI3K-AKT-FOXO1 signaling, and support further investigation of HtrA3 as a potential prognostic biomarker and therapeutic target in CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Gastrointestinal (GI) diseases such as colorectal cancer and inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) contribute substantially to global morbidity, with colorectal cancer accounting for nearly 10% of all cancer diagnoses worldwide. Many existing artificial intelligence (AI) models suffer from limited generalizability and poor clinical interpretability. This study aimed to develop and evaluate an explainable AI (XAI) framework for classifying GI diseases from endoscopic images. Public datasets from the Simula Research Laboratory were used: Hyper-Kvasir (10,662 images) for training, Kvasir-V1 (4,000 images) for validation, and Kvasir-V2 (8,000 images) as an independent test set. Two convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures, GastroNet-dilated multi-scale attention (DMSA) (a proposed DMSA Network) and M2ShallowNet (a lightweight hybrid model), were designed for complementary feature extraction. Deep features were fused using a dual context attentive feature network (DCAF-Net) followed by Aquila Optimizer (AO)-based feature-weight refinement without introducing additional trainable fusion parameters. Performance was assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, and statistical testing. Interpretability was examined using gradient-weighted class activation mapping++ (Grad-CAM++) and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). The best-performing classifier, a multilayer perceptron (MLP), achieved an accuracy of 97.21%, precision of 97.27%, recall of 97.21%, Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) of 96.82%, and F1-score of 97.21% on the independent test set. ROC analysis demonstrated excellent class separability, and statistical testing confirmed reliable generalization. XAI results highlighted regions that qualitatively correspond to pathological areas; formal clinical validation of these interpretations was not performed in this study. The proposed framework offers a promising research prototype for AI-assisted GI disease classification. Its potential for real-world endoscopic deployment requires further prospective validation before clinical adoption.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The gut microbiome has emerged as a key modulator of colorectal cancer biology, influencing tumor progression and therapeutic response. However, most existing studies analyze colorectal cancer as a single entity despite biological and therapeutic differences between colon and rectal cancer. Consequently, longitudinal data linking microbiome dynamics to treatment response, particularly in rectal cancer, remain limited. In this prospective cohort study, 31 patients with rectal cancer were included, of whom 17 received neoadjuvant therapy and 14 underwent primary surgery. A total of 110 stool and tissue samples were collected at defined time points before, during, and after treatment. Microbial composition and diversity were analyzed using 16S rRNA gene sequencing. Alpha and beta diversity metrics, differential abundance analyses, and longitudinal comparisons were performed to assess treatment-related microbiome alterations. Distinct microbial communities were observed between stool and tissue samples, with stool samples enriched in Bacteroidetes and tissue samples dominated by Firmicutes, Actinobacteria, and Verrucomicrobia. Neoadjuvant therapy was associated with a marked reduction in microbial diversity with no recovery before surgery, and community composition shifted significantly over the treatment course (patient-constrained PERMANOVA, p = 0.0016), with Clostridium XIVa becoming the dominant genus before surgery. Longitudinal analyses further revealed exploratory differences between patients with complete and incomplete tumor regression. Between diagnosis and surgery, patients achieving complete tumor regression (Dworak TRG 4) showed an increase in the propionate-producing genus Phascolarctobacterium, the only genus significant after correction for multiple testing, together with an exploratory rise in the butyrate-producing genus Roseburia. Higher Bacteroides in patients with incomplete regression was a descriptive observation that was not statistically significant (p = 0.35, q = 0.71). No genus-level differences between response groups were detected at baseline after correction for multiple testing; however, the small sample size limits the ability to exclude baseline differences. Rectal cancer treatment induces distinct and time-dependent alterations in the gut microbiome. Complete tumor regression was associated with an increase in short-chain fatty acid-producing taxa, led by the propionate producer Phascolarctobacterium, whereas higher Bacteroides in incomplete responders was a non-significant, exploratory observation. Given the growing role of organ-preserving strategies such as watch-and-wait, in which reliable identification of complete response is critical, these exploratory patterns warrant validation in larger cohorts.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) is one of the most common malignant epithelial tumours in cats, typically arising in the oral cavity or at cutaneous sites, whereas involvement of the anal sac region is exceptionally rare, with only two cases previously reported. An 8-year-old neutered male Domestic Shorthair cat was referred for persistent tenesmus, constipation and anorexia. A perianal swelling had initially been interpreted as anal sacculitis on cytology, but incisional biopsies confirmed SCC, characterised histologically by only moderate atypia and a low mitotic count. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography revealed a non-circumferential mass centred on the left anal sac region with infiltration of the perirectal soft tissues causing partial rectal obstruction, together with regional lymphadenomegaly; nodal metastasis was confirmed cytologically. Surgery and radiation therapy were declined, and palliative treatment with toceranib phosphate and meloxicam was started. After approximately one month of clinically stable disease, one session of electrochemotherapy with intravenous bleomycin was performed. Clinical signs transiently improved, but rapid progression occurred shortly thereafter, with invasion of the pelvic urethra. The cat died 68 days after diagnosis. Despite reassuring histological features, the tumour showed aggressive local behaviour and early regional metastasis. Toceranib was associated with transient clinical improvement and electrochemotherapy produced only short-lived improvement, likely because the lesion's extent and depth precluded complete treatment of the tumour volume. This case documents aggressive behaviour in an SCC involving the anal sac region and supports considering SCC in cats with persistent perianal swelling, tenesmus or defecatory difficulty unresponsive to medical treatment.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Endoscopic mucosal resection (EMR) is widely used for large and complex colorectal lesions and offers a less invasive alternative to surgery. Although adenoma recurrence after EMR has been described in procedural cohorts, real-world estimates of subsequent colorectal cancer (CRC) diagnoses after EMR across multicenter electronic health record (EHR) systems remain limited. We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX US Collaborative Network. Patients aged 40 years or older who underwent colonoscopy or sigmoidoscopy with EMR between January 1, 2016 and January 1, 2017 were included. Patients with Crohn's disease, ulcerative colitis, familial adenomatous polyposis, or CRC recorded on or before the index EMR date were excluded. The primary outcome was incident CRC, defined by ICD-10-CM codes C18, C19, and C20, assessed from January 1, 2018 through December 31, 2021 after a one-year washout period. Incidence rates are reported per 1,000 person-years with exact Poisson 95% confidence intervals (CIs). A sensitivity analysis was restricted to patients aged 50-75 years at index EMR. Among 3,081 eligible patients, the mean age was 62.9 ± 8.89 years and 52% were female; 2,735 were at risk at the start of follow-up. Twenty-two incident CRC diagnoses occurred over 10,187.8 person-years, an incidence of 2.16 per 1,000 person-years (95% CI, 1.35-3.27). Each calendar year contained 10 or fewer events, so annual rates could not be estimated. Incidence was 2.54 (95% CI, 1.31-4.44) in males and 1.83 (95% CI, 0.88-3.36) in females. In the 50-75-year sensitivity cohort, 19 events occurred over 8,894.8 person-years (2.14 per 1,000 person-years; 95% CI, 1.29-3.34). During years 1-5 after index EMR, repeat EMR occurred in 119 patients (3.9%), colorectal surgery in 28 (0.9%), and subsequent colorectal polyp diagnoses in 1,321 (42.9%); no ESD procedures were identified. CRC diagnoses after EMR were uncommon in this multicenter EHR cohort, occurring at about 2 per 1,000 person-years. Event counts were too small to estimate annual trends or to compare incidence reliably across race and ethnicity groups. Studies linking EHR data to endoscopy and pathology reports are needed to identify preventable cancers after EMR.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The undulating topography of the intestinal epithelium creates regionalized homeostatic niches at the base of each crypt, with each niche supporting neutrally evolving oligoclonal stem cell populations. At the crypt base, the fate of stem cell progeny is tightly regulated by intercompartmental polarized morphogenetic gradients, which converge to instruct continuous, but controlled, epithelial-cell turnover. To initiate tumorigenesis, a neoplastic clone must defy or escape such morphogenetic constraints either by outcompeting neighbouring stem cells or by establishing an ectopic stem cell population de novo. The position of the cell-of-origin within the crypt thus determines the oncogenic mechanisms required to subvert local homeostatic control. In turn, this defines the route of carcinogenesis and underpins the pervasive heterogeneity of colorectal cancers. Here, we explore the relationship between the position of the cell-of-origin on the vertical crypt axis and the cell plasticity mechanisms co-opted and corrupted to escape homeostatic control. We consider how this influences clonal dynamics at the pre-cancer stage and initiates distinct carcinogenesis pathways engendering morphologically discrete precursor lesions. Finally, we discuss how such lesions progress to molecularly heterogeneous subtypes with distinct clinicopathological features and therapeutic outcomes, and how phenotypic, rather than just genotypic, heterogeneity promotes tumour-cell adaptation, therapeutic resistance and metastasis.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Changes in visceral surgical care in Germany during the early COVID-19 pandemic have not yet been sufficiently described. To date, data on in-hospital mortality and postoperative complications remain limited. In this retrospective analysis, anonymized administrative data from the Federal Statistical Office of Germany (Destatis) for the period from 2018 to 2021 were evaluated comparatively, focusing on the most frequently performed visceral surgical procedures nationwide. Demographic characteristics, procedure volumes, length of hospital stay on regular wards and intensive care units, postoperative complications, and in-hospital mortality were analyzed. A total of approximately 2.1 million procedures were recorded over the 4-year study period. Compared with the pre-pandemic years 2018 and 2019, procedure volumes decreased by approximately 9% in 2020 and 2021, respectively. The average length of stay in the intensive care unit and in hospital decreased during the pandemic. Postoperative complications, including pulmonary embolism, acute kidney injury, sepsis, and peritonitis, increased during the pandemic years compared with the preceding years. Overall in-hospital mortality in visceral surgery increased from 2.43% in 2018 to 2.55% in 2020 and 2.53% in 2021. In particular, in-hospital mortality in colorectal surgery increased from 7.37% in 2019 to 7.95% in 2021, while the mortality among COVID-19-positive patients following colorectal procedures reached 48%. In contrast, mortality rates in esophageal, hepatic, and pancreatic surgery remained largely unchanged. During the COVID-19 pandemic, Germany experienced a substantial reduction in the volume of visceral surgical procedures and hospital length of stay, while postoperative complications and in-hospital mortality increased. A potential causal relationship with SARS-CoV-2 cannot be established based on the available data. These findings emphasize the importance of systematically evaluating the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on surgical care in Germany and of developing evidence-based strategies to maintain surgical capacity and patient safety during future pandemics.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
This study aimed to investigate the preoperative predictive value of multimodal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) radiomics combined with clinical risk factors for lymph node metastasis in rectal cancer, and to construct and validate an efficient and reproducible preoperative prediction model. A retrospective analysis was conducted on 129 patients with pathologically confirmed rectal cancer who underwent surgery at our hospital between 2017 and 2023. Preoperative pelvic T2-weighted imaging (T2WI), contrast-enhanced T1-weighted imaging (T1CE), and complete clinical data were collected. Three-dimensional regions of interest were manually segmented on the tumors using ITK-SNAP software, and radiomic features were selected via variance filtering and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression. Patients were randomly divided into a training cohort (n = 90) and an internal validation cohort (n = 39) at a 7:3 ratio. Five Logistic regression prediction models were constructed: single-sequence radiomics, multimodal radiomics, multimodal radiomics combined with clinical risk factors, and clinical factors alone. Using postoperative pathology as the gold standard, the diagnostic performance of each model was evaluated by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy. The multimodal radiomics combined with clinical risk factors model demonstrated the best predictive performance, with an AUC of 0.885 (95% CI: 0.819-0.937), sensitivity of 85.3%, specificity of 82.1%, and accuracy of 83.6% in the internal validation cohort. Its performance was significantly superior to that of the single-sequence models, the multimodal radiomics model, and the clinical model alone (all P < 0.05). Entropy from T2WI, peak enhancement from T1CE, tumor volume, tumor size, carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA), and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) were identified as independent predictors of lymph node metastasis. Calibration curves and decision curve analysis confirmed that the model was well-calibrated and provided substantial net clinical benefit. Integrating multimodal MRI radiomics from T2WI and T1CE with clinical indicators such as CEA and NLR significantly improves the preoperative prediction of lymph node metastasis in rectal cancer, demonstrating promising clinical applicability. However, as this was a single-center retrospective study, further multicenter, large-sample external validation is warranted to confirm the stability and generalizability of the model.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
BRAF V600E mutations occur in approximately 8 to 12% of metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) cases and define an aggressive phenotype with poor prognosis. While the BEACON CRC trial established encorafenib-based combinations as effective second-line options, direct head-to-head comparisons among available BRAF-targeted regimens are lacking. This network meta-analysis (NMA) compared the relative efficacy and safety of second- and later-line BRAF-targeted regimens in BRAF V600E-mutant mCRC. PubMed, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from inception through January 2026. Eligible studies enrolled adult patients with BRAF V600E-mutant mCRC receiving second- or later-line BRAF-targeted therapy and reported time-to-event survival outcomes. A frequentist NMA was conducted under a random-effects model using the netmeta package in R. Hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled for progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS). Where HRs were unavailable, individual patient data were reconstructed from Kaplan-Meier curves using the Guyot method. Treatment ranking used P-scores, with irinotecan plus cetuximab as the reference comparator. Four trials enrolling 922 patients across 9 treatment arms were included. All 4 experimental regimens demonstrated significant PFS benefit over irinotecan plus cetuximab. Encorafenib plus cetuximab plus alpelisib ranked highest for PFS (HR 0.33, 95% CI 0.15-0.71; P-score 0.789), followed by encorafenib plus binimetinib plus cetuximab (EBC; HR 0.38, 95% CI 0.29-0.49), encorafenib plus cetuximab (EC; HR 0.40, 95% CI 0.31-0.50), and vemurafenib plus irinotecan plus cetuximab (HR 0.50, 95% CI 0.32-0.77). For OS, only EBC (HR 0.52, 95% CI 0.39-0.69) and EC (HR 0.59, 95% CI 0.46-0.76) achieved statistically significant benefits. No significant difference was detected between EBC and EC on either endpoint. No between-study heterogeneity was detected (I2 = 0%). In the exploratory safety network, encorafenib plus cetuximab was the only encorafenib-based regimen associated with significantly fewer grade ≥ 3 adverse events than irinotecan plus cetuximab (odds ratio 0.67, 95% CI 0.47-0.96). These findings position encorafenib-based therapy, and encorafenib plus cetuximab in particular, as the reference standard for previously treated BRAF V600E-mutant mCRC, while underscoring that the incremental value of more intensive regimens must be weighed against tolerability and confirmed in adequately powered trials.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Real-world safety profiles of targeted therapies for colorectal cancer (CRC) remain incompletely characterized, particularly across different chemotherapy backbones. This study characterizes adverse event (AE) reporting patterns for bevacizumab (BVZ), cetuximab (C225), and panitumumab (VEC), used as monotherapy or in combination with folinic acid, fluorouracil, and oxaliplatin (FOLFOX) or folinic acid, fluorouracil, and irinotecan (FOLFIRI), within CRC-related reports. CRC-related AE reports from 2006 to 2025 for BVZ, C225, and VEC were extracted from the U.S. FDA Adverse Event Reporting System. Disproportionality signals were evaluated using 4 algorithms: the reporting odds ratio (ROR), proportional reporting ratio, Bayesian confidence propagation neural network, and multi-item gamma Poisson shrinker. Time-to-onset, regimen-stratified, and exploratory univariable logistic regression analyses were also conducted. The non-case reference population was restricted to the CRC-related reporting subcohort rather than the entire FDA Adverse Event Reporting System database. A total of 38,117 reports were identified, mainly involving BVZ (n = 20,521). Hematologic, hepatobiliary, and gastrointestinal toxicities showed prominent reporting signals across regimens (ROR = 4.15, 2.84, and 2.46, respectively). BVZ was associated with proteinuria and hand-foot syndrome, while C225 and VEC showed prominent cutaneous and marrow-suppression signals. Nine AE terms overlapped across agents, including thrombocytopenia, with fatality proportions of 23%, 13%, and 10% for BVZ, C225, and VEC, respectively. Median onset of nonfatal thrombocytopenia differed by agent: 121 days for BVZ, 6 days for C225, and 40 days for VEC; fatal C225-associated events also occurred early (median 6 days, P = .006). FOLFOX strengthened thrombocytopenia signals, especially with VEC-FOLFOX (ROR = 10.5) and C225-FOLFOX (ROR = 9.3), and peripheral neuropathy was reported across FOLFOX-containing regimens. CRC targeted therapies showed agent- and regimen-specific AE reporting patterns. Thrombocytopenia varied by onset and fatality and was more prominent with FOLFOX-containing regimens. These findings support tailored monitoring, particularly platelet surveillance for C225 and FOLFOX-based combinations, with longer-term vigilance for BVZ. Given the limitations of spontaneous reporting, including potential co-medication, indication-related, and residual confounding, these signals should not be interpreted as establishing causality.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Chromosomal instability (CIN), a common hallmark in most solid cancers, is characterized by structural and numerical errors during cell division. Maintenance and repression of constitutive heterochromatin, including regions like telomeres and pericentromeres, as well as repetitive elements (RE), is a critical step in preventing CIN. The histone chaperone DAXX, together with other epigenetic factors, helps preserve repression at these loci by depositing histone H3.3 and supporting histone repressive marks and DNA methylation. In the present study, we knocked down DAXX in the CIN-stable colorectal cancer cell line HCT116. We observed an increase in micronuclei and loss of DNA methylation at specific heterochromatic regions, which in turn led to the abnormal expression of repetitive elements such as the LRT7Y subfamily, normally active only during development. These findings highlight the role of DAXX in maintaining genomic stability by regulating heterochromatin and silencing specific repetitive elements.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) leaves a large mucosal defect that predisposes patients to delayed adverse events, chiefly delayed bleeding. Prophylactic closure of the defect has been proposed to improve safety, but its overall efficacy remains uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis provides an updated synthesis of the safety and efficacy of prophylactic mucosal defect closure after colorectal ESD. PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched from inception to June 2026, without language restrictions, for randomized controlled trials and comparative observational studies comparing prophylactic closure with no closure after colorectal ESD. The primary outcome was delayed bleeding; secondary outcomes were delayed perforation, post-ESD coagulation syndrome (PECS), and length of hospital stay. Pooled RRs and mean differences with 95% CIs were calculated using random-effects models, and the certainty of evidence was assessed with GRADE. Sixteen studies comprising 5,830 procedures were included. Prophylactic closure was associated with a lower risk of delayed bleeding (RR 0.42; 95% CI, 0.28 to 0.62; I² = 63.9%), with pooled delayed bleeding rates of 2.4% with closure and 6.9% without closure. No difference was observed for delayed perforation (RR 0.89; 95% CI, 0.37 to 2.17), PECS (RR 1.12; 95% CI, 0.50 to 2.49), or length of hospital stay (mean difference 0.16 days; 95% CI, -0.61 to 0.93). Small-study effects were detected for delayed bleeding, and the certainty of evidence ranged from low to very low. Prophylactic closure after colorectal ESD reduced delayed bleeding. No effect on delayed perforation, PECS, or length of hospital stay was shown, although these estimates were imprecise. Closure may be best reserved for patients at high risk of bleeding.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Filopodia are thin extensions of the plasma membrane that are rich in actin, which helps in cancer cells migration and invasion characters. TRIM11 (Tripartite motif 11), an E3 ubiquitin ligase, plays an important part in the progression and advanced stage of colorectal cancer (CRC); however, its role in the remodeling of the cytoskeleton is not well established. This present study explored the role of TRIM11 in regulating filopodia formation and metastatic behavior in CRC cells by bioinformatic, molecular docking and functional analysis. TRIM11 was knocked down in CRC (HCT116) using siRNA targeting TRIM11 and it was validated by western blot analysis. The migration and invasion of CRC cells dramatically impaired by silencing TRIM11 in HCT116 confirmed by trans well invasion assay and Scratch wound healing assay. Moreover, TRIM11 knockdown facilitated autophagy related markers. Reduced expression of antiapoptotic marker (BCL2) and inhibition of EMT (Epithelial to mesenchymal transition) marker further confirmed the enhanced apoptosis and decreased metastatic progression in TRIM11-silenced HCT116 cells. Immunofluorescence investigation validated that TRIM11 silencing impaired the length and quantity of filopodia on the cellular surface. Mechanically, the expression of TRIM11 was found to have a positive correlation with the expression of key modulators involved in the reorganization of the actin cytoskeleton, such as ARP2, ARP3, WAVE2, and N-WASP. Filopodia development in CRC cells was inhibited by the suppression of N-WASP/ARP2/ARP3 pathway.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
T cell senescence is an important dysfunctional state associated with tumor progression, but whether senescent T (Tsen) cells directly reprogram tumor cell behavior remains unknown. Here, single-cell transcriptomic analyses identify abundant Tsen cells across breast, colorectal, and lung cancers. Tsen cells actively promote tumor growth, metastasis, stemness, and chemotherapy resistance by reprogramming tumor cells in vitro and in vivo. Mechanistically, lipid-enriched senescence-associated secretory phenotypes (SASPs) from Tsen cells drive metabolic remodeling and activate STAT1/STAT3 signaling in tumor cells, establishing a pro-tumorigenic state. Therapeutically, depletion of Tsen cells or disruption of tumor lipid metabolic reprogramming suppresses Tsen-mediated tumor progression and metastasis in vivo. Our findings establish Tsen cells as active orchestrators of tumor cell biological functions through lipid-rich SASP-dependent intercellular communication and reveal a previously unrecognized mechanism linking immune senescence to cancer progression. Targeting Tsen cells or their metabolic crosstalk with tumor cells can enhance anti-tumor immunity and improve therapeutic responses.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a major health burden, while the therapeutic application of artesunate (ART) is limited by its chemical instability, rapid systemic clearance, and insufficient local retention. In this study, ART-loaded fungal chitosan (FCS)/poly(ε-caprolactone) (PCL) core-shell nanofibrous membranes were fabricated by coaxial electrospinning for sustained ART delivery and in vitro colorectal cancer cell inhibition. Morphological characterization confirmed the formation of continuous nanofibers with a distinct core-shell architecture, while ART loading produced formulation-dependent changes in fiber diameter, mechanical properties, surface wettability, swelling behavior, and thermal characteristics. ART@FCS/PCL mitigated burst release and exhibited sustained, pH-dependent ART release, with cumulative release exceeding 90% within 24 h at pH 6.5, compared with approximately 60% at pH 7.4. Biological evaluations demonstrated acceptable cytocompatibility toward normal colonic epithelial cells and inhibitory effects on CRC cells. At 72 h, ART10@FCS/PCL maintained approximately 87% viability in NCM460 cells while reducing RKO cell viability to approximately 68%. Apoptosis-related analysis showed that ART10@FCS/PCL upregulated Bax, downregulated Bcl-2, and increased cleaved Caspase-3 expression. Collectively, the FCS/PCL core-shell nanofibers provide a potential platform for sustained ART delivery and in vitro colorectal cancer cell inhibition, although further in vivo validation is required.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Small-molecule therapy for colorectal cancer (CRC) has expanded beyond conventional chemotherapy and broad multikinase inhibition, yet its clinical impact remains constrained by pathway redundancy, molecular heterogeneity, adaptive resistance, and narrow therapeutic windows. This review examines CRC drug discovery from a medicinal chemistry perspective, focusing on how chemical design can be aligned with disease biology and therapeutic context. We first evaluate clinically investigated strategies targeting major signaling pathways and molecular nodes, including the MAPK, PI3K/AKT/mTOR, WNT/β-catenin and receptor tyrosine kinase targets. Among the 89 representative compounds reviewed, 70 have been clinically investigated in CRC, providing a disease-specific translational context for analyzing scaffold evolution, binding-mode optimization, covalent and allosteric mechanisms, and structure-activity relationships. We then examine emerging small molecules that exploit adaptive vulnerabilities or enable context-dependent therapeutic strategies, including approaches to restore drug sensitivity, exploit adaptive vulnerabilities, and improve pharmacological deployment. These developments indicate a shift from target-centered inhibitor optimization toward target-state-context alignment. Future CRC medicinal chemistry will increasingly depend not only on potency and selectivity, but also on matching chemical mechanisms to the appropriate genotype, resistance state, tissue environment, and treatment setting.

Risk stratification in localized colorectal cancer (CRC) remains inadequate. Transcriptome-based classifiers such as consensus molecular subtyping (CMS) improve this, but are challenging to implement. We determined the performance of a novel image-based method for CRC CMS subtyping (imCMS) using routine pathology images from the SCOT trial and investigated association of imCMS subtypes with clinicopathologic and tumor molecular and immune factors, treatment benefit, and survival. We applied a novel imCMS classifier to stage II/III CRCs from the SCOT trial (ISRCTN59757862) which examined 3 versus 6 months of adjuvant oxaliplatin-based chemotherapy following curative-intent surgery. We determined correlates of imCMS subgroups and investigated imCMS prognostic and predictive value for CRC recurrence-free interval, overall survival (OS), and survival after CRC recurrence (SAR) by univariable and multivariable Cox regression. Analysis confirmed expected associations of imCMS1 with deficient DNA mismatch repair (dMMR) and imCMS3 with imCMS classification improves CRC prognostication beyond existing tumor factors and is potentially deliverable in clinical practice. imCMS prediction of therapeutic benefit requires further study.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The goal of this project was to develop a joint European clinical practice guideline for the diagnosis and treatment of obstructed defecation syndrome (ODS), based on the best available evidence. These guidelines are intended to support all healthcare professionals involved in the care of patients with ODS, such as general practitioners, colorectal surgeons, gastroenterologists, gynecologists, radiologists, physiotherapists, and psychologists, as well as to provide accessible information for patients themselves. A multidisciplinary Guideline Development Group representing seven European scientific societies and including patient representatives formulated PICO-based clinical questions. Evidence was identified through a systematic literature review and assessed using the GRADE approach. Recommendations were formulated according to the available evidence and, where evidence was insufficient, as expert opinions. The final guideline includes 28 statements (1 moderate grade evidence, 2 low grade evidence, 3 very low grade evidence, 22 expert opinion) covering the diagnosis, conservative and surgical management of ODS, including indications for various imaging modalities, functional tests, and both transanal and transabdominal surgical approaches. Multidisciplinary assessment is recommended throughout the diagnostic and therapeutic pathway. Conservative treatment represents the initial management strategy, with biofeedback recommended before surgery in patients with ODS and dyssynergic defecation who fail dietary and laxative treatment. Surgery should be reserved for selected patients with persistent symptoms after conservative treatment and considered following multidisciplinary pelvic floor evaluation. These multidisciplinary European guidelines offer a comprehensive and evidence-based framework for the diagnosis and management of ODS. They are intended to promote standardized, high-quality care across Europe and to improve outcomes and quality of life for individuals affected by this complex condition. Given the limited quality of evidence supporting many interventions, individualized decision-making within a multidisciplinary setting remains central to ODS management.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Low dietary calcium intake (DCI) is a modifiable risk factor for colorectal cancer (CRC). This study examined CRC burden attributable to low DCI in China and globally from 1990 to 2023 using Global Burden of Disease 2023 data. Joinpoint regression assessed temporal trends, age-period-cohort analysis characterized age, period, and cohort patterns, and Bayesian age-period-cohort modeling projected burden through 2040. In 2023, China had 15,934 attributable deaths (95% uncertainty interval [UI]: 10,999-22,042) and 371,105 disability-adjusted life years (DALYs; 95% UI: 253,587-509,717), representing decreases of 14.67% and 31.77% since 1990, respectively, whereas global counts increased. China's age-standardized mortality and DALY rates declined by 70.00% and 72.19%, with average annual percentage changes of -3.60% and -3.82%, respectively. Both rates increased during 2020-2023. Women had a higher attributable burden than men, and mortality rates were relatively high in older age groups. Period and cohort rate ratios declined in China. By 2040, attributable deaths and DALYs in China were projected to reach 44,191 and 837,178, respectively, with larger relative increases than globally. Despite long-term declines, the recent rebound and projected increases highlight the continuing relevance of improving dietary calcium adequacy and CRC prevention in China, with attention to age- and sex-specific differences in attributable burden.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Circadian physiology coordinates systemic and cellular metabolism through a light-entrained central clock and metabolically synchronized peripheral clocks. Whether feeding-fasting cycles or tumor-intrinsic clocks primarily set tumor metabolic state is unclear. Here, we profiled colorectal cancer (CRC) responses to PPAR antagonists across 2D and 3D CRC models and tumor-bearing mice. In standard high-glucose, low-fat medium, Bmal1 oscillations and daily variation in PPAR antagonist sensitivity were apparent in CRC cells. By contrast, nutrient-defined media that recapitulate feeding and nighttime fasting abolished time-dependent variability and unified drug responses across models. Still, the fed state selectively sensitized spheroids and patient-derived organoids to PPAR-γ antagonism. In mice, dosing PPAR-γ antagonist in the fed state prolonged survival and reduced hepatotoxicity. The use of Bmal-1-silenced CRC cells validated that feeding-fasting rhythms, not tumor-intrinsic clocks, govern CRC sensitivity to PPAR antagonists. Our study also supports the predictive capacity of nutrient-alternating 3D tumor models, enabling metabolism-targeted anticancer treatment evaluation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Robotic surgery has become an established approach for the management of patients with sigmoid colon and upper rectal cancer (SURC). Natural orifice specimen extraction surgery (NOSES), which avoids an additional abdominal wall incision, is a widely used minimally invasive approach in colorectal cancer (CRC) surgery. It remains uncertain whether transanal specimen extraction, classified as type IV natural orifice specimen extraction surgery (NOSES-IV), offers advantages over conventional transabdominal specimen extraction (TASE) during robot-assisted surgery for SURC. We retrospectively compared the perioperative outcomes of the two extraction strategies. We retrospectively reviewed 254 patients who underwent robot-assisted surgery for SURC at the First Affiliated Hospital of Jiangxi Medical College, Nanchang University, between January 2019 and January 2026. Ninety-one patients received NOSES-IV, and 163 received TASE. After 1:1 propensity score matching (PSM), 83 patients per group were included, and their short-term perioperative outcomes were compared. After matching, the baseline characteristics did not differ significantly between the two groups. Compared with the TASE group, the NOSES-IV group had a shorter gastrointestinal reconstruction time (P < 0.001) and less intraoperative blood loss (P = 0.022). Patients in the NOSES-IV group also ambulated (P = 0.029), passed flatus (P = 0.018), and resumed semiliquid diet earlier (P = 0.038). On postoperative days 1, 3 and 5, their C-reactive protein levels were lower (P = 0.017). They also had fewer incision-related complications (P = 0.014), a shorter postoperative hospital stay (P = 0.034), and lower visual analogue scale (VAS) pain scores (P = 0.008). In this retrospective, propensity score-matched cohort, compared with TASE, robot-assisted NOSES-IV for SURC was associated with fewer incision-related complications, less postoperative pain, and earlier recovery. The total operative time, lymph node yield, resection margin status, and anorectal function at 3 months did not differ between the groups. These findings suggest that NOSES-IV is a feasible option for appropriately selected patients, but confirmation in larger, multicentre, prospective studies with longer follow-up is needed.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) is rising across Southeast Asia (SEA) and leads by incidence in Brunei Darussalam. Machine learning (ML) applications for CRC in ASEAN remain endoscopy-based and diagnostic; no risk-stratification model using routinely collected non-invasive data has been reported. This review asks not which predictors associate with CRC risk, but which can serve as valid, equitable ML inputs in multiethnic SEA populations, where lifestyle variables may encode ethnic or religious identity rather than biological risk (proxy-mediated bias). This narrative review used qualitative synthesis rather than meta-analysis. PubMed, Scopus and Google Scholar were searched to 9 July 2026 (English language). Six predictor categories were appraised for Asian evidence strength, SEA-specific data, and proxy-bias risk: dietary and lifestyle factors, anthropometric measures, faecal immunochemical test (FIT), complete blood count (CBC), medication history, and emerging predictors; 22 studies were prioritised for appraisal. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Skin-level anal stricture following posterior sagittal anorectoplasty and congenital short-segment anal stenosis are known causes of obstructive defecation in children. This study evaluated the feasibility and preliminary outcomes of Heineke-Mikulicz anoplasty for these superficial stenoses. This retrospective study reviewed 21 pediatric patients who underwent HMA between January 2021 and December 2025 at a tertiary children's hospital. Patients included those with either postoperative skin-level strictures or congenital short-segment anal stenosis. Demographic, clinical, surgical, and follow-up data were analyzed. The cohort included 15 males and 6 females, with a mean age of 13.3 ± 6.2 months at the time of surgery. Fourteen patients had postoperative strictures, and seven had congenital stenosis. The average increase in anal caliber was from Hegar size 8.9 ± 1.0 to 14.7 ± 0.8. No intraoperative or postoperative complications occurred, and none required repeat HMA. All patients with preoperative constipation showed functional improvement. Sixteen patients were discharged within 24 h postoperatively, and five stayed for 6 days due to concurrent colostomy closure. HMA was technically feasible and associated with immediate anal enlargement and encouraging preliminary clinical outcomes in selected children with superficial anal stenoses. No complications or repeat HMA were recorded during available follow-up. Long-term functional outcomes, late recurrence, and comparative effectiveness remain uncertain.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Adequate intestinal perfusion is essential in pediatric colorectal surgery. Indocyanine green fluorescence angiography (ICG-FA) is increasingly used to assess perfusion, yet its impact on postoperative outcomes remains unclear. We evaluated the association between ICG-FA use and clinical outcomes in children undergoing colorectal procedures. We performed a retrospective cohort study of pediatric patients undergoing posterior sagittal anorectoplasty (PSARP) for anorectal malformations, pull-through for Hirschsprung disease, or cloacal repair between 2016 and 2025. Primary outcomes included anastomotic disruption, stricture, and reoperation. Among 184 patients, 37 (20.1%) underwent intraoperative ICG-FA. Patients receiving ICG-FA were older and more likely to undergo complex procedures (59.5% vs. 15.7%, p < 0.001). ICG-FA altered intraoperative decision-making in five cases (13.5%). Rates of anastomotic disruption and reoperation were similar between groups. Stricture rates were significantly lower in the ICG group (2.7% vs. 17.0%, p = 0.032). Among complex cases, no strictures occurred in the ICG group compared with 7 (30.4%) in the non-ICG group (p = 0.009). On multivariable logistic regression, ICG use remained associated with lower observed stricture rates (OR 0.12, 95% CI 0.01-0.61). ICG can influence surgical decision-making and may be particularly useful in complex colorectal reconstructions. Postoperative stricture rates were lower among patients who underwent ICG-FA, particularly those undergoing more complex operations.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Medical-legal partnerships can address health-harming legal needs (HHLNs) but caregiver-inclusive models are understudied. To evaluate the feasibility, acceptability, and preliminary efficacy in addressing HHLNs of proactive legal care for patient-caregiver dyads. This single-arm pilot trial (NCT07153016) enrolled patients with advanced-stage colorectal cancer and their self-nominated caregiver. Cancer Legal Care (CLC) provided personalized legal checkups and 3-month follow-up at no cost. Feasibility was assessed by rates of initial checkup, 3-month engagement, and receipt of legal service. Acceptability was assessed by likelihood of recommending the intervention to others. Participant-reported outcomes, implementation measures, and interviews were summarized. We enrolled 9 of 10 planned dyads. Among the 9 enrolled, 8 completed baseline surveys, 7 completed initial legal checkups, and 7 completed 3-month assessments. Initial legal checkups lasted a median of 45 minutes, and CLC provided median 4 hours of legal service per dyad. At baseline, 7 of 16 participants self-identified HHLNs, while CLC identified 1.7 additional HHLNs per dyad. The study met predefined feasibility benchmarks [initial engagement (16/18, 89%), 3-month questionnaire completion (14/18, 78%), and receipt of ≥ 1 legal service (14/18, 78%)] and acceptability (12/14, 86% recommended the intervention) benchmarks. Dyads noted improvements in financial control, support-seeking, and maintaining daily activities; however, caregiver-specific needs were not consistently identified or prioritized. Proactive legal care for recently diagnosed patient-caregiver dyads was feasible and acceptable, and identified and addressed HHLNs. However, caregiver-inclusive medical-legal partnership models may require caregiver-specific intake, longitudinal follow-up, and clearer distinction between patient, caregiver, and shared needs.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Neoplastic polyps are precancerous lesions of colorectal cancer (CRC), yet proteomic studies for stratifying their malignant potential remain limited. In this study, we used the Olink proteomics platform to systematically analyze the expression of inflammation- and oncology-related proteins in colorectal polyp tissues from 94 patients. The results showed that most inflammation- and oncology-related proteins were expressed at higher levels in neoplastic polyps than in non-neoplastic polyps. We further screened differentially expressed proteins using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, random forest, and LASSO regression. These findings were then validated using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), public transcriptomic and single-cell transcriptomic datasets, and colonic immunohistochemistry (IHC) in colitis-associated colorectal cancer (CAC) and Apcmin/+ mouse models. In addition, 38 intestinal fluid samples were collected for supplementary validation. We ultimately identified ADAM8, WISP-1, MMP-1, and PPY as potential biomarkers of precancerous colorectal lesions. These proteins may provide valuable molecular evidence for deeper mechanistic studies of the CRC precancerous stage, early biomarker discovery, and prevention-oriented therapeutic development.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Synchronous rectal and prostate adenocarcinomas are uncommon and present a real surgical challenge because the tumors share the same tight pelvic space, particularly in men, and often require combined multimodal treatment. We describe the case of a 79-year-old man who was found to have a non-stenosing distal rectal adenocarcinoma (moderately differentiated, arising from a tubulo-villous adenoma with high-grade dysplasia, staged cT3 cN1 cM0) together with a concurrent prostate adenocarcinoma (cT1c cN0 cM0, Gleason 4 + 3 = 7, PSA 7.2 ng/mL, PI-RADS 4 lesion). After standard neoadjuvant radiochemotherapy for the rectal cancer, restaging showed a good local response. In July 2024, he underwent a planned single-stage combined robot-assisted procedure: abdominoperineal rectum extirpation with total mesorectal excision and terminal descendostomy, immediately followed by radical prostatectomy with bilateral pelvic lymphadenectomy. Final pathology confirmed significant treatment response in the rectum (ypT1 pN0 (0/19) R0 with 30% vital tumor) and ypT3a pN0 R0 prostate cancer. The whole procedure took approximately 7 h with minimal blood loss. He was discharged on day 8 with a functioning descendostomy and initial signs of good recovery. This case demonstrates the feasibility of a single-stage minimally invasive approach in a carefully selected older patient with comorbidities.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Bulk-tissue transcriptome-wide association studies (TWAS) have identified colorectal cancer (CRC) susceptibility genes, but cell-type-specific regulatory mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we performed single-cell TWAS integrating matched germline genotypes and single-cell transcriptomes from normal colorectal mucosa (381 donors) and polyps (84 donors), cell-type-specific chromatin accessibility, and GWAS from 132,261 cases and 1,752,398 controls. We identified 546 gene-cell-type associations implicating 347 candidate susceptibility genes across seven normal and nine polyp epithelial populations, including 213 previously unreported genes, with 74% exhibiting cell-type-specific associations. Integrated co-expression and ChIP-seq analyses revealed distinct TF-risk gene networks, highlighting GATA6, MAX and RAD21 in normal mucosa, and TFAP4- and CEBPB-associated networks in premalignant polyp populations. Further multi-omics analyses supported dysregulation of 233 genes (67%), while drug-target analyses identified 63 potentially druggable genes. DepMap and CRISPR-Cas9 analyses implicated 35 genes in CRC cell viability. These findings reveal cell-type-specific susceptibility mechanisms and prioritize candidate therapeutic targets for CRC prevention.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) represents a major global public health challenge, yet age- and sex-specific patterns in mortality burden and risk factor contributions remain incompletely characterised. We aimed to analyse global age- and sex-specific mortality patterns of CRC from 1990 to 2021, project trends to 2050, and assess the mortality burden attributable to risk factors. We extracted CRC mortality data from 204 countries and territories between 1990 and 2021 from Global Burden of Disease 2021. We stratified the population into very early-onset CRC (VEOCRC) (aged 15-34 years), early-onset CRC (EOCRC) (aged 35-49 years), and late-onset CRC (LOCRC) (aged 50-95 years). Age-specific mortality rates (MRs) characterised mortality burden, and estimated annual percentage changes quantified temporal trends. We applied population attributable fractions (PAFs) to estimate the mortality burden attributable to risk factors and used Bayesian age-period-cohort models to project global mortality trends from 2022 to 2050. From 1990 to 2021, LOCRC accounted for the greatest global mortality burden, followed by EOCRC and VEOCRC. The VEOCRC and EOCRC MRs were highest in East Asia, while LOCRC rates were highest among females in Australasia and males in Western Europe. All three subtypes had the highest MRs in the high-middle sociodemographic index region. Males consistently had higher MRs than females across all three subtypes. Generally, MRs declined from 1990 to 2021 across all three CRC subtypes, although some low- and middle-income regions, particularly East Asia, Latin America, and Africa, showed increasing trends. The PAFs of risk factors increased with age, particularly for behavioural, metabolic, and dietary factors. Projections suggested declining global CRC age-standardised MRs by 2050, while LOCRC would remain the major contributor, with rates of 57.47 per 100,000 in males and 31.40 in females. We found substantial age, sex, and regional disparities in global CRC mortality. Despite projected declines by 2050, LOCRC will remain the dominant contributor, while younger-onset CRC warrants greater attention.
