ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Most colorectal cancers (CRCs) arise from polyps that develop malignant traits over time. As the majority of these are sporadic, environmental determinants including the gut microbiota are increasingly implicated. Dysbiosis is consistently observed in CRC; however, its association with precancerous polyps is less defined. A systematic review of PubMed, Embase and Web of Science from January 2015 to June 2025 was therefore performed, using the following strings: ('colon' OR 'colorectal') AND ('adenoma' OR 'polyp' OR 'neoplasia') AND ('microbiota' OR 'bacteria') AND ('mucosa' OR 'tissue'). Human studies comparing microbiota of polyp patients with healthy controls were included. Controls were defined a priori as subjects with a normal colonoscopy. Laboratory methods were extracted and study heterogeneity was addressed through narrative synthesis. The search yielded 722 articles, with 27 studies included, involving 4510 participants. Alpha diversity was unchanged in most studies (n = 11/14), whereas beta diversity was altered in the majority (n = 7/13). Escherichia coli, Bacteroides fragilis and Fusobacterium nucleatum were consistently enriched taxa in polyp cohorts (n = 11/27 studies). Bacterial traits associated with adhesion, invasion, and genotoxicity were enriched in polyp subjects alongside metabolic adaptations for stress. However, overt tissue-invasive behaviour was not observed. A decrease in the Firmicutes:Bacteroidetes (F:B) ratio is proposed as a potentially relevant biomarker but requires validation. Future translation of this data into clinical settings requires integration of histopathologic and longitudinal analyses.

Colorectal cancer (CRC) with KRAS mutations represents a clinically challenging subgroup with variable treatment responses. Among these tumors, codon 12 mutations are associated with poor prognosis and treatment resistance, while KRASG12D-mutant CRCs lack effective mutation-specific therapeutic options. Toxoplasma gondii dense granule protein 16 (GRA16) is a parasite-derived host-modulating effector that modulates phosphatase and tensin homolog (PTEN)/p53, protein phosphatase 2A-B55 (PP2A-B55)-associated signaling, and cancer-associated metabolic pathways. We evaluated the anticancer effects of GRA16 in KRASG12D-mutant LS174T cells using KRASG13D-mutant HCT116 cells as a comparative TP53-wild-type CRC model. Stable GRA16-expressing cells were generated by lentiviral transduction and assessed for proliferation, cell death-associated responses, DNA damage/apoptosis-related protein markers, key signaling proteins, and targeted transcriptional changes. GRA16 inhibited proliferation and increased cell death-associated populations in both cell lines, accompanied by elevated γ-H2A.X, cleaved PARP, and cleaved caspase-3 levels. In HCT116 cells, GRA16 increased PTEN, p53, and PP2A-B55 protein levels and reduced total AKT and Survivin proteins, together with BAX induction and suppression of cell-cycle/checkpoint-, epithelial mesenchymal transition/motility-, and glycolysis-associated transcripts. In LS174T cells, GRA16 increased PP2A-B55 and reduced Survivin protein levels, whereas PTEN protein was unchanged, p53 was reduced, and total AKT was increased. These changes were accompanied by limited p53/BAX-associated transcriptional engagement, glycolytic attenuation, shared cell-cycle/checkpoint-associated gene suppression, and stress-adaptive remodeling. These findings suggest that GRA16 induces cell line-dependent anticancer-associated responses in KRAS-mutant CRC cells, with a prominent PTEN/p53-associated response in HCT116 cells and preserved PP2A-B55 induction and Survivin suppression in LS174T cells.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) remains a significant clinical challenge due to the emergence of drug resistance, highlighting the need for new therapeutic strategies. Aberrant regulation of the proteome drives cancer progression, and dissecting these alterations offers opportunities for targeted intervention. We aimed to identify candidate kinase dependencies in mCRC and to test a rational combination strategy in patient-derived models. We performed proteomic and phosphoproteomic profiling of 10 mCRC tissues, their matched patient-derived organoids (PDOs) and normal colon mucosa, integrated with whole-exome sequencing. Kinase activities were inferred by kinase-substrate enrichment analysis. Silmitasertib-mediated casein kinase II (CKII) inhibition, alone and combined with the MEK inhibitor trametinib, was evaluated by ex vivo drug screening, western blot, flow cytometry and drug-interaction analysis across the PDO cohort and in normal colon PDOs. PDOs recapitulated the molecular features of matched tumours. Both tissues and PDOs showed consistently elevated CKII activity. Silmitasertib exerted heterogeneous antitumour activity, and resistance was associated with MAPK and Akt-mTOR signalling activity. Combining silmitasertib with trametinib produced an additive reduction of both resistance-associated pathways with little effect on the viability of normal colon PDOs. The combination also significantly reduced CKII activity, the abundance of active β-catenin and the colorectal cancer stem cell pool. Phosphoproteomic profiling identified CKII as a therapeutic vulnerability in mCRC and provided a rationale for combining silmitasertib with MEK inhibition, offering a candidate combination strategy for mCRC.

Robotic hernia repair has spread without demonstrated superiority, and its device-related adverse event reports are unstudied. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Pathogenic exonuclease domain mutations in POLE define a hypermutated subtype of colorectal and endometrial cancers, with prognostic and therapeutic implications, particularly for immunotherapy. Detection currently relies on next-generation sequencing, which is sensitive but costly and time-consuming. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Text message reminders (TMRs) and patient navigation (PN) increase bowel cancer screening uptake. To date, no studies have directly compared these interventions with one another. We conducted a three-arm randomised controlled trial with individuals, in London, who had not completed bowel cancer screening within 18 weeks of invitation. Participants were randomised to receive no reminder (usual care), TMRs at 19, 21, 23 and 25 weeks, or a TMR at 19 weeks, with telephone PN at 21, 23 and 25 weeks. The primary outcome was participation within 26 weeks of invitation. Differences were assessed using logistic regression. On an intention-to-treat basis (n = 3129), uptake was higher in the TMR and PN groups, compared with usual care (6.5% vs. 2.0%, p < 0.001; 7.5% vs. 2.0%, p < 0.001). There was no significant difference between TMR and PN groups. In the per-protocol analysis (n = 2294), uptake was significantly higher in the PN group than the TMR group (8.6 vs. 12.6%, p < 0.025). Subgroup analyses revealed telephone PN was significantly more effective than TMRs for men, specifically (14.5% vs. 6.7%, p < 0.001). While TMRs are no more effective than PN in general, implementing PN could help reduce disparities in uptake between men and women. ISRCTN17245519.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colonoscopy is central to colorectal cancer prevention because it enables early detection and removal of premalignant lesions. However, lesions can still be missed, and endoscopic differentiation of neoplastic from nonneoplastic polyps remains variable, particularly for diminutive lesions. The potential of artificial intelligence (AI) as a supportive technology for improving both polyp detection and characterization during colonoscopy has therefore been investigated. Since early studies of convolutional neural network-based computer-aided detection (CADe), the focus has shifted from retrospective image-based validation to real-time randomized trials, meta-analyses, and clinical guideline discussions. Accumulating evidence suggests that CADe improves surrogate detection outcomes, including the adenoma detection rate (ADR), polyp detection rate, adenomas per colonoscopy, and adenoma miss rate. Although a higher ADR is associated with a lower risk of postcolonoscopy colorectal cancer, it remains unknown whether the incremental improvement in the ADR achieved by CADe translates into lower postcolonoscopy colorectal cancer incidence or colorectal cancer-related mortality. Recent multicenter data further support the effectiveness of real-time CADe systems in improving detection-related outcomes, while also indicating that benefit varies with lesion characteristics and user experience. In parallel, computer-aided diagnosis (CADx) has been developed to assist the optical characterization of colorectal polyps, particularly for diminutive lesions and potential resect-and-discard or diagnose-and-leave strategies. CADx systems using white-light imaging and structured high-confidence diagnostic rules show promise, but the clinical implementation of CADx remains less mature than that of CADe. This review summarizes current evidence for AI-assisted polyp detection and characterization and discusses limitations and future directions for integrating CADe and CADx into human-centered colonoscopy practices.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Sphincter-preserving rectal surgery may be associated with functional disorders. Low anterior resection syndrome (LARS) is a complication that presents as faecal incontinence, urgency and fragmented stools. Its treatment is stepwise, with transanal irrigation (TAI) being a second-line treatment in refractory cases and a first-line treatment in major LARS. The aim is to analyse the usefulness of TAI in improving symptoms and quality of life in patients with major LARS or LARS refractory to treatment. A retrospective descriptive study of patients with LARS treated with TAI at our hospital. Demographic and clinical variables, details of previous treatments, factors related to rectal cancer and TAI, and scores on the LARS and EuroQol-5D scales were recorded before and 6 months after treatment. A sample of 25 patients with a mean age of 63.8 years, most of whom had undergone surgery for rectal cancer with end-to-end colorectal anastomosis. The LARS score improved from 33.5 to 24.6 following treatment. The EuroQol-5D score increased from 36 to 62.8, with both changes showing a statistically significant difference (p < 0.0001). Five patients (20%) discontinued treatment due to a lack of subjective improvement, and three (12%) showed poor adherence due to technical difficulties. In patients with major LARS or LARS refractory to medical treatment, TAI may be a useful and effective treatment, improving their symptoms and quality of life. It is a simple therapeutic strategy with few serious complications, although a considerable proportion of patients discontinue treatment. More extensive and structured programmes of education, training and follow-up should be implemented for patients eligible for this treatment.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Patient-reported outcomes (PROs) for individual patients with colorectal cancer (CRC) can be interpreted by using PRO scores with thresholds for clinical importance (TCIs). This study established TCIs for the European Organisation for Research and Treatment of Cancer Quality of Life Questionnaire Colorectal Cancer 29 (EORTC QLQ-CR29), a widely used PRO measure (PROM) in research and practice. Patients with CRC from six countries completed the EORTC QLQ-CR29. To establish TCIs, patients completed anchor questions assessing limitations in daily life, need for help and/or care, and patient and partner/family worries for each item. Diagnostic accuracy for each scale was then determined using ROC analysis, along with the sensitivity and specificity of the TCIs. In total, 240 patients (mean age: 62.2, 53% men) completed the EORTC QLQ-CR29 and anchor items on clinical importance. Area Under the ROC (AUC), a measure of diagnostic accuracy, was 0.80 or higher for 17 of the 22 QLQ-CR29 scales, with lower values observed for urinary frequency (0.79), blood and mucus in stool (0.79), dyspareunia (0.77), stoma care problems (0.74), and sexual interest (0.66). Sensitivity and specificity values for all TCIs ranged from 0.59 to 1.00, except for the sexual interest scale with a sensitivity of 0.35. TCIs for the EORTC QLQ-CR29 supporting the interpretation of absolute PROMs scores of individual patients were established. These will facilitate the use of the QLQ-CR29 in clinical practice, supporting the identification of clinically important health domains of individual patients with CRC from absolute PROM scores.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Circular RNAs (circRNAs) play a crucial role in regulating the progression of various cancers and the cancer immune microenvironment. However, the molecular mechanisms how the circRNAs influence colorectal cancer (CRC) development and tumor immune remain to be thoroughly explored and elucidated. We identified a novel CRC-associated circRNA (circRNA9389) through high-throughput sequencing. The circular structure of circRNA9389 was confirmed using Sanger sequencing and DNA electrophoresis with convergent and divergent primers. Quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR) was employed to explore the expression of circRNA9389 in cancerous and adjacent tissues and its correlation with PD-L1 expression. CRC cells and animal models were utilized to assess the effects of circRNA9389 on CRC proliferation and metastasis. Western blotting (WB), RNA immunoprecipitation (RIP), chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP), and dual-luciferase reporter assays were conducted to explore the mechanisms by which circRNA9389 promotes CRC progression and PD-L1 expression. CircRNA9389 was derived from Aspartate Beta-Hydroxylase (ASPH) gene, and significantly upregulated in CRC tissues, with high expression levels correlating with advanced TNM stage. A strong positive correlation was observed between circRNA9389 and PD-L1 mRNA expression. Overexpression of circRNA9389 promoted CRC cell proliferation, metastasis, and invasion, while its inhibition had the opposite effects. Mechanistically, circRNA9389 bound to the non-canonical nuclear localization signal (NLS) of the R3H domain of NKRF protein, thereby blocking its nuclear translocation, activating the NF-κB signaling pathway, and upregulating PD-L1 expression. Additionally, p65 in the NF-κB pathway bound to the P2 promoter region of the ASPH gene to enhance the synthesis of circRNA9389. Our study identifies a novel circRNA (circRNA9389), and reveals the mechanisms for circRNA9389 promoting CRC progression. Collectively, circRNA9389 might be a novel therapeutic target for CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colonoscopy quality and polyp findings were both associated with risk of post-colonoscopy colorectal cancer (PCCRC), yet their independent and joint effects remain unclear. We identified patients undergoing colonoscopy within the Mass General Brigham healthcare system during 2007-2023. Adenoma detection rate (ADR) and ten other quality indicators were assessed for each endoscopist. Index polyp findings were classified into no polyps, low-risk polyps, or high-risk polyps, according to polyp histology, size, and multiplicity. Multivariable-adjusted Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for PCCRC according to colonoscopy quality indicators and polyp findings. We further performed a joint analysis of ADR and index polyp findings. During a median follow-up of 9.2 years among 172,875 participants, we identified 233 PCCRC cases. Lower colonoscopy quality assessed by all indicators except advanced adenoma detection rate was consistently associated with higher PCCRC risk. Increasing ADR to ≥30% in women and ≥40% in men could prevent 46% of PCCRC cases (95%CI, 27-76%). In joint analyses, ADR and index polyp findings were independently associated with PCCRC risk (P for interaction=0.97). Compared with patients with no polyps and a high-ADR (quartile 4, median [interquartile range, IQR]: 42.4 [38.8-48.9]) colonoscopy, those with no polyps, low-risk polyps, and high-risk polyps and a low-ADR (quartile 1, median [IQR]: 17.6 [14.8-20.4]) colonoscopy exhibited higher PCCRC risks, with HRs (95%CIs) of 2.75 (1.27-5.95), 4.11 (1.77-9.57), and 7.69 (3.24-18.25), respectively. Colonoscopy quality and polyp findings jointly determine PCCRC risk, underscoring the importance of optimizing procedure quality and maintaining surveillance.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Published descriptions of retroperitoneal lymph node dissection (RPLND) vary considerably in the anatomical landmarks used to define dissection boundaries and in the terminology used to describe surgical templates. Although consensus guidelines such as the National Comprehensive Cancer Network recommendations exist for testicular cancer, the consistency with which anatomical borders are described across the urological, gynecological, and colorectal literature more broadly remains unclear. A systematic review was conducted in accordance with Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses and a prospectively registered protocol (PROSPERO CRD420251241950). The search strategy was designed to capture gynecological, colorectal, and urological literature reporting RPLND, and PubMed and Scopus were searched from inception to December 16, 2025. Two reviewers independently screened records, assessed full texts, and extracted data on study characteristics, anatomical borders, template nomenclature, and selected perioperative and oncological outcomes. Eighteen studies met inclusion criteria. Despite a search strategy designed to capture gynecological, colorectal, and urological literature, the available evidence was exclusively urological in origin, comprising 16 studies of testicular germ cell tumors, one study of renal cell carcinoma, and one study of prostate cancer; no eligible gynecological or colorectal studies were identified. Substantial heterogeneity was identified across all reported template dimensions despite the existence of National Comprehensive Cancer Network consensus recommendations for testicular cancer. The ureter was the most consistently used lateral boundary, whereas cranial, caudal, posterior, and interaortocaval limits varied widely between studies and across tumor types. The cranial border was the most commonly defined at the renal artery or renal vessels, but some series used the renal vein, renal hilum, or more restricted landmarks. Reporting of posterior boundaries and interaortocaval extent was frequently incomplete. Contemporary literature demonstrates marked inconsistency and in how RPLND boundaries are defined and reported across urological malignancies, even where consensus guidelines exist. Furthermore, there is a marked gap in RPLND reporting in gynecological and colorectal literature. Standardized, tumor-specific reporting of template borders is needed across the malignancies in which RPLND is performed, to improve comparison of outcomes, clarify the relationship between extent of dissection and morbidity, and support future consensus development grounded in patterns of nodal disease distribution.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
In Japan, physical restraints are commonly used in surgical care, despite growing concerns regarding their adverse effects. We aimed to examine the association between physical restraint on the day of surgery and subsequent restraint use, as well as length of stay among older adults undergoing colectomy for colon cancer who were eligible for dementia care. A retrospective cohort study. Patients aged ≥65 years who had undergone colectomy for colon cancer and were eligible for dementia care in Japan were included in the study. Data collected in the Japanese Diagnosis Procedure Combination database between April 2020 and March 2021 were retrospectively reviewed. The associations between physical restraint on the day of surgery (postoperative day 0 [POD 0]) and restraint use on POD 7 and postoperative length of stay were examined using multivariable regression analyses. For the analysis of postoperative length of stay, a modified study population was used in which complete restraint data through POD 7 were not required, provided that restraint status on POD 0 was ascertainable. Among the 760 patients included in the primary analysis, 28.3% were physically restrained on POD 0. Restraint on POD 0 was associated with higher odds of restraint on POD 7 (odds ratio, 7.27; 95% CI, 4.56-11.60). In the secondary analysis (n = 962), restraint on POD 0 was not associated with postoperative length of stay (adjusted coefficient, 0.05 days; 95% CI, -1.32 to 1.42). Physical restraint on the day of surgery was associated with restraint use on POD 7, suggesting the need for careful evaluation at the time of initiation. Patients restrained early after surgery may warrant careful reassessment of the continued need for restraint during the postoperative period.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Radiotherapy is clinically established in rectal cancer and is also used in selected colon cancer settings. However, treatment resistance and post-irradiation tumor regrowth remain major clinical challenges, and the residual cellular states that survive irradiation and later drive tumor regrowth remain poorly defined. We investigated irradiation-surviving persister populations in colorectal cancer (CRC), with a particular focus on cancer stem cell-associated changes, using CRC cell lines and patient-derived CRC organoids, including radiation-resistant models. Cells were analyzed before and after irradiation by flow cytometry, cell-tracing experiments, proliferation and drug sensitivity assays, xenograft studies, RNA sequencing, and DNA methylation profiling. In conventional CRC cell lines, CD44 and CD133 distributions remained largely unchanged after irradiation, even in radiation-resistant models. In contrast, patient-derived CRC organoids revealed the emergence of a CD44low persister population after irradiation. Cell-tracing experiments demonstrated that this population arose predominantly from parental CD44high cells rather than from expansion of pre-existing CD44low cells. Surviving CD44low cells regenerated CD44high cells, reconstituted parental-like heterogeneity, and exhibited enhanced proliferative capacity, chemoresistance, and tumor-forming ability with more prominent mucinous features compared with the surviving CD44high fraction. In radiation-resistant organoids, the CD44low/SSEA-4high persister population was associated with global hypomethylation and activation of pluripotency-related programs, including upregulation of NANOG, POU5F1, and SOX2 with reduced promoter-region methylation. These findings support the presence of an irradiation-associated, reversible CD44low/SSEA-4high persister state with epigenetic alterations linked to tumor regrowth and therapeutic resistance. Treatment-induced plasticity and associated epigenetic alterations may represent potential avenues for therapeutic intervention to achieve more durable radiotherapy responses in CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Missed diagnostic opportunities [MDOs] for cancer are a significant safety issue. This map identifies and characterises intervention evaluations, highlights evidence gaps and informs the focus of an effectiveness review. A policy and practice stakeholder group informed the work. We systematically searched 19 databases for primary studies and systematic reviews published between 2005 and 2025. Eligible evaluations addressed interventions to reduce MDOs in cancer within primary care, in high income countries. Review quality was assessed using AMSTAR-2, and the findings of the mapping exercise are presented in an online interactive map. We mapped 100 primary studies and 12 systematic reviews. Studies mostly targeted skin cancer and to a lesser extent, bowel cancer, with gaps for six other error-prone cancers such as lung and pancreatic. Education, and dermoscopy/teledermoscopy were commonly evaluated for skin cancer whereas biomarkers and direct test access were common for bowel cancer. Few studies assessed education outside skin cancer, examined core service delivery functions (e.g., follow-up and tracking), patient-focused approaches, patient outcomes, and equity. Most existing systematic reviews were low quality. Stakeholders interested in English policy prioritised generalisable approaches such as decision support and direct test access, which were present but not dominant. Significant gaps remain in evidence on interventions for error-prone cancers (e.g. lung and pancreatic), on specific intervention approaches (e.g., education, core service delivery functions and patient-centred approaches), patient outcomes, equity considerations, and high-quality systematic reviews. Further research is essential for improving diagnostic safety in primary care. This map can guide research efforts.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Deciphering cancer metabolic reprogramming mechanisms can identify new targets to potentiate EZH2 inhibitor efficacy. Using an in vivo genome-wide CRISPR loss-of-function screen in a CRC mouse model, we pinpointed IDO1 as a key mediator of EZH2 inhibitor resistance. EZH2 blockade remodeled CRC cell metabolism by upregulating IDO1 protein and hyperactivating the tryptophan-kynurenine pathway. Both genetic and pharmacological inhibition of IDO1 suppressed tumor growth and rescued EZH2 inhibitor resistance in vitro and in vivo. Mechanistically, EZH2 directly binds and methylates IDO1. Methylation of IDO1 facilitates IDO1 ubiquitination and subsequent degradation. Accordingly, EZH2 inhibition stabilizes IDO1, augments tryptophan-kynurenine metabolic flux, and ultimately confers therapeutic resistance. In summary, our study identifies IDO1 as a non-histone substrate of EZH2 methyltransferase activity and validates that disrupting IDO1-mediated tryptophan metabolism is a viable strategy to overcome EZH2 targeted therapy resistance in cancers.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Spatial transcriptomics enables direct profiling of cellular organization within intact tissues, yet two challenges limit its full exploitation: accurate reference-free deconvolution of mixed expression signals (including species-admixed models such as xenografts), and lack of tools that can translate per-spot program usage values into spatial niches. We developed spOT-NMF, an optimal transport-based non-negative matrix factorization method that replaces standard reconstruction loss with the Wasserstein distance to disentangle mixed signals without requiring matched single-cell atlases. While the generalized OT-NMF factorization is applicable to any expression matrix, a proximity-based niche inference module further translates program co-usage from spatial transcriptomes into directional co-occurrence networks that define tissue compartments and their boundaries. Benchmarking across five gold-standard datasets spanning sub-cellular to multi-cellular resolutions, multiple platforms, and two-species admixture scenarios, spOT-NMF ranks first among reference-free methods, with particular advantage under the signal imbalance conditions characteristic of xenografts. We show that reference-free deconvolution recovers cell populations absent from matched single-cell atlases, highlighting the value of unsupervised analysis. Applied to glioblastoma xenografts and human colorectal cancer, spOT-NMF reveals spatially restricted interferon signaling, invasion routes, and CAF-tumor boundaries. spOT-NMF is available as an open-source Python package with GPU, CPU, and HPC support.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
To investigate the potential mechanism of cinobufotalin against colorectal cancer (CRC) through network pharmacology and experimental approaches. Overlapping targets between cinobufotalin and CRC were identified, yielding 165 potential therapeutic targets. A protein-protein interaction (PPI) network was constructed using Cytoscape software, and key genes were subjected to Gene Ontology (GO) functional annotation and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) pathway enrichment analysis. In vitro experiments were performed to evaluate the effects of cinobufotalin on CRC cell proliferation, apoptosis, and autophagy-related markers. Pharmacological inhibition of autophagy was also applied to examine its modulation of the antiproliferative effect of cinobufotalin. Enrichment analysis indicated that the overlapping targets were significantly associated with apoptosis signaling and autophagy pathways. In vitro experiments confirmed that cinobufotalin inhibited CRC cell proliferation and induced apoptosis, accompanied by changes in autophagy-related markers. Pharmacological inhibition of autophagy enhanced the antiproliferative effect of cinobufotalin, suggesting a regulatory role of autophagy in cellular response. Cinobufotalin exerts antitumor effects against CRC by promoting apoptosis and targeting autophagy pathways, and modulation of autophagy can further enhance its therapeutic efficacy.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Postoperative ileus (POI) is a common complication following major abdominal surgery. Currently, limited treatment options for POI exist. Recent preclinical studies show that direct electrical stimulation of the gastrointestinal tract may prevent POI. The aim was to evaluate the safety and feasibility of direct electrical stimulation of the stomach in patients undergoing major abdominal surgery. A single-center, randomized blinded feasibility study conducted at Aarhus University Hospital, Denmark. Patients who underwent cytoreductive surgery with heated intraperitoneal chemotherapy for low-grade appendiceal mucinous neoplasm or colorectal or appendiceal cancer with peritoneal metastases were eligible. After surgery, a pace lead was attached to the stomach and connected to an external stimulator (Enterra Medical, Minneapolis, USA). Participants were randomized, 1:1, to an intervention group (stimulator on) or a control group (stimulator off). The primary outcome was completion of the intervention as a measure of tolerability. Of 63 eligible patients, 27 consented to participate (43%). Seven patients were excluded perioperatively. Twenty patients were randomized. Nineteen patients were eligible for analysis, 10 in the intervention group and 9 in the control group. The treatment was well tolerated. The completion rate was 8/10 in the intervention group and 9/10 in the control group. Abdominal muscle spasms were the most common adverse events reported in both groups. Electrical stimulation appears safe, feasible and well tolerated. This study supports further clinical studies on electrical stimulation as prevention of POI. The study was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05752071).

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) is the third most common malignancy worldwide and the second leading cause of cancer-related death, and chromosomal instability (CIN) underlies 65-70% of sporadic cases. Here we review the evidence that the gut microbiota acts as an environmental instigator of CIN through three mechanistically intertwined routes. The first is direct genotoxicity: pks+ Escherichia coli produce colibactin, which alkylates deoxyadenosine to form DNA interstrand cross-links whose repair generates double-strand break intermediates and the mutational signatures SBS88 and ID18; transient exposure of primary colon epithelial cells suffices to provoke chromosomal aberrations and malignant transformation. The second is community-level dysbiosis: the oncomicrobial community subtypes OCS2 and OCS3 are enriched in CIN-positive tumours and carry the reactive oxygen species-related signature SBS18, while at strain-level resolution Fusobacterium nucleatum subspecies animalis clade C2 shows the strongest association with the tumour niche, and Parvimonas micra and Peptostreptococcus stomatis contribute through WNT/β-catenin activation and Th17-skewed immunity. The third, advanced here as a working framework rather than an established mechanism, is the microbiota-induced bystander effect (MIBE), in which microbiota-driven para-inflammation creates a milieu rich in reactive oxygen and nitrogen species and inflammatory cytokines that damages DNA in neighbouring epithelial cells and establishes a field of cancerization. We integrate these routes into a three-stage model (initiation, propagation, perpetuation) linking microbial exposure to APC, KRAS and TP53 alterations, discuss translation towards risk stratification, faecal metagenomic diagnosis, OCS-based prognostication and targeted prevention, and delineate the limitations of the current evidence.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
2-(benzotriazole-2-yl)-4,6-bis(2-methylbutan-2-yl) phenol (UV-328) is a persistent benzotriazole ultraviolet stabilizer, but its potential relationship with colorectal cancer (CRC)-related molecular features and malignant cell phenotypes remains unclear. This study integrated public transcriptomic datasets, UV-328 target prediction, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), machine-learning, single-cell transcriptomic analysis, molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulation, and in vitro assays. Candidate targets were screened by intersecting CRC-associated genes with predicted UV-328 targets, followed by machine-learning-based feature prioritization, survival analysis, single-cell localization, structural modeling, and functional validation in CRC cells. The integrated workflow prioritized BRAF, DYRK1A, RXRB, RPS24, and TP53 as candidate predicted UV-328 targets. Single-cell analysis localized these genes mainly to epithelial compartments, providing a cell-type context for their interpretation. Docking, 100 ns MD simulations, and MM/PBSA analyses provided complementary structural and energetic support for the selected BRAF-, DYRK1A-, and RXRB-UV-328 candidate interactions. Short-term treatment with 10 µM UV-328 increased CCK-8 signals in SW480 and HCT116 cells and enhanced SW480 cell migration and invasion. Seven-day exposure to a nominal concentration of 10 nM UV-328 also increased CCK-8 signals in SW480, HCT116, and RKO cells. UV-328 treatment modestly increased DYRK1A protein abundance, whereas DYRK1A knockdown partially attenuated the associated CCK-8 response in SW480 cells. Together, these findings outline an integrated, hypothesis-generating framework connecting UV-328-associated molecular features with CRC-related cellular responses and prioritizing candidate targets for further mechanistic validation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Ammer et al. reported no significant difference in low anterior resection syndrome (LARS) between open and robotic rectal cancer surgery. This commentary addresses the interindividual variability in LARS outcomes. This conceptual commentary critically reviews the outcome assessment strategy used in the original study and integrates supporting evidence from the psycho-oncology literature. Functional burden, as captured by the LARS score, does not necessarily equal psychological burden. Psychological adaptation-resilience, coping style, distress, and illness perception-is hypothesised to mediate the relationship between functional impairment and patient-reported quality of life. Functional burden and psychological burden are related but distinct constructs. Future studies should test mediation and moderation models to determine whether psychological adaptation explains the variability between LARS severity and quality of life.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Cancer has been the leading cause of death in Japan since the 1980s, with known variation across prefectures, but evidence on how this pattern has changed over time is limited. We analysed age-standardized cancer mortality across all 47 Japanese prefectures in 1995 and 2023 using vital statistics data. For each prefecture, excess mortality was calculated relative to a leave-one-out national reference and standardized to the 1995 national population. Excess mortality was decomposed by cancer site. We also compared prefectures' age-standardized mortality rates (ASMRs) between the two years. All-cancer ASMR declined in every prefecture. In 2023, excess mortality ranged from 32·6 per 100 000 (95% CI 26·8 to 38·4) in Aomori to -22·4 (-26·1 to -18·6) in Nagano, a gap of 55·0 deaths per 100 000, with 30 prefectures differing significantly from the national reference. The geographic pattern shifted between 1995 and 2023. In 1995, excess mortality was concentrated in western Japan, particularly Osaka and Fukuoka, and was largely driven by liver cancer. By 2023, excess mortality had shifted to northern prefectures, led by Aomori and Hokkaido, and was distributed across multiple cancer types, including colorectal, lung, and stomach cancer. The overall gap narrowed from 69·6 to 55·0 per 100 000. Geographic inequality in cancer mortality persisted in Japan, but its pattern changed substantially. The findings suggest that national cancer control should monitor subnational inequality directly and support regionally targeted strategies.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Certain ribosomal proteins (RPs) function as tumor suppressors. For example, RPL5 and RPL11 suppress oncogenesis by binding to MDM2 and thereby up-regulating p53, a mechanism referred to as the RP-MDM2-p53 cascade. However, whether other cancer-associated ribosomal proteins actually function as tumor suppressors has remained largely unclear. Previously, we showed that siRNA-mediated silencing of RPS17, in combination with expression of HPV16 E7 and activated KRAS G12V, transformed normal human fibroblasts. Here, we expanded our study to perform a functional analysis of RPS17 as a tumor suppressor. We first demonstrate that shRNA-mediated RPS17 silencing also promotes oncogenic transformation of human fibroblasts in vitro and in vivo. Conversely, its overexpression inhibits the soft agar colony formation of colon cancer-derived HCT116 cells in a p53-dependent manner. RPS17 weakly interacts with MDM2. However, unlike RPL5 and RPL11, overexpression of RPS17 does not increase p53 levels and its silencing induces p53, suggesting that the RP-MDM2-p53 cascade might not be a major pathway for its tumor-suppressive function. We further show that RPS17 binds to nucleophosmin and modulates its nuclear localization. Although the detailed molecular mechanisms underlying the tumor-suppressive function of RPS17 remain to be elucidated, this study provides evidence that RPS17 can function as a tumor suppressor.

This is an open access article distributed under the terms of the Creative Commons Attribution License (CC BY 4.0), which permits unrestricted use, distribution, and reproduction in any medium, provided the original author and source are credited. Oncogenic signaling in cancer cells is essential for proliferation, and its disruption, either through inhibition or overactivation, can provide therapeutic opportunities. Dual specificity phosphatase 4 (DUSP4), a negative regulator of the MAPK pathway that dephosphorylates ERK, has been proposed as a potential target; however, its therapeutic relevance has not been evaluated in vivo. In this study, we show that DUSP4 knockdown induces G1 cell cycle arrest and reduces proliferation in BRAFV600E-mutant and BRAF inhibitor-resistant colorectal cancer models, both in vitro and in vivo, while also inducing a DUSP5-mediated adaptive response. While treatment achieved tumor stasis, indicating disease control, it did not yield tumor regression, suggesting that DUSP4 may have limited efficacy as a monotherapy target in cancer.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The pan-immune inflammation value (PIV) and prognostic nutritional index (PNI) are established markers of systemic inflammatory/immune status and nutritional status, respectively. The potential synergistic effect of combining these indices remains unexplored. This study aimed to evaluate the utility of a novel combined PIV-PNI score for predicting chemosensitivity and survival outcomes in patients with locally advanced colon cancer (LACC) undergoing neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NACT), within a cohort from the Yunnan Plateau region. We conducted a retrospective analysis of 241 LACC patients who received NACT followed by radical resection. Tumor response was classified according to AJCC/CAP guidelines, with patients stratified into a TRG3 (minimal or no pathological response) group (n = 40) and a non-TRG3 group (n = 201). Pre-treatment PIV and PNI were measured, with optimal cut-off values identified by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. The PIV-PNI score was calculated as follows: a score of 2 indicated high PIV and low PNI; a score of 1 indicated either high PIV or low PNI alone; and a score of 0 indicated neither. The PIV-PNI score was significantly higher in the TRG3 group compared to the non-TRG3 group (p < 0.0001). The optimal cut-off values for PIV and PNI via ROC analysis were ≥ 218.7 and ≤ 50.6, respectively. A higher PIV-PNI score was associated with inferior survival outcomes. Multivariate analysis identified the PIV-PNI score as an independent prognostic factor for both overall survival and disease-free survival. The PIV-PNI score, a low-cost and readily available composite index, demonstrates significant clinical utility as a predictive marker for tumor response to NACT and prognosis in LACC patients. PIV-PNI score, which integrates systemic inflammation and immunonutritional status, demonstrates strong predictive value for chemosensitivity and long-term survival, offering a clinically accessible tool to guide personalized treatment strategies in the neoadjuvant setting.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The scope of primary care cancer research on the island of Ireland has not been clearly mapped, despite primary care's pivotal role across the cancer care continuum. We conducted a systematic search of studies from the Republic of Ireland (RoI) and Northern Ireland (NI) up until October 2022 and summarized the literature using bibliometric analysis and narrative synthesis. From 3911 screened abstracts, 100 eligible outputs were identified: 60 journal articles, 38 conference abstracts, and 2 doctoral theses. Most papers (92%) were published after 2000. Research output from NI and the RoI was proportional to population size; only one cross-border study was identified. Study designs were predominantly comparative observational (51%), with fewer non-comparative observational (23%), qualitative (23%), and experimental studies (3%). The most frequently studied cancers were cervical, breast, prostate, lung, and colorectal. This review provides a foundation for strategically directing future primary care cancer research in Ireland.

Primary hepatic perivascular epithelioid cell tumor (PEComa) is a rare mesenchymal neoplasm that can mimic common hepatic malignancies. A 28-year-old African woman with colorectal cancer in remission presented with 3 months of epigastric pain and tender hepatomegaly. Tumor markers were normal. Ultrasound and triphasic CT showed 2 large heterogeneous hypervascular hepatic masses with progressive enhancement and early venous drainage; hepatobiliary iminodiacetic acid scan (HIDA) SPECT-CT demonstrated photopenic lesions. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Reduced-port laparoscopic colectomy (RPLC) has emerged as an alternative to multi-port laparoscopic colectomy (MPLC) for colorectal cancer surgery, aiming to reduce operative morbidity and improve cosmetic outcomes. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated and compared operative, postoperative, and oncologic outcomes between RPLC and MPLC. Following PRISMA guidelines, we systematically searched PubMed, Cochrane Library, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar from inception to June 2025. The protocol was registered on PROSPERO (CRD420251078328). Included studies were randomized controlled trials (RCTs) or cohort studies comparing RPLC and MPLC. Primary outcomes were estimated blood loss, operative time, hospital stay, lymph node yield, and postoperative recovery indicators. Secondary outcomes included conversion rates, complications, and Clavien-Dindo graded adverse events. Risk of bias was evaluated using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale and Cochrane RoB 2.0 tool. A random-effects meta-regression was performed to explore the impact of high-stage tumors on the outcomes. Thirteen studies ( RPLC appears to provide comparable postoperative outcomes to MPLC with modest intraoperative advantages. As the evidence is largely retrospective and heterogeneous, these findings indicate the feasibility of RPLC rather than its superiority over MPLC. High-quality clinical trials with longer follow-up are required to confirm these findings and optimize clinical decision-making. PROSPERO registration ID: CRD420251078328.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Malignant transformation of intestinal endometriosis is rare and may closely mimic primary colorectal adenocarcinoma. A 43-year-old woman with a history of ovarian endometriosis presented with melena and a rectosigmoid tumor with uterine invasion and multiple lymph node metastases. Histopathological examination revealed moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma with intestinal endometriosis but no definitive transition between the endometriosis and the carcinoma, supporting an initial diagnosis of primary colorectal adenocarcinoma. Five years later, biopsy of a recurrent vaginal stump lesion showed an adenocarcinoma positive for estrogen receptor, paired box gene 8, and cytokeratin 7 and negative for cytokeratin 20 and caudal-type homeobox transcription factor 2. Retrospective immunohistochemical evaluation of the original tumor demonstrated a similar phenotype, supporting a Müllerian origin and malignant transformation of intestinal endometriosis. This case illustrates the difficulty of determining tumor origin based on morphology alone and highlights the diagnostic value of immunohistochemistry.

The rapid growth of metabolomics data has increased the need for integrated storage, analysis, and reuse. Here, we present Metabolomics Subcenter (Met-SC) V1.0 (https://metabolomics.dicp.ac.cn/), an integrated database and platform for standardized data deposition, spectral-resource management, online analysis, and disease-focused knowledge mining. The deposition framework captures project, sample, pretreatment, and instrument metadata across chromatographic, capillary electrophoresis-mass spectrometry, and nuclear magnetic resonance workflows. Met-SC contains 7 756 867 reference spectra associated with 1 989 680 unique compounds and 73 014 049 unknown-feature spectra derived from diverse biological matrices and experimental conditions. Its web-based analysis module provides 27 functions for data preprocessing, quality-control visualization, and statistical analysis. Metabolism-centered knowledge graph for colorectal cancer (MetKG-CRC) comprises 108 679 biomolecular entities and 600 093 literature-supported evidence triples. By linking data deposition, spectral resources, analysis, and evidence-supported knowledge exploration in a single platform, Met-SC facilitates reproducible metabolomics data management and downstream discovery.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Second primary cancer (SPC) risk differs by race and ethnicity among U.S. breast cancer survivors, yet limited data disaggregate Asian American (AA) and Pacific Islander (PI) women. We identified 64,277 AA and 5455 PI women diagnosed with invasive unilateral breast cancer between 2000 and 2019 (followed through 2020) and survived ≥ 1 year in the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results database. We examined SPC risk (all SPCs, non-breast SPCs, and site-specific SPCs) by race (AA, PI) and Asian ethnogeographic regions (East, South, and Southeast). Subdistribution hazard ratios (SHRs) and cumulative incidence of SPCs were estimated, accounting for competing risks. Over 6.13 median years of follow-up, 4083 AA women (East = 1922; South = 312; Southeast = 1579; Other/Unknown = 270) and 498 PI women developed SPCs. Overall, PI women had higher SPC risk than AA women (SHR = 1.44, 95% CI = 1.31-1.58), driven by contralateral breast, lung/bronchus, ovarian, and digestive system cancers. Among AA women, South AA women had lower SPC risk than East AA women (SHR = 0.85, 95% CI = 0.75-0.96), driven by lower lung/bronchus, digestive system, and colorectal cancer risk. Southeast AA women had similar SPC risk to East AA women, but lower digestive system cancer risk (SHR = 0.77, 95% CI = 0.66-0.89), and higher uterine (SHR = 1.29, 95% CI = 1.02-1.63) and thyroid cancer risk (SHR = 1.97, 95% CI = 1.47-2.64). One in 10 PI women developed an SPC within 10-years (10.32%) compared with one in 14 AA women (AA = 6.91%; East AA = 7.66%; South AA = 6.25%; Southeast AA = 7.26%). SPC risks were highest among PI breast cancer survivors and differed across Asian ethnogeographic regions. These findings highlight the need to understand factors associated with SPC risks and develop tailored interventions to address these disparities.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Consumption of coffee is associated with a reduced risk of colorectal cancer (CRC); however, the underlying mechanisms are not fully understood. Gut serotonin (5-HT) plays a complex role in CRC development. Intestinal 5-HT levels are regulated by the serotonin transporter (SERT), in intestinal epithelial cells. Recent evidence suggests a correlation between SERT expression and DNA methylation of a functional CpG site (CpG3) in the promoter region of SLC6A4, the SERT gene. This study investigated the effects of coffee on SERT expression in Caco-2 cells, an intestinal epithelial cell model. Exposure of Caco-2 cells to instant coffee solution 1-10% (v/v) for 48 h was found to result in a concentration-dependent decrease in SERT-mediated 5-HT uptake and SERT mRNA expression. This effect was observed for different instant coffee brands and coffee bean species, and was not reproduced by exposure to major coffee components such as caffeine and chlorogenic acid, or by extracts from unroasted green coffee beans. Pyrosequencing revealed that coffee exposure altered the DNA methylation of CpG3. This preliminary study suggests a novel mechanism by which coffee protects against CRC: suppression of SERT expression in intestinal epithelial cells, possibly via epigenetic modification of SLC6A4.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) are increasingly being prescribed for metabolic diseases. At times, patients taking GLP-1RAs are also undergoing cancer treatment and surgeries, but their potential interactions with cancer therapies are not well delineated. The purpose of this narrative review is to synthesize the limited pre-clinical, translational, and the clinical evidence available, examining the biological rationale and mechanisms for GLP-1RA-cancer therapy interactions. Oncology research on GLP-1RAs has primarily focused on cancer incidence and survival, yielding generally reassuring safety data and potential outcome improvements. While emerging evidence and biological studies suggest GLP-1RAs could influence treatment tolerance and toxicity, the current clinical data remains limited, observational, and poorly integrated. However, there has been decent mechanistic research that suggests biologically plausible interactions of GLP1-RAs and cancer therapies, specifically through the AMPK and mTOR pathways. The available clinical evidence suggests that GLP-1 receptor agonist use is associated withimproved survival outcomes and reduced treatment-related complications among patients with colorectalcancer receiving chemotherapy, immunotherapy, or surgery. However, these findings are mostlyobservational, and conflicting preclinical evidence highlights the need for prospective studies to clarifythe underlying mechanisms, establish causality, and determine the clinical implications of theseinteractions.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Pulsed low-dose-rate radiotherapy (PLDR) is a promising reirradiation strategy for refractory solid tumors because of its potential to reduce normal tissue toxicity; however, its immunomodulatory mechanisms remain poorly understood. In this study, we retrospectively analyzed clinical outcomes and treatment-related adverse events in 16 patients with refractory solid tumors treated with PLDR. Using MC38 tumor-bearing mice, we compared PLDR and conventional radiotherapy (cRT) under biologically equivalent dose conditions and performed single-cell RNA sequencing to characterize treatment-associated remodeling of the tumor immune microenvironment (TIM). Multiplex immunofluorescence staining and spatial analysis were further conducted in an independent cohort of 114 patients with rectal cancer to evaluate the clinical relevance of identified immune features. PLDR achieved comparable local tumor control to cRT while reducing treatment-related toxicity and improving overall survival (OS) in mouse models. In the combination-treatment setting, single-cell analyses showed that PLDR + immunotherapy with an anti-PD-1 antibody combined with the targeted agent anlotinib (ITT), compared with cRT + ITT, was associated with enrichment of Gzmk⁺ CD8⁺ T cells, reduced Spp1⁺ tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) abundance, and altered cell-cell communication between these populations. In our independent rectal cancer cohort, the spatial distance between SPP1⁺ TAMs and GZMK⁺ CD8⁺ T cells was independently associated with OS. These findings suggest that the interaction between SPP1⁺ TAMs and GZMK⁺ CD8⁺ T cells may be closely associated with PLDR-related TIM remodeling and may also serve as a potential prognostic biomarker in rectal cancer.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Anastomotic leakage (AL) remains one of the most serious complications following laparoscopic low anterior resection for rectal cancer. Although preventive stoma is widely used to reduce AL risk, it requires additional hospitalization and stoma closure surgery, increasing overall treatment burden. Anastomotic reinforcement suturing has been proposed as a potential alternative strategy; however, high-quality comparative evidence remains limited. This retrospective study conducted across multiple tertiary referral centers included 345 patients with rectal cancer who underwent laparoscopic low anterior resection between January 2022 and December 2023. Patients were categorized according to surgical strategy, including reinforcement suturing and preventive stoma formation. The primary outcome was 30-day AL incidence. Secondary outcomes included perioperative risk factors, subgroup analysis based on anastomotic height, and postoperative hospitalization outcomes. The overall 30-day AL rate was 3.19% (11/345). Before propensity score matching, AL occurred in 7/228 (3.07%) patients in the reinforcement group and 4/117 (3.42%) patients in the preventive stoma group. After matching, AL occurred in 4/72 (5.6%) patients in the reinforcement group and 3/72 (4.2%) in the preventive stoma group (paired risk difference, + 1.39 percentage points; 95% CI - 5.56 to + 8.33; exact McNemar P = 1.000). All AL events were classified as ISREC grade C and Clavien-Dindo grade IIIb. Reinforcement suturing was associated with a low observed AL rate in selected patients while avoiding planned stoma-related secondary surgery. However, the retrospective design and potential treatment-selection bias preclude conclusions regarding a causal protective effect or equivalence to preventive stoma.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The management of locally advanced rectal cancer is increasingly moving beyond a uniform cytotoxic framework toward biomarker-informed multimodal treatment. Short-course radiotherapy (SCRT) is an established and convenient radiotherapy option and may also provide an immunomodulatory context for immune checkpoint blockade. Preclinical evidence suggests that hypofractionated radiotherapy can promote immunogenic cell death and modulate the tumor immune microenvironment; however, whether the fractionation schedule of SCRT provides a clinically meaningful immunological advantage over long-course chemoradiotherapy remains uncertain. Early randomized studies of SCRT-based chemoimmunotherapy in predominantly proficient mismatch repair/microsatellite-stable (pMMR/MSS) populations have reported encouraging improvements in pathological or overall complete response rates compared with their respective control regimens. Nevertheless, differences in comparator arms, chemotherapy exposure, immunotherapy schedules, endpoint definitions, and follow-up duration preclude firm conclusions regarding the optimal radiotherapy backbone or long-term survival benefit. These findings support further prospective evaluation of SCRT-based combinations and response-adapted non-operative management in appropriately selected patients. Longitudinal circulating tumor DNA, multi-omics profiling, MR-guided adaptive radiotherapy, and computational models such as "digital twins" may contribute to improved patient selection and surveillance, but their clinical utility requires prospective validation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Approximately 10-20% of prostate cancer (PCa) patients have a germline mutation. These mutations are associated with more aggressive disease and worse outcomes. The relationship between a history of prior cancers and germline mutation patterns has not been well studied among PCa patients. To evaluate whether a history of prior cancers is associated with a positive germline mutation in PCa patients. We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the Myriad Collaborative Research Registry of PCa patients who underwent germline testing between 2013 and 2024. Multivariable regression models analyzed demographic factors, clinical factors, and prior cancer history to determine the associations with germline mutation status. A total of 42,645 PCa patients were included. Of the cohort, 86% had no prior cancer, 11% had one prior cancer, and 3% had two or more prior cancers. Germline mutation prevalence increased with cancer history, 10% for no prior cancer, 15% for one prior cancer, and 18% for two or more cancers (p < 0.001). In adjusted analyses, one prior cancer (OR = 1.27, 95% CI: 1.15-1.40) and ≥2 prior cancers (OR = 1.46, 95% CI: 1.25-1.70) were associated with higher odds of germline positivity. Specific prior malignancies with the strongest associations included ureteral (OR = 4.81, 95% CI: 1.77-13.07), bladder (OR = 1.56, 95% CI: 1.19-2.05), and colon cancer (OR = 1.29, 95% CI: 1.14-1.46). Notably, MSH2 mutations were elevated among patients with multiple prior cancers. Family history was not significantly associated with germline mutation status. This study is limited by its retrospective design and by selection bias, since only patients referred for genetic testing by their providers are included. A personal history of a prior cancer is strongly associated with a positive germline mutation in PCa patients, with risk increasing with the number of prior cancers. Prior cancer history may be a useful predictor of germline mutations, but it should be tested in a validated risk model before being added to germline testing criteria.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) participate in colorectal cancer (CRC) progression and immune regulation. However, the biological functions of lncRNA RP3-380B8.4 (RP3) in CRC and its relationship with the tumor immune microenvironment remain unclear. RP3 expression in CRC was assessed using public datasets and validated by in situ hybridization (ISH). We further examined the expression levels and intracellular localization of RP3 in CRC cells by qRT-PCR. The effect of RP3 on the cell growth, migration, invasion and epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) was investigated by in vitro experiments and western blot. In vivo experiments confirmed that RP3 potentiated tumor growth and liver metastasis in CRC. We predicted the mechanism by RNA-seq, and confirmed them by western blot. The impact of RP3 on the tumor immune microenvironment was analyzed by bioinformatics analysis and flow cytometry. RP3 was substantially elevated in CRC tissues and associated with poor prognosis. RP3 overexpression increased CRC cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and EMT in vitro. RP3 overexpression accelerated orthotopic colorectal cancer growth and liver metastasis in nude mice. On the contrary, knockdown of RP3 achieved the opposite effect. Mechanistically, gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) and western blot analysis revealed that RP3 overexpression is associated with enrichment of MYC target gene programs and elevated c-Myc protein levels in colorectal cancer. Furthermore, overexpression of RP3 significantly reduced the infiltration of CD8 RP3 facilitates CRC proliferation and metastasis and exerts immunosuppression in the tumor microenvironment. These findings implicate RP3 as a candidate regulator in CRC whose mechanistic and therapeutic potential requires further validation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Dendritic cells (DCs) are the most well-known immune cells for cancer immunotherapy progress. The engineered extracellular vesicles (EVs) from DCs (DCs-EVs) for immunotherapy have emerged as a novel and effective therapeutic approach because they naturally contribute to regulating immune responses by transporting therapeutic agents to target cells with minimal toxicity and high specificity. DCs-EVs, are heterogeneous extracellular particles, generally contribute to intracellular communication and immune regulation due to the presence of immune-regulatory molecules, antigens, major histocompatibility complexes, and co-stimulatory molecules. As a result, engineered DCs-EVs are defined as lipid bilayer delimited EVs released by DCs that have been intentionally pre- or post-isolated to change their surface composition, cargo, targeting properties, biodistribution, or immunomodulatory function. DCs-EVs have been examined for breast cancer, colorectal cancer, melanoma, and glioblastoma. Although engineered DCs-EVs have demonstrated hopeful results in preclinical experiments, for clinical translation, some limitations remain to be addressed in further studies. In addition, for clinical trials, these EVs must comply with good manufacturing practice (GMP). This narrative review was informed by a structured literature search about the application of engineered DCs-EVs in cancer immunotherapy utilizing sources like Google Scholar, Scopus, ScienceDirect, PubMed, and WOS. Furthermore, it discussed EVs biology, engineering methods, and clinical trials, as well as outlined challenges and perspectives in this field.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The gut microbiota produces metabolites, such as short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) that modulate histone acylation and serve as precursors for non-acetyl acyl marks, representing a mechanism in host-microbiome epigenetic crosstalk. However, the reliable quantification of these low-abundance modifications in complex tissues remains challenging. Here, we established an optimized, non-acetyl histone acylation-focused super-SILAC strategy for profiling histone post-translational modifications (HPTM) in the gut epithelium. We generated a functionally optimized internal standard from heavy-labeled colon cancer cells (HCT-116 and Caco-2) treated with propionate, butyrate, and crotonate, thereby enriching the standard in non-canonical acylations. This custom super-SILAC mixture enabled robust normalization and improved the quantification of low-abundance histone acylations in biological tissues. Our in vitro characterization revealed that SCFAs induced distinct and overlapping acylation profiles, with propionate leading to the most pronounced changes, including increased H3K14pr and H4K16pr. Applying this method to mouse models, we found that antibiotic-induced microbiota depletion led to the loss of marks associated with active chromatin (H3K14pr and H4K16pr) and a concurrent increase in heterochromatin-associated marks (H3K9me2/3). In contrast, Dextran Sodium Sulfate (DSS)-induced early-stage intestinal inflammation caused H4 hyperacetylation, increased H3K14pr, and reduced H3K27ac. In conclusion, the super-SILAC method enables robust identification and quantification of low-abundance histone acylations in cells and tissues under both physiological and disease conditions.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) continues to be a major global cause of cancer-related morbidity and mortality, with little effective treatment options. One of the main contributors of CRC is chronic inflammation, and nitric oxide (NO) has become a key factor in the pathophysiology of tumors. The concentration, cellular source, spatial distribution, and redox environment of NO within the tumor microenvironment (TME) determine its highly context-dependent effects in CRC. Prolonged sub-lethal NO production, mediated mainly by NOS2/iNOS, alters the CRC TME by regulating immune cell function, stromal activation, angiogenesis, and vascular permeability, thereby promoting tumor-cell intravasation and survival during metastasis. Therapy-induced NO signaling, which can paradoxically promote tumor progression after chemotherapy, radiation, and anti-angiogenic treatments, is given special attention. Lastly, we assess new therapeutic approaches that target NO signaling in CRC, such as NOS2/iNOS inhibition, NO-donor compounds, nanotechnology-based delivery systems, and logical combinations with immunotherapy and chemotherapy. Overall, this review emphasizes NO as a crucial but intricate regulator of colorectal cancer biology and emphasizes the necessity of accurate, situation-specific modulation of NO signaling. The translation of NO-based strategies into successful treatments for patients with advanced and treatment-resistant colorectal cancer may be made possible by a better understanding of NO dynamics, the creation of CRC-specific biomarkers, and targeted delivery platforms.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Disulfidptosis is a newly identified form of regulated cell death driven by high SLC7A11 expression under glucose starvation. Mechanistically, massive cystine influx via SLC7A11, coupled with NADPH depletion due to glucose deprivation, leads to cystine accumulation, disulfide stress, aberrant crosslinking of actin cytoskeleton (notably at Cys257, Cys284, and Cys373), and eventual membrane rupture. This process is independent of apoptosis, ferroptosis, and necroptosis. This review systematically outlines the molecular regulatory network of disulfidptosis, including upstream triggers, key execution molecules (glutathione and thioredoxin systems, RAC1/WRC/Arp2/3 axis), and downstream effectors. We further evaluate its therapeutic potential across various malignancies (glioblastoma, hepatocellular, gastric, colorectal, pancreatic, breast, lung, and prostate cancers) and other diseases (neurodegenerative, metabolic, orthopedic, cardiovascular). Recent advances in nanodelivery systems for selective disulfidptosis induction are summarized. Key translational challenges are critically analyzed, including targeting specificity, safety, delivery barriers, resistance mechanisms, and biomarker deficiency. By exploiting metabolic vulnerabilities (high SLC7A11 expression and glucose dependence) of pathological cells, disulfidptosis may offer a potential therapeutic window. Preclinical evidence suggests possible synergy with ferroptosis, cuproptosis, and immunotherapy, though clinical validation is currently lacking. This review provides a comprehensive framework for basic research and clinical translation of disulfidptosis-targeted therapies. We further propose a phased clinical development roadmap encompassing biomarker-driven patient selection, repurposed drug evaluation, and combination trial designs, providing an actionable framework for translating disulfidptosis biology into clinical practice.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
A multi-epitope vaccine candidate, A-20EFγ, was rationally designed against Fusobacterium nucleatum using proteomic and genomic information. The construct comprises a B-cell epitope (epitope 20) derived from the ABC transporter permease, along with cytotoxic T-lymphocyte (CTL) and helper T-lymphocyte (HTL) epitopes (epitopes E, F, and γ) selected from the nickel ABC transporter permease. All epitopes demonstrated favorable immunological properties, including high antigenicity, surface accessibility, and the absence of allergenicity and toxicity. These epitopes were assembled using suitable linkers, and outer membrane protein A was incorporated as an adjuvant to enhance immunogenicity. Additionally, the PADRE sequence was included to improve immune stimulation and population coverage, resulting in a remarkable increase in predicted MHC class II and combined population coverage to 99.98%. The three-dimensional structure of the finalized vaccine was modeled using multiple computational approaches and validated through structural quality assessments and molecular dynamics simulations, with the RoseTTAFold model showing superior stability. Molecular docking, network normal mode, and binding free energy analyses revealed stable interactions between the vaccine and Toll-like receptors 2 and 4. Immune simulations further suggested that A-20EFγ could elicit a robust and long-lasting humoral immune response, characterized by high IgG and IgM levels and enhanced memory B-cell activity. Lastly, codon optimization and in silico cloning were conducted to facilitate in vitro synthesis and predict efficient expression in E. coli using the pET-28a (+) vector. Overall, these preliminary findings suggest A-20EFγ as a potential prophylactic vaccine candidate for the prevention of F. nucleatum-associated colorectal cancer.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Up to 3% of endometrial cancers may be associated with Lynch syndrome (LS). For endometrial cancer, the preferred approach to universal LS screening is immunohistochemical staining for the mismatch repair proteins MLH1, PMS2, MSH2, and MSH6, with about one-third of endometrial cancers showing abnormal results. We describe the case of a 57-year-old woman with an endometrial endometrioid carcinoma that demonstrated a rare "null" mismatch repair protein immunohistochemical profile with complete loss of MLH1, PMS2, MSH2, and MSH6 expression, with positive staining in the internal and external controls. Subsequent MLH1 methylation testing, genetic counseling, and somatic tumor tissue testing revealed MLH1 promoter methylation, no germline alterations, a somatic frameshift mutation in MLH1 and 2 somatic nonsense mutations in MSH2, a high tumor mutational burden (68.8 mut/Mb), and microsatellite instability in 55 of 104 microsatellite sites assessed. Although the patient had a family history of colon cancer, the MMR-null immunophenotype is attributed to a combination of methylation and somatic events. However, in gastrointestinal cancer cases, the MMR-null immunophenotype has been associated with LS, and therefore, in gynecologic cases, we recommend MLH1 promoter methylation testing and germline genetic counseling and testing for cases demonstrating this rare finding.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
BACKGROUND Hepatic artery infusion (HAI) chemotherapy has been established as an indispensable treatment for hepatic metastatic colorectal cancer (CRLM), particularly in patients with multiple lesions. CASE REPORT We report the case of a patient diagnosed with liver metastasis from sigmoid colon cancer. The patient underwent hepatic segmentectomy and resection of the colon lesion in April 2019, following 8 cycles of systemic chemotherapy. After 4 postoperative courses of chemotherapy, the patient was monitored with regular follow-up. However, by November 2021, the patient had experienced 2 episodes of hepatic lesion recurrence and received late-line chemotherapy, combined with transcatheter arterial chemoembolization (TACE) and radiotherapy. In April 2024, the patient presented with severe jaundice, with total bilirubin (TB) up to 204 μmol/L (≈12 mg/dL), and concurrent abdominal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) demonstrated multiple hepatic lesions without evidence of biliary obstruction. After thorough discussion, shared decisionmaking led to the initiation a treatment regimen consisting of HAI with fluorouracil and bevacizumab, along with regorafenib. Because the bilirubin level decreased the next morning after the first infusion, additional cycles were performed, and subsequent arteriography showed a gradual transition from diffuse neoplastic abnormal staining to normal vascular patterns, and the liver lesions were significantly reduced in size. CONCLUSIONS Given the patient's poor adherence to regorafenib and its low late-line efficacy reported in the literature, we believe that HAI likely contributed more significantly to this case. While regorafenib's contribution cannot be fully excluded, this case shows that patients with heavily pretreated CRLM accompanied by jaundice can tolerate HAI of bevacizumab and fluorouracil.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Reliable sub-state cancer screening estimates are needed to identify geographic disparities and guide interventions, but survey data often lack sufficient precision for small-area analyses. Multi-payer claims data offer a promising alternative, though constructing screening-eligible cohorts is complicated by transitions across payers over time. We used the University of North Carolina Cancer Information and Population Health Resource to develop a longitudinal multi-payer cohort of insured North Carolina residents from 2003 to 2020. Deterministic linkage based on Social Security Number (SSN), date of birth, and sex was used to identify unique individuals across private insurance, Medicare, and Medicaid. As a use case, we constructed annual colorectal cancer (CRC) screening-eligible cohorts for 2012-2020 using two definitions of 10-year enrollment. The parent cohort included 12,010,374 unique individuals with 74,779,932 person-years of follow-up. Median continuous enrollment was 60 months (interquartile range, 19-122), and 24.7% linked to multiple payers over time. In 2020, the annual CRC screening cohort covered an estimated 56% of insured North Carolina residents aged 45-75 years. A flexible enrollment definition increased cohort size by approximately 10% with minimal demographic differences. Statewide up-to-date CRC screening prevalence was approximately 80% and stable across the study period, with geographic variation observed across small areas. This resource provides a scalable framework for constructing screening-eligible populations from multi-payer claims and generating small-area cancer screening estimates. This infrastructure has particular value for identifying screening disparities in underserved populations that are poorly captured by traditional survey methods.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Patients with oligometastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) remain at high risk of recurrence after curative surgery, yet the benefit of adjuvant chemotherapy remains inconclusive. This study evaluated the feasibility and efficacy of adjuvant modified (m)FOLFOXIRI (irinotecan, oxaliplatin, L-leucovorin (L-LV), 5-fluorouracil (5-FU)), as well as the utility of circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) as a prognostic and predictive biomarker in mCRC. Between October 2020 and January 2024, patients with histologically confirmed mCRC undergoing complete metastasectomy were enrolled in this multicentre non-randomized phase II study. Eligible and consenting patients received eight cycles of mFOLFOXIRI followed by four cycles of 5-FU/L-LV; ineligible/non-consenting patients received standard of care (SOC; CAPOX (capecitabine and oxaliplatin), 5-FU, or observation). ctDNA was assessed using the tumour-informed personalized Signatera™ assay (Natera, Austin, TX, USA) at 28 days and 7 months after surgery. The primary endpoint was completion of eight cycles of mFOLFOXIRI in a target sample of 36 patients. Of the 83 registered patients, 73 were enrolled (39 mFOLFOXIRI, 34 SOC). The mFOLFOXIRI completion rate was 74% (80% confidence interval 63% to 83%; P < 0.001). ctDNA positivity predicted significantly inferior recurrence-free survival across both the mFOLFOXIRI and SOC treatment groups at 28 days (hazard ratios (HR) 7.27 and 7.17, respectively) and 7 months (HR 3.96 and 4.38, respectively) after surgery. Multivariate analysis identified ctDNA positivity, RAS mutation, metachronous metastases, and mFOLFOXIRI as significant prognostic factors. mFOLFOXIRI improved recurrence-free survival compared with SOC in the overall population (HR 0.44; P = 0.012), with a trend towards benefit in ctDNA-positive but not ctDNA-negative patients. ctDNA clearance rates were 33% (mFOLFOXIRI) and 20% (SOC). This study indicates the feasibility of adjuvant mFOLFOXIRI in patients with mCRC, with an acceptable safety profile and potential clinical benefit among those with ctDNA positivity 28 days after surgery.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Hepatic metastasis is facilitated by colorectal cancer cells adhering to and disrupting liver vascular endothelial cells. The function of the neuropeptide phoenixin-14 and its receptor GPR173 in this process is examined in this work. Compared with controls and peritumoral areas, we observed substantially dysregulated phoenixin-14/GPR173 signaling in CRC patients, with lower serum phoenixin-14 levels and lower GPR173 expression in tumor tissues. We showed that CRC cells increase endothelial paracellular permeability and decrease transendothelial electrical resistance, suggesting barrier failure, using a co-culture approach with primary human hepatic artery endothelial cells and CRC cell lines HT-29 and Colo205. These effects were reversed by phoenixin-14 administration (5-10 nM), which restored Claudin-5 expression, inhibited the elevation of endothelial adhesion molecules (ICAM-1, E-selectin), suppressed the transcription factor Egr-1 induced by CRC co-culture, and reduced CRC cell transendothelial migration across the endothelial monolayer. According to our research, the phoenixin-14/GPR173 signaling pathway targets Egr-1 to preserve the vascular endothelial barrier, suggesting a new strategy to prevent endothelial dysfunction and hepatic metastases from colorectal cancer.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Cytoreductive surgery with hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy (CRS/HIPEC) is an established treatment for peritoneal surface malignancies, but is associated with substantial morbidity, particularly when pelvic anastomoses are performed. Diverting ostomies are commonly used to mitigate complications related to anastomotic leak; however, ostomy formation carries its own morbidity, and its benefit in this setting remains controversial. PubMed and Embase were queried for studies of patients undergoing CRS/HIPEC with a pelvic anastomosis, documented use of diverting ostomy, and reported anastomotic leak rates. Eligible studies required combined CRS/HIPEC, explicit reporting of diversion status, and perioperative outcomes stratified by ostomy presence. Abstracts were independently screened by two reviewers, followed by full-text review for final inclusion. A binary odds ratio meta-analysis was performed comparing anastomotic leak between diverted and non-diverted patients. Of 506 studies identified, 10 met inclusion criteria and were combined with our institutional cohort, comprising 1506 patients. Overall, diversion was not associated with a statistically significant reduction in anastomotic leak (OR 0.67, 95% CI 0.32-1.39, p = 0.28). No differences were observed in grade ≥ 3 complications or length of stay. Diversion was associated with increased 60-day readmissions (OR 3.29, 95% CI 1.52-7.11, p < 0.01). Diverting ostomies were not associated with a statistically significant reduction in anastomotic leak in patients undergoing CRS/HIPEC with a pelvic anastomosis. These findings suggest consideration of a selective, rather than routine, diversion strategy in appropriately selected patients.
