ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains difficult to treat because of tumor heterogeneity and an immunosuppressive microenvironment. Although combining chemotherapy with cuproptosis offers complementary antitumor effects, its efficacy is constrained by poor tumor-selective delivery and ATP7B-associated copper efflux. We developed YC@BS-MOF, a yuanhuacine (YC)-loaded copper metal-organic framework (MOF) with Golgi-targeting capability, to integrate chemotherapy, photodynamic therapy, and cuproptosis. Composed of Cu2+ nodes and Golgi-targeting BS-TCPP photosensitizing ligands, BS-MOF acted as a copper reservoir and, upon light irradiation, induced Golgi disruption that impaired ATP7B-associated Cu handling and promoted intracellular copper retention. Copper retention amplified YC-mediated apoptosis and copper-dependent oxidative stress, leading to enhanced cuproptosis, immunogenic cell death, and activation of the immune microenvironment. Biodistribution analyses showed increased YC tumor accumulation, and in vivo studies demonstrated potent tumor suppression, immune remodeling, and favorable biosafety. This work establishes Golgi-directed regulation of copper trafficking as a subcellular strategy to potentiate chemo-cuproptosis for CRC treatment.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
This meta-analysis and systematic review examined gut microbial metabolites and the tumor microenvironment (TME) in colorectal cancer (CRC), as well as the influence of microbial metabolites on cancer development and treatment. The focus was on explaining how microbial metabolites influence cancer development and treatment outcome. A systematic search of PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library was conducted (January 2010-December 2020) following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Literature search yielded 765 articles, from which 22 studies were identified as meeting inclusion criteria after stringent screening. Included studies encompassed in vitro, in vivo, and patient-derived data on the role of gut microbial metabolites (e.g., short-chain fatty acids [SCFAs], bile acids, polyamines, and trimethylamine-N-oxide) in characterizing the CRC TME. Meta-analysis found that SCFAs, particularly butyrate, consistently played protective and regulatory functions, suppressing inflammation and stimulating antitumor immunity. In contrast, bile acids and certain microbial populations (e.g., Fusobacterium nucleatum) were associated with tumor-promoting pathways, including NF-κB and STAT3 activation. The overall result was moderately heterogeneous (I The findings exhibit the therapeutic promise of microbiome-targeting treatments and dietary manipulation in modifying the TME. However, they remain to be confirmed by follow-up large-scale clinical trials to consolidate the evidence base.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Chronic circadian disruption is associated with colorectal cancer (CRC), but whether it exacerbates CRC progression and influences the protective effects of dietary interventions remains unclear. We examined pterostilbene (PSB) and 3'-hydroxypterostilbene (3'-HPSB) in an azoxymethane/dextran sulfate sodium-induced CRC mouse model exposed to chronic jet lag. Chronic jet lag aggravated disease activity, intestinal pathology, inflammation, and tumor burden. Dietary PSB and 3'-HPSB supplementations, initiated before CRC induction, attenuated these pathological changes and reduced macroscopic tumors (≥2 mm) by approximately 36% and 49%, respectively. These effects were accompanied by alterations in circadian clock-related and Wnt/β-catenin signaling-related proteins and by reduced intestinal epithelial proliferation. Supplementation was also associated with changes in gut microbiota composition and fecal short-chain fatty acid levels. These findings support preventive/protective effects of PSB and 3'-HPSB under chronic circadian disruption and identify associated molecular and microbial alterations warranting further mechanistic investigation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Patients with gastrointestinal cancers face site-specific threats to nutritional intake, muscle function, organ reserve, and recovery. This critical narrative review examines host fitness as an organizing concept for these vulnerabilities rather than as a validated composite score. A targeted PubMed update identified publications from 2022 through September 14, 2026, using gastrointestinal cancer terms combined with prehabilitation, microbiome-immunotherapy, geriatric assessment, exercise, and digital assessment terms, while retaining relevant foundational studies. The review distinguishes guideline-supported care from prognostic associations and research-stage applications. Geriatric and nutritional assessments can guide established supportive care, whereas computed tomography-derived body composition and inflammatory indices primarily provide prognostic information. Microbiome signatures, epigenetic clocks, and integrated digital models require further validation before they can guide treatment decisions. Intervention effects vary by tumor site and treatment phase: selected prehabilitation trials demonstrate short-term benefits, although findings remain inconsistent, while long-term exercise after adjuvant chemotherapy for colon cancer represents a distinct evidence base. An operational assessment protocol and multidisciplinary workflow are presented to link documented impairments with existing care pathways and repeated assessment. No host-fitness threshold is proposed for treatment escalation, de-escalation, or sequencing. Prospective studies should establish incremental predictive value and patient benefit beyond existing assessments before this integrated framework is used to support precision treatment decisions.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colonoscopy surveillance is recommended following colorectal cancer (CRC) surgery, yet the evidence supporting the recommendations has major quality issues. This study assessed the independent impact of colonoscopy surveillance within 5 years after CRC surgery. A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted. Medline, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched from inception until 18 June 2026 for randomized clinical trials comparing follow-up protocols including colonoscopy surveillance (intervention) to those without colonoscopy surveillance (control) within 5 years after CRC surgery. Risk of bias was assessed using the RoB 2 tool. Random-effects meta-analyses were conducted to estimate the strength of associations with recurrence detection, reoperation rate, and survival. The number needed to scope (NNS) to detect one recurrence and health economic considerations were estimated. The study protocol has been registered in PROSPERO. Of 4381 records, five trials with 2337 patients were included. Four trials enrolled patients between 1983 and 1994, predating subsequent advances in CRC treatment. All trials used additional surveillance modalities, leading to a high risk of bias. Follow-up protocols with colonoscopy were not associated with recurrence profile, with risk ratios (RRs) of 0.74 (95% confidence interval (c.i.) 0.32 to 1.69), 1.23 (95% c.i. 0.93 to 1.63), and 0.93 (95% c.i. 0.76 to 1.14) for intraluminal, locoregional, and distant recurrence, respectively. Colonoscopy during follow-up was associated with a higher rate of asymptomatic recurrence (RR 2.38; 95% c.i. 1.53 to 3.69). More curative-intent reoperations were performed in the intervention than control group (RR 1.66; 95% c.i. 1.16 to 2.37), but this was not translated into improved survival (hazard ratio 0.92; 95% c.i. 0.77 to 1.11). The NNS was 159 (95% c.i. 101 to 267), resulting in estimated cost per colonoscopy-detected recurrence of €104 100 (95% c.i. €66 200 to 174 900). Current evidence from randomized trials does not clearly demonstrate that postoperative colonoscopy surveillance improves survival, although interpretation is limited by the age of the trials and confounding from concurrent surveillance modalities. Contemporary randomized trials are required to better define the independent contribution of colonoscopy within modern multimodal surveillance pathways.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Health economic (HE) evaluations are essential for healthcare decision-making, yet the rapid pace of innovation demands accelerated HE evaluations. Integrating Generative AI (GenAI), particularly Large Language Models (LLMs), into HE simulation modeling offers a promising opportunity to enhance model development efficiency and speed. We propose a framework for automating HE model development through expert-AI co-creation. This framework enables GenAI to generate simulation models in a structured and transparent manner. The proposed approach is expert-led and incorporates iterative prompt-response cycles. GPT5-mini and GPT-5.2-codex are employed using zero-shot prompting. As LLM results are non-deterministic, we introduced a Prompt Robustness Test (PRT) to assess the stability of LLM-generated outputs, indicating whether a prompt is sufficiently reliable to support automated model development. The methodology is applied to replicate a published discrete-event simulation comparing two post-surgery treatment strategies for colon cancer. The original model is complex and representative of real-world HE practice. Using our framework, we replicated the model in Python, achieving cost and QALY estimates within 2% of the original. While the overall pathway structure was successfully reconstructed, several logic discrepancies remained compared with the original model. Our framework provides methodological guidance on the expert-AI co-creation of complex HE models, emphasizing that expert oversight is essential throughout the process.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Aberrant WNT/β-catenin signaling drives tumorigenesis and metastasis in cancer. Although enzymatic inhibitors of tankyrase (TNKS) effectively block AXIN degradation and stabilize the β-catenin destruction complex (DC), they have demonstrated limited efficacy in various colorectal cancer (CRC) models. Here, we demonstrate that, unexpectedly, the induction of AXIN puncta represents a major barrier to achieving therapeutic efficacy. Mechanistically, catalytic inhibition of TNKS prevents TNKS turnover and drives its accumulation in the DC, wherein the scaffolding function of TNKS induces AXIN puncta formation, rigidifies the DC, and impedes β-catenin turnover. Chemically induced degradation of TNKS overcomes this limitation by stabilizing AXIN without puncta formation, providing a deeper suppression of the WNT/β-catenin pathway activity and the proliferation of CRC cells harboring dysfunctional APC mutations. Collectively, these findings provide an explanation for the unsatisfactory outcomes of drugging the WNT/β-catenin signaling pathway by TNKS inhibitors and highlight TNKS degradation as a promising approach to treat WNT/β-catenin-driven CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Severe postoperative complications after rectal cancer surgery increase morbidity, delay recovery, and may compromise oncologic outcomes. Existing risk models show limited accuracy and generalizability. Machine learning can integrate complex clinical and surgical variables to improve individualized risk prediction. To develop and prospectively validate machine learning-based models for predicting severe postoperative complications after rectal cancer surgery. Retrospective model development and prospective temporal internal validation study. Single tertiary referral center in South Korea. A total of 3,503 patients who underwent curative rectal cancer resection with anastomosis between 2011 and 2025 were included, comprising 3,402 retrospective and 101 prospective cases. Severe postoperative complications defined as Clavien-Dindo grade ≥ 3 within 30days after surgery. Severe complications occurred in 9.8% of the retrospective and 13.9% of the prospective cohort. Four machine-learning algorithms - logistic regression, random forest, artificial neural network, and gradient boosting - were trained using 5-fold crossvalidation. In internal validation, the random forest model achieved the best performance (area under the receiver operating characteristic Curve 0.898; Sensitivity 0.685), while gradient boosting performed best in the temporal internal validation cohort (area under the receiver operating characteristic Curve 0.910; Sensitivity 0.707). The most influential predictors were tumor perforation, intraoperative transfusion, protective stoma, bowel obstruction, and cerebrovascular accident. Validation was single institution (temporal internal, not external) with a small prospective cohort. Machine learning-based models accurately predicted severe postoperative complications after rectal cancer surgery, with strong discrimination maintained on temporal internal validation. Applied immediately after surgery, they may support individualized postoperative risk stratification and monitoring; external validation is warranted. See Video Abstract.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Low anterior resection syndrome, characterized by a constellation of defecatory dysfunction symptoms, is a frequent complication after low anterior resection surgery. However, the mechanisms underlying low anterior resection syndrome, including potential associations with intestinal microbiota, remain poorly defined. To characterize the onset and progression of low anterior resection syndrome across the rectal cancer treatment pathway and to examine microbial community shifts in relation to low anterior resection syndrome development. Prospective cohort study with a nested subgroup undergoing repeated clinical and microbial assessments. St Paul's Hospital, Vancouver, Canada. Rectal adenocarcinoma patients undergoing curative-intent resection with restoration of bowel continuity. Prospectively collected cohort without intervention. The primary outcome was presence of low anterior resection syndrome (score ≥ 21). Secondary outcomes included microbial diversity and composition changes. Pretreatment bowel dysfunction meeting low anterior resection syndrome-score criteria was present in 42% (30/71) of patients, without significant association with demographic or clinical variables. By the end of follow-up, 64% exhibited low anterior resection syndrome. New-onset low anterior resection syndrome correlated with lower tumor height (p = 0.04). Microbial beta diversity differed between no pretreatment bowel dysfunction and pretreatment bowel dysfunction meeting low anterior resection syndrome criteria at baseline (p < 0.001), but alpha diversity did not, and no microbial features predicted subsequent new-onset low anterior resection syndrome. Single-center design with small sample size. Bowel dysfunction meeting low anterior resection syndrome criteria is common before rectal cancer treatment and increased postoperatively. Although baseline microbial profiles differed, no association between bacterial diversity and low anterior resection syndrome development could be demonstrated. Routine pretreatment bowel dysfunction assessment may guide patient counseling and quality of life. See Video Abstract.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Aspirin (ASA), a classical nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug, is known to inhibit glycolysis in cancer cells; however, the underlying mechanism remain incompletely understood. Here, we identify lysine salicylation (Ksa) as an ASA-dependent protein modification that suppresses glycolysis and proliferation in colorectal cancer cells. Specifically, ASA causes Ksa on the key glycolytic enzyme aldolase A (ALDOA), markedly reducing its enzymatic activity without altering protein level. Metabolomic analysis revealed that ASA impairs the conversion of fructose-1,6-bisphosphate (F16BP) to glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate (GAP), thereby disrupting glycolytic flux. In a xenograft mouse model, ASA administration not only inhibited tumor growth but also enhanced ALDOA Ksa level and blocked F16BP-to-GAP conversion. Besides, site-directed mutagenesis and genetic code expansion experiments confirmed that ALDOA K13sa is critical for ASA-mediated inhibition of glycolysis and cancer cell proliferation. Together, this study uncovers Ksa as an innovative mechanism by which ASA affects glycolysis and cancer cell proliferation, providing further insights into its potential role in cancer prevention and therapy.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Implementation of Enhanced Recovery After Surgery requires coordinated multidisciplinary practice change and remains challenging in resource-constrained health care settings because implementation barriers often extend beyond knowledge deficits. This article describes the development, implementation and implementation-focused evaluation of a multidisciplinary perioperative education programme designed to support Enhanced Recovery After Surgery implementation across two public-sector hospitals in India. The programme was developed through a sequential, evidence-informed process. Findings from a prospective observational evaluation and a sequential explanatory mixed-methods study were synthesised and mapped to the Enhanced Recovery After Surgery Society Guideline for Perioperative Care in Elective Colorectal Surgery and overarching Enhanced Recovery After Surgery principles. This informed the development of a workflow-integrated educational programme incorporating orientation sessions, micro-training, bedside coaching, structured communication, nursing and clinician champions, bedside checklists, visual reminders and audit-feedback. The programme was implemented across a tertiary teaching hospital and a district hospital. Educational activities were embedded within routine perioperative workflows, promoting multidisciplinary engagement, behavioural reinforcement, workflow integration and adoption of standardised recovery practices. A structured, evidence-informed educational strategy integrated within routine clinical workflows provides a practical approach to supporting sustainable Enhanced Recovery After Surgery implementation in resource-constrained public-sector hospitals.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal liver metastasis (CRLM) is a leading cause of mortality in colorectal cancer (CRC), yet current surveillance often misses occult micrometastases, underscoring an urgent need for early non-invasive biomarkers and mechanistic insights. This study aimed to investigate gut microbiota dysbiosis and functional alterations associated with CRLM and explore potential non-invasive biomarkers. Fecal metagenomic sequencing was performed in 60 participants, comprising healthy controls, patients with non-metastatic CRC, and patients with synchronous CRLM (n = 20 per group). Microbial composition, functional pathways, co-occurrence networks, and clinical associations were systematically analyzed, and a random forest model was constructed to identify potential diagnostic biomarkers. Results showed that gut microbiota dysbiosis intensified as CRC progressed toward CRLM, characterized by the depletion of commensal flora and significant enrichment of specific genera, such as Eikenella and Porphyromonas. Functionally, the gut microbiome displayed stage-specific remodeling, shifting from infection- and virulence-related pathways in CRC to functions associated with microbial secondary metabolism and stress adaptation in CRLM. Furthermore, SPIEC-EASI-based network analysis revealed a sparser and more compartmentalized microbial ecological structure in CRLM, with [Clostridium] symbiosum, Campylobacter concisus, and Coprococcus eutactus emerging as module hubs. A random forest model integrating nine core taxa and one virulence factor (VF0160 FeoAB) achieved an overall 97.5% classification accuracy in discriminating CRLM from non-metastatic CRC, indicating the potential of fecal metagenomic biomarkers for future risk stratification. However, prospective validation in larger multicenter cohorts is required before clinical translational utility. Collectively, our findings suggest that gut microbiota dysbiosis and functional reprogramming are strongly associated with CRLM progression, potentially through remodeling the hepatic pre-metastatic niche via the gut-liver axis.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Comprehensive genomic profiling (CGP) is standard for advanced solid tumors. Evidence reporting its real-world utilization pattern and time course for guided therapy is limited. This retrospective study in Japan assessed the real-world utility of CGP tests for advanced or metastatic solid tumors using data from the C-CAT registry from June 1, 2019, to August 23, 2025. We evaluated the proportion of patients who received genomically matched therapy with expert panel (EP) recommendation and their overall survival (OS) compared with patients who did not receive genomically matched therapy. The study population comprised 89,552 patients who underwent CGP: median age 64.0 (interquartile range: 54.0-72.0) years, with pancreatic cancer (13,827; 15.4%) and colorectal cancer (11,322; 12.6%) the most common tumor types. System-generated matched treatment options presented as reference information during EP review were identified in 80,185, of whom 77,337 (96.4%) received EP review, 37,245 (46.4%) were offered new therapeutic recommendations, and 7124 (8.9%) initiated EP-recommended therapies. Among 2049 patients who were newly identified with companion diagnostic (CDx)-related druggable alterations, 319 (15.6%) received matched therapies. Patients receiving matched therapies experienced longer OS compared with others in the overall cohort (median: 538 days vs. 356 days) and across cancer types. OS varied by the final treatment line before CGP testing, with earlier lines associated with longer survival in biliary tract, ovarian, pancreatic, and thyroid cancers. These findings highlight the need for timely CGP implementation to maximize the impact of precision oncology. Trial Registration: Japan Registry of Clinical Trials identifier: jRCT1030250365.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Oxaliplatin-based neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NACT) is increasingly used in locally advanced colorectal cancer (CRC); however, early acquired resistance substantially limits its efficacy. We revealed an enrichment of therapy-induced senescence (TIS)-like phenotypes in short-term oxaliplatin-exposed CRC. Consistently, a similar upregulation of senescence markers was observed in oxaliplatin-resistant CRC cells. Senolytic treatment attenuated senescence features and restored oxaliplatin sensitivity in vitro and in vivo. Integrative analysis of RNA-sequencing data from resistant tumours and ABT263-treated resistant tumours identified adenosine A1 receptor (ADORA1) as a key mediator of senescence and oxaliplatin resistance. ADORA1 is highly expressed in CRC tumours and is further induced by oxaliplatin, with elevated ADORA1 levels enriched in chemoresistant patients and associated with poor outcomes following chemotherapy. Mechanistically, ADORA1 directly interacts with and stabilises fatty acid synthase (FASN) by suppressing its ubiquitin-mediated degradation, thereby promoting palmitic acid (PA) synthesis, lipid droplet accumulation and p53/p21-driven senescence. Conversely, ADORA1 knockdown attenuates these phenotypes and restores oxaliplatin sensitivity. Together, these findings identify the ADORA1-FASN-PA metabolic reprogramming as a central mechanistic link between TIS and oxaliplatin resistance in CRC, highlighting this pathway as a promising therapeutic target for overcoming early acquired resistance.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) are recognized as critical components of the colorectal cancer (CRC) immune microenvironment, demonstrating significant prognostic and predictive implications. However, a clear and widely accepted definition of colorectal TILs has not yet been established, and TILs are not systematically used as biomarkers in current oncology practice. This highlights the need for standardized assessment methods and a deeper understanding of the complex role of TILs in CRC, necessitating collaborative work to achieve clinical importance. This report, on behalf of the International Immuno-Oncology Biomarker Working Group (ITWG), provides a comprehensive overview of TILs in CRC, including a TILs-assessment method. It details their multifaceted role of TILs within the tumour microenvironment, details current and emerging methods for their assessment and reviews their prognostic and predictive importance. The report also explores the relationship of TILs to other established and emerging biomarkers in CRC. Emerging trends, including AI-driven analysis for automated TIL quantification, and single-cell and spatial technologies for in-depth characterization of the tumour microenvironment (TME), are also highlighted. The report concludes with a discussion of future directions and the ongoing efforts of the ITWG to address the challenges and standardize and advance the clinical application of TIL assessment in CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Polystyrene nanoplastics (PS-NPs) directly encounter the gastrointestinal epithelium after ingestion, yet the epithelial molecular states linking exposure to colon cancer cell behavior remain unclear. We integrated bulk transcriptomics, interpretable machine learning, WGCNA, single-cell and spatial transcriptomics, structural analyses, and in vitro experiments to investigate CA1-associated epithelial responses. Intersecting 2139 colon cancer differentially expressed genes with 766 styrene-associated genes yielded 159 candidates. Among 45 classification models, LASSO + GBM ranked highest in an exploratory cross-cohort comparison, with an apparent training AUC of 1.000 and comparison-cohort AUCs of 0.999 and 0.925. CA1 had the highest SHAP importance and was located in the WGCNA module most strongly associated with tumor/normal status. Single-cell and organoid analyses showed attenuation of epithelial CA1/CA2 and carbonic anhydrase-bicarbonate-related programs, with concordant spatial trends; TCGA-COAD and Human Protein Atlas data further supported reduced CA1 expression. Low CA1 was associated with reduced metabolic and bicarbonate-related programs and enhanced inflammatory signaling. Docking and 100 ns molecular dynamics showed only weak, dynamic styrene-CA1 contacts. In HCT116 cells, PS-NPs decreased CA1, CA2, and Occludin expression, altered stress-, inflammation-, and apoptosis-related molecules, and increased scratch closure, with generally stronger changes at higher doses and after Tioxolone co-treatment. Collectively, these findings identify a CA1/CA2-low epithelial state associated with PS-NP exposure and suggest that CA1-associated epithelial-state remodeling may be part of the cellular response to PS-NPs.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Huangqin Tang (HQT), documented in the Shanghan Lun, is traditionally prescribed for "dysenteric disorders" (Li Ji). Modern clinical studies confirm its efficacy against ulcerative colitis and colorectal cancer-associated inflammation, providing a verified traditional basis for investigating its immunomodulatory effects in colorectal malignancy. However, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate the regulatory role of lactate-induced protein lactylation in MIF-driven PD-1 resistance and to determine if HQT can reverse this phenotype through metabolic reprogramming. CT26-bearing BALB/c mice were administered HQT intragastrically combined with intraperitoneal anti-PD-1 antibodies. Tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes were profiled by flow cytometry. Integrative transcriptomics and network pharmacology were utilized to screen candidate targets. LC-MS/MS-based lactylomic profiling identified specific modification sites. Lactate modulation assays, and site-directed mutagenesis (NF-κB1 K249R) coupled with rescue experiments were performed in vitro to validate the molecular cascade mechanistically. HQT synergized with anti-PD-1 to suppress tumor growth and prolong survival. This combination remodeled the immune microenvironment, increasing CD8 NF-κB1 K249 lactylation acts as a critical post-translational switch linking tumor glycolysis to Treg-mediated immunosuppression. HQT overcomes PD-1 resistance by suppressing this axis. These findings support combining metabolic intervention with immunotherapy and highlight K249 lactylation as a potential biomarker for treatment response.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Adjuvant chemotherapy is a standard component of care for patients with resected stage II-III colorectal cancer (CRC), improving survival outcomes but often at the expense of quality of life (QoL) and functional status. Exercise and physical activity (PA) have emerged as a potential strategy to mitigate treatment-related toxicities and improve oncologic outcomes. This study aimed to evaluate the impact of PA and exercise and its interventions during adjuvant chemotherapy. A systematic review was performed using the MEDLINE, EMBASE, Web of Science, SCOPUS, CINAHL, and PsycINFO databases up to June 2025. Studies including adult CRC patients undergoing or recently completed adjuvant chemotherapy and participating in structured exercise program or PA assessment were eligible. Nine studies encompassing 4070 patients were included, of whom 631 participated in structured exercise interventions. The interventions varied in modality, incorporating aerobic, resistance, and combined programs delivered in both supervised and home-based settings. Engagement in PA was associated with improvements in overall survival (OS) and disease-free survival (DFS) in selected studies, although measures and outcomes were highly heterogeneous. QoL findings were variable but generally favored exercise, with reported benefits in physical functioning, fatigue, cardiorespiratory fitness, and psychological well-being. In addition, exercise was linked in some studies to improved chemotherapy tolerance, including higher treatment completion rates and reduced treatment-related toxicities such as fatigue and neurotoxicity. Exercise during adjuvant chemotherapy in CRC is feasible and appears to improve functional and patient-reported outcomes, with a consistent signal toward improved survival. Supervised interventions may offer additional benefits through enhanced adherence and optimization of exercise delivery. However, heterogeneity in study design and outcome reporting limits definitive conclusions. Further high-quality randomized trials are needed to establish standardized exercise protocols and clarify their impact on long-term oncologic outcomes.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
To prospectively validate an AI-accelerated MRI protocol combining L₁-regularized compressed sensing and deep learning reconstruction for colon cancer staging, compared with contrast-enhanced CT (CECT). This single-center study (August 2022-April 2024) enrolled 132 patients with pathologically confirmed colon cancer who underwent both 3.0-T non-contrast MRI and CECT within 1 week. Patients unable to complete an MRI were excluded. MRI sequences included T1- and T2-weighted imaging and diffusion-weighted imaging. Image quality was assessed using a 4-point Likert scale, alongside quantitative analysis of contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) and edge rise distance (ERD). Surgical pathology correlation was available for 33 cases. Five radiologists independently reviewed the images. Among 153 matched examination pairs from 132 patients (mean age, 58 ± 11 years), AI-MRI outperformed CECT in both qualitative and quantitative measures. MRI yielded higher image quality scores (4 [IQR 3-4] vs. 3 [IQR 3-3]), improved CNR (5.5 [IQR 4.2-7.0] vs. 1.3 [IQR 0.7-2.2]), and reduced ERD (1.6 mm [IQR 1.2-2.8] vs. 3.7 mm [IQR 2.8-5.0]). MRI provided superior peritoneal sharpness (75.8%) and colonic wall visualization (100%), and superior or equivalent tumor conspicuity (92.2%) and nodal assessment (86.9%), whereas CECT demonstrated better artifact control (45.1%). In preliminary analyses, MRI achieved higher T-staging accuracy (78.8% vs. 30.3%) and N-staging specificity (93.3% vs. 13.3%). The AI-accelerated MRI protocol significantly outperformed CECT in image quality and preliminary staging accuracy for colon cancer evaluation while eliminating radiation exposure. Question Can an AI-accelerated MRI protocol provide superior image quality and staging performance compared with contrast-enhanced CT, which has limited diagnostic accuracy for colon cancer staging? Findings AI-accelerated MRI using L₁-regularized compressed sensing and deep learning reconstruction achieved superior image quality and higher preliminary staging accuracy than contrast-enhanced CT. Critical Relevance Statement AI-accelerated MRI improves image quality and staging confidence without radiation exposure, supporting its potential to enhance preoperative assessment and clinical decision-making in colon cancer.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Linalool is a naturally occurring volatile monoterpene that exhibits significant anticancer potency across several malignancies via multitargeted molecular mechanisms. However, the translational research requires a clear anticancer potency with molecular targets and bioavailability data with respect to cancer type as identified via adequate cell and animal models, which lead to clinical trials. Nevertheless, the translation of linalool for clinical use is restricted by the lack of clinical trials and its limited in vivo bioavailability as reported in pre-clinical studies, high volatility and poor aqueous solubility. Therefore, this review examines the reported anticancer potency, probable molecular mechanisms, bioavailability research findings, and current nanoformulation of linalool for future application as an effective medicine. Inadequate in vivo validation and limited intravenous delivery data further highlight the need for advanced nanoformulation techniques and thorough translational studies. The literature for this review was methodically collected from research findings published between 2000 and 2025, capturing foundational and current breakthroughs on linalool's anticancer potency. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
To determine whether regional variation in diagnostic procedures and treatment for cancer exists among American Indian and Alaska Native (AIAN) patients. We used data from the Surveillance Epidemiology and End Results (SEER) 17 database to examine differences in diagnostic, treatment, and care quality-related variables for female breast, lung, and colorectal cancers diagnosed among AIAN patients. We used unadjusted and multivariable-adjusted logistic regression models to examine differences across Indian Health Service regions adjusted for age at diagnosis, diagnosis year, residence in a purchased/referred care delivery area, and stage at diagnosis, using the Pacific Coast region as the reference. The study sample included female breast (n=7,221), lung (n=5,403), and colorectal cancer (n=5,626) patients. Among AIAN female breast cancer patients, those in Alaska, the East, and the Southwest had higher odds of timely treatment; those in Alaska had higher odds of receipt of chemotherapy and hormone receptor testing; while those in the Southwest had lower odds of hormone receptor testing. For lung cancer patients, those in Alaska, the Southwest, and the East had higher odds of timely treatment; those in Alaska had higher odds of receiving radiation and lower odds of receiving surgery. Finally, for colorectal cancer patients, those in Alaska, the Southwest, and the East had higher odds of receiving timely treatment. Differences described herein may reflect differences in clinical characteristics, practice patterns, or access to care. Further research on how treatment differences lead to regional variations in cancer outcomes for AIAN patients are warranted.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a major global health burden, with metabolic alterations contributing to its malignant behavior. Pectolinarigenin (PEC), a naturally occurring flavonoid, exhibits antitumor activity in several cancers, but its metabolism-associated effects in CRC remain poorly characterized. This study aimed to investigate the anticancer activity of PEC and its effects on glycolysis-associated metabolism and AMPK/FOXO3a-related signaling in CRC. PEC targets were predicted using PharmMapper and SwissTargetPrediction and intersected with CRC-related differentially expressed genes. Functional enrichment analysis, protein-protein interaction analysis, LASSO regression, and single-cell RNA sequencing were integrated to identify candidate genes associated with PEC activity. The effects of PEC were evaluated in HT29 and MC38 cells using proliferation, colony formation, invasion, apoptosis, qRT-PCR, and western blotting assays. AMPK/FOXO3a-related signaling changes were examined in both CRC cell models and MC38 tumor tissues, with selected molecular alterations further assessed by immunohistochemistry in MC38 syngeneic tumors. PEC suppressed CRC cell proliferation, colony formation, and invasion and promoted apoptosis. PEC treatment reduced the expression of the glycolysis-associated molecules GLUT1, HK2, and LDHA, accompanied by increased AMPK phosphorylation and reduced inhibitory FOXO3a phosphorylation in CRC cells. Integrated bioinformatic analyses identified CA1 and CA7 as candidate genes associated with PEC activity, with both genes predominantly localized to epithelial cell populations in single-cell datasets. PEC increased CA1 and CA7 expression in CRC cells and MC38 tumor tissues. Western blotting of tumor tissues further showed increased p-AMPK and reduced p-FOXO3a levels following PEC treatment, consistent with the corresponding changes observed in CRC cells. Immunohistochemical analysis further confirmed increased p-AMPK, CA1, and CA7 staining and reduced p-FOXO3a staining in PEC-treated tumor tissues. PEC exhibits antitumor activity against CRC and is associated with coordinated changes in glycolysis-associated molecules and AMPK/FOXO3a-related signaling. CA1 and CA7 emerged from integrated bioinformatic analyses as metabolism-associated candidate genes and showed consistent expression changes following PEC treatment in CRC cells and tumor tissues. These findings provide a basis for further investigation of the molecular and metabolic responses associated with PEC in CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
We evaluated whether an automated electronic health record (EHR)-based frailty index (eFI) is associated with hospitalization and overall survival (OS) in older adults receiving chemotherapy. We identified 509 consecutive patients aged ≥65 years with newly diagnosed lung, colorectal, or breast cancer treated with chemotherapy (2017-2020). An automated eFI score was calculated using data from ≥2 visits in the 2 years before chemotherapy, including vital signs, smoking status, diagnoses, selected laboratory values, and functional measures. Frailty was categorized using a cumulative deficit approach as fit (eFI ≤0.10), pre-frail (0.10-0.21), or frail (>0.21). Hospitalizations at 3 and 6 months were compared across groups. Adjusted associations between eFI and hospitalization and mortality were assessed using Cox regression models. OS was estimated by Kaplan-Meier methods and compared using log-rank tests. Among 509 patients (median age, 72.2 years), 27.7% were fit, 42.4% pre-frail, 14.9% frail, and 14.9% had non-calculable eFI. Six-month hospitalization increased with frailty: 24% (fit), 42% (pre-frail), 62% (frail), and 50% (non-calculable) (P<.0001). Median OS was 38 months (fit), 23 months (pre-frail), 17 months (frail), and 10 months (not calculable) (p < 0.0001). In adjusted models, mortality risk was higher in pre-frail (HR 1.7, 95% CI 1.2-2.3), frail (HR 2.0, 95% CI 1.3-3.1), and not calculable groups (HR 2.6, 95% CI 1.7-4.0) compared with fit patients. EHR-derived frailty was associated with hospitalization and survival, supporting the eFI as a scalable approach to risk stratification in older adults undergoing chemotherapy.

The liver is the main site of colorectal metastatic disease. This study evaluated the association of Neutrophil-to-Lymphocyte Ratio (NLR), Platelet-to-Lymphocyte Ratio (PLR), and Monocyte-to-Lymphocyte Ratio (MLR) among patients with colorectal liver metastases (CRLM) undergoing liver resection. A cohort of patients undergoing curative-intent liver resection for CRLM between 2009 and 2020 was evaluated. Association between inflammatory indices and overall survival (OS), disease-free survival (DFS), and postoperative morbidity and mortality were studied. Subgroup analyses included patients undergoing major hepatectomies (≥ 3 segments) and those receiving preoperative chemotherapy. The indices variation before and after chemotherapy were assessed for OS, DFS, and complete pathological response rates. After exclusion criteria, 380 patients were selected for the study. No significant associations were found between inflammatory indices and OS or DFS. Lower preoperative PLR was associated with higher postoperative morbidity (p = 0.021) after major hepatectomies. Among patients receiving chemotherapy, a greater reduction in PLR was associated with a higher complete pathological response rate (p = 0.002). Although inflammatory indices were not predictive of survival outcomes, PLR was associated with postoperative morbidity and pathological response in specific subgroups; although these findings require validation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Despite advances in treatment of primary colon cancer, approximately 5 to 10% of patients will develop a locoregional recurrence of colon cancer. Early recurrences diagnosed within 1 year have been associated with worse outcomes, but evidence is limited and conflicting. This study aimed to evaluate the prognostic impact of timing of locoregional recurrence detection. This is a cross-sectional multicenter cohort study. Multicenter collaborative study involving 50 Dutch hospitals. Patients with locoregional recurrence after colon cancer resection between January 2014 and December 2015, stratified by timing of locoregional recurrence diagnosis (early < 1 year, late ≥ 1 year). Overall survival stratified by treatment intent. Among 9,523 patients, 676 (7.1%) developed locoregional recurrence (291 early, 385 late). Median time to locoregional recurrence diagnosis was 13.7 months (IQR 8.6-23.4). Late diagnosis of locoregional recurrence was independently associated with higher probability of overall survival (median 18.0 vs 9.1 months; HR 0.83, 95% CI 0.69-0.99) and was more often treated with curative intent (34.6 vs 24.0%, p = 0.01). In patients treated with curative intent, overall survival did not differ between early and late locoregional recurrence (median 40.1 vs 40.7 months; HR 1.05, 95% CI 0.73-1.51, p = 0.79). In palliatively treated patients, late locoregional recurrence was associated with longer overall survival compared to early locoregional recurrence (median 10.1 vs 6.8months; HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.58-0.84, p < 0.001). This study is limited by its retrospective design. Late diagnosis of locoregional recurrence was associated with better survival, but survival from the moment of locoregional recurrence was not different between patients with early and late recurrences who were treated with curative intent. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Watch-and-wait has allowed organ preservation in patients with locally advanced rectal cancer who have a clinical complete response to neoadjuvant therapy. The expansion of non-operative management to patients with a near-complete response raises the question of oncological safety in a nonoperative approach in this subset of patients. We aimed to assess the prognostic impact of clinical response after neoadjuvant therapy and to assess the oncologic safety of nonoperative management in patients with near-complete or complete clinical responses. We systematically reviewed PubMed, Embase and Web of Science in October 2025 to identify studies comparing oncological outcomes of patients with clinical or near-complete response. Studies comparing clinical response after neoadjuvant therapy in patients with locally advanced rectal cancer were included. We excluded conference abstracts. Primary outcome was overall survival. Secondary outcomes included distant metastasis, local regrowth, local regrowth-free survival, and organ preservation rate. We included 10 studies and 1,763 patients. Near-complete response after neoadjuvant therapy for rectal cancer is associated with higher risk of distant metastasis (16.8 vs 7.3%; RR 2.31; 95% CI: 1.63-3.26; p < 0.001; I² = 0%), and local regrowth (32.8 vs 19.7%; RR 1.75; 95% CI: 1.31-2.34; p < 0.001; I² = 42%), as well as reduced organ preservation (73.5 vs 80.7%; RR 0.84; 95% CI: 0.74-0.95; p = 0.007; I² = 69%) compared with clinical complete response. No statistical differences were seen in overall survival (HR 1.43; 95% CI: 0.94-2.16; p = 0.076; I² = 0%). Heterogeneous definitions of near-complete response and lack of standardized reassessment timing and management. In contrast to individual studies, we found that near-complete response after neoadjuvant therapy may have an increased risk of distant metastasis compared to patients with a complete clinical response.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Up to 80% of patients who undergo rectal resection suffer from low anterior resection syndrome, with approximately half continuing to experience symptoms more than 10 years after surgery. While short-term outcomes are well documented, evidence on long-term functional and health-related quality of life trajectories remains fragmented. There is some improvement over time, but symptoms often persist. To systematically review the prevalence, severity, and long-term trajectory of low anterior resection syndrome, and its association with health-related quality of life, in rectal cancer survivors followed for at least five years after sphincter-preserving surgery. A systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library from inception through September 2025. Eligible studies reported low anterior resection syndrome scores in patients at ≥5 years following sphincter-preserving rectal cancer resection. Studies lacking long-term functional assessment or not reporting low anterior resection syndrome were excluded. None; all included studies comprised observational cohort data assessing long-term functional outcomes. Prevalence of major and minor Low Anterior Resection Syndrome, distribution of long-term low anterior resection syndrome severity categories, and associations between low anterior resection syndrome severity and health-related quality of life measures. Six studies comprising 1,000 patients were included, with median follow-up ranging from 6.9 to 14.6 years. Across cohorts, major low anterior resection syndrome was reported in 20.5-53.0% of patients and minor low anterior resection syndrome in 14.6-27.0%. Overall, 39.3% of patients experienced major low anterior resection syndrome, 21.5% minor low anterior resection syndrome, and 39.2% reported no low anterior resection syndrome at long-term follow-up. Major low anterior resection syndrome was consistently associated with significant health-related quality of life impairment across multiple domains. Neoadjuvant radiotherapy emerged as the most consistent risk factor for persistent bowel dysfunction. Heterogeneity in neoadjuvant radiotherapy, tumor height, and exclusion of patients with permanent or secondary stomas; observational designs. Nearly half of rectal cancer survivors experience major Low Anterior Resection Syndrome ≥5 years postoperatively, highlighting the persistence of bowel dysfunction and its lasting impact on health-related quality of life. These findings underscore the need for long-term survivorship care and functional outcome monitoring.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a leading cause of mortality, underscoring the urgent need for predictive precision medicine tools. While patient-derived organoids have advanced drug screening, they often lack the dynamic physical microenvironment found in vivo. Organ-on-a-chip (OOC) systems offer superior physiological relevance; however, their translation from bench to bedside has been stalled by a lack of validation against clinical patient outcomes. Here, we bridge this critical translational gap by demonstrating the feasibility and predictive utility of a scalable, patient-derived OOC (PDOC) platform. From a cohort of 14 primary locally advanced CRC cases, we engineered 8 patient-specific PDOCs that maintained high-fidelity histological recapitulation of the parental tumor tissue. Leveraging an automated, high-content imaging workflow alongside metabolic assays, we profiled responses to standard-of-care chemotherapies (irinotecan, FOLFOX, and FOLFIRI). The platform successfully stratified patients into distinct phenotypic response groups, revealing specific sensitivities to FOLFOX versus FOLFIRI. Crucially, we present preliminary clinical evidence supporting these ex vivo predictions: in a 7-month follow-up, all patients identified as FOLFOX-sensitive by our platform remained disease-free post-surgery. These findings support the PDOC platform not just as a complex in vitro model, but as a viable, predictive technology for functional precision oncology. This work represents an important step toward integrating microphysiological systems into prospective clinical decision-making for CRC and other solid tumors.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
It is well established that endogenous and exogenous corticotrophin-releasing factor (CRF) stimulates colonic motility in rodents. Electroacupuncture (EA) has shown promise in relieving stress responses and alleviating colonic dysmotility, but less is known about its underlying mechanism of action in this context. This study was designed to elucidate the effects of EA on colorectal dysfunction in a rat model of stress and to clarify the underlying mechanism. A rat model of stress was induced using exogenous CRF. Colonic propulsion was evaluated by the bead latency test, and colorectal motility was recorded in vivo by implanting a manometric capsule into the colorectal lumen. To clarify the role of CRF receptors type 1 and 2 on stress-induced colonic dysfunction, corresponding selective antagonists (CP-154526 and Astressin 2B, respectively) were administered accordingly. Western blot analysis was used to detect protein expression of CRF and its receptors in the hypothalamus and colorectum. CRF-induced stress significantly accelerated colonic motility. EA treatment alleviated colonic motor dysfunction and reduced colonic propulsion. CP-154526, but not Astressin 2B, reversed CRF-induced colonic dysmotility, suggesting an essential role of CRF receptor type 1 in stress-induced colonic motor disorders. EA treatment resulted in an inhibition of the protein overexpression of CRF receptor type 1 in both the hypothalamus and colorectum in this rat model of stress. EA ameliorated stress-induced colonic dysmotility, most likely through regulation of central and peripheral expression of CRF receptor type 1.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
To evaluate perioperative morbidity, factors associated with postoperative complications and documented recurrence after one-stage laparoscopic resection for multicompartment deep endometriosis. Retrospective multicentre cohort study. Two tertiary referral centres specialised in endometriosis surgery (Bern, Switzerland; Budapest, Hungary). A total of 299 consecutive patients with pathologically confirmed deep endometriosis undergoing one-stage laparoscopic resection between January 2017 and December 2025. One-stage laparoscopic resection of multicompartment deep endometriosis. Clinically relevant postoperative complications were defined as Clavien-Dindo Grade ≥ II. Multivariable logistic regression assessed associated factors. Recurrence-free survival was evaluated using Kaplan-Meier analysis in patients with an available recurrence time or censoring time. Postoperative complications occurred in 36/299 patients (12.0%), including 35/299 (11.7%) with Grade ≥ II complications and 14/299 (4.7%) with Grade ≥ IIIb complications. Greater #ENZIAN deep endometriosis anatomical extent was independently associated with clinically relevant complications (adjusted odds ratio 1.51 per additional involved compartment, 95% confidence interval 1.04-2.18). Documented recurrence occurred in 43/299 patients (14.4%) and 26/299 (8.7%) underwent reoperation for recurrence. Follow-up duration was available for 231/299 patients (77.3%). Recurrence-free survival did not differ significantly according to bowel (log-rank p = 0.431) or bladder surgical technique (p = 0.116). Greater #ENZIAN deep endometriosis anatomical extent was independently associated with clinically relevant postoperative complications following one-stage surgery for multicompartment deep endometriosis, suggesting that overall anatomical disease extent may better reflect surgical complexity than involvement of a single anatomical site. These findings support the role of anatomical disease extent in preoperative counselling and individualised surgical planning.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Oxaliplatin (OXA) resistance affects the efficacy of colorectal cancer (CRC) treatment. Gene expression profiles of OXA-resistant and OXA-sensitive cells were compared to identify differentially expressed non-coding RNAs. A dual-luciferase assay was used to research the targeting relationship and binding region of TUG1 and miR-449a. SiRNA interference was used to construct cell models of OXA-resistant cells with low expression of TUG1 and OXA-sensitive cells with high expression of HDAC, as well as animal models based on these two types of cells. Then, cellular function was assessed. Histopathologic conditions were assessed by immunohistochemistry. TUG1, miR-449a and Histone Deacetylase 4 (HDAC4) were all upregulated in OXA-resistant cells, and the increase of HDAC4 was accompanied by a decrease in acetylation level. TUG1 binds to miR-449a, and TUG1 was located in the cytoplasm of OXA-resistant cells. Downregulated expression of TUG1 could inhibit proliferation and induce apoptosis in OXA-resistant cells and reverse OXA resistance. Downregulated expression of HDAC4 could reduce the expression of TUG1, and inhibit proliferation and induce apoptosis of OXA-resistant cells. Treatment with 2 mmol/L sodium butyrate (NaB), a histone deacetylase inhibitor, markedly suppressed tumor cell growth through regulation of TUG1 compared with 0.01 mmol/L NaB. The OXA-resistant tumor-bearing mouse experiment further confirmed the inhibitory effect of NaB on tumor. High-dose NaB can inhibit the expression of HDAC4, and then reduce the expression of TUG1 through acetylation modification, thereby inhibiting the development of CRC and reversing OXA resistance in CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Preoperative immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) are active in patients with deficient mismatch repair (dMMR) colon cancer (CC), whereas proficient mismatch repair (pMMR) CC has been consistently considered resistant to first-generation ICIs. In the phase 2 UNICORN trial, we evaluated short-course preoperative botensilimab (BOT; multifunctional Fc-enhanced anti-CTLA-4 monoclonal antibody) alone or in combination with the anti-PD-1 monoclonal antibody balstilimab (BOT + BAL) in 56 patients with resectable, locally advanced CC. Twenty-eight patients with pMMR CC were sequentially enrolled in BOT (n = 14) and BOT + BAL (n = 14) cohorts. Twenty-eight patients with dMMR CC followed the same sequential allocation strategy. The primary endpoint of centrally assessed pathological major response (pMR) rate (≤10% of residual viable tumor) was met in all cohorts, except pMMR BOT. Specifically, the pMR rate was 0% (95% confidence interval (CI): 0-23.2%) in pMMR BOT, 36% (95% CI: 12.8-64.9%) in pMMR BOT + BAL, 36% (95% CI: 12.8-64.9%) in dMMR BOT and 100% (95% CI: 76.8-100%) in dMMR BOT + BAL. Secondary endpoints included safety, quality of life, describing treatment-induced transcriptional dynamics, peripheral blood mononuclear cell dynamics, radiomics and radiogenomics features, fecal microbiota composition and circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) dynamics. Eight (29%) and 15 (54%) patients treated with BOT and BOT + BAL, respectively, experienced immune-related adverse events, most commonly flu-like syndrome and diarrhea. Single-cell spatial transcriptomic analysis of matched baseline and post-treatment samples highlighted high baseline PD-L1 stromal expression and low post-treatment regulatory T cell signatures in pMMR responders, whereas dMMR responders displayed high baseline FCGR2A and FCGR3A expression on intratumoral macrophages. Clearance of ctDNA before surgery correlated with pathological response and lack of recurrence at data cutoff. Preoperative BOT + BAL elicits pathological responses in patients with pMMR or dMMR CC, supporting the combination as a promising strategy to expand ICI benefits to the early-stage setting. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05845450 .

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Previous studies on indocyanine green (ICG) in colorectal surgery have mainly focused on lymphatic mapping, sentinel node detection, and the number of harvested lymph nodes. However, evidence regarding long-term oncologic outcomes following ICG fluorescence-guided colorectal cancer (CRC) surgery remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate the prognostic impact of ICG fluorescence-guided laparoscopic radical resection compared with conventional laparoscopic surgery in CRC patients. A retrospective cohort study was performed among 367 CRC patients who underwent laparoscopic radical resection between December 2016 and December 2020 in a single center. Patients were divided into ICG-guided and non-ICG groups and matched using propensity score matching (PSM). The primary endpoint was disease-free survival (DFS), while secondary endpoints included overall survival, cancer-specific survival (CSS), number of harvested lymph nodes, and postoperative complications. After PSM, 204 patients were analyzed (133 in the ICG group and 71 in the non-ICG group). The ICG group had a higher mean number of harvested lymph nodes (15.2 ± 8.0 vs. 12.9 ± 5.7, p = 0.036) and negative lymph nodes (13.5 ± 8.3 vs. 11.2 ± 5.9; p = 0.038). The CSS in the ICG group was significantly better than that in the non-ICG group (p < 0.05). Multivariate Cox regression identified ICG-guided surgery as an independent protective factor for CSS (HR = 0.303, 95% CI 0.113-0.812, p = 0.018). Subgroup analysis demonstrated that ICG guidance conferred a survival benefit in stage III CRC patients for both DFS and CSS. ICG fluorescence-guided laparoscopic radical resection increased lymph node yield, particularly negative nodes, and resulted in favorable disease-free and cancer-specific survival in CRC patients, with the most pronounced benefit observed in stage III disease.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a paradigmatic disease for understanding cancer evolution. CRC is common and accessible for sampling, and malignant progression occurs through clearly defined morphological stages. In this Review, we describe how the pattern of somatic alterations that accrue in the genomes and epigenomes of colorectal cells reveal the dynamics and molecular drivers of CRC evolution, from initial transformation through to metastatic dissemination and treatment resistance. We consider the latest evidence of genetic, epigenetic and immune changes that accompany multistep carcinogenesis. We explore the role of the epigenome and cell plasticity in progression and treatment resistance, and their interrelationship with genetic changes. Finally, we discuss how these evolutionary principles are redefining clinical strategies and explore the translational frontiers in evolution-informed therapy.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) is one of the most diagnosed malignancies worldwide, with chronic inflammation playing a critical role in its pathogenesis and progression. Surgery represents the primary treatment option, though some patients suffer from relapse, leading to considerable morbidity and mortality. A better molecular understanding of CRC pathogenesis is therefore essential for identifying patients at increased risk of recurrence and improving clinical management. Here we identified the X-linked inhibitor of apoptosis protein (XIAP) as an independent predictor of overall survival in primary resected CRC patients. To model CRC patients with low versus high XIAP expression, we established conditional mouse lines for intestinal epithelial cell (IECs)-specific Xiap knock-out and XIAP knock-in, and employed a colitis-associated murine model for CRC. We found that XIAP promotes inflammatory signalling and exacerbates colitis-driven colorectal tumorigenesis by shaping a distinct tumor inflammatory microenvironment characterized by increased immune-cell infiltration, including neutrophils, and enhanced vascularisation. The pro-inflammatory role of XIAP was further validated in CRC patient-derived organoids and human CRC tumor specimens. Collectively, our findings identify XIAP as a potential biomarker of CRC-associated inflammation and a candidate marker for identifying patients at increased risk of disease recurrence. Moreover, these results provide a rationale for exploring XIAP-targeting strategies as a potential component of multimodal therapeutic approaches for CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Background Initial non-cancer diagnoses that plausibly explain cancer symptoms may be underexplored missed opportunities in cancer diagnosis. Aim To characterise "interim diagnoses" representing potential missed opportunities to diagnose cancer; namely, non-cancer conditions diagnosed before cancer that are associated both with cancer and better and/or worse cancer outcomes. Design and Setting Observational case-control and case-only analyses of registry-linked Clinical Practice Research Datalink data from English primary care. Methods Cancer cases (cancer registry diagnoses, 1/1/2012-31/12/2018) were matched to cancer-free controls on birth year, gender and general practice. Incident non-cancer diagnoses sharing cancer symptoms were sought in the year before the case's diagnosis. Conditional logistic regression characterised non-cancer diagnoses associated with cancer (Bonferroni-corrected p<0.05). Associations between non-cancer diagnoses and cancer outcomes were tested using logistic regression (stage, route to diagnosis) and parametric regression accelerated failure-time models (1-year survival). Results Analyses of 223,422 patients yielded evidence of 37 "interim diagnoses" across 7 cancer sites that were consistently associated with worse (n=18) or better (n=8) cancer outcomes, or a mixture of worse and better outcomes within or between cancer sites (n=11). For example, gastro-oesophageal reflux disease, gastritis, oesophagitis, or peptic ulcer were associated with worse outcomes in pancreatic, colorectal and ovarian cancers, with better outcomes in stomach cancer, and a mixture in oesophageal cancer. Conclusion We characterise 37 "interim" diagnoses as potential missed opportunities in cancer diagnosis. Safety-netting around these non-cancer diagnoses, focussing on management of clinical uncertainty and robust patient follow-up, may help avoid missed opportunities to diagnose cancer and improve outcomes.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Endoplasmic reticulum (ER) redox homeostasis is essential for protein folding and processing. Persistent oxidative stress perturbs ER proteostasis, leading to maladaptive ER stress responses; however, the molecular mechanism by which ER-associated oxidative stress culminates in immunogenic cell death remains unclear. We previously demonstrated that L-selenocystine (SeC) suppresses Nrf2-dependent antioxidant signaling in Nrf2-addicted colorectal cancer (CRC) cells. These findings implicated impaired antioxidant defense in SeC sensitivity but did not establish how persistent redox imbalance leads to organelle dysfunction and subsequent cell death. Here, we investigated whether SeC perturbs ER redox homeostasis, resulting in persistent ER oxidative stress and subsequent immunogenic cell death. SeC preferentially accumulated within the ER, inducing ER-associated oxidative stress accompanied by GSH depletion and ROS-mediated cytotoxicity in WiDr colorectal cancer cells. Selenium enrichment within ER-derived vesicles and localized ROS generation further supported direct ER redox perturbation by SeC. SeC-induced persistent ER-associated oxidative stress disrupted ER proteostasis, including proteasome inhibition, polyubiquitinated protein accumulation, and UPR/ERAD dysregulation. SeC treatment induced extensive ER swelling and cytoplasmic vacuolization in CRC cells. SeC also triggered ICD-associated danger signaling characterized by extracellular ATP release and HMGB1 secretion. Conditioned medium derived from SeC-treated WiDr CRC cells promoted dendritic cell maturation and polarized THP-1 macrophages toward a pro-inflammatory M1-like phenotype, and SeC-CM-matured dendritic cells further enhanced T cell activation. In contrast, normal colonic epithelial CCD841-CoN cells exhibited attenuated ER stress responses and markedly reduced cytotoxicity following SeC treatment, suggesting a greater adaptive proteostasis capacity in normal cells. Consistently, Hrd1 knockdown sensitized CCD841-CoN cells to SeC, supporting a protective role of ERAD-mediated proteostasis in normal cells. Collectively, our findings support persistent ER oxidative stress-driven proteostasis disruption as a key contributor to immunogenic cell death in colorectal cancer cells. These findings provide mechanistic insights into selenium-mediated redox regulation and support selenium-based chemo-immunotherapeutic strategies for colorectal cancer.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Simultaneous colorectal and liver resection for synchronous colorectal liver metastasis (CRLM) avoids a second operation but may increase morbidity. Prior studies comparing simultaneous and staged approaches have not accounted for heterogeneity across specific procedure combinations. This study evaluated Textbook Outcomes (TO) across liver-colorectal procedure combinations to guide surgical decision-making. A retrospective cohort study using the ACS-NSQIP database (2015-2019) classified adults undergoing hepatic resection for CRLM into liver resection alone or simultaneous liver-colorectal resection groups. TO was defined as the composite absence of 30-day mortality, major morbidity, unplanned readmission, reoperation, and length of stay exceeding the 75th percentile. Among 7,778 patients, 6,699 (86.1%) underwent liver resection alone, and 1,079 (13.9%) underwent combined resection. TO was achieved in 57.7% versus 29.0%, respectively (p < 0.001), despite equivalent 30-day mortality (0.9%). Combination-level analysis revealed marked heterogeneity: left hepatectomy with low anterior resection achieved the highest TO rate among major hepatectomy combinations (47.1%), while right hepatectomy with right hemicolectomy yielded only 16.3%. No patient achieved TO in combinations involving total abdominal colectomy/proctocolectomy (0/18). TO rates varied substantially across specific liver-colorectal procedure combinations, providing a reference for multidisciplinary assessment of perioperative risk when considering simultaneous versus staged resection.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal surgery is technically demanding, with outcomes dependent on surgeon skill alongside patient physiology and disease state. With the burden of colorectal disease expected to increase, the variability in surgeon performance will inevitably impact a growing number of patients. Robotic technologies offer potential solutions, but they remain fully teleoperated, with no currently deployed fully autonomous surgical systems. This review examines the current state, limitations, and translational prospects of autonomous colorectal surgery. We conducted a narrative review of English-language literature on surgical autonomy and elective colorectal surgery from inception to July 2026, searching PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science. Findings were synthesized thematically. Autonomy in colorectal surgery is limited to isolated tasks rather than integrated across whole procedures. Clinically deployed systems remain confined to assistive and task-level functions, requiring the surgeon to manually initiate every tissue-manipulating action. The Smart Tissue Autonomous Robot has demonstrated supervised, conditional autonomy for intestinal anastomosis in phantom and porcine models. These demonstrations required fluorescent markers or prepared operative fields, substantially increased operative time, and have not been extended to humans in any colorectal application. As current validation of such systems remains fragmented, we propose autonomy-specific reporting measures describing system performance, safety, procedural integration, and human-robot interaction. Autonomous colorectal surgery remains at an early stage, with Smart Tissue Autonomous Robot demonstrating supervised soft-tissue autonomy in controlled settings. Translation is limited by the difficulty of modeling deformable tissue and complex pelvic anatomy, as well as by the absence of validation standards. Progress will depend on incremental, supervised integration, autonomy-specific reporting, and continued human oversight.

Perfluorohexanesulfonic acid (PFHxS) is a persistent per- and polyfluoroalkyl substance (PFAS) widely detected in human biospecimens, yet its relationship with colorectal cancer (CRC) progression remains poorly defined. We integrated network toxicology, bulk transcriptomics, machine-learning-based prognostic modeling, single-cell and spatial transcriptomics, and functional experiments to characterize PFHxS-associated molecular features in CRC. A 14-gene gradient boosting machine signature stratified overall survival in TCGA and two external cohorts and remained independently prognostic after adjustment for clinical covariates. Single-cell analysis and SHAP-based model attribution prioritized DVL3 for experimental investigation. Chronic PFHxS exposure increased DVL3 abundance and malignant phenotypes in CRC models. DVL3 knockdown attenuated PFHxS-associated clonogenic and invasive phenotypes and reduced Wnt/β-catenin transcriptional activity and downstream target-gene expression, with key findings reproduced in CT26 cells. Collectively, these findings link PFHxS exposure to aggressive CRC phenotypes and support DVL3 as a functional contributor to Wnt/β-catenin transcriptional responses.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Although human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (ERBB2/HER2) is a validated therapeutic target, the significance of ERBB3 (HER3) alterations across solid tumours remains poorly defined. We characterised such alterations to clarify the genomic landscape relevant to HER3-directed strategies, distinguishing somatic events from germline polymorphisms. We analysed real-world data from 5416 patients with metastatic solid tumours who underwent next-generation sequencing. As tumour-only sequencing cannot separate germline from somatic variants, recurrent germline-pattern variants were reclassified using gnomAD and Korean population databases, and remaining somatic variants were annotated for oncogenicity using OncoKB (v7.3, Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center, New York, NY). Overall survival (OS) was analysed via Cox regression analysis stratified according to tumour type. ERBB3 alterations were initially identified in 12.9% of patients, dominated by mutations (12.3%) rather than amplifications (0.8%). However, the two most common variants, K498I and R1127H, proved to be common germline polymorphisms, and germline-pattern variants accounted for 63% of all mutation calls. After germline exclusion, the prevalence of somatic mutations was 4.5%, and oncogenic/likely-oncogenic mutations only 1.6%, matching a large pan-cancer series. Oncogenic mutations clustered in extracellular domains, were tumour-type-specific (V104M/L in colorectal and urothelial; G284R in gastric and biliary tract cancer), and persisted in nonhypermutated tumours. The ERBB3 mutation status was not prognostic (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 0.97, P = 0.52), whereas ERBB3 amplification was independently associated with a worse OS (HR 1.43, P = 0.024). Most apparent ERBB3 mutations in this East Asian tumour-only cohort were likely germline polymorphisms; true somatic oncogenic mutations were uncommon and tumour-type-specific, whereas amplification was rare but prognostically adverse. As HER3-directed antibody-drug conjugates depend on HER3 protein expression, the integration of such data with HER3 immunohistochemistry and outcomes is essential to define the target population.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Constitutional mismatch repair deficiency syndrome (CMMRD) syndrome, caused by inherited biallelic mismatch repair (MMR) gene loss, is characterized by early-onset cancers and neurofibromatosis Type 1 (NF1) features. Genetic heterogeneity of syndromes with replication repair deficiency (RRD) and non-RRD conditions (eg, Lynch syndrome (LS) and NF1, respectively) leads to diagnostic challenges. Seven diagnostic criteria (CMMRD1-CMMRD7) were established in 2022 incorporating germline results, ancillary tests, and clinical manifestation. This study reviews the use of these criteria in identifying CMMRD. Individuals suspected of CMMRD referred to the International Replication Repair Deficiency Consortium in Toronto, Canada, had clinical manifestation, family history, germline, MMR immunohistochemistry (IHC) of non-neoplastic (NN-IHC) and tumor tissue, and LOGIC obtained to assess the diagnostic criteria. A total of 580 individuals were identified, with 159 excluded because of insufficient information resulting in 421 individuals assessed using the diagnostic criteria. Of these, 358 (85%) were classified as CMMRD/suspected CMMRD (n = 270), LS/likely LS (n = 78), or other hereditary conditions (n = 10). Sixty-three individuals could not be classified because of the lack of or discordant results. Of the 270 patients with CMMRD syndrome, 241 met the published criteria and 29 were suspected of CMMRD on the basis of fulfilling criteria with a discordant functional result or suspicious genotype/phenotype. CMMRD1-CMMRD7 criteria were all identified, with 57% (n = 137) fulfilling CMMRD1 criteria. Early-onset gliomas and GI cancers occurred in LS, The 2022 CMMRD syndrome diagnostic criteria provided a useful framework for establishing CMMRD syndrome and distinguishing it from similar conditions. A clinically meaningful subset remained difficult to classify despite suspicion of CMMRD. Refinement of CMMRD syndrome diagnostic criteria may address atypical presentation and discordant functional results. Limitations include incomplete availability of germline/functional testing, discordant/inconclusive results, and inherent referral bias to a specialized RRD consortium.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Local therapy (LT) for metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) is recommended when eradicating all metastases is feasible. Although LT is widely used, its population-level impact remains unclear. This study aims to use real-world population-based data to assess LT utilization and survival trends in mCRC. Patients diagnosed with mCRC from 2010 to 2023 were included, using data from the Cancer Registry of Norway and the Norwegian Patient Registry. LT was defined as surgery, stereotactic radiotherapy (SRT), or ablation targeting liver, lung, or brain metastases. Outcomes were reported as median overall survival (OS) and 2-, 5-, and 10-year OS. The effect of the first versus last time period on survival was assessed using univariable and multivariable Cox regression. Among 64,112 CRC cases, 20,210 had mCRC. Of these, 21% received LT, 39% systemic therapy only, 12% other therapies, and 29% no therapy. Metastasectomy was the primary LT (87%), whereas SRT use was limited. LT use increased by 12% annually from 2010 to 2015 and then stabilized. The overall mCRC survival improved, with the 5-year OS increasing from 16% to 23% and the median OS from 15 to 18 months (adjusted hazard ratio, 0.92; 95% CI, 0.89 to 0.95). No significant survival improvement was observed between time periods in the LT or systemic therapy only subgroups. The 5-year OS for patients receiving LT for liver, lung, and brain metastases was 50%, 62%, and 5%, respectively. LT utilization increased, with outcomes comparable with more selected populations. Survival in treatment subgroups remained stable over time, but improved in the overall mCRC population, suggesting that the population-level gains may reflect changes in treatment allocation rather than improvements within modalities.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Patient navigation is an evidence-based approach for increasing colorectal cancer (CRC) screening. Research examining common navigator activities to support cancer screening emphasizes helping patients address barriers to screening. Understanding the techniques navigators employ to resolve specific barriers to CRC screening could more precisely define the mechanisms by which navigation works and inform the design and evaluation of future programs. The Colonoscopy Outreach for Rural Communities trial assessed a patient navigation program to increase colonoscopy completion. In this article, we explore how the Colonoscopy Outreach for Rural Communities study navigator was able to help patients resolve barriers to completing primary screening colonoscopy, and under what circumstances the navigator was not successful. We used qualitative thematic analysis supported by the Framework Method to analyze navigator notes and interview transcripts to understand navigator resolution techniques. We conducted a descriptive analysis of navigation data to assess the proportion of barriers that were resolved for each participant in the program. We identified eight navigation techniques for primary screening colonoscopy barrier resolution: educating about colonoscopies (colonoscopy education), providing information about the health care system (system education), facilitating patient conversations with health care teams or insurance (facilitation), bridging to the health care system to coordinate care on behalf of the patient (bridge), helping the patient with accountability (accountability), providing emotional support (support), brainstorming solutions with patients (brainstorming), and helping with interpretation and translation (interpretation). These techniques were particularly successful in resolving scheduling (88%), knowledge (98%), transportation (82%), and language (83%) barriers. Understanding eight distinct techniques a navigator uses to support primary screening colonoscopy completion for colorectal cancer screening advances our understanding of how navigators can help patients resolve barriers to colonoscopy completion, and in what settings the techniques may be most effective. They may also offer a framework for design of navigation programs delivered both within and outside of the clinic setting. ClinicalTrials.gov. Identifier: NCT05453630. Registered July 6, 2022.
