ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related morbidity and mortality worldwide, and the liver is its predominant site of metastatic spread; approximately half of patients with CRC develop colorectal liver metastases (CRLM). Management has shifted from largely palliative intent to a multidisciplinary strategy with curative potential. Complete resection offers a chance of cure, although long-term survival varies substantially with tumor biology, disease burden, and patient selection. This review summarizes advances in prognostic stratification, molecular profiling, and the evolving definition of resectability, together with surgical innovations including parenchymal-sparing and two-stage hepatectomy, portal vein embolization, associating liver partition and portal vein ligation for staged hepatectomy (ALPPS), liver venous deprivation, and minimally invasive approaches. We review conversion chemotherapy informed by the TRIBE, TRIBE2, CAIRO5, and PARADIGM trials, perioperative systemic therapy, and biomarker-directed agents for RAS wild-type, BRAF V600E-mutant, KRAS G12C-mutant, and HER2-amplified tumors, alongside immune checkpoint inhibition for microsatellite instability-high disease. Locoregional therapies, including thermal ablation, stereotactic radiotherapy, and selective internal radiation therapy, are discussed in light of the COLLISION and CLOCC trials. Finally, we consider emerging roles for circulating tumor DNA in minimal residual disease assessment and for liver transplantation in highly selected patients with unresectable disease (SECA, TransMet).

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Robot-assisted surgery has been applied to a range of pelvic urinary tract fistulas, but the literature is dispersed across urology, gynecology, colorectal surgery, and reconstructive practice. We examined how this literature developed, how its contributing communities interact, and whether its clinical themes converge. English-language articles and reviews indexed in the Science Citation Index Expanded within the Web of Science Core Collection from inception to 1 August 2026 were screened for clinical or technical relevance. The final corpus contained 104 publications, comprising 85 articles and 19 reviews, published between 2005 and 2026. Publication and disciplinary trends, geographic collaboration, historical foundations, reference-based networks, Author Keyword themes, thematic evolution, and journal citation pathways were analyzed. Output remained low and uneven, although higher annual counts became more frequent after 2021. Urology remained the principal disciplinary setting, with broader participation from gynecology, reproductive health, and surgery. Authors from 31 countries or regions contributed; the United States led in both publication output and citations, while international collaboration remained concentrated within a limited network. Historical and thematic analyses identified vesicovaginal fistula repair as the main intellectual and conceptual backbone; colovesical, ureteral, rectourinary, and congenital applications formed smaller, partly separate streams. The literature has acquired a recognizable cross-specialty structure, but its principal clinical strands have not yet converged into a comparable evidence base. Future studies should prioritize multicenter designs and consistent reporting of anatomy, prior treatment, reconstruction, and clinically relevant outcomes.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
This study aimed to assess the effectiveness of the Node Reporting and Data System version 1.0 (Node-RADS 1.0) for preoperative evaluation of lymph node metastasis (LNM) in colon cancer and to benchmark its diagnostic performance against conventional CT-based size criteria. This retrospective study enrolled patients who underwent radical resection for colon cancer at Shantou Central Hospital between January 2015 and January 2019. All patients received radical resection followed by histopathological evaluation of regional lymph nodes. Preoperative computed tomography (CT) images were independently reviewed by two experienced radiologists using the Node-RADS scoring system. Inter-observer agreement was assessed, and diagnostic performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. A total of 360 patients were included. Lymph node positivity was associated with several CT features, including nodal size, internal heterogeneity, necrosis, margin characteristics, fatty hilum status, and the Node-RADS score (all p < 0.05). The Node-RADS score demonstrated the highest diagnostic performance (area under the curve (AUC) = 0.835, 95% CI: 0.792-0.871) with an optimal cutoff of ≥3, good inter-observer reliability (intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) = 0.962), and higher discriminative ability than the conventional 10-mm size criterion (AUC 0.546; p < 0.05). In this large retrospective cohort, contrast-enhanced CT-based Node-RADS demonstrated reliable diagnostic performance for preoperative assessment of LNM in colon cancer and outperformed the conventional size-based criterion. The good inter-observer agreement further supports the reproducibility and clinical feasibility of Node-RADS in routine clinical practice. Question Can CT-based Node-RADS overcome the low sensitivity and underestimation of nodal metastasis associated with the conventional 10-mm short-axis criterion in preoperative colon cancer staging? Findings In 360 patients, Node-RADS at ≥3 achieved an AUC of 0.835, 96.6% sensitivity, and good interobserver agreement, outperforming the 10-mm criterion with fewer missed metastases. Critical relevance statement In 360 patients, Node-RADS at ≥3 achieved an AUC of 0.835, 96.6% sensitivity, and good interobserver agreement, outperforming the 10-mm criterion with fewer missed metastases.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Cytomegalovirus (CMV) is a widely spread β-herpesvirus that can establish life-long latency in the human host and remains asymptomatic in healthy immunocompetent hosts. In immunocompromised populations, such as transplant recipients, HIV/AIDS patients, and cancer patients, CMV presents an opportunity to reactivate and influence disease progression. There is a growing, but still contested, body of evidence suggesting that while CMV is not a classical oncogenic virus, it may act as an oncomodulatory virus, exerting an indirect impact on tumor biology. CMV DNA, RNA, or proteins have been detected in tumors such as glioblastoma, breast, colorectal, and pancreatic cancers in several studies, although other studies using comparable or more sensitive assays have failed to detect the virus in the same tumor types, so this association should not be regarded as established. In addition, CMV presence in tumor tissues is associated with immune suppression, therapy resistance, angiogenesis, and inflammation-all indicators of hallmark cancer progression. Of particular interest related to CMV in the context of cancer is its potential relationship with cancer stem cells (CSCs), a rare cell subpopulation of tumor cells, although a potent subpopulation for self-renewal, metastasis, and resistance to conventional cancer therapies. CMV has been shown to modulate numerous signaling pathways (Wnt/β-catenin, PI3K/Akt, Notch, and This review summarizes emerging connections between CMV infection and CSC biology, highlighting the ability of the virus to alter tumor behavior through effects on pluripotent transcription factors (i.e., Oct4, Sox2, Nanog), modulation of cytokine networks (i.e., IL-10, TGF-β), and inducing immune escape mechanisms. As we develop a better understanding of the CMV-CSC connection, this may inform new therapeutic strategies that utilize antiviral approaches to work alongside contemporary CSC-targeted therapies, providing relief in instances of drug resistance, relapse, and poor prognosis in CMV-positive tumors. We also critically appraise the strength and consistency of the underlying evidence, propose reasons for conflicting findings, and put forward a context-dependent, bidirectional model of CMV-CSC interaction together with testable predictions.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a malignant tumor that develops in the colon or rectum, usually originating from abnormal growth of cells in the intestinal lining. Pinoresinol diglucoside (PDG) is a lignan compound, which exhibits various pharmacological activities, such as anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, antihypertensive, and anticancer. The aim of the current study was to explore the anticancer effect of PDG against 1,2-dimethylhydrazine (DMH)-induced CRC. Subcutaneous administration of DMH (20 mg/kg) was used for the induction of CRC in the rats, and the rats were received the oral administration of PDG (2.5, 5, and 10 mg/kg) for 15 weeks. The body weight, colon weight, colon length, cancer marker, phase I, II, antioxidant, cytokines, and inflammatory parameters were estimated. The messenger ribonucleic acid expression and histopathology study were also performed. The gut microbiota was estimated in the facal of all group rats. PDG treatment significantly (P < 0.001) improved the body weight, colon length, and colon weight, along with a reduction in the level of cancer markers such as tissue polypeptide-specific antigen, tumor-associated glycoprotein 72, carcinoembryonic antigen, and carbohydrate antigen 19.9. PDG treatment also altered the level of alkaline phosphatase, lactate dehydrogenase, phase I and II enzymes, antioxidant parameters, cytokines, and inflammatory parameters, respectively. PDG treatment significantly (P < 0.001) altered the F/B ratio and relative abundance of Bacteroidetes, Firmicutes, Actinobacteriota, and Desulfobacterota and altered the histopathological alteration. PDG exhibited a chemoprotective effect against DMH-induced CRC via regulation of the nuclear factor-kappa B/inducible nitric oxide synthase/cyclooxygenase-2 signaling and gut dysbiosis.

Between 2000-2005 and 2018-2023, no primary-site surgery increased from 10.2% to 30.1% in rectal cancer and from 2.9% to 6.5% in colon cancer. Rectal cancer odds increased by 5.4% per year before 2018 and 17.5% per year after 2018. The colon trend was approximately linear, with a 4.2% annual increase in odds. A stage-adjusted analysis in the 2004-2015 stage I-III subset supported an earlier increase but could not evaluate the post-2018 acceleration.DiscussionRegistry-coded no primary-site surgery increased in both cancers, with a greater and accelerating rise in rectal cancer. These descriptive findings extend contemporary observations and support site-specific interpretation. The unadjusted post-2018 pattern cannot establish changes independent of stage or identify planned watch-and-wait, treatment refusal, or absence of cancer-directed therapy.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The clinical application of camptothecin (CPT) is limited by poor solubility and severe toxicity. This study compares the therapeutic performance of a cucurbit[7]uril-based CPT complex (CB[7]-CPT) with free CPT and β-cyclodextrin-CPT (β-CD-CPT) in colorectal cancer models. In vitro, free CPT, β-CD-CPT, and CB[7]-CPT were tested on normal LO2 and cancerous HCT116 cells. CB[7] encapsulation reduced toxicity toward normal LO2 cells (IC50: 0.47 μM, ∼25-fold higher than the IC50 of free CPT) while improving potency against HCT116 cells (CB[7]-CPT IC50: 0.24 μM; free CPT IC50: 0.55 μM, ∼2-fold more potent than free CPT). The selectivity index improved from 0.034 (CPT) to 1.976 (CB[7]-CPT), indicating a wide safety margin. Apoptosis assays confirmed that CB[7]-CPT induced significantly greater apoptotic cell death at equivalent concentrations than either free CPT or β-CD-CPT. In HCT116 xenograft models, CB[7]-CPT achieved a tumor inhibition rate of 76%, markedly outperforming free CPT (46%) and β-CD-CPT (62%). This enhanced efficacy was accompanied by increased intratumoral apoptosis, reduced proliferation, and decreased microvessel density. Importantly, CB[7]-CPT markedly attenuated liver, kidney, and gastrointestinal toxicity typically associated with CPT exposure. Pharmacokinetically, CB[7]-CPT displayed a 1.94-fold higher AUC and a 1.59-fold prolonged elimination half-life relative to free CPT, reflecting extended circulation and improved systemic exposure. These findings collectively establish CB[7]-CPT as a highly effective and safer alternative not only to free CPT but also to conventional cyclodextrin-based formulations, demonstrating enhanced selectivity, robust pro-apoptotic activity, and a superior safety profile.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Glatiramer acetate (GA) is a heterogeneous mixture of peptides that we have previously explored as an intratumoral immunomodulator. However, its chemical complexity complicates the mechanistic interpretation and rational design. In this study, we evaluated a set of sequence-defined "glatiramoid" peptides engineered to preserve the amino acid composition while varying the primary sequence. Biophysical characterization by circular dichroism, fluorescence spectroscopy, and transmission electron microscopy revealed sequence-dependent differences in supramolecular organization without pronounced changes in the secondary structure. Treatment of murine bone marrow-derived dendritic cells with these peptides produced distinct innate cytokine and chemokine secretion profiles, suggesting that sequence order influences immune signaling outcomes in vitro. In the CT26 mouse model of colon carcinoma, intratumoral administration of selected glatiramoid peptides in combination with anti-PD-1 therapy produced tumor growth responses that were not statistically distinguishable from those of commercial GA formulations. Systemic cytokine levels measured at study termination were generally lower for the sequence-defined peptide relative to GA. Together, these findings indicate that sequence-defined glatiramoid peptides reproduce selected GA-like biophysical and immunomodulatory properties. Further studies are required to establish their mechanisms of action, intratumoral behavior, and therapeutic contribution to checkpoint blockade.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
In vivo pretargeting is an emergent approach to nuclear imaging and radiopharmaceutical therapy that leverages the exquisite selectivity and affinity of full-length immunoglobulins while skirting their pharmacokinetic and dosimetric limitations. One particularly promising approach to pretargeting is predicated on the inverse electron-demand Diels-Alder reaction between a trans-cyclooctene (TCO)-bearing antibody and a tetrazine (Tz)-based radioligand. This methodology has been validated with a wide variety of antibody-antigen systems paired with radionuclides for positron emission tomography (PET), single photon emission computed tomography (SPECT), and radioimmunotherapy. The halogen group of the periodic table offers an abundance of isotopes that emit β--particles (i.e. 131I), α-particles (i.e. 211At), and Auger electrons (i.e. 125I) for radiopharmaceutical therapy. Herein, we describe the synthesis and characterization of a pair of Tz radioligands containing 131I-labeled residualizing guanidinium prosthetic groups: iso-[131I]GMIB-PEG6-Tz and iso-[131I]GMIB-Tz. Subsequently, these two radioligands were used in conjunction with a TCO-bearing variant of the A33 antigen-targeting mAb huA33 (i.e. huA33-TCO) for in vivo pretargeting experiments in a murine model of colorectal carcinoma. The biodistribution and dosimetry data from these preclinical experiments suggested that the PEG6-containing radioligand offered a superior pharmacokinetic profile, and protocols were developed for the synthesis of iso-[211At]AGMB-PEG6-Tz. Finally, the in vivo behavior of iso-[211At]AGMB-PEG6-Tz was probed in both healthy mice and in a pretargeting system paired with huA33-TCO in a murine model of colorectal carcinoma.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) mediate host-microbiota interactions and are typically measured in feces as markers of gut microbial activity. However, whether fecal SCFAs adequately reflect disease-associated host-microbiota dysfunction remains unclear. We hypothesized that circulating SCFAs, which integrate microbial production, intestinal absorption, barrier function, and host metabolism, provide a more informative representation of gut-related diseases. Seven fecal and serum SCFAs were quantified by gas chromatography-mass spectrometry in 193 individuals, including patients with colorectal cancer (CRC, n = 30), celiac disease (CD, n = 35), obesity (OB, n = 33), and healthy controls (HCs, n = 95). We developed an interpretable machine-learning framework combining stacking ensembles, bootstrap validation, permutation testing, SHAP and LIME analyses. Cross-compartment predictive modeling was used to assess the reciprocal informativeness of fecal and circulating SCFAs. Circulating SCFAs exhibited markedly stronger disease-associated signatures than fecal SCFAs across all groups. Serum-based models achieved excellent classification performance (95% accuracy; multiclass ROC-AUC 1.00), whereas fecal SCFAs provided substantially lower predictive power (59% accuracy). Combining serum and fecal datasets yielded only marginal improvement (97.4% accuracy), indicating most diagnostic relevant information was already captured in circulation. Valeric, propionic, 2-methylbutyric, and isovaleric acids were consistently identified as the main contributors to disease discrimination. Cross-compartment modeling revealed weak predictive relationships between fecal and serum SCFAs, indicating these pools are largely non-redundant and reflect distinct biological processes. Circulating SCFAs outperform fecal SCFAs as biomarkers of gut-related diseases, capturing the integrated effects of microbial activity and host physiology. These findings support blood-based SCFA profiling as a promising approach for precision diagnostics in microbiota-associated disorders.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
This study aimed to investigate the dose-response relationships between exercise prescription parameters and a range of health outcomes in patients with colorectal cancer (CRC). The following PRISMA guidelines, a systematic search of five databases was conducted. The inclusion criteria were randomized controlled trials (RCTs) of exercise interventions lasting ≥ 4 weeks in patients with CRC. Robust Variance Estimation (RVE) was used to synthesize the overall effects of exercise interventions across six outcome domains, including cardiorespiratory fitness (CRF) and muscular fitness (MF). Univariable RVE regression models and MetaForest analyses were employed to examine the moderating effects of two groups of variables: exercise prescription moderators and patient background characteristics. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane tool, and the quality of evidence was evaluated using the GRADE approach. A total of 26 RCTs, involving 1731 CRC patients and 266 effect sizes, were included. CRF (ES = 0.35, p < 0.01) and MF (ES = 0.45, p < 0.01) showed statistically significant improvements. Regression analyses revealed threshold effects for both CRF and MF, with maximal improvements requiring sustained engagement in moderate-to-high intensity exercise. Subgroup analyses indicated that prehabilitation interventions were the most effective, while interventions during active treatment exhibited a decline-rebound trend over time. Based on these findings, high-frequency and moderate-to-high volume interventions with individualized load regulation are recommended during the pre-treatment phase. During active treatment, a more cautious approach is advised, involving reduced exercise volume during peak symptom periods and gradual progression during recovery.

Interleukin-37, a member of the interleukin-1 family, is increasingly recognized as a regulator of cancer biology and tumor immunity. Across cancer types, interleukin-37 expression exhibits divergent patterns and clinical associations. In non-small cell lung cancer, hepatocellular carcinoma, colorectal cancer, renal cell carcinoma, and acute myeloid leukemia, decreased interleukin-37 expression is more often associated with aggressive clinicopathologic features and poor outcomes. By contrast, in gastric cancer, epithelial ovarian cancer, melanoma, and several other malignancies, increased interleukin-37 expression has been linked to tumor progression and adverse prognosis. Mechanistically, interleukin-37 acts through intracellular and extracellular pathways, including Smad3-dependent nuclear translocation and signaling through the interleukin-18 receptor alpha/interleukin-1 receptor 8 complex, with downstream effects on signal transducer and activator of transcription 3, nuclear factor kappa B, transforming growth factor beta/Smad, and related networks. Depending on cancer type, immune context, isoform usage, and disease stage, interleukin-37 may inhibit proliferation, metabolic reprogramming, angiogenesis, invasion, and metastatic dissemination or promote immune suppression and premetastatic niche formation. Beyond its tumor-intrinsic effects, interleukin-37 reshapes the tumor microenvironment by modulating macrophages, dendritic cells, natural killer cells, myeloid-derived suppressor cells, and T-cell subsets. This narrative review summarizes current evidence on the dual roles of interleukin-37 in cancer, discusses major sources of inconsistency across studies, and highlights its potential relevance to prognostic stratification, biomarker development, and therapeutic targeting.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Background Caudal-type homeobox 2 (CDX2) is a nuclear transcription factor that maintains intestinal epithelial differentiation. Reduced CDX2 expression has been associated with adverse pathological features and inferior outcomes in colorectal cancer, but its clinicopathological value depends on the scoring method and tumor context. Methods This single-center observational study evaluated 50 histopathologically confirmed colorectal malignancies. CDX2 immunohistochemistry was scored semi-quantitatively by multiplying nuclear staining proportion (0-4) by staining intensity (0-3), yielding an immunoreactivity score (IRS) of 0-12. Low/reduced expression was defined as IRS ≤4 and high/preserved expression as IRS ≥5. The patient-level master chart was used to summarize IRS and its associations with stage and grade; the histology comparison retained the original aggregated subtype counts. Exact tests used evaluable cases; pooled stage/grade analyses were exploratory, and subtype analysis was limited to major adenocarcinomas. The primary analytical endpoint was the association between CDX2 expression and pathological stage. The original pathology records for six cases recorded as pTis with N1/N2 disease were rechecked, and a conservative sensitivity analysis excluding these records was performed. Results CDX2 was evaluable in 48 of 50 cases; 29/48 (60.4%) showed low expression and 19/48 (39.6%) showed high expression. Median IRS was 2 (range 0-12). Among 43 cases with complete stage information and evaluable CDX2, low expression increased from 44.4% in stage 0, 30.0% in stage I, and 40.0% in stage II to 83.3% in stage III and 100% in the single stage IV case (Fisher-Freeman-Halton p=0.023). Advanced stage was associated with higher odds of low CDX2 expression (odds ratio (OR) 8.89, 95% confidence interval (CI) 2.01-39.22; p=0.004), although the wide confidence interval indicates imprecision. All 19 high-grade tumors showed low CDX2, compared with 9/27 (33.3%) low-grade tumors and 1/2 (50.0%) intermediate-grade tumors (p<0.001). Low CDX2 was also more frequent in mucinous adenocarcinoma (8/10, 80.0%) and signet-ring cell carcinoma (5/5, 100%) than in conventional adenocarcinoma (10/22, 45.5%; p=0.026). Pathology records confirmed that six entries combined primary lesions documented as pTis with separately submitted regional lymph nodes containing metastatic tumor. In a conservative sensitivity analysis excluding these six records, the early-versus-advanced-stage association persisted (low CDX2: 10/13 (76.9%) versus 9/24 (37.5%); OR 5.56, 95% CI 1.20-25.71; two-sided Fisher's exact p=0.038), whereas the overall five-stage association is not statistically significant (exact p=0.182). Conclusion Reduced CDX2 expression tracked closely with advanced pathological stage, high tumor grade, and aggressive adenocarcinoma morphology. These findings support CDX2 as a practical adjunct marker of adverse tumor biology in colorectal malignancies. Because survival, recurrence, and molecular profiling were not evaluated, the present study supports clinicopathological prognostic association rather than independent survival prognostication. Because the cohort included different tumor classes and the detailed five-stage result was sensitive to the handling of six nonstandard pTis/node-positive records, the stage and grade findings should be considered exploratory.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Leucine-rich repeat-containing G protein-coupled receptor 5 (LGR5) is a marker of cancer stem-like cells frequently upregulated in colorectal cancer (CRC) with lower expression in normal tissues, making it a favorable target for antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs). ADCs combine antibody specificity with potent cytotoxic payloads to enhance efficacy while minimizing systemic toxicity. LGR5-targeting ADCs incorporating different payloads demonstrate strong initial tumor inhibition, yet tumors eventually recur due in part to LGR5 downregulation, necessitating more effective strategies to prevent relapse. We show treatment with chemotherapies or an LGR5-targeting ADC coupled to a topoisomerase 1 inhibitor payload (8E11-CPT2) reduces LGR5 levels and increases MET receptor expression and/or activation in CRC cells, supporting a therapeutic approach to target LGR5 and MET simultaneously. Accordingly, we engineered a MET-targeting ADC (ABT-700-SG3199) via site-specific conjugation of the anti-MET antibody telisotuzumab (ABT-700) with the DNA-crosslinking pyrrolobenzodiazepine (PBD) dimer SG3199. ABT-700-SG3199 exhibited superior potency and efficacy in CRC models compared to the clinical-stage MET-targeting ADCs ABBV-399 and ABBV-400, which use the same antibody backbone conjugated to different payloads. Treatment with ABT-700-SG3199 increased LGR5 expression, and the combination of ABT-700-SG3199 with 8E11-CPT2 enhanced CRC cell-killing efficacy, reinforcing the rationale for a dual-targeting approach. In patient-derived xenografts, combined administration of 8E11-CPT2 and ABT-700-SG3199 markedly delayed tumor relapse and prolonged survival compared with single-agent treatment. Taken together, these findings reveal a reciprocal regulation between MET and LGR5 in response to LGR5- or MET-targeting ADCs in CRC models and support a LGR5/MET dual-targeting therapeutic strategy to enhance efficacy and potentially overcome resistance and relapse.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
DNA replication licensing is tightly coordinated with cell-cycle progression to ensure genome stability. Here we demonstrate that CIZ1, a nuclear matrix scaffold protein in human cells, coordinates DNA replication licensing through direct interactions with the Origin Recognition Complex (ORC), CDC6, and Cyclins E/A-CDK2. The C-terminal zinc finger region of CIZ1 mediates binding to the cyclin-binding motifs of ORC1 and CDC6, and Cyclin-CDK-dependent phosphorylation regulates these interactions. Cell cycle analyses demonstrated a dynamic association of CIZ1 with ORC1 and CDC6. Functional studies showed that CIZ1 depletion impaired MCM loading, reduced DNA synthesis, delayed S-phase progression and inhibited cell proliferation. Cancer cells overexpressing CIZ1 exhibited an enhanced dependency on its expression, and CRISPR tiling screens identified the C-terminal regulatory region containing cyclin-binding motifs and CDK phosphorylation sites as essential for cell proliferation. Acute degradation of CIZ1 further revealed an unexpected role in maintaining CCCTC-binding factor (CTCF) occupancy at specific genomic loci and regulating transcriptional programs associated with cell adhesion and migration, indicating that CIZ1 links DNA replication with higher-order genome organization. Finally, depletion of CIZ1 significantly suppressed colorectal tumor growth in xenograft models. Together, these findings establish CIZ1 as a multifunctional scaffold that integrates DNA replication licensing, Cyclin- CDK signaling, and chromatin architecture.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Immune cells in the tumor microenvironment are organized, and in colorectal and pancreatic cancer their arrangement around the tumor epithelium carries prognostic information. Multiplexed tissue imaging records the position and phenotype of every cell in a section, and studies of such images now routinely report that two cell types are spatially associated. However, the summaries behind these reports answer different questions. A proximity statistic asks whether two cell types lie close together more often than expected by chance. A conditional network asks whether their local densities rise and fall together once the other cell types are held fixed. The two can disagree, because every cell type is abundant where tissue is cell-dense and because the images of one patient are repeated measurements of that patient. We asked how epithelial and immune cells are organized in two settings: colorectal cancer with a Crohn's-like reaction (CLR) or diffuse inflammatory infiltration (DII), in 140 CODEX images from 35 patients, and pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) against its precursor, intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasm (IPMN), in 207 multiplex immunofluorescence images from 141 patients. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Extracellular matrix (ECM) leads to worse outcomes in lymph node metastases (LNM) in colorectal cancer (CRC). However, the link between ECM-related genes (ECMRGs) and LNM in CRC is poorly understood. This study aims to create a prognostic model related to ECM and LNM for CRC patients, to optimize prognostic assessment for CRC patients. The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA)-CRC and GSE38832 datasets, together with 84 curated ECMRGs, served as the analytical basis. Candidate genes were screened by intersecting LNM-associated differentially expressed genes (DEGs) with key module genes identified through weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA). Prognostic genes were subsequently determined via Cox regression analyses to establish a risk model. An individualized nomogram was developed by incorporating the risk score with clinicopathological variables. Additional analyses included gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), immune microenvironment profiling, and reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) validation in clinical specimens. Six genes-NKAIN4, VAX2, CILP2, MMP17, GRP, and RGCC-were identified as independent prognostic factors from 28 ECM- and LNM-related candidates. The risk model showed reliable performance in predicting CRC patient survival. A nomogram integrating risk score, age, pathological N stage, and pathological M stage achieved satisfactory prognostic accuracy. ECM-receptor interaction and nitrogen metabolism pathways were significantly enriched across risk strata. Among 12 differentially infiltrated immune cell populations, GRP was negatively correlated with neutrophil abundance, while RGCC showed the strongest positive correlation with plasmacytoid dendritic cells. RT-qPCR confirmed significant upregulation of NKAIN4, CILP2, GRP, and RGCC in CRC-LNM versus CRC-non-lymph node metastasis (NLNM) specimens. Six prognostic genes (NKAIN4, VAX2, CILP2, MMP17, GRP and RGCC) related to ECM and LNM in CRC were identified, based on which a prognostic model with outstanding predictive ability was constructed, offering a fresh reference for prognostic risk assessment of CRC patients.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) is widely used for liver metastases from well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumors, which are typically hypervascular. In contrast, gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine carcinoma liver metastases (GEP-NECLM) may be less hypervascular, raising uncertainty regarding the role of embolization-based therapy in this population. Nevertheless, TACE has also demonstrated antitumor activity in relatively hypovascular liver metastases, such as colorectal liver metastases. In clinical practice, TACE may also be combined with hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy (HAIC) as part of a multimodal liver-directed strategy. We therefore hypothesized that TACE-based multimodal liver-directed therapy could provide intrahepatic antitumor activity in patients with unresectable GEP-NECLM and aimed to evaluate its efficacy, safety, and prognostic factors. Patients with unresectable GEP-NECLM who underwent TACE-based multimodal liver-directed therapy between February 2012 and June 2024 were retrospectively reviewed. Pathological diagnoses were reassessed according to the 2019 World Health Organization classification. The primary endpoint was overall survival (OS), defined as the time from the first TACE session to death from any cause. Secondary endpoints included progression-free survival (PFS), defined as the time from the first TACE session to progressive disease in any organ or all-cause mortality; hepatic progression-free survival (hPFS), defined as the time from the first TACE session to intrahepatic disease progression or all-cause mortality; objective response rate (ORR), disease control rate (DCR), and safety. A total of 34 patients were included; 24 (70.6%) received TACE in combination with HAIC, and 29 (85.3%) had received at least one line of prior systemic therapy. The ORR and DCR were 41.2% and 76.5%, respectively. After a median follow-up of 45.1 months, the median PFS was 4.4 months, the median hPFS was 5.5 months and the median OS was 10.8 months. Colorectal primary site was independently associated with shorter PFS, with a hazard ratio (HR) of 3.189 (P=0.01). Ki-67 proliferation index (Ki-67) ≥55% (HR =6.172; P=0.006) was independently associated with worse OS. A total of 34 patients underwent 60 interventional treatment sessions. The treatment showed an acceptable safety profile, with no 30-day mortality or hepatic decompensation. Post-embolization syndrome was the most common treatment-emergent adverse event, occurring in 32 of 60 sessions (53.3%). All adverse events were manageable with symptomatic treatment. TACE-based multimodal liver-directed therapy was associated with measurable intrahepatic antitumor activity and an acceptable safety profile in patients with unresectable GEP-NECLM. Colorectal primary site was independently associated with shorter PFS, whereas a Ki-67 ≥55% was independently associated with worse OS. These findings require further validation in larger prospective studies.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
This review compares perioperative and selected postoperative outcomes between robotic-assisted surgery and conventional laparoscopy in females undergoing surgical treatment for colorectal or rectosigmoid endometriosis. This systematic review and meta-analysis followed the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, Scopus, Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature (CINAHL), and African Journals Online (AJOL) were searched from January 2020 to August 2026 for comparative observational studies evaluating robotic-assisted versus conventional laparoscopic surgery specifically for colorectal or rectosigmoid endometriosis. Manual bibliographic searches of the reference lists of relevant articles were also conducted to identify additional eligible studies. Studies involving general, superficial, ovarian, or deep endometriosis without separately identifiable colorectal disease were excluded. Study selection, data extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment were performed independently by two reviewers, with disagreements resolved by discussion. Risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS), and random-effects meta-analysis was undertaken only for outcomes with sufficiently comparable and non-duplicated data. Eight comparative observational reports met the eligibility criteria. Across studies reporting operative duration, robotic-assisted surgery was generally associated with longer operative time than conventional laparoscopy, although the magnitude and statistical significance of this difference varied between cohorts. Estimated blood loss, overall postoperative complications, conversion to open surgery, and most other perioperative outcomes were broadly comparable between approaches. Length of hospital stay showed inconsistent findings across studies, while selected reports suggested possible differences in voiding dysfunction, reoperation, recurrence, postoperative opioid use, and other longer-term outcomes. Considerable clinical and methodological heterogeneity was present because of differences in colorectal lesion complexity, extent of bowel surgery, associated pelvic procedures, institutional experience, follow-up duration, and outcome definitions. Potential overlap between several reports from the same specialist centre was addressed at the outcome level to avoid duplicate contribution of participants to pooled estimates. Overall, robotic-assisted surgery appears to be a feasible alternative to conventional laparoscopy for colorectal endometriosis, but current evidence does not demonstrate a consistent perioperative superiority of either approach. Because all available evidence is observational and susceptible to selection bias, residual confounding, temporal effects, and cohort overlap, causal conclusions cannot be drawn. Further prospective, multicentre, independently recruited comparative studies with standardized perioperative and long-term outcome reporting are required.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Nephrogenic adenoma (NA) of the bladder, also known as We report a case of a 76-year-old man with a history of colon cancer and benign prostatic hyperplasia who presented with recurrent urinary frequency, urgency, dysuria, and gross hematuria. His symptoms worsened despite conservative treatment. Imaging revealed bladder wall thickening, and cystoscopy showed erythematous, plaque-like lesions. Transurethral resection of the bladder lesion was performed. Histopathology confirmed NA with chronic granulomatous inflammation, and immunohistochemistry was positive for PAX8, CK7, and GATA3, supporting the diagnosis. Notably, the patient's computed tomography urogram (CTU) also suggested thickening of the left renal pelvis and ureter, raising the possibility of concomitant upper tract NA; however, these findings were radiologically suspected only, because the recommended further evaluation and resection of the upper tract lesions were declined, so upper tract urothelial carcinoma and inflammatory lesions remained possible alternatives. After 3 years of follow-up, his urinary frequency and urgency had not improved, and visible blood in the urine continued to be reported, although a causal relationship between the untreated upper tract lesions and these persistent lower urinary tract symptoms could not be established. This case underscores the diagnostic challenges of NA, particularly its mimicry of urothelial carcinoma, and highlights the pivotal role of thorough histopathological and immunohistochemical evaluation. The persistence of symptoms after resection of only the bladder lesion, along with radiological evidence of possible upper tract involvement, suggests that when NA is suspected, complete evaluation of the entire urinary tract is necessary, and that suspected upper urinary tract lesions should be carefully evaluated and, whenever feasible, confirmed histologically; however, the present case does not establish that these lesions caused the symptoms or that their resection would have relieved them. Clinicians should maintain a high index of suspicion for NA to ensure accurate diagnosis, appropriate treatment, and avoidance of unnecessary interventions. Long-term follow up is warranted given the potential for recurrence.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
To date, no randomized controlled trial has compared different dose-schedule patterns of raltitrexed combined with irinotecan for the second-line treatment of metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC). This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of raltitrexed combined with irinotecan administered by different dose-schedule patterns as a second-line treatment for mCRC. This was an exploratory, observational post hoc analysis of data from the SALLY study, a prospective, multicenter, noninterventional, real-world trial conducted in China. The core eligibility criteria of the SALLY study were mCRC that had failed to respond to first-line treatments comprising 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) + platinum-based chemotherapy. The regimen was administered every 2 or 3 weeks at the corresponding dose. The treatment frequency was determined by the attending physician. Among the 1,066 enrolled patients in the SALLY study, 618 (58.0%) received treatment every 3 weeks and 441 (41.3%) received treatment every 2 weeks in the full analysis set (FAS). There were no statistically significant differences in progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), objective response rate (ORR), or disease control rate (DCR) between the two groups in the FAS or in the per-protocol set (PPS). In the every-2-week group, 75.1% of patients experienced treatment-related adverse effects (AEs), compared with 77.5% of patients in the every-3-week group (P=0.38). The incidences of grade 3 or 4 toxicities were 10.9% (48/441) and 14.4% (89/619), respectively (P=0.11). In the second-line treatment of mCRC, the efficacy of irinotecan plus raltitrexed administered every 2 weeks with its corresponding dose did not differ significantly from that administered every 3 weeks.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Complete surgical resection remains the mainstay of cure in colorectal cancer (CRC), but anastomotic leak and postoperative recurrence compromise outcomes. The gut microbiota has been implicated in both. This review aims to synthesize evidence on the gut microbiota across the CRC surgical continuum, distinguish established mechanisms from extrapolated and hypothetical links, and identify stage-specific research priorities. We searched PubMed for English-language studies published from 2006 to 2026, combining terms for gut microbiota with CRC, checkpoint immunotherapy, anastomotic leak, and recurrence. Priority went to landmark original studies and to mechanistic or clinical work bearing directly on the surgical continuum; selection was purposive, without formal systematic-review criteria. The 46 cited studies comprise 22 preclinical mechanistic studies, 8 clinical cohort or observational studies, 7 clinical trials, 3 systematic reviews or meta-analyses, 4 reviews, and 2 commentaries. We trace the microbiota across four stages: tumor initiation and immune evasion, checkpoint immunotherapy, perioperative anastomotic healing, and postoperative recurrence and metastasis. A small set of overlapping taxa, Fusobacterium nucleatum being chief among them, recurs across these stages. Microbial activation of matrix metalloproteinase-9 (MMP-9) degrades the collagen of a healing anastomosis; whether a comparable breach of the mucosal barrier releases residual tumor cells is not known. We therefore grade this axis explicitly, and apply the grading in text, tables, and figures: established at the healing end, extrapolated from non-CRCs at the immunotherapy end, hypothetical at the seeding end. Read this way, a fragmented literature becomes a stage-specific research agenda: candidate preoperative signatures and phase-matched strategies are testable propositions, not validated biomarkers or tested interventions. We also address a gap this literature shares: the decades of prediagnosis exposure that shape tumor biology before the continuum begins. Most of this evidence is preclinical or borrowed from other cancers. Testing it will require CRC-specific trials, prospective prediagnosis cohorts, and strain-level, multi-omic analysis. The gut microbiota may act at several points along the CRC surgical continuum; whether MMP-9 is a single continuous driver across it remains to be tested.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) prognosis and treatment selection are increasingly informed by established molecular biomarkers, circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA), immune contexture, and multidimensional prediction models. However, these approaches mainly define tumor identity, treatment eligibility, residual disease burden, or observable tumor states and may incompletely explain how adaptive transcriptional states arise under oncogenic, stromal, immune, metastatic, or therapeutic pressure. This review evaluates Mediator complex-related transcriptional programs as a candidate regulatory layer that may complement existing CRC biomarker frameworks. English-language literature was reviewed using PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, and Scopus, with Google Scholar used for citation tracking. The initial search was performed on June 7, 2026, and a focused supplementary update was performed on August 17, 2026. Recent CRC biomarker studies, Mediator-related transcriptional regulation, functional heterogeneity, therapy adaptation, and germline variation in Mediator-related genes were emphasized, while earlier landmark mechanistic studies and guidelines were retained when necessary. Established clinicopathological and molecular biomarkers primarily define baseline risk, molecular identity, and treatment eligibility. Dynamic and multidimensional approaches add residual-disease, immune, stromal, spatial, and transcriptomic state information. Mediator-related programs may provide a mechanistic interpretation layer by linking transcription-factor and enhancer inputs, chromatin context, and RNA polymerase II-dependent output. Cyclin-dependent kinase 8 (CDK8)-Wnt/β-catenin represents a mechanistically strong CRC axis; Mediator subunit 12 (MED12)-linked transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β)/epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) programs are strongly context dependent; emerging cyclin-dependent kinase 19 (CDK19) evidence links metabolic remodeling with immune-evasive states; and Mediator subunits 19 and 28 remain lower-maturity candidates. Current evidence does not establish germline MED12/CDK8 variants as CRC prognostic or predictive biomarkers. CRC biomarker development should integrate rather than replace complementary information layers. Mediator-related programs are not mature stand-alone clinical biomarkers but may help interpret adaptive tumor states. Prospective clinically annotated cohorts, functional perturbation, single-cell and spatial profiling, and demonstration of incremental value beyond established biomarkers are required before clinical implementation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The Angiopoietin-Tie2 system is crucial in tumor angiogenesis for colorectal cancer (CRC), while investigations into integrating angiopoietin-Tie2 into the booming immunotherapy are underway. Here, we investigated the expression patterns and prognostic value of the Angiopoietin-Tie2 system in CRC. The expression patterns of angiopoietin-2 (ANGPT2) and angiopoietin-1 (ANGPT1), two major ligands of the angiopoietin-Tie2 system, as well as their correlation with clinical characteristics and prognosis were analyzed in The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA), and the related functions based on protein-protein interaction (PPI) networks in CRC were explored. The impact of ANGPT2 on tumor angiogenesis and immunity was validated ANGPT2 expression is upregulated in CRC, while ANGPT1 shows an opposite trend, but neither affects clinical characteristics. ANGPT2 and ANGPT1 are mainly involved in regulation of vasculature and cell chemotaxis migration. Knockdown of ANGPT2 reduced angiogenesis ANGPT2, rather than ANGPT1, likely plays a significant role in vascular regulation and immune landscape in CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Over 17% of gastrointestinal (GI) malignancies involve deficient DNA damage repair (DDR) mechanisms that have poor outcomes on standard chemotherapy but are sensitive to targeted therapies like immune checkpoint inhibitors and poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitors. Lurbinectedin is an alkylating agent that demonstrated a 35.2% overall response rate (ORR) as second-line therapy in small-cell lung cancer patients who progressed on platinum-based chemotherapies. The drug inhibits DDR, promoting apoptosis in tumor cells through double-stranded DNA breaks (DSBs). Since repair-deficient tumors cannot efficiently and adequately fix these DSBs, DNA damage accumulates and results in enhanced tumor killing. Therefore, lurbinectedin's mechanism makes it suitable for use in cancers with DDR mutations. Our study evaluated the efficacy of lurbinectedin monotherapy in patients with advanced GI malignancies who harbored DDR mutations. This was a prospective open-label, single-arm phase II study at a single institution. Participants were age ≥18 years, had Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status score ≤1, and locally advanced unresectable or metastatic GI cancer with ≥1 deleterious DDR mutation. Intravenous lurbinectedin was administered at 3.2 mg/m Eight participants (7 pancreatic cancer, 1 rectal cancer) with at least two prior therapy lines were enrolled and had DDR mutations in ATM (25.0%), ARID1A (62.5%), BRCA1 (25.0%), CHEK2 (12.5%), and FANC (12.5%). Median age was 63.5 years, 62.5% were female, and 87.5% were white. The ORR at 12 weeks was 0%. Median (95% confidence interval) PFS and OS were 1.2 (0.7-2.8) and 2.4 (1.2-4.1) months, respectively. The most common related adverse events (AEs) were grade 1 and 2 anorexia (50.0%) and constipation (25.0%); and grade 2 nausea (37.5%), anemia (25.0%), and fatigue (25.0%). Two patients (25.0%) experienced grade 3 and 4 neutropenia (1 each). In this trial of individuals with advanced GI malignancies with known DDR mutations, there was no clinical benefit of lurbinectedin, as all experienced progressive disease while on the agent (NCT05229588). Interpretation of the study is limited by the small sample size, only two types of GI cancers represented, early termination, and that most participants (62.5%) only completed one dose of the drug.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Robotic surgery has rapidly gained acceptance in rectal cancer owing to improved visualization and precision. This study compared perioperative and short-term oncologic outcomes of laparoscopic versus robotic rectal resections at a single tertiary oncology centre. All patients undergoing curative rectal cancer resection between 2016 and 2022 (laparoscopic) and 2022-2025 (robotic) were retrospectively reviewed. Propensity score matching (1:1) was performed based on age, neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (NACRT), pathological stage, tumour grade, circumferential resection margin (CRM) and preoperative CEA, yielding 35 matched cases per group. Balance between groups before and after matching was assessed using standardized mean differences (SMD), with an SMD < 0.1 considered indicative of adequate covariate balance. Perioperative parameters, complications, and disease-free survival (DFS) were compared. Kaplan-Meier analysis was used; projected 36-month DFS was reported where robotic follow-up was < 36 months. Seventy matched patients were analysed. Baseline characteristics, including CRM status and lymph node harvest, were comparable. Estimated blood loss was significantly lower in the robotic group (82.6 ± 22.3 ml vs. 129.4 ± 48.6 ml; Robotic rectal resection offers reduced intraoperative blood loss with comparable postoperative morbidity and short-term oncologic outcomes to laparoscopy. Longer follow-up is needed to validate survival outcomes.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Proficient mismatch repair/microsatellite stable (pMMR/MSS) colorectal cancer (CRC) constitutes the predominant molecular subgroup of CRC and usually shows limited benefit from immune checkpoint blockade. This study aimed to characterize immunogenic cell death (ICD)-associated transcriptomic patterns and develop an ICD-related prognostic model for pMMR/MSS CRC. Public gene-expression profiles and clinical annotations were retrieved from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO). The GSE39582-pMMR cohort was used for subtype identification and model development (n=459), and eligible pMMR/MSS cases from GSE143985 and GSE92921 were combined for external validation (n=132). Thirty-four ICD-related genes were used for consensus clustering. Differential expression analysis, functional enrichment analysis, Estimation of Stromal and Immune cells in Malignant Tumor tissues using Expression data (ESTIMATE), single-sample gene set enrichment analysis, immune checkpoint and human leukocyte antigen (HLA) assessment, Tumor Immune Dysfunction and Exclusion (TIDE) prediction, Kaplan-Meier analysis, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) Cox regression, time-dependent receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, and Cox proportional hazards models were applied. Consensus clustering divided the GSE39582-pMMR cohort into ICD-high (n=155) and ICD-low (n=304) subtypes. The ICD-high subtype showed higher immune and stromal scores, lower tumor purity, broader immune-cell infiltration, and increased expression of checkpoint and HLA genes, although overall survival did not differ significantly between subtypes. Subtype-related genes were enriched in immune response, leukocyte migration, chemokine and complement activity, adhesion, and extracellular matrix pathways. A seven-gene model consisting of ICD-associated transcriptional patterns identified immune-distinct subtypes in pMMR/MSS CRC and yielded a prognostic signature associated with survival and predicted immunotherapy response. The ICD-high subtype showed an immune-infiltrated but immunosuppression-associated phenotype, supporting further investigation of ICD-related models for risk stratification and treatment-response estimation in pMMR/MSS CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Trastuzumab rezetecan (SHR-A1811) is a novel human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-directed antibody-drug conjugate (ADC). Its activity in HER2-positive advanced colorectal cancer (CRC) has been suggested by a phase I cohort (n=37; objective response rate 40.5%), but real-world experience is lacking. We describe two patients with advanced CRC whose tumors were reported as HER2-positive by immunohistochemistry (IHC) score 2+ but were not confirmed by in situ hybridization (ISH)/fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) before treatment. Case 1 was a 53-year-old man with RAS/BRAF wild-type sigmoid and left colon adenocarcinoma with liver and peritoneal metastases who had received three prior lines of therapy (>15 cycles of cumulative irinotecan exposure and prior anti-EGFR therapy). He received three cycles of SHR-A1811 200 mg plus bevacizumab (starting June 5, 2026) and developed progressive disease-an enlarging left iliopsoas lesion with worsening abdominal pain, and a rise in carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) from 157.0 to 253.0 ng/mL. Biopsy of the progressing left psoas lesion was HER2-negative (IHC 0). Case 2 was an 80-year-old man with KRAS G12S-mutant anal mucinous adenocarcinoma, bilateral lung metastases, and baseline interstitial lung changes. He received three cycles of SHR-A1811 200 mg plus bevacizumab, after which bevacizumab was discontinued for bleeding and replaced by tislelizumab for the fourth cycle; FISH was negative (HER2-low). The lung lesions remained stable without worsening of the interstitial lung changes, although CA72-4 rose from 16.27 to 36.38 U/mL. Neither patient experienced grade ≥3 adverse events attributable to SHR-A1811. Neither patient achieved an objective response [one progressive disease, one stable disease (SD)]. Confirmatory testing showed the progressing lesion in Case 1 to be HER2-negative (IHC 0) and Case 2 to be FISH-negative (HER2-low). These observations illustrate that an IHC 2+ result alone does not establish HER2 positivity and may not predict benefit from HER2-directed ADC therapy, supporting confirmatory ISH/FISH testing before treatment selection.

意义与启示：该模型整合连续LNR与常规病理特征，对III期肠癌术后复发有中等区分度，但LNR增量价值有限；提示肝转移风险分层需结合更多分子标志物。

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Postoperative recurrence remains a major determinant of long-term outcomes in stage III colorectal cancer (CRC). The extent to which the lymph node ratio (LNR), when combined with routinely reported pathologic features, improves individualized recurrence-risk estimation remains uncertain. We aimed to develop and temporally validate a pathology-based recurrence model incorporating LNR and routinely available clinicopathologic features in stage III CRC. We retrospectively analyzed 400 patients with pathologic stage III CRC who underwent curative-intent resection at a single institution. Patients treated from January 2020 to August 2023 formed the training cohort (n=300), and those treated from September 2023 to March 2024 formed a temporally separated validation cohort (n=100). Recurrence-free survival (RFS) was the primary endpoint. Missing covariate data were handled using 30 multiple imputations. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO)-Cox selection was repeated in each imputed training dataset, and variables selected in at least 24 of 30 datasets were entered into pooled multivariable Cox models. LNR was modeled continuously in the primary analysis. Model performance was assessed using Harrell's C-index, time-dependent receiver operating characteristic curves, calibration, decision curve analysis, risk stratification, and incremental comparisons beyond tumor (T)/node (N) stage. Eight variables met the prespecified stability-selection threshold, and a parsimonious five-variable model retained tumor size, perineural invasion, continuous LNR, tumor budding, and tumor deposits. Each 0.1 increase in LNR was associated with a higher recurrence risk [hazard ratio (HR) 1.20, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.09-1.32]. The model achieved C-indices of 0.750 (95% CI: 0.705-0.793) in training and 0.746 (95% CI: 0.637-0.848) in temporal validation. Time-dependent areas under the curve (AUCs) were 0.789, 0.778, and 0.808 at 1, 2, and 3 years in training and 0.818 and 0.776 at 1 and 2 years in validation. Calibration was acceptable, although estimates in the validation cohort were imprecise. Adding LNR to a model containing T/N stage and other pathologic factors resulted in only modest increases in discrimination in both cohorts. A pathology-based prognostic model incorporating continuous LNR with routinely available pathologic features showed moderate discrimination for postoperative recurrence in stage III CRC. The model may complement TNM staging for risk stratification, but the incremental discriminative contribution of LNR beyond T/N stage and other pathologic factors was modest. Independent multicenter validation with longer follow-up is required before clinical implementation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Surgical benchmarking provides a reproducible framework for evaluating adherence to quality standards in real-world oncologic settings. We report a 14-year structured benchmarking analysis of surgical quality indicators and Kaplan-Meier (KM) survival outcomes following curative-intent colorectal cancer (CRC) resection at a low-volume tertiary referral center in Mexico. Retrospective, single-center, STROBE-compliant cohort study (January 2010-December 2024). Co-primary outcomes: margin-negative (R0) resection rate and adequate lymph node harvest (≥ 12 nodes). Secondary outcomes: postoperative morbidity (Clavien-Dindo), perioperative 30-day mortality, composite textbook outcome, KM overall survival (OS), and KM disease-free survival (DFS). KM survival was estimated using an interval-censoring approximation from cross-sectional status data. Exact 95% Clopper-Pearson confidence intervals (CI) were reported for all proportions. Analytic cohort: Structured institutional benchmarking including formal KM survival analysis is feasible in LMIC tertiary settings with historical registry data constraints. The 12.5% perioperative mortality is contextualized by 27.1% emergency operations and 75.0% ASA ≥ III - the primary quality improvement target. KM survival outcomes are consistent with an advanced-stage mixed-site referral cohort. Transparent, risk-contextualized benchmarking generates the evidence base most urgently needed in LMIC surgical oncology programs. The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s13193-026-02585-9.

Anastomotic leakage (AL) remains a major complication following sphincter-preserving rectal cancer surgery. This study evaluates the association between intraoperative indocyanine green (ICG) fluorescence angiography and AL reduction. A retrospective propensity score-matched cohort study including 318 consecutive patients undergoing minimally invasive anterior resection (AR), low anterior resection (LAR), or ultra-low anterior resection (ULAR). AL was defined according to ISREC criteria and confirmed clinically and/or radiologically. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Diet is an important modifiable determinant of cancer risk, but its effects are complex, site-specific, and increasingly shaped by rapid changes in global food systems. This narrative review summarizes current evidence linking major food groups with cancer risk and examines emerging dietary exposures to be considered in future research. Whole grains and dietary fiber show the most consistent protective associations, particularly for colorectal cancer, while fruits and vegetables appear to confer more modest and site-specific benefits. Dairy products show heterogeneous associations across cancer sites, whereas processed meat is consistently associated with increased colorectal cancer risk. Growing consumption of ultra-processed foods (UPFs) has introduced additional concerns related to excess energy intake, adiposity, altered food matrices, sodium, additives, processing contaminants, and food-contact chemicals. Although prospective studies generally associate higher UPF consumption with increased overall and selected site-specific cancer risks, some limitations related to relative novelty of this field of research still constrain causal interpretation. Emerging products may reduce exposure to compounds associated with cancer risk (i.e., heme iron, nitrites, and meat-derived carcinogens) as well as increase consumption of health-promoting dietary components (i.e., fiber), but their cancer-related effects depend strongly on formulation, processing, sodium content, additives, and preparation methods. Future nutritional oncology should therefore move beyond broad food categories and processing classifications toward detailed assessment of food formulation, substitution patterns, additives, and food-system dynamics to identify modifiable exposures relevant to cancer prevention.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Cells coordinate through coupled dynamics, yet whether observed correlations reflect genuine coupling is rarely tested. Signal Associa is an open-source framework uniting six coupling methods with automated stationarization and surrogate testing. Benchmarking against six ground truth systems reveals a trichotomy of coupling regimes, each with a different best method: correlation for coupling carried by shared trends and cycles, Granger causality for linear stochastic coupling, and convergent cross-mapping for nonlinear coupling; agreement across methods identifies the regime from data. In 13 movies of natural killer (NK) cells across three colorectal tumor microenvironments, NK cells formed field-spanning coupling networks at a conserved rate; at matched exposure to tumor signal, NK cells around hot tumors were more globally integrated, and hot tumors with a more integrated NK network tended to attract more NK cells. In focal adhesions, stiffness strengthened vinculin-FAK coupling, most at protruding edges. Surrogates cut lagged-correlation false positives from 23-92% to about 5%.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Same-day discharge after minimally invasive colorectal surgery is increasingly implemented, yet little is known about patient perspectives. Incorporating these perspectives is essential to ensure that same-day discharge pathways remain patient-centered and aligned with recovery needs. A qualitative descriptive study was conducted among adults who underwent elective minimally invasive colectomy or stoma reversal planned for same-day discharge at a university-affiliated colorectal referral center (February 2020-March 2023). Semistructured telephone interviews with 12 core open-ended questions were performed postoperatively between June and August 2023. Purposeful sampling ensured variation in surgical indication, baseline characteristics, and same-day discharge success. Transcriptions were independently coded by 2 reviewers using an inductive thematic analysis. Of 191 patients planned for same-day discharge, 25 were approached and 17 completed interviews when thematic saturation was reached. Mean time from surgery to interview was 15.3 months (standard deviation 8.3). Mean age was 51 years (standard deviation 16), 58.8% were female, and colon cancer was the most common indication (n = 9). Four themes emerged: (1) need for preparedness and foresight, (2) adjusting to the homecare model, (3) comfort and return of daily function, and (4) factors limiting homecare. Patients emphasized preoperative education, social support, and timely access to care. Reported benefits included improved sleep, emotional comfort, and dietary freedom, whereas challenges involved wound care, injectable medications, and limited community resources. Despite initial hesitancy, most participants expressed satisfaction and willingness to choose same-day discharge again. Same-day discharge was perceived positively, given adequate preparation, home support, and timely access to services. Incorporating patient input may optimize same-day discharge protocols and recovery experiences.

Right-sided colon cancer (CC) represents a substantial proportion of colorectal malignancies, and laparoscopic right hemicolectomy has become the established surgical standard of care. However, consensus on the optimal anastomotic configuration-end-to-side vs functional end-to-end-remains lacking in current clinical practice. This study aimed to compare end-to-side anastomosis (ESA) with functional end-to-end anastomosis (FEEA) in laparoscopic right hemicolectomy for CC involving extracorporeal anastomosis, thereby providing evidence-based guidance for selecting the optimal anastomotic technique. We systematically searched PubMed, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, and Embase for studies comparing ESA with FEEA in laparoscopic right hemicolectomy for CC involving extracorporeal anastomosis. The search included publications up to January 2026 with no language restrictions. Eligible studies were selected based on the population, intervention, comparison, outcome, and study design framework. A total of 5 studies were included in the analysis. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Postoperative ileus (POI) is a common complication after colorectal surgery, delaying recovery and prolonging hospitalization. We aimed to identify factors associated with POI after laparoscopic radical resection for colorectal cancer and to develop and internally validate a postoperative risk-stratification nomogram. This single-center retrospective study included 300 patients undergoing laparoscopic radical resection for colorectal cancer between January 2021 and March 2025. The patients were randomly assigned to the development (n = 210) and validation (n = 90) cohorts. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors independently associated with POI. Model performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic, calibration, and decision curves. POI occurred in 23.8% and 22.2% of the development and validation cohorts, respectively. Previous abdominal surgery (odds ratio [OR], 3.031; 95% CI, 1.226-7.493; The developed nomogram showed acceptable internal performance and may support early postoperative POI risk reassessment and individualized management. External validation is required before broader clinical application.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Brain metastasis is a significant cause of patient morbidity and mortality. There is increasing evidence that genomic instability features such as aneuploidy are associated with metastases to the brain and other organs. We analyzed the genomic instability of brain metastases among different cancer types. This included brain metastases from non-small cell lung, breast, melanoma and colorectal cancer. Our study identified a significantly higher degree of genomic instability in colorectal brain metastases compared to the other types of brain metastases. Nex, we examined the brain metastases for the types of aneuploidy events, namely chromosomal arm imbalances that involved gains or losses. Colorectal cancer brain metastases had specific chromosomal arm imbalance profiles that included gains of 13q and 20q which were significantly more frequent compared to the other cancer types. We examined other colorectal cancer metastatic sites in the lung, liver, lymph nodes and the primary colon. Examining colorectal cancer metastases more closely, aneuploidy gains across either arms for chromosomes 7 and 16 were also higher among brain metastases compared to liver, lung and lymph node metastases. Overall, this study shows that colorectal cancer brain metastasis has specific aneuploidy profiles different than other cancer types as well as being different among other metastatic organ sites.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) can induce durable clinical responses, yet relationships among the gut microbiome, microbial function, intestinal metabolism, and host immunity remain incompletely resolved. We performed dense longitudinal multi-omics profiling of a single patient with colorectal cancer metastatic to the liver during ICI therapy and sustained tumor regression. Eleven serial stool samples spanning approximately 7.3 months were analyzed by 16S rRNA sequencing, microbial metatranscriptomics, metabolomics, lipidomics, and stool host-RNA immune profiling and aligned with serial clinical imaging. A major intestinal ecosystem transition accompanied the emergence of clinical response. Microbial abundance and transcriptional activity were frequently discordant, demonstrating that compositional profiling alone incompletely captured microbial dynamics. Taxon-resolved functional analysis revealed sequential microbial states rather than a single responder-associated configuration. Loss of early Bacteroides/Fusobacterium-associated functions accompanied purine/sphingolipid remodeling and changes in myeloid-associated immune signatures. At T5, a transient Bifidobacterium carbohydrate/fermentation program coincided with lactate/indole-3-lactate remodeling and broad adaptive T-cell, memory/regulatory, mucosal, and B-cell immune changes. At T6, marked Clostridium transcriptional emergence and lipid/coenzyme-A pathway activation coincided with fatty-acid/lysophospholipid remodeling and a distinct immune configuration. Historical HUMAnN reconstruction using original UniRef90 and MetaCyc resources confirmed taxon-specific, reaction-associated gene-family support for prioritized functional programs. These findings define a temporally ordered microbial-metabolic-immune succession during ICI response. Although this N-of-1 design cannot establish population generalizability, dense within-person multi-omics resolves transient functional states obscured by cross-sectional analyses and generates testable hypotheses for larger prospective cohorts and personalized studies of ICI response.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Engineered bacteria enable self-amplifying therapeutic delivery and immune activation, yet these same features drive systemic toxicity and off-target growth. Here, we create a "tumorobe" that overcomes these limitations by integrating reduced immunogenicity, tumour-restricted growth, and enhanced payload release. Specifically, we identify lipopolysaccharide modifications that reduce immunogenicity while preserving fitness, restrict growth to tumours using a hypoxia-lactate "AND" gate, and enhance extracellular payload release via lipoprotein deletion. This strain expands the maximum tolerated dose in a route-dependent manner by up to 1,000-fold. Across multiple murine models, including colorectal cancer and glioblastoma, the strain drives robust antitumour efficacy as both a standalone therapeutic and an immunotherapeutic delivery platform, achieving durable complete responses in up to 75% of colorectal tumours when armed with a cytokine payload. Together, these results establish a broadly applicable platform for safe and effective bacterial cancer therapy.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Multiple rectal neuroendocrine tumors (MR-NETs) are rare. There is no consensus on their characteristics and treatment. We aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of endoscopic resection (ER) for MR-NETs. We performed a retrospective review of 24 patients with 57 rectal NETs who underwent ER at Zhongshan Hospital, Fudan University. Baseline information, procedure-related characteristics and postoperative outcomes were analyzed. The mean maximal diameter was 8.2 ± 4.5 mm, with 43 lesions < 10 mm and 14 lesions ≥ 10 mm. Seventeen patients had 2 lesions, 6 patients had 3 lesions and 1 patient had 5 lesions. There were 53 lesions treated by endoscopic submucosal dissection, 2 lesions treated by endoscopic mucosal resection, and 2 lesions treated by endoscopic submucosal excavation. The en bloc resection rate and technical success rate were both 100%. There were no delayed bleeding or perforation. All patients were eventually discharged safely, with a mean post-procedure hospital stay of 1.81 ± 0.48 days. Tumor grade was G1 in 54 (94.7%) lesions and G2 in 3 lesions (5.3%). Positive margins were found in 10 lesions, including 2 lesions (3.5%) with lateral margin involvement, and 8 cases (14.0%) with basal margin involvement. Mean follow-up was 34.96 ± 23.20 months, with only 3 local recurrences which were successfully managed by salvage ER. There were no recurrences in the 10 lesions with positive margins. ER is a safe and effective technique for small MR-NETs. Positive resection margins do not appear to adversely affect the prognosis of small MR-NETs. Salvage ER may be a viable option in recurrent cases.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Evidence regarding the association between multidisciplinary team (MDT) discussion and survival outcomes in patients with colorectal cancer liver metastases (CRLM) undergoing hepatic resection remains limited and inconsistent. This study aimed to evaluate the association between preoperative MDT discussion and survival outcomes in this surgically treated population. We retrospectively analyzed consecutive patients with pathologically confirmed CRLM who underwent initial hepatic resection at our center between September 2020 and December 2024. Patients were categorized into MDT and non-MDT groups based on whether a preoperative MDT discussion was conducted. To improve balance in observed baseline characteristics, 1:1 propensity score matching (PSM) was performed. Overall survival (OS) was the primary endpoint, and recurrence-free survival (RFS) was analyzed as a secondary endpoint. Survival curves were estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method and compared with the log-rank test. Missing data were handled using multiple imputation (MI), and univariable and multivariable Cox regression analyses were performed to assess the association between MDT discussion and survival outcomes. Sensitivity analyses using complete-case multivariable Cox regression, Cox regression in the propensity score-matched cohort, and average treatment effect among the treated (ATT) weighting were performed to assess the robustness of the findings. A total of 256 patients were included, including 79 in the MDT group and 177 in the non-MDT group. After 1:1 PSM, 72 matched pairs were identified. Before PSM, the MDT group had significantly better OS than the non-MDT group (P=0.03). The 1- and 3-year OS rates were 97.2% and 77.9% in the MDT group, compared with 88.8% and 57.5% in the non-MDT group, respectively. After PSM, the difference in OS remained significant (P=0.01), with corresponding 1- and 3-year OS rates of 98.5% and 77.9% versus 85.3% and 49.1%, respectively. No significant difference in RFS was observed before (P=0.52) or after PSM (P=0.16). In MI-pooled univariable Cox regression analysis, MDT discussion was associated with improved OS [hazard ratio (HR): 0.541; 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.301-0.975; P=0.04], and this association remained significant in multivariable analysis (HR: 0.483; 95% CI: 0.260-0.897; P=0.02). MDT discussion was not independently associated with RFS in multivariable analysis (HR: 0.928; 95% CI: 0.654-1.317; P=0.67). Sensitivity analyses using complete-case multivariable Cox regression, Cox regression in the propensity score-matched cohort, and ATT weighting yielded generally consistent results with the primary analysis. Preoperative MDT discussion was associated with improved OS but not RFS in patients with CRLM undergoing initial hepatic resection. These findings support the potential value of MDT discussion in preoperative decision-making for this patient population.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
An 83-year-old woman was admitted to our hospital because of right lower abdominal pain. A CT scan revealed intestinal intussusception caused by a tumor in the ascending colon. Because endoscopic reduction of the intussusception was difficult, an emergency laparoscopy-assisted right hemicolectomy was performed. The resected specimen revealed a 50 × 46 mm Type 2 tumor causing the intussusception. The histopathological diagnosis was muc>por1>tub2, pT3N2aM0, pStage Ⅲb. She declined adjuvant therapy due to her age and activities of daily living (ADL). Five months after operation, tumor markers increased, and imaging findings revealed liver metastasis and lymph node metastases that were located at the abdominal aorta and hepatoduodenal ligament. Genetic examination detected microsatellite instability-high status (MSI-high), and pembrolizumab was initiated as first-line therapy. Pembrolizumab was administered at a dose of 200 mg every 6 weeks. Fifteen months after the administration of pembrolizumab, metastatic lesions have continued to shrink, and she is continuing treatment without any significant adverse events. We report a case of successful treatment with pembrolizumab for an 80s elderly patient with MSI-high unresectable colon cancer by adjusting the dosing interval.
