ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Our previous research showed that infectious complications are associated with worse outcomes in colorectal cancer. In older adults, diminished oral function may reduce the consumption of main dishes that require mastication, which may contribute to inadequate protein intake, malnutrition, and poor prognosis. We also found that reduced occlusal support was associated with infectious complications; however, the relationship between infectious complications and the number of remaining teeth (a simple measure of oral function) remains unclear. Therefore, we investigated this potential association. We analyzed 169 patients aged ≥65 years with colorectal cancer, with food consistency adjusted according to the number of remaining teeth. Patients with ≤19 teeth had a lower prognostic nutritional index, a higher modified Glasgow prognostic score, a reduced psoas muscle index, and were more likely to live alone than those with ≥20 teeth. Additionally, patients with ≤19 teeth showed a higher incidence of infectious complications, although their nutritional intake did not differ from that of patients with ≥20 teeth. Patients with ≤19 teeth exhibited poorer preoperative nutritional and systemic status and a higher incidence of infectious complications.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The patient was a 70-year-old woman. Colonoscopy performed for the evaluation of hematochezia revealed a type 2 lesion involving two-thirds of the circumference of the Rb rectum, mainly on the posterior wall. The pretreatment diagnosis was cT4N2aM0, cStage Ⅲc rectal cancer, with invasion into the puborectalis muscle. Therefore, 4 courses of FOLFOXIRI plus bevacizumab therapy were administered as neoadjuvant treatment to keep the circumferential margin negative. After chemotherapy, the tumor showed marked shrinkage, and invasion into the puborectalis muscle was improved; thus, laparoscopic partial intersphincteric resection was planned. Laparoscopically, and dissection was going to between the internal and external anal sphincters as partially resected the external anal sphincter to keep the circumferential margin negative. Transanally, the internal sphincter was divided at the dentate line, and a single-layer full-thickness anastomosis was performed. Postoperative histopathological examination revealed pT2 (MP) pN0, pStage Ⅰ disease, and the therapeutic effect of chemotherapy was Grade 1b. The postoperative course was uneventful, and no recurrence has been observed. Various approaches to anus-preserving treatment using multidisciplinary therapy have been reported and achieving a balance between functional preservation and oncological control, as well as managing complications and postoperative sequelae, is considered important.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Identification of the primary lesion responsible for recurrence is crucial in patients with multiple colorectal cancers harboring distinct molecular profiles. We report 2 recurrent cases in which circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) analysis using the BEAMing assay contributed to treatment selection. Case 1: A 72-year-old man underwent subtotal colectomy for synchronous colorectal cancers. The cecal tumor was RAS-mutant, whereas the descending colon tumor was RAS wild-type with BRAF V600E mutation. Early peritoneal recurrence developed during adjuvant chemotherapy. BEAMing analysis detected no RAS mutation, suggesting recurrence from the descending colon cancer. Encorafenib plus cetuximab therapy was initiated. Case 2: A 76-year-old woman underwent resection of multiple colorectal cancers. The transverse colon cancer was RAS wild-type, whereas the ascending colon cancer was RAS-mutant. Following recurrence with multiple lung and ovarian metastases, BEAMing analysis revealed RAS mutation, indicating recurrence from the ascending colon cancer. mFOLFOX6 plus bevacizumab therapy was started. BEAMing-based ctDNA analysis is a minimally invasive and rapid approach for estimating the origin of recurrence in multiple colorectal cancers with different molecular profiles and may facilitate optimal therapeutic decision-making.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Microsatellite instability-high (MSI-H) or mismatch repair-deficient (dMMR) colorectal cancer is a biologically distinct sub-type characterized by hypermutation, abundant neoantigens, and marked sensitivity to immune checkpoint inhibition. In unresectable or metastatic disease, pembrolizumab has become a standard first-line option based on KEYNOTE-177, and nivolumab plus ipilimumab has emerged as another major strategy based on the phase Ⅲ CheckMate 8HW results. In locally advanced rectal cancer, PD-1 blockade has opened a realistic path toward organ preservation, with dostarlimab-based treatment producing remarkably high clinical complete response rates and enabling a watch-and-wait strategy in selected patients. In locally advanced colon cancer, neoadjuvant immunotherapy has shown extraordinary pathological activity, as exemplified by NICHE-2. In the adjuvant setting, fluoropyrimidine monotherapy remains of limited value in stage Ⅱ dMMR colon cancer, whereas the ATOMIC trial suggests that adding immune checkpoint inhibition to oxaliplatin-based chemotherapy may improve disease-free survival in resected stage Ⅲ disease. This review summarizes current evidence and practical treatment strategies for MSI-H/dMMR colorectal cancer across metastatic, neoadjuvant, and adjuvant settings, and discusses unresolved issues, including the selection of PD-1 monotherapy versus dual checkpoint blockade, optimal treatment duration, surveillance after clinical complete response, and the future role of ctDNA-guided perioperative decision-making.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
To explore the status of demoralization syndrome and its influencing factors in postoperative patients with colorectal cancer (CRC). Convenience sampling was adopted to select 243 patients who had undergone CRC surgery from a Grade A tertiary hospital in China as the research participants. Demographic characteristics, disease-related information, medical coping styles, social support level, illness perception degree, and positive psychological capital status were collected. Statistical analyses were performed using independent samples t tests or one-way analysis of variance. Pearson's correlation analysis and multiple linear regression analysis were also conducted. 232 patients post-CRC surgery completed the survey, with the majority presenting moderate or severe demoralization syndrome (moderate: 57%; severe: 42%). The main factors influencing patients' demoralization syndrome include marital status (widowed), education level, per capita monthly household income (renminbi/month), tumor staging, and ostomy status, as well as resignation coping style, illness perception degree, and positive psychological capital score (all p < 0.05). Nurses should prioritize populations at high risk for demoralization, identify those who are prone to psychological distress, and develop and implement targeted nursing interventions, such as incorporating peer support platforms and patient education, to reduce the risk of postoperative demoralization syndrome.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Bilateral lower extremity edema may serve as an early clinical manifestation of pulmonary sarcoidosis. Identifying sarcoidosis as the underlying cause can be challenging in patients with or without a prior history of the disease, as lower extremity edema is not typically considered part of its clinical spectrum. A 63-year-old man presented with a complex medical history, including non-Hodgkin lymphoma, bilateral renal cell carcinoma, colon cancer, and pleomorphic sarcoma of the upper extremity. He also had a history of recurrent pulmonary sarcoidosis. He reported a 6-month history of bilateral pitting lower extremity edema that developed several months before the onset of dyspnea. In patients with multiple comorbidities, recognizing sarcoidosis as a potential cause of bilateral lower extremity edema requires careful exclusion of systemic and malignant etiologies. Sarcoidosis should be considered when more common causes have been excluded.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Cancer remains a major public health issue globally, with a growing burden due to population aging and lifestyle changes. This study provides the estimates of cancer burden in China for 2024. Cancer data of year 2019 from 919 population-based cancer registries across China submitted to the National Cancer Center were selected, with 106 registries providing continuous data from 2010 to 2019 being used to predict the burden of cancer in 2024. The Segi's world standard population was used to estimate the age-standardized rates. Joinpoint regression analysis was used to evaluate the trends from 2000 to 2019 by calculating the annual percentage changes (APC) and average annual percentage changes (AAPC). In 2024, an estimated 5,150,000 new cancer cases and 2,580,000 cancer deaths occurred in China. The age-standardized incidence rate (ASIR) was 207.70 per 100,000 population and the age-standardized mortality rate (ASMR) was 90.90 per 100,000 population. Lung cancer was the most diagnosed cancer, followed by thyroid, colorectal, breast, and liver cancers. Collectively these top five cancers accounted for 59.13 % of all new cases. The leading cause of cancer death was lung cancer, followed by liver cancer, colorectal cancer, stomach cancer, and esophageal cancer, which together comprised of 66.75 % of all cancer deaths. The age-specific incidence rates increased with age for most cancer sites in men, but for cancers of breast, thyroid, ovarian, and cervix in women, the rates increased significantly in young and middle ages. The age-specific mortality rate increased with age and showed a higher level in men than in women. From 2000 to 2019, the ASIR for all cancers combined increased significantly (AAPC = 1.6 %), while the ASMR decreased (AAPC = -1.4 %). Cancers of the esophagus, stomach, and liver showed declining incidence and mortality trends, whereas thyroid, prostate, and cervical cancers exhibited significant increases in incidence. The cancer burden in China continued to be substantial, characterized by a coexistence of cancer patterns of both developing and developed countries. The results highlight the necessity for targeted policies within the "Healthy China 2030" initiative to address sex and age disparities, as well as evolving cancer patterns.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Standardized letters of evaluation are central to colorectal surgery residency selection; yet, variability in evaluator scoring patterns and differences in applicant evaluation by residency training environment remain insufficiently understood. This study evaluated differences in applicant ratings based on residency program type and evaluator role. A retrospective review of colorectal surgery residency applications submitted to a single academic institution across 3 application cycles (2023, 2024, and 2025) was performed. Applicant characteristics, residency training environment (academic versus community), evaluator characteristics, and domain ratings were abstracted. Nonparametric comparisons were performed using Mann-Whitney U tests. A total of 342 applications and 1,287 letters of recommendation were analyzed. Across all cycles, ratings were heavily clustered within the top 2 performance categories across domains. Colorectal surgery program directors consistently demonstrated more conservative scoring patterns, particularly in technical ability and select cognitive domains; however, differences were domain dependent and not uniformly significant across all categories. Applicants from academic programs generally received higher ratings across multiple domains compared with community programs, with statistically significant differences observed in select measures, though many domain-level comparisons were not significant. Despite these differences, substantial overlap in score distributions was observed between groups. Colorectal surgery program directors apply systematically more conservative scoring than other evaluators in performance-based domains. This pattern has direct implications for how standardized letters are interpreted during selection. Applicant training environments contribute to smaller, domain-dependent differences. However, high ratings remain common across all groups, limiting discrimination in applicant assessment.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Hypoxia-inducible factor 3 alpha (HIF-3α) has long been considered a minor, inhibitory branch of the HIF pathway. However, accumulating evidence suggests that HIF-3α is a context-dependent regulator with transcriptional activator and dominant-negative functions. The human HIF3A locus undergoes extensive alternative splicing, yielding at least eight to ten protein isoforms. In contrast, the mouse Hif3a gene produces only three major variants. This creates substantial species divergence in isoform architecture and expression. Full-length human isoforms, such as HIF-3α1, HIF-3α2, and HIF-3α9, are bona fide transcription factors that regulate both canonical and non-canonical hypoxic targets, including EPO, LC3C, REDD1, SQRDL, and IGFBP-1. In contrast, truncated variants, such as HIF-3α4, antagonize HIF-1/2-dependent angiogenic and metabolic programs in a tissue-specific manner. Mouse models demonstrate that canonical HIF-3α integrates developmental and redox cues in the lungs, heart, and metabolism. Furthermore, human HIF3A methylation and isoform-specific expression have been linked to obesity, liver dysfunction, diabetes, chronic lung disease, neurodegeneration, and cancer. Full-length isoforms often promote tumor growth and metastasis (e.g., in colorectal and pancreatic cancers), whereas truncated isoforms constrain angiogenesis or stabilize oncogenic HIF-2α in certain contexts. In this review, we integrate these findings into an isoform-resolved, cross-species framework that distinguishes experimentally validated HIF-3α functions from indirect associations and proposed redox mechanisms. We propose that HIF-3α acts less as a single hypoxia transcription factor and more as an isoform-specific rheostat that shapes acute, chronic, and redox-stressed states. Finally, we outline the need for long-read transcriptomics, isoform-specific assays, evidence-stratified disease models, and targeted modulation of individual HIF-3α variants to translate this complexity into therapeutic strategies for redox-driven human diseases.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is the most common chronic liver disease globally, and its high prevalence underscores the central role of metabolic dysregulation in its pathogenesis. Recent epidemiological studies have shown that MASLD is associated not only with hepatocellular carcinoma but also with an increased risk of several extrahepatic malignancies, including esophageal, gastric, colorectal, pancreatic, thyroid, breast, endometrial, renal, and prostate cancers. This review summarizes the emerging epidemiological links between MASLD and these extrahepatic cancers and discusses the biological mechanisms that may underlie these associations. We aim to describe both shared and organ-specific pathogenic pathways, highlight the importance of viewing MASLD as a systemic metabolic disorder in cancer prevention and clinical management, and outline future research directions from both conceptual and clinical perspectives. Future efforts should focus on biomarker development, multidisciplinary collaboration, and interventions targeting metabolic pathways.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Ginkgolide B (GB), a bioactive constituent isolated from Potential therapeutic targets of GB against CRC were identified by integrating GB-related and CRC-associated genes. Protein-protein interaction (PPI) networks and functional enrichment analysis (FEA) identified key targets and pathways. Interactions between GB and hub proteins were assessed by docking. The antitumor effects of GB were evaluated in CRC cells using assays for cell proliferation, colony formation, and apoptosis, as well as Western blotting. These data were validated in an MC38 syngeneic subcutaneous tumor model. A total of 288 target proteins were shared between the 522 predicted GB targets and the 4199 CRC-associated targets. FEA indicated that these targets were primarily associated with the phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K) / protein kinase B (AKT) and mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) axes. Docking predicted favorable binding of GB to several hub proteins, with AKT1 showing the strongest predicted affinity. Experimental validation demonstrated that GB inhibited CRC cell proliferation and colony formation, promoted apoptosis, decreased B-cell lymphoma 2 (BCL-2), increased BCL-2-associated X protein (BAX) and Cleaved Caspase-3, and reduced the phosphorylation of AKT and extracellular signal-regulated kinase (ERK). Notably, GB significantly suppressed tumor growth and reduced Ki-67 expression in the MC38 syngeneic subcutaneous tumor model. GB exhibits antitumor activity against CRC by inhibiting proliferation, promoting apoptosis, and inhibiting the PI3K/AKT and MAPK pathways. The study provides a mechanistic basis for the anticancer effects of GB and supports further investigation of its potential as a therapeutic candidate for CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Pressurized intraperitoneal aerosol chemotherapy (PIPAC) has expanded internationally, yet its role remains uncertain due to the lack of high-level evidence and heterogeneous clinical adoption. In this context, national benchmarking is relevant not only for technical standardization but also for governance and patient protection in predominantly palliative settings. We conducted a national, cross-sectional, web-based survey (51 items) among 43 GECOP-affiliated centers (December 2025-March 2026). A total of 32 valid center-level responses were analyzed. Results were summarized descriptively. Most responding centers were tertiary-level hospitals (78.1%) and public institutions (87.5%), all with established HIPEC programs and extensive experience in peritoneal disease management (81.3% > 10 years). An active PIPAC program was reported by 11/32 centers (34.4%), while 21/32 (65.6%) were not currently performing PIPAC. Among the 14/21 non-adopting centers that provided a reason, the main barrier was insufficient or inconclusive evidence (9/14, 64.3%), followed by organizational and resource constraints and clinical or implementation-related concerns (both 5/14, 35.7%). Only 5/21 centers (23.8%) explicitly reported referral of selected patients to active centers. Among active centers, procedural aspects were highly standardized, including universal adoption of a two-trocar approach (100%), balloon trocars (100%), and systematic safety checklists (90.9%). However, substantial heterogeneity was observed in oncological management, including chemotherapy regimens, dosing strategies, and integration with systemic therapy. The most commonly used regimen was cisplatin-doxorubicin (81.8%), with additional use of oxaliplatin (45.5%), taxanes (18.2%), or mitomycin C (9.1%). Response assessment consistently included peritoneal biopsies and PRGS (100%), frequently combined with PCI (90.9%), but remained heterogeneous in sampling strategies and adjunctive methods. At least one severe complication (Clavien-Dindo ≥3) was reported by 3/11 active centers (27.3%), this represents a center-level report rather than a procedure-level complication rate. Within Spanish specialized peritoneal oncology units, PIPAC is implemented in a moderate proportion of centers with insufficient or inconclusive evidence being the most frequently reported barrier among centers providing a reason for non-adoption. Its current use is predominantly palliative, with gastric and colorectal cancer and peritoneal mesothelioma being the most frequently reported indications. It is characterized by marked heterogeneity in indications, treatment strategies, and response evaluation. This variability likely reflects the underlying evidence gap. Rather than discouraging its use, these findings support the need for structured development through prospective clinical trials, centralized data collection, and governance within experienced multidisciplinary teams. These findings allow us to propose a three-phase hypothesis of PIPAC implementation, characterized by initial standardization, subsequent diversification, and current uncertainty-driven practice.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a substantial contributor to cancer-allied mortality on a global scale. Numerous studies have established that the progression of CRC is attributed to genetic and epigenetic changes in the colonic epithelium. Epigenetic variations, for example, DNA methylation and chromatin remodelling, are critical factors in CRC implication. The detailed understanding of these epigenetic changes holds promise for the prevention, treatment, and management of CRC. They are also likely to impact the development of new therapeutic interventions significantly. The current research delves into the effects of dietary compounds on modifying epigenetic changes and restoring normal gene expression in CRC. Specifically, the review focuses on the effectiveness of dietary components/ingredients such as vitamins, fibre, folate, and phytochemicals on various epigenetic regulations that reduce the risk of CRC. Here, we discuss the underlying molecular mechanisms of epigenetic alterations that are induced by dietary compounds, which is crucial for advances in CRC mitigation and treatment. Furthermore, the current review also intends to highlight the combination of several dietary interventions with chemotherapeutic medications, which provides a synergistic approach that might help in the management of CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
To identify colorectal cancer patients' stated preferences under hypothetical choice scenarios for "Internet Plus" nutrition management services, quantify attribute importance and willingness-to-pay (WTP), and assess preference heterogeneity. A cross-sectional discrete choice experiment was conducted in three tertiary hospitals. A total of 265 postoperative patients 1-12 months after colorectal cancer surgery were included. Six attributes were developed through literature review, interviews, expert consultation, and pilot testing. A D-efficient Ngene comprised 39 formal choice sets divided into three questionnaire versions, with 13 analytic choice tasks completed by each participant. Mixed logit and conditional logit models estimated preference coefficients, relative attribute importance, WTP, and preference heterogeneity. Across 3445 choice-task observations, the mixed logit model outperformed the conditional logit model. Response timeliness (28.4%) and out-of-pocket cost (26.1%) were the most influential attributes, followed by ONS access/reimbursement (19.3%) and personalization basis (13.6%). Patients preferred responses within 12 h, individualized nutritional adjustment, 60% ONS reimbursement with hospital pickup, and biweekly follow-up. Exploratory subgroup analyses suggested potential preference heterogeneity by digital health literacy, ostomy status, and time since surgery. Postoperative colorectal cancer patients prioritized timely healthcare responses and affordability, while also valuing higher ONS reimbursement and individualized nutritional adjustment. These stated preferences may inform patient-centered internet-based nutrition services but should not be interpreted as evidence of actual uptake, adherence, clinical outcomes, or cost-effectiveness. Eliciting and incorporating patients' preferences may support patient-provider communication, nutrition counselling, patient engagement, and shared decision-making when developing internet-based postoperative nutrition-management services.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a major global health burden, and increasing evidence indicates that disruption of trace element homeostasis may contribute to colorectal carcinogenesis and disease progression. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to critically discuss and evaluate evidence on trace element alterations in CRC from studies employing inductively coupled plasma (ICP)-based analytical techniques. Following PRISMA guidelines and a PECO framework, PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus were systematically searched up to September 17, 2026, for original human studies using inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) or optical emission spectrometry (ICP-OES) to determine trace elements in CRC-related biological matrices compared to healthy controls. Methodological quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS), and random-effects meta-analyses were conducted to calculate pooled standardized mean differences (SMD) and 95% confidence intervals (CI). Nineteen eligible studies, published between 1994 and 2026, were included. The quantitative synthesis demonstrated a pronounced systemic depletion of circulating selenium (SMD = -0.74, alongside a significant circulatory accumulation of copper (SMD = 0.61), lead (SMD = 0.50), and arsenic (SMD = 0.46) in patients with CRC compared with controls. In tumor tissues, the microenvironment was characterized by a localized hyper-accumulation of manganese (SMD = 0.22). These changes suggest that trace element dysregulation in CRC is highly matrix-dependent. Substantial statistical heterogeneity was observed across studies, likely due to differences in patient characteristics, pre-analytical procedures, and biological matrices. The present findings therefore support the biological relevance of trace element dysregulation in CRC, highlighting the potential of multi-element profiles (e.g., Cu/Zn ratios) while emphasizing the importance of standardized analytical and pre-analytical procedures. Rather than establishing ICP-based techniques as novel analytical tools, this review provides substantial discussion related to the CRC-associated elemental alterations and identifies tissue-dependent profiles; however, observational methodological limitations should be considered for further biomarker and clinical translation studies. This study was supported by Brazilian funding agencies (CNPq, INCTBio-LK, FAPESP, FAPERGS) and the review protocol was registered on the Open Science Framework (OSF; osf.io/zjb3y).

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Early-onset gastrointestinal cancers in adolescents and young adults (< 50 years) from a unique subgroup with unclear epidemiological features. We aimed to estimate the burden of early-onset gastrointestinal cancers in China, focusing on the associations with age, period, and birth cohort effects. Cancer-specific estimates for six major types of early-onset gastrointestinal cancers in China were derived from Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2021. We analyzed the incidence and mortality, and calculated temporal trends, mortality-to-incidence ratio, and age distributions. We used an age-period-cohort analysis to estimate longitudinal age trends (age effects) and period/birth cohort relative risks (period/birth cohort effects) during 1990-2021, and calculated overall annual percentage changes (net drifts). There were 6.52 million incident cases and 4.32 million deaths due to early-onset gastrointestinal cancers in China during 1990-2021. Net drifts in incidence increased for colorectal (1.17% to 1.77%) and Gallbladder cancer (1.16% to 1.81%), while decreases were observed for esophageal cancer (-3.37% to -2.58%), gastric (-1.86% to -1.14%) and liver cancer (-1.75% to -1.06%) during 1990-2021. Period effects on incidence risk decreased for esophageal, gastric, and liver cancers from 1997 to 2021, but increased for colorectal and gallbladder cancers from 1997 to 2021. Birth cohort effects on incidence risk decreased for esophageal cancer (1945-1999), gastric (1945-2004) and liver cancer (1965-2004), whereas increases were seen for colorectal (1945-2004) and gallbladder (1945-2004). For pancreatic cancer, however, birth cohort effects remained largely stable across all cohorts. The age, period, and birth cohort effects on incidence and mortality were similarly consistent. These results provided new insights into the temporal trends in early-onset gastrointestinal cancers and their associations with age, period, and birth cohort effects, and may help to guide future public health policies for cancer control in China. The distinct temporal trends and sex-specific disparities identified in this study underscore the need for differentiated prevention and early screening strategies for gastrointestinal cancers among young adults in China.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
We present a case of a giant ileocecal inflammatory myofibroblastic tumor (IMT), which represents one of the largest pediatric colorectal IMTs reported in the literature. An 11-year-old girl presented with a 1-day history of abdominal pain and developed fever (up to 102.2°F). Laboratory evaluation revealed severe anemia (hemoglobin, 53 g/L) and marked systemic inflammatory abnormalities consistent with paraneoplastic inflammatory syndrome. Exploratory laparotomy revealed a 17 × 17 × 8 cm mass intimately adherent to the ileocecal region. Histopathological examination confirmed IMT with focal ALK positivity. The inflammatory and hematologic abnormalities improved rapidly following complete tumor resection.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Chitosan has been investigated for several decades as a carrier for anticancer agents because of its biocompatibility, biodegradability, chemical versatility, and intrinsic pH responsiveness. Most reported platforms fall into two groups: systems in which the drug is covalently linked to chitosan through a single imine (Schiff base) bond, and ligand-functionalized systems in which folic acid, hyaluronic acid, or galactose is introduced onto the backbone to promote receptor-mediated cellular uptake. Both approaches have been discussed extensively elsewhere. However, a comparatively underexplored strategy involves the formation of a bis-imine linkage between a carbonylcontaining anticancer drug and two amino groups of chitosan. In this configuration, the drug serves not only as the therapeutic payload but also as the sole organic linker between two sites on the polymer chain. This ligand-free dual Schiff base architecture is treated here as a distinct class of chitosandrug conjugate. Both of its defining terms have been applied inconsistently in the literature, and "ligand- free" and "dual (bis) Schiff base" are therefore defined operationally, together with representative examples of structures that fall inside and outside each category. Bivalent attachment is then related to physicochemical and release behavior relative to single-imine systems, with attention to the structural consequences of engaging two amines, the acid-catalyzed hydrolysis of the C═N bond, and the electronic character of the carbonyl-bearing drug. Compared with other acid-labile bonds used in polymer-drug conjugates, the imine is less stable and less pH-selective than the acylhydrazone; however, requiring two hydrolysis events rather than one offers a structural route to improved drug retention. Ligand-modified chitosan systems are assessed critically rather than solely in terms of their targeting advantages, with attention to synthetic complexity, effects on drug loading, steric hindrance, and variability in receptor expression. The tumor-associated pH gradient, on which the whole strategy depends, is weighed against the values actually measured in patients rather than assumed to be a sufficient stimulus for imine hydrolysis and controlled release. Particular emphasis is placed on the analytical evidence required to establish the formation of two distinct imine bonds, since confirmation of a bis-imine structure requires more than indirect evidence of drug association with the polymer. Release evaluation is addressed in terms of physiologically relevant pH conditions, appropriate kinetic models, and transparent reporting of release parameters, and the translational outlook is read against the clinical history of polymer-drug conjugates. A three-way comparison is provided between conventional chitosan-based drug carriers, ligand-functionalized chitosan systems, and ligand-free dual Schiff base chitosan-drug conjugates with respect to synthetic complexity, structural stability, drug-loading potential, release behavior, targeting strategy, and translational considerations. Strictly ligand-free bis-imine chitosan-drug conjugates have been reported in only a small number of studies, so parts of the comparison necessarily draw on closely related imine-linked polymer- drug systems. The resulting experimental gaps are therefore identified explicitly, together with the studies needed to establish the reproducibility, structural stability, release characteristics, biological performance, and safety of these conjugates. Addressing these issues will be essential for determining whether ligand-free dual Schiff base chitosan-drug conjugates can progress beyond proof-ofconcept studies toward more comprehensive preclinical and, ultimately, clinical evaluation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Hydroxypropyl Methylcellulose Acetate Succinate (HPMCAS), an amphiphilic polymer, exhibits three distinct features that facilitate regulated drug administration to the colon: pH-dependent dissolution, mucoadhesion, and stabilisation of supersaturation. The review evaluates the structural components of HPMCAS and their roles to illustrate HPMCAS's efficacy in addressing the dual challenges of hydrophobic anticancer drugs in colorectal cancer chemotherapy, characterised by low water solubility and elevated systemic toxicity. The polymer exhibits superior pharmaceutical applications due to its multifunctional properties, facilitating its use in amorphous solid dispersions, nanoparticles, hot-melt extrusion, and 3D printing, while Eudragit and PLGA polymers show subpar performance in targeted colon delivery. The potential of precision oncology is realised by crystallisation inhibition, pH-triggered release, and receptor-targeted administration, utilising ligand conjugation to CD44, EGFR, and folate. The review identifies three primary challenges: hygroscopicity, scalability, and long-term stability, while proposing AI-assisted formulation optimisation and multi-mechanistic hybrid systems as potential solutions. HPMCAS evolves from a fundamental excipient through polymer chemistry to molecular targeting, becoming an innovative drug-delivery system that enhances the efficacy of CRC treatment while minimising adverse side effects.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Oxaliplatin (OXA) resistance remains a major limitation in colorectal cancer (CRC), and ferroptosis is being investigated as a potential therapeutic vulnerability. Non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs) may influence ferroptotic sensitivity through redox metabolism, iron homeostasis, lipid remodeling, and tumor-microenvironment interactions. However, many proposed ncRNA-mediated mechanisms, particularly competing endogenous RNA (ceRNA) models, remain insufficiently validated. This critical narrative review synthesizes selected experimental reports and is not a systematic or exhaustive review. The reports discussed were organized into four evidence categories: direct ncRNA-OXA-ferroptosis investigations; OXA-ferroptosis studies without ncRNA perturbation; ncRNA-ferroptosis studies without OXA testing; and ncRNA-OXA studies lacking ferroptosis-specific validation. These categories describe the directness of evidence, not formal study-quality scores. Among the selected reports, only two linked ncRNA regulation with both OXA response and ferroptosis: SNHG4 via PTEN RNA stability and lncRNA-HMG via p53-MDM2 and SLC7A11/VKORC1L1 regulation. Neither demonstrated a complete PI3K/AKT-NRF2-SLC7A11/GPX4 pathway or endogenous ceRNA competition. Other studies implicated NRF2/GPX4, SLC7A11, ACSL4-dependent lipid remodeling, iron regulation, FSP1, DHODH, mitochondrial metabolism, microbiota, and extracellular vesicles. Given heterogeneity in models, treatments, endpoints, and validation, links across studies remain hypothesis-generating. Overall, the evidence supports a context-dependent ferroptotic-threshold framework rather than a universal ncRNA-driven pathway. Future work should use endogenous ncRNA perturbation, quantitative ceRNA validation, ferroptosis-specific rescue, and patient-derived models.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Cancer stem cells (CSCs) are increasingly recognized as critical mediators of tumour progression, recurrence and treatment resistance in metastatic colorectal cancer (CRC). Hydroxytyrosol, a phenolic compound derived from virgin olive oil, has shown promising anticancer activity against CRC cells. However, its effects on cancer stemness and its potential to enhance the efficacy of conventional chemotherapy drugs remain largely unexplored. To assess whether hydroxytyrosol suppresses CSC-associated traits and improves chemotherapy response using a 3D spheroid model established from the metastatic CRC cell line LoVo. LoVo spheroids were generated under stirred-tank culture conditions and characterized by molecular and functional assays. Hydroxytyrosol effects on LoVo spheroids were assessed using cell viability, ALDH activity, clonogenic and RT-qPCR assays. Drug combination interactions were determined using the Chou-Talalay method. LoVo spheroids recapitulated key tumour features, including a hybrid epithelial-mesenchymal phenotype, enhanced stemness, high clonogenic capacity, and localized hypoxia. Hydroxytyrosol reduced cell proliferation in a dose-dependent manner, with LoVo spheroids exhibiting greater resistance than 2D cultures (IC This study provides the first evidence that hydroxytyrosol targets CRC CSC-associated phenotypes and synergistically enhances irinotecan efficacy in metastatic CRC spheroids. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Despite its established role in tumor progression and therapy resistance, Cytochrome P450 1B1 (CYP1B1) has remained largely underexplored as a therapeutic target in immunotherapy, with no prior reports using CYP1B1-targeted agents to enhance immune checkpoint inhibitor efficacy. To address this, we designed a series of symmetric degraders in which an α-naphthoflavone (ANF) derivative 1 was conjugated to both ends of a polyethylene glycol (PEG) linker. This design enables each terminus to independently engage the CYP1B1 active site, while the unbound ANF moiety, owing to its hydrophobic nature, may protrude from the protein surface and serve as an intrinsic hydrophobic tag to trigger degradation. The symmetrical architecture also increases binding probability by allowing either end to occupy the pocket. Notably, compound 2 induced potent, dose-dependent degradation of CYP1B1 with selectivity over CYP1A1, and did not exhibit the hook effect typically observed in conventional bifunctional degraders. Mechanistic studies, supported by molecular docking and co-immunoprecipitation, revealed that the dual-binding configuration acts as a hydrophobic tag, promoting protein misfolding and recruiting chaperones HSP70 and HSP90 to facilitate proteasomal clearance. Proteomic profiling further demonstrated that compound 2 broadly modulates immune signaling, metabolic pathways, and ferroptosis, with a particular impact on pathways associated with tumor immune resistance. In syngeneic colon cancer models, compound 2 exhibited favorable pharmacokinetics and, at a subtherapeutic dose, synergized with anti-PD-L1 therapy to induce complete tumor regression in a subset of animals. Importantly, a Palbociclib-based Cyclin-dependent kinases (CDK) 4/6 degrader was designed as a proof-of-concept that the ANF derivative 1 serves as a hydrophobic tag, supporting its broader applicability. Collectively, this work provides a novel chemical tool for probing CYP1B1 biology and positions its targeted degradation as a promising avenue to sensitize tumors to immune checkpoint blockade.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Circulating proteins are promising biomarkers of colorectal cancer risk. Most studies combine colon and rectal cancer despite their biological differences. To identify proteins associated with colorectal, colon, and rectal cancer risk and triangulate findings using cross-cohort confirmation and Mendelian randomisation (MR). We profiled 6,402 proteins, using the SomaScan 7K assay in a case-cohort study nested within the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition (EPIC; 658 colon and 319 rectal cancers). Cox models identified proteins associated with cancer risk at a false discovery rate <5%. Findings were confirmed in the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities study (ARIC; SomaScan; 235 colon, 36 rectal) and UK Biobank (Olink Explore; 321 colon, 164 rectal). MR and genetic colocalisation evaluated potential causality. We identified 36 proteins associated with colorectal cancer, 50 with colon cancer, and 2 with rectal cancer; 20 of the 36 were also associated with colon cancer and none with rectal cancer, and no protein was associated with both sites. Seven of the 40 colon cancer proteins available in ARIC were confirmed, including COMP, MIC-1/GDF15, TFF3, and THIK. Of these, MIC-1/GDF15 and TFF3 were also confirmed in UK Biobank. COMP was inversely associated with colon cancer risk observationally and in MR analyses. Colon and rectal cancers have different pre-diagnostic proteomic profiles, underlining the need for site-specific analyses. COMP, MIC-1/GDF15, and TFF3 were the most robustly supported biomarkers of colon cancer risk. Future work should prioritise experimental validation of these associations and use of repeated measures to define timing.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Olfactory receptor 51E2 (OR51E2) is markedly downregulated in colorectal cancer (CRC), yet its functional activation by its natural agonist, β-ionone, suppresses CRC cell growth. In this study, we investigated the tumor-suppressive effects of β-ionone-mediated OR51E2 activation using human CRC cell lines (SW480, SW620, and RKO) and patient-derived organoids (PDOs). We demonstrate that β-ionone treatment stimulates intracellular calcium levels in an OR51E2-dependent manner, upregulating MAPK-directed phosphatases (DUSP1/2/4 and PPP1CA). This calcium-dependent phosphatase activation suppresses the MEK1/2-ERK1/2 signaling axis, leading to G0/G1 cell cycle arrest via the downregulation of CDK2/4/6 and cyclin A/D1. Concurrently, OR51E2 activation induces a senescence-like phenotype, evidenced by increased senescence-associated β-galactosidase activity, chromatin remodeling (reduced LAMIN B1 and increased H3K27me3), and upregulated p16/p21 expression alongside senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) factors. These phenotypic and mechanistic findings were fully recapitulated in CRC-PDOs representing distinct clinical subtypes. Crucially, the residual senescence-like cell population showed increased susceptibility to dasatinib plus quercetin (DQ), which reduced senescence-associated markers and increased apoptosis. Collectively, this study demonstrates that OR51E2 activation coordinates a heterogeneous cell-fate decision encompassing both apoptosis and a senescence-like phenotype. Our findings highlight ectopic olfactory receptor signaling as an underexplored mechanism of tumor suppression and provide in vitro evidence for a sequential approach in CRC in which β-ionone-mediated OR51E2 activation induces a senescence-like state followed by senolytic treatment.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Introduction COVID-19 disrupted colorectal cancer (CRC) screening and diagnostic services, raising concerns that delayed diagnosis would increase emergency presentations and advanced disease. This study evaluated temporal changes in emergency CRC presentation, tumour characteristics, and management within a regional Australian health service. Methods A retrospective cohort study included adults presenting emergently with newly diagnosed CRC between January 2019 and July 2023. Absolute emergency presentation volumes and emergency presentations relative to elective CRC resections were examined before and during COVID-19 restrictions. Temporal trends in tumour characteristics and management were assessed using logistic regression, with secondary analyses adjusted for age and sex. Results A total of 149 patients presented emergently with CRC. Absolute emergency presentation volumes remained stable across the complete calendar years studied, with 30 cases in 2019, 28 in 2020, 32 in 2021, and 30 in 2022. Emergency presentations also remained stable relative to elective CRC resections, accounting for 15.3% of CRC surgical activity in 2019 compared with 15.2% during the COVID-19 restriction period (2020-2022; odds ratio (OR) 0.99, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.63-1.55; p = 0.970). Increasing calendar year was independently associated with greater odds of high-grade disease (adjusted OR (aOR) 1.39 per year, 95% CI 1.07-1.82; p = 0.015) and stoma formation at index presentation (aOR 1.37 per year, 95% CI 1.04-1.80; p = 0.026), although the latter association was influenced by a marked increase in stoma formation in 2022. Stage IV and metastatic disease were more frequent in later years but did not demonstrate statistically significant temporal associations. Conclusion Emergency CRC presentation volumes remained stable during the COVID-19 restriction period within this regional Australian health service, alongside relatively preserved elective CRC surgical activity. Although increasing calendar year was associated with high-grade disease and stoma formation, the stoma association was influenced by a marked increase in 2022 and should be interpreted cautiously. These findings suggest that presentation frequency alone may not capture changes in the characteristics and management complexity of emergency CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Psychosocial interventions are known to improve emotional well-being and quality of life in patients with cancer, but their effects on overall survival (OS) remain unclear. An updated meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) was performed. A systematic literature search was performed in MEDLINE, EMBASE and Cochrane CENTRAL from database inception until December 2025. Randomized controlled trials comparing OS between patients receiving psychosocial interventions and control groups were included. Study characteristics and summary hazard ratios (SHR) were extracted. If SHRs were not provided, they were derived from Kaplan-Meier curves. A meta-analysis was performed using a random effects model. Of 20365 studies identified, 24 RCTs involving 4795 patients met inclusion criteria. Follow-up time ranged from 1 to 18 years. Patients treated with psychosocial interventions had better overall survival outcomes than those in the control groups (SHR = 0.87, 95% CI 0.77-0.99; I² = 45%). Subgroup analyses showed improved OS among studies involving patients treated with curative intent (12 studies; SHR 0.75, 95% CI 0.64-0.87; I² = 20.9%), studies involving colorectal primary cancers (2 studies; SHR 0.69, 95% CI 0.48-0.99; I² = 0%), and intervention duration ≥ 12 months (N = 13, SHR = 0.85, CI: 0.72-0.99, I2 = 46.8%). Adult patients with cancer who were offered psychosocial interventions may have improved OS. Given the moderate heterogeneity in our analysis, an individual patient-level meta-analysis may help identify characteristics of patients who benefit from these interventions.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The 5-year follow-up results of KEYNOTE-177 established pembrolizumab as a standard first-line (1L) treatment for deficient mismatch repair (dMMR) metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC), demonstrating improved response rates, progression-free survival (PFS), and tolerability over chemotherapy. Pembrolizumab became available as a 1L option in Australia following government reimbursement in August 2021. Real-world treatment patterns and outcomes in Australia since then have not previously been reported. Patients with dMMR mCRC diagnosed from August 1, 2021 to May 30, 2025, were analyzed using data from Treatment of Recurrent and Advanced Colorectal Cancer (TRACC) and TRACC-SELECT, Australian multi-site prospective registries. Clinicopathologic characteristics, treatment patterns, and outcomes were examined. Survival outcomes for 1L pembrolizumab-treated patients were analyzed using Kaplan-Meier. From 36 sites, 120 dMMR mCRC patients were identified; 109 (91%) received systemic treatment. 1L treatment included pembrolizumab (n = 103, 94%), clinical trial enrolment (n = 4, 4%), and chemotherapy (n = 2, 2%). Among pembrolizumab-treated patients, median age was 75 years, 49% had a BRAFV600E mutation, and 17% had an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status (ECOG PS) ≥ 2. Median follow-up was 25.8 months. The real-world objective response rate was 58%, while 17% had progressive disease as best response. Median duration of therapy was 15.2 months. Of 74 patients who discontinued pembrolizumab, 21 (28%) completed the 2-year course, 28 (38%) discontinued due to progressive disease, 11 (15%) due to toxicity, 6 (8%) after achieving complete response before 2 years, and 8 (11%) for other reasons. Median PFS was 37.9 months. Median overall survival (OS) was not reached; 12- and 24-month OS rates were 88% and 77%, respectively. This real-world cohort included older patients with higher rates of BRAFV600E mutation and poorer ECOG PS than KEYNOTE-177. There has been rapid and wide uptake of pembrolizumab as a new standard of care, with promising outcomes. Ongoing data collection and analyses will evaluate predictors of immunotherapy response and real-world second-line treatment patterns and outcomes.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Tumor budding (TB) is a key histopathological marker in colorectal cancer (CRC), closely linked to disease progression and prognosis. Deep learning has greatly advanced histological image analysis by enabling robust and efficient pattern recognition. In this study, we developed a SegFormer-based TB segmentation pipeline using pretrained backbones and evaluated two new decoder variants: Feature Pyramid Network (FPN) and a Deformable FPN (DFPN) layer to better capture small and irregular cellular structures. The dataset includes 8606 training images, 201 validation images, and 2036 test images derived from 86 H&E-stained WSIs, plus 176 finely re-annotated test set images. We evaluated the performance of pre-trained encoder models using the MiT-B0 and MiT-B3 backbones. The best-performing models are then further enhanced by replacing their decoder components with either an FPN or a DFPN, aiming to boost segmentation performance metrics. Using the best encoder backbone in SegFormer, we achieved instance dice scores of 0.7847 on test images and 0.8864 on the finely re-annotated test set. Integrating a Deformable FPN (DFPN) decoder substantially improved instance-level Dice, particularly for small and irregular tumor buds, while pixel-level overlap metrics changed more modestly. This demonstrates that decoder-level innovations are critical for enhancing Vision Transformer-based segmentation in pathology. This study highlights the potential of decoder innovations to improve ViT-based segmentation in surgical pathology, with future work focused on expanding annotated datasets and enhancing model adaptability for real-world use.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Anastomotic leak remains a major cause of morbidity and mortality after gastrointestinal surgery. Targeted analysis of intraperitoneal drain fluid biomarkers may enable earlier, more specific detection of anastomotic leak than systemic markers. The aim of this systematic review meta-analysis was to investigate the diagnostic accuracy of peritoneal drain fluid biomarkers for detecting anastomotic leak in both upper and lower gastrointestinal surgery. A systematic review and diagnostic test accuracy meta-analysis was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews-Diagnostic Test Accuracy guidelines. Eligible studies included patients undergoing intra-abdominal gastrointestinal anastomoses, with measurement of drain fluid biomarkers within postoperative days 1-7. Pooled sensitivity, specificity, diagnostic odds ratio, and area under the summary receiver operating characteristic curves were calculated using bivariate and random-effects models. Sixty-five studies were included (18 meta-analyzed, 47 narratively synthesized). In upper gastrointestinal surgery, drain amylase had pooled sensitivity of 77.3% (95% confidence interval, 60.6-88.2) and specificity of 96.0% (95% confidence interval, 87.2-98.8) (diagnostic odds ratio, 50.9; area under the summary receiver operating characteristic curve, 0.70). In colorectal surgery, luminal biomarkers performed best: amylase showed sensitivity of 99.6% (95% confidence interval, 2.1-100) and specificity of 98.5% (95% confidence interval, 76.3-99.9) (diagnostic odds ratio, 92.4; area under the summary receiver operating characteristic curve, 0.93; no defunctioning ileostomies). Low pH had pooled sensitivity of 88.1% (95% confidence interval, 62.5-97.1) and specificity of 94.1% (95% confidence interval, 82.9-98.1) (diagnostic odds ratio, 114.1; area under the summary receiver operating characteristic curve, 0.96). Inflammatory biomarkers, such as C-reactive protein and cytokines, were more frequently studied but less accurate (area under the summary receiver operating characteristic curve, 0.69-0.85). Drain fluid biomarkers, particularly luminal (amylase) and metabolic (pH), demonstrate high diagnostic accuracy for early anastomotic leak detection, outperforming inflammatory markers. Biochemical monitoring of the perianastomotic environment may support postoperative surveillance in selected high-risk patients.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Protective ileostomy is commonly performed after low anterior resection for rectal cancer to mitigate the clinical consequences of anastomotic leakage; however, it is associated with stoma-related and reversal-related morbidity. Ghost ileostomy has emerged as a selective alternative to avoid unnecessary stoma maturation. This systematic review and meta-analysis of comparative studies was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 statement. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched from inception to March 31, 2026. Six comparative studies involving 395 patients were included. The primary outcome was anastomotic leakage. Secondary outcomes were length of hospital stay, readmission/rehospitalization, and postoperative ileus. Random-effects models were used. The risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2 and ROBINS-I, and the certainty of evidence was evaluated using GRADE. The available evidence did not demonstrate a statistically significant difference in anastomotic leakage between ghost and protective ileostomy (RR 1.27, 95% CI 0.64-2.49; I² = 0%). Length of hospital stay was also not significantly different (MD 0.55 days, 95% CI -1.35 to 2.45; I² = 92%). Ghost ileostomy was associated with lower readmission/rehospitalization (RR 0.24, 95% CI 0.06-0.89; I² = 0%) and postoperative ileus (RR 0.33, 95% CI 0.13-0.82; I² = 0%). Leave-one-out sensitivity analysis did not materially alter the interpretation of the heterogeneous hospital-stay outcome. The certainty of evidence was low for anastomotic leakage, readmission, and postoperative ileus and very low for hospital stay. The available evidence did not identify a statistically significant difference in anastomotic leakage between ghost and protective ileostomy, although imprecision and limited sample size preclude a definitive conclusion of equivalence. Ghost ileostomy may reduce postoperative ileus and readmission in carefully selected patients; however, larger, adequately powered randomized trials are required before routine adoption.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
BRAF-mutant (BRAF-MT) colorectal cancer (CRC) represents a clinically aggressive subtype characterized by distinct biological features and significantly worse prognosis compared to BRAF wild-type (BRAF-WT) CRC, with median survival reduced by approximately 40%. The therapeutic resistance of BRAF-MT CRC stems primarily from BRAF-driven dysregulation of tumor cell proliferation. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying the aggressive phenotype and potential therapeutic vulnerabilities remain incompletely understood. Bioinformatic analyses were employed to identify candidate genes. A combination of in vitro (cell proliferation, clonal formation), ex vivo (patient-derived and mouse intestinal organoids), and in vivo (xenograft models) assays were used to assess oncogenic function. Mechanistic investigations included Western blotting, qRT-PCR, co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP), chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP), and luciferase reporter assays to delineate the regulatory axis. Fatty acid metabolism and ferroptosis were evaluated by a combination of metabolomic, biochemical, and cellular assays. Bioinformatic screening identified ankyrin repeat domain 54 (ANKRD54) as selectively overexpressed in BRAF-MT CRC and significantly associated with adverse prognosis. Inhibition of ANKRD54 markedly suppressed clonogenic potential, cellular proliferation in vitro, organoid formation in both PDOs and cKI mouse-derived organoids, and tumor growth in vivo. Mechanistically, lysine acetyltransferase 2 A (KAT2A) promoted ANKRD54 transcriptional activation through H3K27 acetylation. ANKRD54 subsequently formed a functional complex with CCAAT/enhancer binding protein beta (CEBPB), cooperatively inducing ELOVL fatty acid elongase 6 (ELOVL6) expression. This KAT2A-mediated ANKRD54/CEBPB/ELOVL6 transcriptional axis reprogrammed fatty acid metabolism, selectively suppressing ferroptosis in BRAF-MT CRC. Pharmacological targeting of either ANKRD54 or ELOVL6 substantially enhanced the therapeutic efficacy of Vemurafenib-based treatment in BRAF-MT CRC models. Clinical data corroborated that elevated ANKRD54 expression promoted malignant progression and predicted poor outcomes through this ELOVL6-dependent metabolic pathway. This study elucidates a novel KAT2A-mediated ANKRD54/CEBPB/ELOVL6 axis driving aggressive tumor behavior through regulating fatty acid metabolic and ferroptosis evasion. These findings establish ANKRD54 and ELOVL6 as promising therapeutic targets for combination strategies to overcome therapeutic resistance in BRAF-MT CRC patients.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Cancer survivors face challenges in maintaining a healthy lifestyle after treatment. Maintaining a healthy lifestyle can help delay cancer recurrence, improve quality of life, and even extend survival. This study compared levels of healthy lifestyle maintenance by cancer type and sex among breast cancer survivors (BCS) and colorectal cancer survivors (CRCS) and assessed the mediating roles of fear of cancer recurrence and emotional distress in the association between physical cancer-related symptoms and healthy lifestyle maintenance. This cross-sectional study involved 175 BCS and 189 CRCS aged 31-77, 2-5 years after diagnosis. Data were collected online using structured questionnaires. Univariate general linear models and multigroup path analysis with structural equation modeling were conducted. BCS reported higher physical activity and a healthier diet than CRCS. Women in both groups reported higher levels of healthy diet and physical activity. Further analysis of lifestyle by type of cancer and sex, controlling for demographic and cancer-related variables, showed no significant effect of sex. Physical cancer-related symptoms among BCS were associated with a healthy diet via the mediation of fear of recurrence. CRCS had no indirect associations with a healthy diet. Maintenance of a healthy lifestyle differed by breast or colorectal cancer and was not explained by sex, warranting further investigation. Additionally, the study highlighted the role of fear of recurrence as a barrier to healthy lifestyle maintenance. These findings highlight the need for tailored interventions to address the specific challenges faced by BCS and CRCS in promoting a healthy lifestyle. Interventions should focus on the joined effects of physical cancer-related symptoms and fear of recurrence on maintaining a healthy lifestyle.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Despite the growing number of potential predictive biomarkers, molecular testing in daily oncology practice remains fragmented. The GOIM Young Translational Group conducted a survey to map the molecular testing prescription habits of oncologists across diverse Italian institutions. The survey evaluated general practices and specific tumor types-including gastrointestinal, lung, breast, genitourinary, gynecological, melanoma, and cancer of unknown primary (CUP)-exploring variations in testing frequency, technology, timing, and sample types between academic and non-academic institutions. We also evaluated logistical differences between center types and specific topics of interest, such as Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS) implementation, re-biopsy of new lesions, liquid biopsy timing/access and BRCA testing. Sixty-three responses were collected from 46 institutions, spanning diverse geographical regions and institution types. Molecular analyses are performed entirely in-house in only 40% of cases overall. A marked institutional gap emerged: 60% of academic centers perform all testing internally, compared to just 20% of non-academic centers. Academic centers also demonstrated higher participation in external quality control programs (70% vs. 50%) and more frequently served as regional hubs (60%). Furthermore, a pronounced difference was observed in hereditary cancer testing: in-house germline BRCA1/2 testing for breast cancer is available in 81% of academic institutions compared to only 13% of non-academic centers. Access to liquid biopsy varied across tumor types and center settings. In colorectal cancer, 35.7% of all institutions reported a lack of access, with non-academic centers experiencing a higher rate of non-accessibility (47.8% vs. 21.0% academic), highlighting structural disparities across practice settings. This survey provides an overview of current molecular testing practices for solid tumors among a cohort of selected Italian oncology institutions, revealing stark disparities between academic and non-academic centers. While patient-level clinical endpoints, turnaround times, and costs were not directly measured, addressing these institutional variations and supporting patient access to precision oncology will benefit from coordinated nationwide policy harmonization, structural investments in non-academic laboratory infrastructure, and the formalization of managed hub-and-spoke networks.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
This study aimed to compare perioperative results, postoperative anal function, quality of life (QoL), and long-term outcomes between conformal sphincter preservation operation (CSPO) and modified Bacon operation for ultralow rectal cancer. Patients with ultralow rectal cancer undergoing CSPO (n = 123) and modified Bacon (n = 109) were included from Changhai and Xiangya Hospital, respectively, between 2011 and 2020. Propensity score matching (PSM) and inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) were used to balanced baseline characteristics. Anal function was evaluated with Wexner scores and low anterior resection syndrome (LARS) score, and visual analog scale (VAS) for satisfaction. QoL was evaluated via EORTC QLQ-C30 and QLQ-CR38 questionnaires. After exclusions, 122 patients in the CSPO group and 108 in the modified Bacon group were analyzed. Following adjustment via PSM and IPTW, the CSPO group demonstrated a shorter operative time, postoperative hospital stay, flatus and defecation time, postoperative anal function recovery time, and better satisfaction with anal function compared to the modified Bacon group. Multivariable analysis showed that neoadjuvant radiotherapy (β=-1.184, 95% CI -1.95 to 0.42) and postoperative anal function recovery time (β=-0.184, 95% CI -0.25 to -0.12) significantly contributed to lower satisfaction with anal function. This retrospective, observational, multicenter study compared CSPO with the modified Bacon for ultralow rectal cancer. Both approaches demonstrated comparable clinical efficacy, functional outcomes, and QoL. However, CSPO showed potential advantages in perioperative recovery, postoperative anal functional recovery, and patient-reported anal function satisfaction. These findings require confirmation in prospective studies.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
To investigate the association between serum cholesterol and the occurrence of colorectal cancer (CRC), and to construct a prognostic model for CRC based on cholesterol metabolism-related genes (CMG), clarifying the model's relationship with immune infiltration. Serum cholesterol levels were compared among 3865 participants (healthy individuals, patients with intestinal diseases, and cancer patients), and risk factors for CRC were analyzed. Meanwhile, cholesterol metabolism-related genes (CMGs) were screened from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) database. LASSO regression was employed to identify key genes and construct prognostic models. Based on the median risk score, patients with colon and rectal cancers were stratified into high-risk and low-risk groups to evaluate differences in prognosis and immune characteristics. CRC patients exhibited significantly higher serum cholesterol levels than other populations (P < 0.001); total cholesterol was an independent risk factor for CRC (OR = 3.558). Prognostic models identified 9 key genes for colon adenocarcinoma (COAD) and 6 key genes for rectal adenocarcinoma (READ); overall survival was significantly lower in high-risk groups for both cancer types (P < 0.05). Immune infiltration patterns differed: in COAD, high-risk patients showed higher ESTIMATE scores and TIDE scores, with immune scores positively correlating with regulatory T cells (Tregs), macrophages, and monocytes; in READ, immune scores positively correlated with M2 macrophages, while no significant differences in ESTIMATE scores or TIDE scores were observed between risk groups. High serum cholesterol is an independent risk factor for CRC. The prognostic model based on CMGs effectively predicts patient outcomes, offering potential therapeutic targets for clinical application.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
A rectovaginal fistula (RVF) is an abnormal epithelialized connection between the rectum and vagina. Surgical repair is the treatment of choice but is challenging, particularly for fistulas in the middle and lower rectum, where conventional transabdominal or transperineal procedures offer limited access. This study describes a novel minimally invasive transanal repair (MITAR) technique for mid- and lower rectovaginal fistulas. RVF develop following vaginoplasty for a rudimentary vagina, low colorectal anastomosis for rectal carcinoma, and rectocele repair. All had preexisting protective diversion stomas. Patients were operated on under general anesthesia in the prone position. The transanal access port (Gel POINT path platform) was introduced, and the pneumorectum was maintained at 12-14 mmHg. The rectal and vaginal walls were separated at the fistula site and mobilized circumferentially along the rectovaginal septum for at least 1 cm. The mobilized vaginal and rectal walls were closed transversely one after the other through the transanal route. The diversion stoma was subsequently closed. MITAR was completed successfully in all three patients. The technique provides direct access to the fistula site. A magnified and excellent endoscopic view helped with precise and meticulous dissection. Patient recovery was uneventful. At a mean follow-up of 29 months, there was no recurrence. MITAR is a safe, feasible, and effective approach for the repair of middle and low rectovaginal fistulas. This minimally invasive technique offers excellent visualization, precision, and tension-free closure of the fistula. This technique can be considered an alternative to existing techniques for RVF repair.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Early-onset colorectal cancer (EO-CRC) is a growing global health challenge with poorly understood etiology. While gut microbiota and metabolites are implicated in colorectal carcinogenesis, EO-CRC-associated signatures remain poorly characterized. This study presents the first large-scale multi-omics analysis in Japan cohort to characterize gut microbial and metabolic features of EO-CRC, with cross-cohort validation in an independent China cohort. We enrolled 510 participants (EO-CRC n = 120, late-onset CRC [LO-CRC] n = 282, young healthy controls [yHC] n = 59, old healthy controls [oHC] n = 49); after age- and sex-matching, 324 samples were analyzed using metagenomics, metabolomics, and quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR). Fourteen species formed a shared CRC-associated microbiome core enriched in both EO-CRC and LO-CRC relative to age-matched controls, of which seven were reproducible across both Japan and China cohorts. Beyond this core, 34 and 21 species were enriched exclusively in EO-CRC and LO-CRC, respectively. Among EO-CRC-specific virulence findings, the bft gene of enterotoxigenic Bacteroides fragilis, fadA of Fusobacterium nucleatum, and bai operon genes were enriched in EO-CRC, with cross-cohort validation for fadA and bai operon, and stage-specific enrichement of deoxycholic acid at Stage 0 providing preliminary metabolomic support. Targeted clbP qPCR revealed enrichment of colibactin-producing Escherichia coli specifically in EO-CRC against a background of age-increasing carriage. Metabolomic profiling identified kynurenine enrichment and depletion of vitamin B-related metabolites (pyridoxine, riboflavin, and nicotinamide) as EO-CRC-specific findings; LO-CRC showed distinct enrichment of carnitine, succinate, and spermine with relative butyrate depletion. The choline degradation pathway was enriched specifically in EO-CRC based on Enteropathway analysis. Species-based random forest classifiers distinguished EO-CRC from controls (AUPRC = 0.828; SD = 0.013; 95% CI 0.739-0.909) and generalized robustly to an independent cohort (AUPRC = 0.817; 95% CI 0.717-0.894), substantially outperforming functional gene profiles in cross-cohort settings. Within the Japan cohort, adding metabolomics provided modest additional discriminative value. These findings identify a shared CRC microbiome core reproducible across age groups and cohorts, alongside EO-CRC-specific signatures encompassing enrichment of virulence-associated genes (bft, fadA), colibactin-producing E. coli (clbP), secondary bile acid biosynthetic genes (bai operon), and choline degradation capacity, as well as distinct metabolic perturbations including kynurenine enrichment and vitamin B-related metabolite depletion. Species-based classifiers generalize well across age groups and cohorts, with metabolomics providing complementary discriminatory value. All findings represent cross-sectional associations; longitudinal studies are needed to establish temporal ordering and evaluate clinical utility as non-invasive biomarkers for EO-CRC. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Hereditary colorectal cancer syndromes, such as Lynch syndrome and familial adenomatous polyposis, arise from pathogenic/likely pathogenic (P/LP) germline variants in DNA mismatch repair or tumor suppressor genes. Traditional Sanger sequencing could cover only phenotype-driven genes and cannot detect copy number variants (CNVs). Next-generation sequencing (NGS) enables simultaneous multi-gene analysis and CNV detection. In this study, we compared the results of phenotype-driven Sanger sequencing with those of panel-based NGS in patients suspected of having hereditary colorectal cancer syndromes at a single institution. Patients tested for hereditary colorectal cancer syndromes between 2008 and 2018 (Sanger) and 2019-2022 (NGS) were retrospectively analyzed. The NGS assay targeted 171 cancer predisposition genes, and CNVs were inferred by read-depth analysis and confirmed with multiplex ligation-dependent probe amplification. Detected variants were classified per ACMG/AMP 2015 guidelines. Microsatellite instability (MSI) and mismatch repair (MMR) immunohistochemistry (IHC) results were compared with molecular findings. Among 423 patients (254 Sanger, 169 NGS), the detection rate of pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants was higher in NGS (55.0%) than Sanger sequencing (40.6%). NGS additionally identified 17 CNVs (18.1%) that were undetectable by Sanger sequencing and revealed incidental P/LP variants in other cancer-related genes. MSI and MMR IHC results showed strong concordance with molecular findings. Panel-based NGS with CNV analysis was associated with a higher detection rate of clinically relevant variants than phenotype-driven Sanger sequencing in this single-institution cohort. These findings support the clinical utility of comprehensive germline testing for patients suspected of having hereditary colorectal cancer syndromes, particularly when CNV detection or simultaneous multi-gene analysis is required.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
In routine oncology practice, palliative care (PC) is commonly delivered through hospital-based consultation services integrated within existing workflows. Evidence describing real-world end-of-life (EOL) care patterns associated with consultation-based palliative care remains limited. We examined EOL care patterns associated with hospital-based palliative care consultation using linked clinical and nationwide data. This retrospective cohort study used linked data from a tertiary hospital and the Korean National Health Insurance Service. We included 18,048 decedents with advanced lung, stomach, colorectal, liver, or pancreaticobiliary cancer between 2018 and 2022. To minimize selection bias, 1:2 propensity score matching was performed. Outcomes included advance care planning documentation completion, aggressive EOL interventions, hospice utilization, and medical costs. After matching 4,102 patients with PC consultation and 7,910 controls, the consultation group showed significantly higher completion of advance statements (58.0% vs. 32.1%) and more patient-led decisions. During the final month of life, the consultation group had significantly fewer intensive care unit admissions (4.9% vs. 10.3%), emergency department visits (48.6% vs. 54.4%), and cardiopulmonary resuscitations (2.9% vs. 10.7%) (all P < 0.001). Hospice utilization was substantially higher in the consultation group (73.2% vs. 19.5%). Furthermore, PC consultations were associated with significantly lower medical costs during the final month and last two weeks of life. Hospital-based palliative care consultation was associated with higher rates of advance care planning and hospice use, lower use of high-intensity EOL interventions, and modestly lower medical costs. These findings suggest that consultation-based palliative care within routine oncology workflows may meaningfully influence EOL care delivery.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Artificial intelligence (AI) has achieved expert-level performance in medical imaging, but its clinical translation requires a reliable and interpretable system design. Decision-level hierarchical cascaded pipelines are widely used in medical AI, yet their benefits and limitations require further investigation. We compared decision-level hierarchical cascaded and parallel architectures in medical imaging and revealed a trade-off between error vulnerability and diagnostic transparency. Based on these observations, we developed an error-aware framework integrating automated error detection, adaptive correction, and confidence-guided human-AI collaboration. The framework was evaluated on over 10,000 patient cases, including 6,103 colorectal pathology and 7,164 cervical cytology samples, with additional validation in endoscopic and ophthalmological imaging. Decision-level hierarchical cascaded systems, although susceptible to error amplification, were more aligned with hierarchical clinical reasoning and enabled more transparent decision pathways. The proposed framework mitigated error propagation through automated detection and correction. Combined with confidence-guided human-AI collaboration, it achieved absolute accuracy gains of 16.12 and 10.11 percentage points in colorectal pathology and cervical cytology, respectively, compared with parallel systems, with consistent gains across other imaging tasks. Our study highlights the trade-off between error propagation and interpretability in hierarchical cascaded AI systems and demonstrates that error-aware design can improve their robustness and clinical applicability, contributing to the development of more reliable and human-centered medical AI.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Regorafenib is an approved later-line therapy for metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC). Combining regorafenib with PD-1/PD-L1 blockade may enhance antitumor immunity by modifying the tumor microenvironment. This meta-analysis compared the combination with regorafenib monotherapy and explored preliminary treatment signals in microsatellite-stable/proficient mismatch repair (MSS/pMMR) mCRC. A comprehensive search was performed in PubMed, Cochrane Library, Embase, Web of Science, and Chinese databases (Wanfang, VIP, CNKI, CBM) up to February 20, 2026. RCTs and RCSs comparing combination therapy with monotherapy were included. Outcomes were ORR, DCR, PFS, and OS, etc. Study quality was assessed using the Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials and the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS) for observational studies. Analyses were performed using RevMan 5.4, with RR/HR and 95% CIs. Heterogeneity was assessed using I², publication bias via funnel plots, and Egger's/Begg's tests when applicable. Evidence certainty was graded using GRADE. Eight studies (two RCTs and six RCSs; 992 patients) were included. Compared with regorafenib monotherapy, combination therapy improved ORR (RR = 1.81, 95% CI: 1.15-2.85), DCR (RR = 1.34, 95% CI: 1.10-1.62), and PR (RR = 1.66, 95% CI: 1.07-2.59), and reduced the proportion of patients with PD at tumor assessment (RR = 0.65, 95% CI: 0.50-0.86). Combination therapy was also associated with longer PFS (HR = 0.57, 95% CI: 0.37-0.87), whereas the OS estimate was borderline and did not establish a robust survival benefit (HR = 0.73, 95% CI: 0.54-1.00; P = 0.05). Post hoc exploratory analyses based on extractable MSS/pMMR data suggested possible improvements in disease control. Combination therapy was associated with increased odds of hypertension, hypothyroidism, hand-foot skin reaction, liver function abnormalities, and nausea; however, comparative evidence for grade ≥ 3 toxicity was insufficient because reporting was inconsistent. Regorafenib plus PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors may improve tumor response and PFS compared with regorafenib monotherapy in refractory mCRC, but a definitive OS advantage has not been established. The MSS/pMMR findings remain exploratory and hypothesis-generating. Adequately powered, biomarker-stratified randomized trials with standardized MSI/MMR assessment, consistent safety reporting, and longer follow-up are required before this combination can be considered a standard later-line treatment.
