ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
First Nations Australians consistently exhibit lower bowel screening participation rates than non-First Nations Australians. However, limited studies have been conducted to understand the factors associated with bowel cancer screening participation among First Nations Australians. This study aims to identify factors associated with bowel cancer screening participation among older First Nations Peoples receiving home health care services in New South Wales (NSW), Australia. A cross-sectional study among older First Nations customers receiving Australian Unity Aboriginal home health care services in NSW was conducted from June to September 2023. Data were collected through face-to-face interviews administered by trained First Nations staff, using a structured, culturally appropriate online survey. Multivariable logistic regression was performed, and adjusted odds ratios (aOR) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were reported. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05. Of 333 study participants, 72% (95% CI: 67%-77%) reported that they had ever participated in bowel cancer screening. Participants aged 50-54 (aOR = 0.29; 95% CI: 0.09-0.87), 55-59 (aOR = 0.20; 95% CI: 0.08-0.50), and 60-64 years (aOR = 0.16; 95% CI: 0.06-0.39) were less likely to participate in bowel cancer screening than participants aged 70-74. Males were less likely (aOR 0.34; 95% CI: 0.17-0.68) to participate in bowel cancer screening than females. Those who said they had been informed about bowel cancer screening were more likely (aOR: 11.1; 95% CI: 5.45-22.60) to participate in bowel cancer screening than those who said they had not been informed. Those who said they had been given a bowel cancer screening kit by their doctor to perform the test themselves were more likely (aOR: 2.29; 95% CI: 1.15-4.55) to participate in bowel cancer screening than those who said they had not been given it. Being informed about bowel cancer screening was associated with higher bowel cancer screening participation, and culturally appropriate information provision should be further evaluated in intervention studies. Younger age and being male were associated with lower bowel cancer screening participation. Efforts to promote bowel cancer screening should continue, with a particular emphasis on increasing participation among First Nations Australian men.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The impact of sex inequities in healthcare may be magnified in medical oncology, where patients and physicians often navigate life-limiting illnesses and intensive treatments. We examined the associations among patient-physician sex concordance, treatment practices, and cancer outcomes. This was a population-based, retrospective cohort study of adults diagnosed with stage II-IV lung or colon cancer in 2013-2020 in Alberta, Canada and referred to a medical oncologist. We classified patient-physician dyads as sex concordant (female-female, male-male) or discordant (female-male, male-female). We analyzed time-to-event data using Kaplan-Meier methods and associations with Cox and logistic regression models. We identified 12,047 patients treated by 209 medical oncologists. In multivariable analysis of the propensity score-matching (PSM) cohort, sex concordance was not independently associated with overall survival (OS) or cancer-specific survival (CSS) in the overall cohort and in female patients. But among male stage IV patients treated by female physicians, sex discordance was significantly associated with lower OS and CSS (p = 0.02). Upon propensity score-matching, more oncologists prescribing systemic therapy for stage II-III disease were female (25.8% vs. 22.6%, p = 0.02), whereas in stage IV disease, more prescribing oncologists were male (64.7% vs. 57.9%, p < 0.001). Sex discordance was not associated with worse OS or CSS among the overall cohort. Cancer management and outcomes may be prone to the effects of sex bias in specific patient-physician relationships.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Rectal cancer (RC) is a common and lethal malignant tumor, and surgical treatment is essential. The collateral system between the superior mesenteric artery (SMA) and inferior mesenteric artery (IMA) remains controversial, and its potential clinical significance in RC has not been fully clarified. This study aimed to preliminarily explore and classify this collateral system and its clinical roles in laparoscopic RC surgery. This single-center retrospective study enrolled patients who underwent laparoscopic radical resection for RC at Fuyang City People's Hospital from January 2022 to March 2026. Based on arterial-phase contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) images, three-dimensional (3D) reconstructions of the SMA, IMA, and splenic flexure inter-mesenteric anastomosis (SF-ImA) were performed using 3D Slicer. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were conducted to evaluate risk factors for anastomotic leakage (AL). Subgroup analysis was further performed to evaluate the potential clinical value of SF-ImA in laparoscopic RC surgery. SF-ImA was detected in 60.10% of RC patients, including 13.94% with central mesocolic anastomosis and 46.15% with intermediate mesocolic anastomosis. The tumor location (low vs. high, OR: 13.377; 95% CI: 2.262-259.500, P = 0.018), N stage (OR: 1.339; 95% CI: 1.095-14.183, P = 0.038), and surgical duration (OR: 1.026; 95% CI: 1.013-1.042, P = 0.001) were independent risk factors for AL. Preserving left colic artery (LCA) (OR: 0.206; 95% CI: 0.062-0.611, P = 0.006) was an independent protective factor. Subgroup analysis confirmed that LCA preservation exerted a protective effect against AL exclusively in patients without SF-ImA (OR: 0.041, 95% CI: 0.002-0.357, P = 0.012). For patients with SF-ImA, LCA preservation may fail to confer a protective effect against AL and was associated with longer operative duration (P < 0.05). SF-ImA can be effectively evaluated and classified via contrast-enhanced CT combined with 3D reconstruction. Preoperative assessment of SF-ImA may assist individualized surgical planning for RC patients.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Oxaliplatin is a first-line chemotherapeutic agent for colorectal carcinoma (CRC). However, its therapeutic efficacy is often curtailed due to severe side effects and development of drug resistance. Norcantharidin (NCTD) has shown antitumor activity in preclinical studies of colorectal cancer and other malignancies. It also has been utilized as a chemosensitizer in studies of various cancer cell lines in vitro. However, its clinical efficacy in patients with CRC, particularly in combination with oxaliplatin, has not been established. Both of oxaliplatin and NCTD could enhance the reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels in tumor cells. Yet, it remains unclear whether NCTD can augment the sensitivity of CRC cells to oxaliplatin via ROS generation. Given that macrophage polarization is closely associated with tumor cell death and tumor progression, the effects of NCTD and oxaliplatin-induced cell death on macrophage polarization was studied as well. This study used CCK8 assays to investigate the synergistic effects of oxaliplatin and NCTD in CRC cells. ROS and immunofluorescence staining was applied to detect ROS levels and DNA damage levels in CRC cells when treated by oxaliplatin and NCTD. Western blotting and ELISA were applied to determine the levels of proteins in CRC cells. The conditioned media were collected from CRC cell cultures and were used to treat the macrophage cell line RAW264.7 to explore its polarization. Finally, a subcutaneous tumor model was applied to study the effects of oxaliplatin and NCTD on CRC cells in vivo. The in vitro experiments demonstrated the synergistic lethal effects of NCTD and oxaliplatin on CRC cells. Mechanistic investigations revealed that the combination of NCTD and oxaliplatin enhanced reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels, which in turn triggered CRC cell death resembling pyroptosis, which was associated with DNA damage/caspase-3/GSDME. More importantly, the pyroptosis-like cell death (PLCD) in CRC cells induced by the combination of NCTD and oxaliplatin conspicuously shifted M1 polarization of macrophages, which might contribute to the hindrance of tumor progression. The results of animal experiments corroborated those of experiments in vitro. Our data indicate synergistic effects of NCTD and oxaliplatin in CRC models, warranting additional research to characterize the underlying mechanisms and evaluate its translational potential.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) and colorectal liver metastasis (CRLM) posed significant challenges in cancer management. To develop more effective therapies, we investigated the role of Farnesoid X Receptor (FXR, Nr1h4) in the tumor-liver microenvironment, an area with substantial therapeutic potential that had been underexplored. Employing preclinical mouse models of CRLM, we conducted a comprehensive evaluation of FXR expression and its functional significance in modulating the tumor-liver microenvironment. Techniques utilized included histological analysis, single-cell sequencing, immunohistochemistry (IHC), flow cytometry (FCM), and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Antibody depletion experiments, as well as the use of inhibitors and antagonists, were conducted to elucidate the mechanisms underlying FXR's role in colorectal cancer liver metastases. Our findings indicated that FXR knockout or treatment with Ursodeoxycholic Acid (UDCA) promoted CRLM. Single-cell sequencing, FCM, and antibody depletion experiments revealed that FXR affected CRLM prognosis by altering the liver microenvironment, with myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs) identified as the primary cellular mediators in this process. Mechanistically, the gutFXR-FGF15-PPARγ-VEGFα-MDSC axis played a crucial role in MDSC accumulation, thereby promoting liver metastasis of colon cancer. Our study uncovered a novel function of FXR in regulating the liver microenvironment and influencing CRLM progression. Targeting the gutFXR-FGF15-PPARγ-VEGFα-MDSC axis may offer a promising therapeutic strategy for the prevention and treatment of CRLM.

This study aimed to evaluate the reliability and validity of the Modified Chinese version of the CCF-CaQL and its applicability in the Chinese population. Data analyses were performed using R (version 4.3.3). Questionnaire reliability was assessed using Cronbach's alpha and composite reliability, with additional reliability evaluated using Spearman's correlation coefficient and the split-half method. Construct validity was examined using confirmatory factor analysis (CFA), with convergent validity assessed based on factor loadings and discriminant validity evaluated using the heterotrait-monotrait (HTMT) ratio. A total of 215 patients undergoing colorectal cancer surgery were included in this study. The revised questionnaire demonstrated high internal consistency, with a Cronbach's alpha coefficient of 0.882 and composite reliability (CR) values exceeding 0.70 for all factors. Confirmatory factor analysis showed acceptable convergent validity, with all factors yielding average variance extracted (AVE) values greater than 0.40 and CR values ranging from 0.769 to 0.890. The HTMT coefficients indicated adequate discriminant validity, with most values below the recommended threshold of 0.85 and only one slightly above (0.887). All factors were significantly correlated with the total questionnaire score, with correlation coefficients ranging from 0.508 to 0.855. Furthermore, the questionnaire showed strong correlations with the Chinese versions of the EORTC QLQ-C30 and QLQ-CR29. The modified Chinese version of the CCF-CaQL exhibited strong psychometric properties, confirming its validity and reliability as a disease-specific tool for evaluating quality of life in colorectal cancer patients. This study is the first to translate and validate the CCF-CaQL in Chinese, filling a gap in validated tools for assessing postoperative quality of life in patients with colorectal cancer. The availability of this instrument enables reliable clinical and research applications in Chinese-speaking populations.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Anorectal manometry (ARM) provides objective physiological information on anal sphincter function, rectal or neorectal sensation, reservoir capacity, and anorectal reflexes after rectal cancer surgery. In rectal cancer surgery, ARM has been used to evaluate functional changes after sphincter-preserving procedures, reconstruction with colonic J-pouch, neoadjuvant radiotherapy, and postoperative bowel dysfunction, including low anterior resection syndrome (LARS). This review summarizes the clinical applications of ARM in rectal cancer surgery, with emphasis on historical and contemporary manometric parameters, their relationship with patient-reported outcomes, and their limitations in postoperative functional assessment. Although several studies have reported associations between manometric findings and bowel dysfunction, the clinical interpretation of ARM remains limited by heterogeneity in measurement protocols, equipment dependency, timing of assessment, and variable correlation with quality-of-life measures. Recent advances, including high-resolution manometry and standardized testing protocols, may improve the reliability and clinical utility of ARM. ARM may provide adjunctive physiological information in selected patients and research settings, but current evidence does not support its use as a stand-alone diagnostic test for LARS or as a routine treatment-decision tool.

The role of mast cells in colorectal cancer (CRC) liver metastasis remains controversial. This study aimed to explore the effect of mast cells on the CRC liver metastasis and the underlying mechanism. BTG1 knockdown enhances tumorigenicity in vitro and promoted liver metastasis in vivo, these effects partially reversed by JUN inhibition. BTG1 acts as a tumor suppressor in CRC by directly binding to JUN and promoting its degradation, thereby restraining oncogenic signaling.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Homologous recombination (HR) is one of the classical pathways for repairing DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs), a type of lesion that poses a severe threat to genomic stability and cell survival. The role of small nucleolar RNAs (snoRNAs), particularly their interactions with ribosomal proteins, in the HR repair has not been reported. This is the first study to report the role of snoRNA genes SNORD18B and SNORD18C (SNORD18B/C) in HR repair, demonstrating that they exert an oncogenic function in colorectal cancer (CRC) by promoting cell proliferation and radioresistance. Mechanistically, SNORD18B/C directly interacts with the ribosomal protein RPL23A to enhance the translation of BRCA1 independent of the canonical 2'-O-methylation of 28S rRNA, thereby promoting HR efficiency to facilitate radiation-induced DSB repair. Collectively, our findings confirm that the SNORD18B/C-RPL23A-BRCA1 axis is crucial for HR repair and highlight the SNORD18B/C as potential CRC therapeutic targets.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The incidence rate of colorectal cancer is on the rise in Iran. Although the precise etiology of colorectal cancer remains unknown, high-risk human papillomaviruses (HPVs) are suggested as potential contributors to the pathogenesis of colorectal cancer. Information on the prevalence of HPV infection among patients with colorectal cancer can affect targeted prevention and management strategies by improving region-specific screening strategies and HPV vaccination. Therefore, this study was designed to detect high-risk HPVs in colorectal cancer tissue specimens in the South of Iran. Colorectal biopsy samples from 147 patients with colorectal cancer and 144 non-cancerous patients with colorectal inflammation and polyps were tested for the detection of HPVs by nested PCR assay. High-risk HPVs were detected in 2 samples of 128 colorectal cancer samples (1.56%, 95% CI: 0.48%-5.49%), while the non-cancerous colorectal samples were HPV negative. HPV-positive patients were identified in the age group ≥ 80 years (8.33%) and the age group 70-79 years (5.26%), while the age groups < 70 years did not show HPV positivity. The frequency of HPV infection was approximately equal in both genders (1.54% in males and 1.59% in females). HPV DNA was detected in 9.09% of patients resident in Ahram and 4.35% of patients resident in Khormoj, whereas the residents of Bushehr, Borazjan, Dayer, Genaveh, and Kangan were negative for HPV infection. The prevalence of HPV infection among patients with colorectal cancer was not statistically associated with age, gender, and place of residency. Although the patients with rectal adenocarcinoma (3.33%) showed a higher rate of HPV positivity compared to the patients with colon adenocarcinoma (1.02%), the frequency of HPV infection was not significantly associated with the anatomical location of colorectal cancer. This study, despite detecting HPVs in 1.56% of colorectal cancer biopsy specimens, cannot determine the possible association between HPV infection and colorectal carcinogenesis in the South of Iran. The causal relationship between HPV infection and colorectal cancer appears to be influenced by environmental and individual risk factors, the genetic backgrounds, as well as the regional epidemiology of HPV infection.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Chronic diseases are a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, with prevalence rising because of lifestyle factors and increasing life expectancy. In developing countries, including Jordan, these conditions pose growing health and economic burdens. This systematic review assessed available literature on the economic burden of chronic diseases in Jordan. Following PRISMA guidelines, we searched Medline PubMed, Embase, PubMed Central, and Scopus, supplemented by Google/Google Scholar and reference lists, for studies reporting direct medical costs of chronic diseases in Jordan. Titles, abstracts, and full texts were screened independently by two reviewers. Study characteristics and mean annual per-patient costs were extracted and verified. Costs were standardized to per-patient, per-year estimates in 2025 USD, including outpatient, inpatient, diagnostic, emergency, and medication expenses. The quality of included studies was assessed using the adapted version of Drummond checklist for economic studies. Database search identified 147 records. After removal of one duplicate record, 146 records were screened, and 19 full-text articles were assessed for eligibility. Ultimately, eleven studies were included. They reported costs for cancers, diabetic retinopathy, severe renal disease, thalassaemia, paediatric asthma, and multiple sclerosis, mostly using retrospective designs. Mean annual costs ranged from $35 to $30,567 (2025 USD), and the greatest costs were for end-stage renal disease. Of cancer studied, breast cancer and colorectal cancer were associated with substantial annual direct medical costs, although estimates varied considerably between studies because of differences in disease populations, data sources, and cost methodologies. The mean annual cost for all conditions was $10,035 (2025 USD). When weighted against the sample sizes, the pooled mean cost was $6,914 USD. The overall quality of included studies was judged to be moderate, with most studies clearly defining study populations, disease conditions, and data sources used for cost estimation. Chronic kidney disease, breast cancer, and multiple sclerosis imposed substantial medical costs in Jordan. Evidence for other major conditions was limited, highlighting the need for further research to guide health care planning, resource allocation, and cost-effective chronic disease management.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Natural orifice specimen extraction (NOSE) eliminates the abdominal extraction incision after minimally invasive (MIS) colorectal resection and offers favourable short-term recovery, but transanal extraction raises concerns regarding sphincter stretch and anorectal dysfunction. This review evaluated anorectal functional outcomes after transanal NOSE compared with transabdominal specimen extraction (TASE) in MIS colorectal cancer surgery. MEDLINE and EMBASE were searched from inception to August 2024 for comparative studies reporting postoperative anorectal or pelvic floor functional outcomes following transanal NOSE versus TASE. The primary outcome was anorectal continence at the postoperative interval closest to 6 months. Ten retrospective cohort studies were included, of which seven (1362 patients) contributed quantitative data for meta-analysis. Three studies contributed to the pooled Wexner incontinence score analysis and four to the pooled Pelvic Floor Distress Inventory short form (PFDI-20) analysis. At the interval closest to 6 months, Wexner scores were numerically higher after transanal NOSE than TASE, but the difference was small and non-significant (MD 0.17, 95% CI - 0.01 to 0.35; p = 0.07). PFDI-20 scores did not differ between groups (MD - 0.02, 95% CI - 0.21 to 0.18; p = 0.86). Both estimates were robust in leave-one-out and overlap-adjusted analyses excluding potentially overlapping Harbin Medical University cohorts. Early differences appeared to diminish over time, with no clear separation beyond 12 months. Transanal NOSE was associated with a small, non-significant trend toward higher early Wexner scores after MIS colorectal cancer surgery, while broader pelvic floor symptom burden appeared comparable to TASE. The difference was of uncertain clinical significance, was robust to sensitivity analyses, and longer-term data suggested no persistent functional disadvantage.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The gut microbiome can influence cancer susceptibility, progression, and treatment response. Microbes shape carcinogenesis through direct genotoxicity, epithelial barrier disruption, sustained inflammation, immune modulation, and the biotransformation of diet-derived substrates into bioactive metabolites. Diet is an important modifiable determinant of microbial community composition and function: Western dietary patterns may favour pro-carcinogenic microbial activities, whereas plant-rich, fibre-dense diets can support saccharolytic fermentation and commensal functions. These effects depend on substrate availability, microbial strain and host context. This review centres on colorectal and gastric cancers, with selected evidence from hepatocellular, pancreatic, breast and head-and-neck malignancies. Establishing causality remains central: most human evidence is associative, and mechanistic or interventional evidence is required for therapeutic or preventive translation. This review summarises the mechanistic roles of specific bacterial pathobionts, commensals and fungi across these cancer types, distinguishes observational, experimental and clinical interventional evidence for diet-microbiome interactions, and identifies translational priorities.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
With the rising global prevalence of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) and improved patient longevity, the burden of colitis-associated colorectal cancer (CAC) is increasing. Patients with IBD have a higher risk of developing colorectal cancer (CRC) compared with the general population and are typically diagnosed at a younger age than those with sporadic CRC. This elevated risk is driven by chronic and recurrent inflammatory injury to the intestinal mucosa, which plays a central mechanistic role in carcinogenesis. In contrast to the adenoma-carcinoma sequence observed in sporadic CRC, CAC arises through a distinct inflammation-dysplasia-carcinoma pathway with persistent inflammation initiating and promoting tumorigenesis. Evidence strongly implicates the gut microbiota as being a risk factor in both IBD and CRC. This review synthesises current evidence on the role of the gut microbiota across IBD, CRC and CAC, with a particular focus on the impact of IBD therapeutics on colitis-associated carcinogenesis and the intersection with gut microbiota changes. We identify critical gaps in mechanistic understanding and emphasise the urgent need for mechanism-driven, personalised strategies to enable meaningful clinical translation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The gastrointestinal microbiome has emerged as a critical interface between environmental exposures and host biology, shaping carcinogenesis, tumor behavior, and therapeutic responsiveness across digestive tract malignancies. This narrative review synthesizes current evidence on microbiome testing in esophageal, gastric, colorectal, hepatobiliary, pancreatic, and gastrointestinal stromal cancers, highlighting microbial signatures, emerging translational applications, and the methodological challenges that currently limit clinical implementation. Tumor-specific microbial alterations are considered alongside the broader functional consequences of dysbiosis, including its roles in genotoxicity, immune modulation, and metabolic reprogramming. Particular attention is given to the influence of the microbiome on systemic therapies, especially immune checkpoint inhibition, where microbial diversity, compositional signatures, and antibiotic exposure have been associated with differences in treatment efficacy. Emerging mechanistic insights are highlighted, including the role of microbiota-derived metabolites as key mediators of host-tumor immune interactions. The review further discusses microbiome-directed interventions, including fecal microbiota transplantation and dietary modulation, while critically evaluating the barriers to their clinical translation. Although microbiome profiling has considerable potential to improve risk stratification and therapeutic personalization, current evidence remains largely associative or based on early-phase clinical studies, and no microbiome-based testing strategy has yet been validated for routine clinical use beyond Helicobacter pylori eradication for gastric cancer prevention. Large prospective studies, standardized methodologies, and interventional clinical trials are required before microbiome testing can be integrated into routine precision oncology.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Fusobacterium nucleatum (F. nucleatum) is a Gram-negative anaerobic bacterium of the normal human microbiota, originally identified in the oral cavity but now recognised as a constituent of the intratumoural microbiome across a broad range of human malignancies. This structured narrative review summarises the human evidence for F. nucleatum in different tumour entities. Within little more than a decade, F. nucleatum has become one of the most extensively characterised tumour-associated bacteria. Its DNA has been detected in every entity covered here, and in colorectal cancer a substantial and reproducible body of work links intratumoural F. nucleatum to shorter survival across independent cohorts, populations and detection platforms, increasingly resolved to subspecies and clade level. Evidence in other entities is younger and more heterogeneous: several show comparable associations, whereas in oral squamous cell carcinoma F. nucleatum positivity has been linked to improved outcomes. Rather than undermining the field, this heterogeneity points to a context-dependent biology shaped by tumour type and molecular subtype, specimen, detection method and threshold, and treatment setting. Mechanistic work provides a coherent basis for these observations. In experimental models, the adhesins FadA and Fap2 mediate interactions with host cells that promote proliferative signalling, immune evasion and metastatic spread, and bacterial depletion attenuates tumour growth - proof of principle for a targetable microbial component of the tumour. F. nucleatum is therefore a compelling candidate for microbiome-informed oncology. Realising this potential requires standardised assays, validated cut-offs and prospective trials.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The pathogenesis of colorectal cancer (CRC) is inextricably linked to the gut microbiome. However, research has historically concentrated on the bacteriome, leaving the gut virome (predominantly composed of bacteriophages) largely unexplored as biological "dark matter". Recent advancements have illuminated the dual regulatory role of phages within the tumor microenvironment (TME), where they intricately modulate both bacterial community dynamics and host immune responses. This review synthesizes current evidence on viral dysbiosis throughout CRC progression and evaluates the translational potential of virome signatures as highly specific, non-invasive diagnostic and prognostic biomarkers. We then explore emerging virome-based interventions, including precision phage therapies, aimed at reshaping the TME and enhancing synergistic responses to conventional treatments and immunotherapy. To propel the field from correlative observations to actionable clinical applications, significant translational hurdles must be overcome. We highlight the urgent need for standardized bioinformatics pipelines to address reproducibility challenges and emphasize the utility of advanced, culture-independent methodologies like single-cell viral tagging to accurately map host-phage interaction networks. Finally, we advocate for the integration of large-animal models, such as CRC pig models, to validate the causal roles and longitudinal dynamics of the virome, ultimately bridging the gap between basic exploration and precision gastrointestinal oncology.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Guidelines recommend cold snare polypectomy (CSP) for colorectal polyps 10 mm or smaller, but data for larger polyps are limited. We compared delayed post-polypectomy bleeding (DPPB) and resection outcomes after CSP versus conventional endoscopic mucosal resection (EMR) for polyps 15 mm or smaller. We retrospectively analysed 2,673 polyps from 2,083 patients undergoing screening or surveillance colonoscopy between January 2022 and December 2025 (CSP, 1,726; EMR, 947). DPPB was defined as post-discharge bleeding requiring an emergency department visit, hospitalization, transfusion or repeat endoscopy; every candidate event was audited against this definition. One-to-one propensity score matching on seven covariates yielded 652 pairs. Because no bleeding followed CSP (complete separation), the matched analysis was interpreted alongside full-cohort Firth penalized regression, inverse-probability weighting and a patient-level analysis. Follow-up was 30 days. Six DPPB events met the definition, all after EMR (6/947, 0.6%); four further post-discharge bleeds were self-limited and met no criterion. All six events were right-sided. In the matched cohort DPPB occurred in 0/652 versus 2/652 (0.3%; p = 0.50) - underpowered. In the full cohort the difference was significant (0/1,726 versus 6/947; p = 0.002); Firth penalized regression gave an adjusted odds ratio of 14.6 for EMR (95% confidence interval 1.1-201; p = 0.045) - a very wide, imprecise estimate. Larger polyp size independently predicted bleeding (adjusted odds ratio 1.36 per mm; p = 0.002). At patient level, DPPB occurred in 0 of 1,258 CSP-only and 5 of 702 EMR-only patients (0.7%; p = 0.006); the sixth arose from an EMR polyp among 123 patients treated by both. En bloc resection with a tumour-free margin was similar (98.6% versus 99.7%; p = 0.064); CSP required less clipping (40.6% versus 54.8%) and shorter procedures (16.9 versus 20.9 min; both p < 0.001). Delayed bleeding was infrequent, and none followed CSP. The matched comparison was underpowered, whereas full-cohort, adjusted, weighted and patient-level analyses consistently favoured CSP. Given the few events, the wide confidence interval and the retrospective single-centre design, these findings are hypothesis-generating rather than evidence of superiority and require prospective confirmation. Larger polyp size independently predicted bleeding, so caution is warranted for larger lesions.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy is a common and burdensome adverse effect of oxaliplatin-based chemotherapy in patients with colorectal cancer. The Functional Assessment of Cancer Therapy/Gynecologic Oncology Group-Neurotoxicity subscale is used to assess neurotoxicity symptoms, but evidence regarding its psychometric performance and measurement invariance in Chinese patients remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate the psychometric properties and measurement invariance of the Chinese version of the FACT/GOG-Ntx13 in patients with colorectal cancer receiving oxaliplatin-based chemotherapy. A longitudinal quantitative survey was conducted among 534 Chinese patients with colorectal cancer. Data were collected one month and three months after the initiation of chemotherapy. Exploratory factor analysis, confirmatory factor analysis, measurement invariance testing, criterion validity analysis, and internal consistency reliability analysis were performed. Exploratory factor analysis supported a one-factor structure, which was further confirmed by confirmatory factor analysis with acceptable model fit at both time points. The scale demonstrated good criterion-related validity through its positive correlation with the EORTC QLQ-CIPN20 and showed good internal consistency at both assessments. Measurement invariance across gender was supported at configural, metric, and scalar levels. Longitudinally, configural and metric invariance were supported, whereas scalar invariance was not. The Chinese version of the FACT/GOG-Ntx13 is a valid and reliable instrument for assessing oxaliplatin-induced peripheral neuropathy in patients with colorectal cancer. However, changes in scores over time should be interpreted cautiously because longitudinal scalar invariance was not supported.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Gastrointestinal (GI) cancers represent a highly lethal subset of human malignancies. Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains the most prevalent subtype, representing the second-leading cause of cancer death in the USA, with rising incidence in younger adults. To improve outcomes for patients with GI malignancies, use of assays to monitor clinically undetectable molecular residual disease (MRD) via the analysis of circulating tumor DNA has become commonplace. However, rigorous studies evaluating the utility of MRD assays have lagged behind their widespread clinical adoption in the USA. We provide a narrative review of clinical studies characterizing the prognostic performance of MRD assays for patients with non-metastatic CRC and evaluate the evidence supporting use of MRD testing to de-escalate or intensify treatment. We additionally highlight emerging evidence and ongoing studies in populations of special interest, including patients with microsatellite instability-high disease and patients with a targetable molecular alteration. Finally, we summarize emerging MRD data for pancreatic, gastroesophageal, and hepatobiliary malignancies. This review offers a comprehensive evaluation of current MRD evidence for GI malignancies and outlines future pivotal trials that will ultimately inform guidelines and direct patient management.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Patients with thymic epithelial tumors (TETs) are predisposed to autoimmune dis-eases, immunodeficiencies, and extrathymic malignancies. Still, the timing of these conditions relative to TET diagnosis and their prognostic significance remain poorly characterized. This nationwide study included all Danish patients diagnosed with TETs from 2015 to 2020. Data on demographics, tumor subtype, autoimmune diseases, immunodeficiencies, malig-nancies, follow-up, and survival were collected from electronic medical records. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize patient characteristics and disease chronology, while Kaplan-Meier analyses and log-rank tests were applied to assess associating with survival. Among 282 patients with a median age of 66 years, thymoma accounted for 85% of cases, thymic carcinoma for 14%, and thymic neuroendocrine tumors for 1.4%. Prior to TET diagnosis, 105 (37.2%) patients had a previous cancer diagnosis and 88 (31.2%) had autoim-mune disease. Over a median follow-up of 65 months, 33 (11.7%) patients developed new auto-immune diseases, and 41 (14.5%) patients developed new extrathymic cancers. The pattern of malignancies differed over time, with skin and colorectal cancers predominating before TET diagnosis, while lymphoma and prostate cancer were most frequent afterward. Myasthenia gravis was the leading autoimmune disease both before and after TET diagnosis, while Good's syndrome occurred only after diagnosis in six patients. Pre-existing autoimmune disease and pre-existing extrathymic cancer were not significantly associated with overall survival. A substantial burden of autoimmune and malignant disease was observed among patients with TETs, predominated by myasthenia gravis. Pre-existing paraneoplastic diseases were not associated with survival. A trend was observed in the incidence of certain disorders suggesting a shift in the pattern of developed paraneoplastic diseases after TET diagnosis.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Although upfront surgery followed by adjuvant chemotherapy is the standard of care for locally advanced colon cancer (LACC), high rates of recurrence and surgical morbidity remain significant challenges in bulky T4 tumors. Neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) is gaining traction to improve downstaging and resectability. Although doublet regimens (FOLFOX/CAPOX) are established, the use of the intensive triplet regimen FOLFOXIRI in the neoadjuvant setting for nonmetastatic LACC is less common because of toxicity concerns and limited clinical data. A 55-year-old male presented with a bulky, obstructive, right-sided colonic mass (cT4bN+M0). Given the high-risk features and the need for significant cytoreduction in a resource-limited setting where molecular profiling was unavailable, neoadjuvant FOLFOXIRI was initiated. After six cycles, the patient achieved an 85% reduction in tumor volume and normalization of tumor markers (CEA/CA19-9). Despite experiencing manageable Grade 3 neutropenia and anorexia, he underwent successful R0 resection. Histopathology confirmed significant downstaging to ypT2pN0 (0/12), reflecting a near-complete pathological response. Following four cycles of adjuvant CAPOX, the patient remains disease-free at 1.5 years. Neoadjuvant FOLFOXIRI can achieve significant downstaging in bulky tumors and facilitates R0 resection in selected high-risk LACC patients, even in resource-limited settings. Despite requiring careful management of treatment toxicities, triplet NAC offers exploratory, hypothesis-generating option for first colon cancer patients with T4 primary tumors, and can be further supported with future large clinical data.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Macrophages in colorectal cancer (CRC) are predominantly derived from monocytes, yet the mechanisms by which the tumor microenvironment (TME) regulates their differentiation dynamics and phenotypic commitment remains poorly defined. Although we previously identified ANKRD22 as a macrophage immunomodulator, the regulation of ANKRD22 by the TME and its temporal impact on monocyte‒macrophage differentiation are still unclear. We used untargeted metabolomics and cytokine microarrays to identify metabolites and cytokines from CRC cell supernatants that suppress ANKRD22 expression in macrophages. Immune infiltration in tumors was evaluated using cytometry by time-of-flight. The effects of ANKRD22 downregulation on monocyte-to-macrophage differentiation were investigated using scRNA-seq, scATAC-seq, and multiplex immunofluorescence staining. CRC cell-derived metabolites and cytokines downregulated ANKRD22 expression in macrophages via the p38 MAPK/MAX pathway. ANKRD22 downregulation reprograms fatty acid metabolism to activate the Notch4/HES1 pathway, promoting immunosuppressive macrophage polarization. ANKRD22 is a key regulator of macrophage plasticity and a promising therapeutic target for reprogramming the immunosuppressive TME in CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Metformin exerts anticancer effects by targeting various cancer cells while also providing anti-inflammatory and antioxidant benefits. Inflammation is a complex process involving the release of soluble factors such as cytokines. Among these, IL-6 plays a pivotal role in mediating chronic inflammation and promoting tumour growth, thereby contributing to cancer progression. Patients with advanced or metastatic colon cancer exhibit elevated serum IL-6 levels. The autophagic process serves a dual role in colorectal carcinogenesis, partly promoting and partly inhibiting tumour growth. However, there are currently no reliable data on the role of autophagy in colorectal cancer. The present study evaluated the impact of metformin on normal human colonic cells. The viability of colonocytes from healthy donors was assessed, and the effects of metformin on inflammation and autophagy were investigated using immunofluorescence, western blot analysis, and real-time PCR evaluation of MAPLC3, IL-6, and BCL2 mRNA expression levels. Metformin did not affect the viability of normal colonocytes. Moreover, it exerted both anti-inflammatory and anti-autophagic effects on these cells, as evidenced by downregulation of IL-6 and MAPLC3 expression at both the protein and mRNA levels, while maintaining cell viability as shown by BCL2 expression. These observations support the hypothesis of cellular selectivity of metformin, suggesting that it may exert differential effects on cancer versus normal cells. Metformin appears to attenuate autophagy in healthy cells while potentially driving apoptosis or autophagy in tumour cells, representing a strategy to minimise damage to normal tissue while effectively targeting cancerous cells.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Endothelial cell-specific molecule-1 (ESM1, also known as endocan), is a sulfated proteoglycan primarily secreted by vascular endothelial cells, although it can also be expressed by tumor cells and stromal cells. Since its overexpression in multiple tumors was systematically confirmed in 2006, ESM1 has become a research hotspot as a tumor biomarker and therapeutic target. This review systematically elaborates on the role of ESM1 in tumors at three levels. First, we analyze the multilayered regulatory mechanisms underlying its upregulation, including transcription factor activation, growth factor and inflammatory signaling, epigenetic modifications, and non-coding RNA regulation, as well as induction by the metabolic microenvironment and pathogen infection. Second, we clarify the dual biological functions of ESM1. In most tumors, ESM1 drives malignant progression through five major dimensions: angiogenesis, malignant behavior and epithelial-mesenchymal transition, metabolic reprogramming, therapeutic resistance, and immune remodeling. Limited evidence suggests that ESM1 may exert antitumor effects in specific contexts, such as prostate cancer, gastric cancer, colon cancer, and non-glycosylated forms of ESM1; however, such evidence is far less abundant than that supporting its pro-tumorigenic role, and its determinants: tumor type, cell source, glycosylation status, disease stage, and experimental model remain unclear. Finally, we evaluate its clinical translational value. As a diagnostic biomarker and prognostic indicator, ESM1 can be detected in various body fluids and is associated with tumor invasion, metastasis, and survival. However, current diagnostic and prognostic evidence is largely retrospective, single-center, and based on non-standardized detection methods. Circulating ESM1 is also confounded by infection, inflammation, tissue damage and bone marrow regeneration, and its cross-cancer diagnostic value has not yet been confirmed. As a therapeutic target, anti-ESM1 strategies show promising prospects for reversing drug resistance and combination therapy, but prospective clinical validation, safety assessment, and evidence for the feasibility of tumor-selective targeting are still lacking. In addition, ESM1 of endothelial origin and ESM1 of tumor or stromal origin may differ in functional interpretation and biomarker interpretation, yet most existing studies have not rigorously distinguished between these sources. In summary, ESM1 is a key molecular node integrating tumor angiogenesis, immune evasion, and therapeutic resistance, and its clinical translational potential as a circulating biomarker and targeted therapy warrants further exploration.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Lysine crotonylation(Kcr), an important protein post-translational modification, establishes a connection between cellular metabolism and epigenetic regulation. This modification utilizes crotonyl-CoA as a donor and is co-regulated by "writers", "erasers" and "readers". Furthermore, it participates in key biological processes including gene transcription, metabolic reprogramming, DNA damage repair, and remodeling of the tumor immune microenvironment. Recent studies have demonstrated that crotonylation is dysregulated in various malignant tumors, including breast cancer, colorectal cancer, liver cancer, lung cancer, and glioma. It drives tumor proliferation, invasion, metastasis, and drug resistance by influencing metabolic enzyme activity, chromatin status, DNA repair efficiency, and immune signaling pathways. Lysine crotonylation demonstrates significant environmental-dependence across different cancers; Not only can it promote the malignant phenotype of tumor cells, but it can also potentiate the response to immunotherapy under specific metabolic conditions. Preclinical studies have explored therapeutic strategies targeting tumor crotonylation, including metabolic interventions, enzymatic regulation, and combination immunotherapy; however, these approaches remain investigational and have not been clinically validated. This narrative review summarizes the molecular mechanisms, biological functions, and current advances of crotonylation in diverse malignancies, and highlights unresolved questions and emerging therapeutic hypotheses.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Accurate data on microsatellite instability (MSI) in second primary colorectal cancer (CRC) are needed for precision oncology and guideline development. This study includes structured clinicopathological records from 77 cancer survivors diagnosed with second primary CRC. Variables encompass demographics, prior malignancy and treatment history, tumor location, histology, MSI status assessed via immunohistochemistry and polymerase chain reaction (PCR), and timing between malignancies. Data were systematically extracted following clear inclusion and exclusion criteria, with standardized definitions and quality checks. MSI status was determined using staining for four mismatch repair proteins, with PCR confirmation for equivocal results. The dataset's structure ensures accessibility, interoperability, and reproducibility. It enables analyses of MSI prevalence, anatomical predictors, and clinical associations in second primary CRC, supporting secondary research on risk factors, biomarker correlates, and population-level outcomes.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
BackgroundColorectal cancer (CRC) remains a major cause of morbidity and mortality in Portugal. Limited health literacy (HL) is a determinant of unequal access to colorectal cancer screening (CRCS), influencing knowledge, beliefs, and adherence. Promoting HL at the community level may enhance informed decision-making and participation in CRCS.ObjectiveTo describe and evaluate a community-based nursing intervention, grounded in the Health Planning methodology, aimed at improving HL related to colorectal cancer screening among individuals without access to a family health team in a Public Health Unit (PHU) in the Lisbon region.MethodsA community-based intervention study was conducted between October 2022 and March 2023, following the Health Planning methodology. Baseline HL was assessed using the validated HLS19-Q12 questionnaire, complemented by sociodemographic data, in a convenience sample of 54 individuals aged 50-74 years. Based on the situational diagnosis, educational strategies were developed, including a nursing-led video, posters with QR-code access, and health professional guidance. A separate anonymous post-intervention questionnaire was administered between January 6 and February 15, 2023. Thirty responses were received; 28 respondents were eligible for CRCS and included in the post-intervention descriptive analysis. Because post-intervention responses were not individually linked to baseline HLS19-Q12 responses, paired pre-post analysis was not performed.ResultsAt baseline, 29% of participants had excellent HL, 44% sufficient, 23% problematic, and 4% inadequate. The most critical domain was Disease Prevention, particularly access to information. In the post-intervention evaluation (n = 28 eligible respondents), 22 participants (78.6%) reported improved knowledge about CRCS, 27 (96.4%) reported increased awareness of the importance of CRCS, 23 (82.1%) reported improved knowledge about access pathways, and 25 (89.3%) expressed willingness to maintain or initiate participation in CRCS. The most commonly reported contact routes were posters displayed in health centres/QR-code pathway (13/28, 46.4%) and health professionals (11/28, 39.3%).ConclusionThis community-based nursing intervention, grounded in a baseline HL diagnosis, was feasible to implement in a primary care/public health context and was followed by favourable short-term self-reported outcomes regarding CRCS awareness, knowledge of access pathways, perceived clarity of educational materials, and intention to participate in screening. However, due to the descriptive design, small convenience sample, and absence of individual-level longitudinal follow-up, causal effects on HL or screening uptake cannot be inferred.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
IntroductionGastrointestinal cancers (GICs) impose substantial health loss in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). We examined long-term burden patterns and temporal changes from 1990 to 2023.MethodsThis ecological secondary analysis used Global Burden of Disease 2023 estimates of disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) and age-standardised DALY rates (ASDRs) for six GIC types in 130 LMICs from 1990 to 2023. Joinpoint regression described temporal trends, and decomposition analysis separated population growth, population aging, and changes in age-specific DALY rates.ResultsFrom 1990 to 2023, total GIC-related DALYs increased from 34.72 to 43.16 million in upper-middle-income countries (UMCs), from 7.20 to 19.76 million in lower-middle-income countries (LMCs), and from 1.88 to 4.69 million in low-income countries (LCs). In UMCs, ASDRs for all GICs except pancreatic cancer declined, especially for esophageal and stomach cancers. In LMCs and LCs, ASDRs for stomach and liver cancers declined, whereas the other four subtypes increased. The shares of global DALYs occurring in UMCs increased for colorectal and pancreatic cancers but decreased for stomach and liver cancers. In contrast, DALYs rose for all six subtypes in LMCs and LCs. Decomposition analysis indicated that population growth and aging were important demographic contributors to the increase in DALYs, whereas the epidemiological changes was negative in UMCs and counterbalanced part of the demographic contribution.ConclusionThe overall DALY burden of GICs increased across LMICs, whereas ASDR trends were heterogeneous across cancer subtypes. These findings support country- and cancer-specific prevention and care priorities.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
There is a growing body of evidence showing that the postoperative wound healing response shares molecular machinery with tumor pathways. Within larger surgical fields such as breast or colorectal cancer, strong preclinical and clinical evidence exists demonstrating a link between postoperative wound complications and cancer recurrence. Head and neck surgery represents a unique landscape with high rates of surgical site infections (SSIs; 20-30%), driven in part by inherent wound contamination from the aerodigestive tract, in addition to prolonged operative times, malnutrition, smoking, and poor overall health. Despite this, studies addressing postoperative wound healing and head and neck cancer (HNC) recurrence remain fragmented at best, with studies demonstrating significant heterogeneity and conflicting results. A thorough understanding of the oncologic implications of wound complications in HNC is vitally important to improve patient outcomes and identify novel therapeutic strategies. This narrative review seeks to synthesize preclinical and clinical studies linking the postoperative wound environment to HNC recurrence. We also seek to highlight emerging approaches to optimize postoperative wound healing for an oncologic benefit, including the role of surgical drain fluid as a novel bioresource, alternative reconstructive hardware, the role of neoadjuvant immunotherapy, and emerging biomaterials.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
A significant mortality is attributed to a common cancer called colorectal cancer (CRC), and current screening methods for CRC could be improved. Circulating microRNAs (miRNAs) have been identified as promising diagnostic biomarkers in body fluids by their rearrangement between healthy and diseased individuals. This study reviewed studies on miRNAs to investigate their use as screening tools for CRC diagnosis. We searched PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science (WoS) databases to discover and find relevant miRNAs that could be used as diagnostic biomarkers in CRC. Patient number and demographic characteristics, patient sample type, miRNA detection method, normalization type, and significantly dysregulated miRNAs were recorded. Meta-analysis was performed across studies with similar dysregulated miRNAs. Initially, 1207 identified articles were entered into ENDNOTE, of which 422, 393, and 392 were from Scopus, WoS, and PubMed, respectively. After reviewing and screening studies by two researchers separately and removing duplicates and irrelevant ones, 126 articles remained as final articles. In the meta-analysis, 6 distinct miRNAs including miR-21, miR-29, miR-92, miR-135, miR-210, and miR-1290 were identified in 42 studies. To evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of these miRNAs in colorectal cancer, Forest plots were drawn and statistical analysis was performed using the area under the ROC curve (AUC), sensitivity (95% CI), and specificity (95% CI). The results showed that the identified miRNAs discriminated colorectal cancer (CRC) patients from healthy individuals with high sensitivity and specificity and outperformed conventional tumor biomarkers, making miRNAs a potential blood-based marker for colorectal cancer diagnosis.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
To characterize the clinical, endoscopic, and pathological features of synchronous multiple early-stage colorectal cancer (sMECRC) and develop a prediction model to identify patients at risk of synchronous lesions at index colonoscopy. We retrospectively analyzed 1,081 consecutive patients with early-stage colorectal cancer who underwent endoscopic treatment at Peking University Third Hospital (2013-2024; development cohort) and 161 patients treated at Peking University International Hospital (2016-2024; external validation cohort). A prediction model was developed using Firth penalized logistic regression, internally validated using 1,000 bootstrap resamples, and externally validated. Sensitivity analyses were also performed. Of the 1,081 patients in the development cohort, 47 (4.3%) had sMECRC. Compared with patients with a single lesion, those with sMECRC had more concomitant adenomatous polyps (median, 5 vs. 2), larger index lesions (2.50 vs. 2.00 cm), a higher rate of FOB positivity (72.2% vs. 46.5%), and a higher frequency of index lesions in the descending colon (17.0% vs. 4.7%). Independent predictors of sMECRC were positive FOB [odds ratio [OR], 2.441; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.157-5.150], number of adenomatous polyps (OR, 1.166 per polyp; 95% CI, 1.094-1.244), index lesion size (OR, 1.247 per cm; 95% CI, 1.099-1.416), and descending colon location (OR, 4.411; 95% CI, 1.627-11.959). The model showed moderate-to-good discrimination in the development cohort [apparent area under the curve (AUC),0.767;bootstrap optimism-corrected AUC, 0.748] and had a Brier score of 0.040, although calibration was suboptimal. External validation in an independent cohort of 161 patients, including 16 with sMECRC, confirmed good discrimination (AUC, 0.864; 95% CI, 0.778-0.950), with improved calibration after intercept-and-slope recalibration. Significant correlations were found between index and second lesions for diameter, Paris classification, depressed morphology, depth of invasion, and histological differentiation. FOB positivity, a greater adenomatous polyp burden, larger index lesion size, and an index lesion located in the descending colon independently predicted sMECRC.Using routine clinical variables, the model exhibited moderate to good discrimination in the development cohort and preserved good discrimination on external validation, but required recalibration for reliable absolute risk estimates. Concordance between the characteristics of index and second lesions may help guide more targeted inspection of the remaining colon.

脂质代谢介导结直肠癌奥沙利铂耐药机制综述
Lipid metabolism mediating oxaliplatin resistance in colorectal cancer.
Frontiers in Oncology · 2026 · Han S, Gu L, Ren Z, Hu J, Zhao Y, Zhao Z, et al.
意义与启示：系统阐述脂质代谢通过DNA损伤、铁死亡、免疫等途径介导奥沙利铂耐药，为肠癌化疗增敏及代谢干预联合策略提供理论依据。

展开英文原题摘要与原文链接
ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
As a core drug in chemotherapy regimens for colorectal cancer, the clinical efficacy of oxaliplatin is compromised by multiple resistance mechanisms. Lipid metabolism, a crucial component of metabolic pathways, is known to affect the efficacy of various chemotherapeutic agents. However, to the best of our knowledge, the role of lipid metabolism in oxaliplatin resistance remains unreviewed. In this review, we analyze the relationship between lipid metabolism and oxaliplatin efficacy from the perspectives of DNA damage, ferroptosis, ROS accumulation, cellular dormancy, antitumor immunity, vascular remodeling, and autophagy. This review covers nearly all known oxaliplatin resistance factors, summarizing the regulatory role of lipid metabolism across both basic and clinical studies. Given that clinical studies remain relatively scarce compared to basic research, the impact of factors directly regulated by lipid metabolism on clinical outcomes is analyzed. Based on this, their relationship with oxaliplatin efficacy is inferred, and potential directions for future clinical research are highlighted. By summarizing the relationship between lipid metabolism and oxaliplatin resistance, this review provides an important theoretical basis for improving chemotherapy efficacy in colorectal cancer and developing novel combination therapies based on metabolic interventions.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal mucinous adenocarcinoma (CMA) is a histologically and molecularly distinct subtype of colorectal cancer (CRC), marked by abundant extracellular mucin, a predilection for the proximal colon, and frequent overlap with deficient mismatch repair/high microsatellite instability (dMMR/MSI-H), BRAF V600E mutation, CpG island methylator phenotype-high (CIMP-high) status, and serrated pathway biology. Although immune checkpoint inhibitors and molecularly targeted therapies have expanded treatment options for selected patients with advanced CRC, treatment strategies tailored to the histologic phenotype, lineage programs, and microenvironmental architecture of CMA remain limited. CLDN18.2, the gastric isoform encoded by CLDN18, is now a clinically validated therapeutic target in gastric and gastroesophageal junction (GEJ) adenocarcinomas. Recent pathology-based studies suggest that CLDN18.2 expression is uncommon in unselected conventional colorectal adenocarcinoma but enriched in CMA, mucin-rich CRC, and tumors with gastric-type or foregut-like differentiation, particularly those arising in the proximal colon or harboring dMMR/MSI-H status or BRAF V600E mutation. This pattern suggests that CLDN18.2 in CMA is unlikely to be a classic oncogenic driver; instead, it is better viewed as a therapeutically accessible, lineage-associated membrane antigen. This review summarizes the biological rationale, expression data, companion diagnostic issues, therapeutic platforms, and translational barriers relevant to CLDN18.2 in CMA. We propose a framework centered on lineage reprogramming, antigen enrichment, assay standardization, and therapeutic translation. Current evidence supports CLDN18.2 as a candidate biomarker for biomarker-enriched investigation, not as an established therapeutic target in CMA. Future work should prioritize CMA-specific preclinical models, standardized membranous immunohistochemistry (IHC) scoring, and prospective trials that integrate CLDN18.2 expression with molecular subtype and tumor microenvironmental features.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a major cause of cancer-related morbidity and mortality worldwide, and mismatch repair-proficient/microsatellite-stable (pMMR/MSS) tumors account for the majority of metastatic CRC cases. In contrast to dMMR/MSI-H CRC, pMMR/MSS tumors are typically characterized by low immunogenicity, limited neoantigen presentation, insufficient effector T-cell infiltration, and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, which collectively restrict the efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) monotherapy. Vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF)/VEGF receptor (VEGFR) signaling contributes not only to abnormal angiogenesis but also to immune suppression by impairing dendritic-cell maturation, reducing immune-cell trafficking, promoting T-cell dysfunction, and facilitating the accumulation of immunosuppressive cell populations. These mechanisms provide a strong rationale for combining VEGF/VEGFR-targeted therapy with ICIs to normalize tumor vasculature and remodel the immune microenvironment. Clinical evidence for this strategy in advanced pMMR/MSS CRC remains heterogeneous. Treatment activity varies across therapeutic settings, antiangiogenic agents, and combination regimens, while many studies are limited by small sample sizes, single-arm designs, and substantial differences in patient characteristics. Emerging data suggest that metastatic pattern, molecular features, baseline immune contexture, and treatment line may influence clinical activity; however, no biomarker has yet been validated for routine patient selection. Multi-agent strategies may provide broader immune modulation but also increase toxicity, treatment complexity, and cost. This review summarizes the biological rationale, clinical efficacy, safety, and potential predictive factors of VEGF/VEGFR-targeted therapy combined with ICIs in advanced pMMR/MSS CRC. Particular emphasis is placed on the heterogeneity of clinical outcomes and on distinguishing mechanistic immune remodeling from the potential enhancement of tumor immune sensitivity. Future studies should prioritize biomarker-guided patient selection, randomized comparative trials, and comprehensive assessment of efficacy, safety, quality of life, and long-term clinical benefit.

Branched-chain amino acids in skeletal and cardiac muscles: a review of metabolic variations and cancer's impact.
Frontiers in Physiology · 2026 · Chrzanowski J, Graboń W, Buchajska K, Cudnoch-Jędrzejewska A
意义与启示：系统阐明肿瘤驱动BCAA代谢重编程与恶病质肌/心消耗的机制，提示肠癌恶病质管理需早期干预BCAA并联合抗炎与线粒体保护。

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Branched-chain amino acids (BCAA) - leucine, isoleucine, and valine - serve as essential regulators of energy homeostasis, protein turnover, and nutrient signaling in striated muscle. However, their metabolic processing varies substantially across tissues. This review contrasts BCAA metabolism in skeletal versus cardiac muscle and evaluates how cancer alters it. Skeletal muscle functions as the main site for whole-body BCAA transamination and oxidation, distributing these amino acids between protein synthesis and oxidative catabolism in line with physiological needs. In comparison, the myocardium maintains low baseline BCAA oxidation, depends primarily on fatty acids and glucose, and tightly limits BCAA catabolic flux to prevent the buildup of intermediates that would undermine mitochondrial function. In malignancies, BCAA metabolism is reconfigured in a way that depends on tumor type: many tumors increase BCAA uptake and suppress catabolism in order to preserve intracellular stores, as a result maintaining mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1 (mTORC1) signaling and supporting proliferation. Using lung, pancreatic and colorectal cancers as main examples, we outline how this tumor-driven metabolic rewiring is linked to cancer cachexia - a multi-organ syndrome in which inflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and impaired anabolic signaling promote muscle and cardiac wasting rather than simple substrate limitation. We describe first the mechanisms shared by skeletal and cardiac muscle, then the features specific to each tumor type, and we distinguish throughout between cardiac evidence obtained in tumor-bearing hosts and inferences extrapolated from heart failure. We conclude that interventions directed at BCAA are most reasonable early in the disease course, and only when paired with approaches that suppress inflammation and restore mitochondrial quality control. We also identify priorities for tissue-specific biomarkers and for future research.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Early-onset colorectal cancer (EOCRC), defined as colorectal cancer diagnosed before 50 years of age, represents an emerging global health challenge with rapidly increasing incidence. Although EOCRC exhibits distinct clinical and molecular characteristics, the cellular ecosystem and mechanisms underlying its aggressive behavior remain incompletely understood. Here, we integrated seven independent single-cell RNA sequencing cohorts comprising 473,939 high-quality cells from 174 colorectal cancer (CRC) patients (39 EOCRC and 135 average-onset CRC [AOCRC]) to construct a comprehensive cellular landscape across age groups. After Harmony-based integration, nine major cellular lineages were identified, and malignant epithelial cells were characterized using chromosome-level copy number variation inference. We systematically compared malignant and stromal compartments, followed by malignant-state characterization, trajectory analysis, and cell -cell communication modeling using Slingshot, CellChat, and NicheNet. EOCRC displayed extensive remodeling of the tumor ecosystem rather than isolated epithelial alterations. Malignant epithelial cells in EOCRC showed increased enrichment of inflammation-associated and Cycling (S/DNA damage response [DDR]) states. In parallel, proliferating endothelial cells and MKI67-positive proliferative cancer-associated fibroblasts were expanded in EOCRC, indicating stromal-state remodeling. Copy number variation analyses demonstrated that genomic instability differences between EOCRC and AOCRC were primarily explained by differential microsatellite instability (MSI) status distribution rather than age-related genomic alterations. Cell -cell communication analyses revealed selective remodeling of epithelial-stromal signaling networks, with recurrent involvement of NOTCH-associated mediators. NicheNet prioritized NOTCH-associated ligands (DLL4, JAG1) among candidate stromal-derived regulators of EOCRC transcriptional programs. A refined five-gene NOTCH-epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) panel (HEY1, ZEB1, TWIST1, VIM, FN1) was associated with EOCRC-specific poor survival across two independent cohorts, and Together, our study establishes EOCRC as a multicellular ecosystem characterized by coordinated malignant, stromal, and signaling reprogramming. These findings identify NOTCH signaling as a potential age-specific prognostic association that warrants functional validation in EOCRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Lynch Syndrome (LS) is a genetic condition associated with a high risk of colorectal cancer, often linked to microsatellite instability (MSI), which is caused by defects in DNA mismatch repair (MMR) genes such as MLH1 and MSH2. Although MMR deficiency and MSI are well-documented in the literature, the role of these genes in adenomas remains unclear. To evaluate, through meta-analysis, the correlation between loss of expression of the MLH1 and MSH2 genes and MSI in adenomas from patients with LS. A systematic search was conducted in the MEDLINE, SCOPUS, and Web of Science databases up to 06/09/2025, using a strategy with descriptors related to MSI, LS, and precursor lesions. Data were analyzed using the Inverse Variance method, with 95% confidence intervals. Heterogeneity was assessed using the I-squared ( I²) statistic. Outliers were identified through statistical influence diagnostics applied to each study. Publication bias was assessed using funnel plots and Egger's regression test. Statistical analyses were performed using RStudio, version 4.4.0. 5 studies were included, totaling 145 adenomas from individuals with LS. A highly significant correlation was found between MSI and MSH2 expression loss (OR=13,91 [3,97-48,72]; P=0,000038; I²=0%). No significant correlation was found between MSI and loss of MLH1 expression (OR=2,19 [0,93-5,16]; P=0,073; I²=0%). Funnel plot analysis and Egger's regression test showed no significant evidence of publication bias for MLH1 (t=0.25, df=3, P-value=0.8155) or MSH2 (t=-0.79, df=3, P-value=0.4860). This meta-analysis found a strong, significant and consistent correlation between MSI and MSH2 expression loss in adenomas, but a non-significant association for MLH1 expression loss. The lack of statistical significance in Egger's test for both genes should be interpreted with caution due to the small number of included studies (k=5). The limited literature available highlights the need for further, larger-scale research.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
IntroductionThe incidence of early-onset colorectal cancer (EO-CRC) is steadily rising, although the cause is unclear. CRC patients often experience high symptom burden, including pain, fatigue, and distress, but symptom presentations in EO-CRC patients are poorly understood. The aim of the current study was to characterize baseline symptoms (pain, fatigue, distress) and symptom classes in a sample of symptomatic EO-CRC patients.MethodsAnalysis of cross-sectional baseline data from patients enrolled in a mHealth symptom management randomized controlled trial. Participants were 18-50 years old with a CRC diagnosis (stage I-IV) in the last 3 years and self-reported severity of ≥3/10 on at least 2 symptoms (pain, fatigue, distress). Participants completed measures assessing pain (BPI), fatigue (PROMIS), and distress (BSI). Latent class analysis was used to examine symptom classes and moderating variables [sex, cancer stage, site of disease, treatment in past 7 days, body mass index (BMI), years since diagnosis].ResultsParticipants (N=165, M age=42.2 years (SD=5.7), 53% female, 70% White, 48% Stage IV disease, M time since diagnosis=1 year), on average, endorsed mild pain (M=3.0, SD=2.1), high fatigue (M=55.9, SD=7.1), and moderate distress (M=58.2, SD=8.8). A two-class latent class model was fit. Classes were identified as: low pain, moderate fatigue, moderate distress (Class 1; 60%); moderate pain, high fatigue, high distress (Class 2, 40%). Probability profiles differed by sex and BMI, but not by cancer stage, site of disease (colon; rectum), recent active treatment, or years from diagnosis.ConclusionSymptomatic EO-CRC patients enrolled in a symptom management trial experience elevated fatigue, distress, and to a lesser extent, pain. Symptoms presented in two distinct classes characterized by overall low-moderate and moderate-high symptom burden. Sex-based and BMI differences in class membership exist; findings warrant replication. Findings support developing multi-symptom interventions tailored to the needs of EO-CRC patients.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Topical haemostatic agents such as FloSeal are widely used to manage low-grade bleeding in areas where conventional haemostatic techniques may risk damage to critical structures or are unsuccessful. While effective, these agents can cause unexpected complications. This case report highlights small bowel obstruction (SBO) as a rare but important adverse outcome following FloSeal use in colorectal surgery. A 55-year-old male underwent laparoscopic right hemicolectomy for hepatic flexure adenocarcinoma. Due to raw surface oozing near Gerota's fascia and proximity to the duodenum, FloSeal was applied intra-operatively. On postoperative day 3, the patient developed nausea, absent flatus and bowel sounds and a rising C-reactive protein (CRP) (366 mg/L), progressing to 540 mg/L by day 4. CT imaging showed ileus with an intact anastomosis and no closed-loop features. Exploratory laparotomy identified a transition point where the distal ileum was adhered to residual FloSeal, resulting in a high-grade obstruction. Following adhesiolysis and irrigation, the patient recovered uneventfully. Normal lactate and a negative septic screen argued against bacterial translocation with systemic sepsis as the driver of the CRP rise, suggesting instead a localised inflammatory response to mechanical obstruction. We frame this as a preventable, surgical technique-related complication rather than an intrinsic hazard of FloSeal, arising from a deliberate deviation from manufacturer instructions to remove excess material. Surgeons should maintain a high index of suspicion for SBO in patients with rising CRP and no radiological leak, and should clearly document whenever haemostatic material is deliberately retained.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
HCLS1-associated protein X-1 (HAX1) is widely expressed in human tissues and was first identified as a binding partner of hematopoietic cell-specific protein 1. Through interactions with proteins and RNAs, HAX1 regulates gene expression and contributes to cell survival and cytoskeletal remodeling. Recent studies have reported increased HAX1 expression in several malignant tumors, including breast, gastric, colorectal, and other cancers, where it promotes cell survival, proliferation, migration, and invasion. It also supports angiogenesis, hypoxic adaptation, and resistance to anticancer treatment. Noncoding RNAs and ubiquitination regulate HAX1 abundance and molecular state, influencing its cellular functions. Clinical evidence links HAX1 expression and subcellular localization to aggressive clinicopathological features and poor patient outcomes. This supports HAX1 as both a prognostic biomarker and a therapeutic target. This review summarizes the molecular characteristics and regulation of HAX1, and examines how its interactions contribute to tumor progression. It also discusses the implications for cancer prognosis and treatment. Future research should focus on clinical validation and further investigation of HAX1 interactions to guide selective therapeutic targeting.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs), long recognized as effectors of innate host defense, are now firmly implicated in remodeling the tumor microenvironment and facilitating tumor progression. Tumor-associated NETs expose proteases, damage-associated molecular patterns, and self-DNA that activate protease-activated receptor 2 (PAR2) on tumor and stromal cells, engaging downstream cascades (Gαq/11-PLCβ-PKC-MEK-ERK, RhoA-ROCK, β-arrestin-biased signaling, and RTK transactivation), which jointly drive epithelial-mesenchymal transition, matrix degradation, and angiogenesis, ultimately favoring invasion and metastasis. Direct evidence that NET-derived proteases engage PAR2 on tumor or stromal cells rests, however, on a limited number of studies, and much of the literature concerns NETs or PAR2 individually rather than their coupling. We searched PubMed with structured queries combining "neutrophil extracellular traps"/"NETs", "protease-activated receptor 2"/"PAR2"/"F2RL1", and cancer-related descriptors, supplemented by citation tracing, with coverage through August 2026, and graded each mechanistic claim at claim level as strong, moderate, or emerging according to explicit criteria (see Literature search and evidence grading); findings supported for NETs or PAR2 alone are labeled as such throughout. The axis is documented most completely in breast, pancreatic, lung, and colorectal cancers, where tumor-type-specific drivers have been defined (dormant-cell reawakening in breast cancer, stromal reprogramming in pancreatic cancer, bypass of targeted therapy in lung cancer, and bidirectional signaling in colorectal cancer), whereas in biliary and cervical cancers only descriptive NET data are available; therapeutic strategies targeting the axis (PAD4 inhibitors, DNase I, PAR2 antagonists/antibodies, and combinations with immune checkpoint blockade) show preclinical promise. However, validated biomarkers of pathway activity and safety data for chronic PAR2 blockade are lacking. The NETs-PAR2 axis is an emerging targetable driver of tumor invasion, and biomarker-guided, tumor-type-aware clinical development is required to translate axis-directed therapy into the clinic.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal anastomotic leakage is commonly framed as a technical complication or a consequence of intestinal dysbiosis. Neither view fully explains how a contaminated mucosal wound restores epithelial continuity while preserving a load-bearing submucosal matrix. We define anastomotic healing as a spatially organized mucosal immune process: luminal microbes and metabolites, the epithelial wound edge, recruited immune cells, fibroblasts, collagen, and vascular support occupy distinct but interacting compartments. The most compelling available anastomosis-specific evidence supports a destructive pathway in which expressed microbial virulence, host plasminogen activation, epithelial inflammatory signaling, sustained neutrophil recruitment, and MMP9 converge on collagen loss. A complementary repair pathway is supported by human-to-mouse microbiota-transfer and metabolite-rescue experiments, but this evidence is less direct and more heterogeneous. It links commensal function and AhR-dependent IL-22 signaling to epithelial restitution, myeloid resolution, and matrix repair. NLRP3, NLRP6, and NLRC4 remain candidate threshold regulators rather than demonstrated mediators of colorectal anastomotic healing. Human macrophage atlases refine cell-state definitions, but prospective evidence linking anastomotic macrophage states or efferocytosis to leakage remains limited. We propose an evidence-weighted framework that separates human association, direct microbial-function measurements, experimental causation, and human intervention evidence. Translation will require paired spatial sampling and functional microbial assays, together with immune, matrix, mechanical, target-engagement, and ecological-safety endpoints. This framework extends beyond taxonomic dysbiosis toward testable wound-immune endotypes and mechanism-matched prevention.
