ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Osteoarthritis is a whole-joint disease involving articular cartilage, subchondral bone, synovium, vasculature, and peripheral nerves. However, whether joint innervation merely conveys nociceptive input or actively contributes to disease progression remains unresolved. This review integrates evidence on subchondral bone remodeling, synovial inflammation, neurovascular reorganization, and pain sensitization, and proposes a bidirectional neural crosstalk model between subchondral bone and synovium. In subchondral bone, abnormal mechanical loading and osteoclast activation promote sensory nerve ingrowth and neurovascular remodeling through Netrin-1-deleted in colorectal cancer receptor signaling, prostaglandin E2-prostaglandin E receptor 4 signaling, and Slit guidance ligand 3-related pathways. In the synovium, nerve growth factor and inflammatory mediators reinforce sensory sprouting, neuronal excitability, and neuropeptide release. Calcitonin gene-related peptide, substance P, norepinephrine, and neuropeptide Y act on osteoclasts, osteoblast-lineage cells, fibroblast-like synoviocytes, macrophages, and endothelial cells, thereby linking neural activity to bone turnover, synovial immunity, and vascular remodeling. These signals converge on the receptor activator of nuclear factor-κB ligand-osteoprotegerin axis, nuclear factor-κB, and vascular endothelial growth factor-related pathways. Osteochondral channels, periosteal-synovial interfaces, and neurovascular networks may provide anatomical routes for this cross-compartment communication, forming a feedback circuit that sustains structural damage and chronic pain. Neural effects vary across disease stages and tissue compartments, and pain relief does not necessarily confer structural protection. Future therapies should therefore prioritize stage-specific and compartment-selective neuromodulation while assessing pain, function, and joint structural safety in parallel.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), encompassing ulcerative colitis (UC) and Crohn's disease (CD), is managed according to clinical practice guidelines that integrate evidence appraisal with regional healthcare contexts. This narrative, comparative review examined selected guideline documents from the Japanese Society of Gastroenterology (JSGE), European Crohn's and Colitis Organisation (ECCO), American Gastroenterological Association (AGA), and American College of Gastroenterology (ACG) using the JSGE guidelines as the organizing framework to highlight similarities and differences in recommendation direction and contextual nuance. The analysis focused on the guideline architecture and selected domains of monitoring and medical therapy, with particular attention to how document structure, scope, publication timing, and update strategies shape the interpretation of similarities and differences in recommendation direction. Across the guideline systems, general agreement in overall direction was observed regarding the shift from symptom-based assessment alone towards objective monitoring, the sustained role of 5-aminosalicylic acid (5-ASA) in the treatment of UC, the expanding integration of advanced therapies, and the adoption of risk-based surveillance principles for IBD-associated colorectal neoplasia. The most notable divergence concerned the use of 5-ASA in CD treatment: the JSGE guidelines retained a more pragmatic role for this therapy, whereas the recent ECCO, AGA, and ACG guidelines generally limited routine use. Treatment withdrawal and de-escalation emerged as particularly heterogeneous domains, reflecting the uneven treatment of drug-specific recommendations. The JSGE guidelines were notable for their distinctive single-volume integration of diagnostic criteria, treatment strategy, and follow-up, as well as their explicit inclusion of Japan-specific considerations, such as nucleoside diphosphate-linked moiety X-type motif 15 genotyping, cytapheresis, and oral tacrolimus. These findings suggest that apparent differences among IBD guidelines should be understood not only as differences in clinical judgment, but also as products of guideline architecture, update timing, and intended scope. See also the graphical abstract(Fig. 1).

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), encompassing Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis, is a chronic relapsing inflammatory disorder of the gastrointestinal tract characterized by dysregulated immune responses, impaired epithelial barrier function, and alterations in the gut microbiota. Although considerable progress has been made in understanding the immunopathogenesis of IBD, increasing evidence indicates that metabolic signaling pathways are integral regulators of intestinal inflammation, tissue repair, and disease progression. Among these, insulin, insulin-like growth factors (IGFs), and glucagon-like peptides (GLPs) constitute an interconnected immunometabolic network that links nutrient sensing, energy metabolism, epithelial regeneration, and immune homeostasis. Insulin signaling plays context-dependent roles in IBD by regulating glucose metabolism, epithelial repair, inflammatory responses, and interactions with the gut microbiota and bile acid metabolism. While insulin promotes mucosal healing and barrier restoration in intestinal epithelial cells, excessive activation of insulin signaling in immune cells may exacerbate chronic inflammation through epigenetic and cytokine-mediated mechanisms. The IGF axis is also profoundly altered during active IBD, with systemic suppression of IGF-1 and IGFBP-3 accompanying disease activity, whereas local IGF signaling promotes epithelial regeneration, wound healing, and immune regulation. In addition, IGF-binding proteins (IGFBPs) function as active modulators of inflammation, fibrosis, and colitis-associated colorectal cancer in an isoform-specific manner. GLP signaling further integrates metabolism with intestinal immunity; GLP-1 receptor agonists exhibit anti-inflammatory, metabolic, and microbiota-modulating effects, whereas GLP-2 primarily enhances epithelial proliferation, barrier integrity, and mucosal repair. Emerging preclinical and observational clinical studies suggest that GLP-based therapies may improve disease outcomes, although prospective randomized trials are still required. This review summarizes current knowledge regarding the biological functions and molecular mechanisms of insulin, IGFs, IGFBPs, and GLPs in IBD, highlighting their coordinated roles in regulating metabolism, immunity, epithelial homeostasis, and tissue remodeling. A better understanding of these interconnected signaling pathways may facilitate the development of novel immunometabolic therapeutic strategies aimed at promoting mucosal healing, limiting chronic inflammation, and improving long-term outcomes in patients with IBD.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Globally, colorectal cancer (CRC) ranks as the third most common malignancy in terms of incidence. Colorectal polyps (CP) are the most common precancerous lesions of CRC, making the timely identification of their risk factors critically important. Although the CALLY index has theoretical promise as a tool for stratifying the risk of CP occurrence, its clinical utility remains unvalidated and warrants rigorous empirical assessment. Traditional risk factor models primarily focus on measurable biological indicators, often overlooking differences in an individual's overall functional state. Incorporating traditional Chinese medicine constitution (TCMC) is expected to enable the development of more comprehensive risk prediction models. Therefore, this study aims to validate whether CALLY is an independent risk factor for CP and to conduct preliminary exploration of its potential biological mechanisms, based on systematic control of traditional medical risk factors and TCMC. This study is a retrospective cross-sectional study that enrolled 452 hospitalized patients undergoing colonoscopy between October and December 2025. By constructing a stepwise-adjusted logistic regression model, conducting interaction analyses, testing mediating effects, and performing sensitivity analyses, we systematically investigated the relationship between CALLY and CP and its potential mechanisms. Multivariate logistic regression analysis revealed no significant statistical association between CALLY quartile groups and CP risk (all comparisons Among hospitalized gastroenterology patients, CALLY is not an independent risk marker for CP and is not recommended as a routine screening indicator for this population for the time being. Risk assessment for such patients should focus on their gender, age, diabetes and gastric polyps. The phlegm-dampness constitution should be considered a preliminary finding due to the small subgroup size and wide confidence intervals; its role as a stable risk factor requires independent validation in larger prospective cohorts.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Anastomotic leakage is a major colorectal surgical complication that may be exacerbated by perioperative inflammatory stress. How transcriptomic profiles and tissue-adherent microbiota change under such stress, and whether postoperative inulin supplementation is associated with microbiota changes and improved healing after inflammatory priming, remain unclear. Two independent animal experiments were conducted. Experiment 1 compared control (CON) and LPS-primed mice using scheduled, repeated-cross-sectional sampling for microbiota profiling on POD0, 1, 3, 5, 7, and 14 and for RNA-seq on POD0, 1, 3, 5, and 7. Experiment 2 used the same murine colonic anastomosis model to evaluate postoperative exclusive enteral nutrition (EEN) with or without inulin supplementation (dietary fiber, DF) in a 2 × 2 factorial design comprising CON, CON-DF, LPS, and LPS-DF groups. Healing was assessed by survival, recovery scores, anastomotic burst pressure, histology, immunostaining, and short-chain-fatty-acid quantification. Within Experiment 2, a dedicated LPS priming impaired healing and induced niche-specific microbiota alterations with altered bacterial microspatial patterns at the suture line. DF supplementation was associated with improved recovery and anastomotic strength, reduced inflammatory infiltration, increased proliferation, decreased apoptosis, and altered inflammatory- and repair-associated immune markers. The planned LPS-DF versus LPS survival comparison in the POD5 four-group cohort was not significant after multiplicity correction. At POD5, DF was associated with lower Shannon diversity and an altered short-chain-fatty-acid profile, including higher acetate; the LPS × inulin interactions for these measures were not significant. Brief postoperative inulin-supplemented EEN improved anastomotic healing following inflammatory priming, concurrent with microbiota remodeling and short-chain-fatty-acid differences, including higher acetate. These concurrent changes do not establish microbiota- or SCFA-mediated causality.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Multiple primary malignancies (MPMs) are increasingly encountered in clinical practice as cancer survivorship improves. The coexistence of colorectal cancer (CRC) and lymphoma is rare, and long-term survival exceeding 10 years in such patients has seldom been reported. We report a 63-year-old male patient who presented with sigmoid colon adenocarcinoma with synchronous multiple liver metastases (cT4N1M1, Stage IV) in 2015. Molecular testing of the primary sigmoid colon tumor specimen revealed wild-type KRAS, NRAS, BRAF, and PIK3CA.After multidisciplinary team (MDT) discussion, the patient received 4 cycles of FOLFIRI regimen chemotherapy as conversion therapy, achieving partial response (PR). He subsequently underwent special hepatic segmentectomy and laparoscopic-assisted radical sigmoidectomy, followed by additional chemotherapy. Evaluation in May 2016 showed complete response (CR) with no evidence of disease (NED). During regular follow-up in 2021, a left inguinal lymph node enlargement was detected. Biopsy confirmed peripheral T-cell lymphoma, not otherwise specified (PTCL-NOS), CD30-positive. The patient received 6 cycles of CHOP chemotherapy combined with local radiotherapy, achieving CR. In March 2026, retroperitoneal lymph node recurrence was confirmed, and continued chemotherapy was recommended. The patient has achieved an overall survival of over 10 years since the initial CRC diagnosis. This case suggests that, with MDT-guided individualized treatment, long-term survival may be achievable in patients with advanced CRC and liver metastases following conversion therapy and radical surgery. The subsequent development of a second primary PTCL-NOS highlights the importance of vigilant long-term surveillance in cancer survivors. This report adds to the limited literature on MPMs involving CRC and lymphoma with extended survival.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
To synthesize the best available evidence on early mobilization following radical surgery for colorectal cancer, both domestically and internationally, with the aim of providing evidence-based guidance for clinical healthcare providers. We conducted a literature search using the "6S" evidence model to identify studies on early mobilization following colorectal cancer surgery. Given the limited number of studies exclusively focusing on laparoscopic approaches, we included evidence from broader elective colorectal surgery populations to provide comprehensive guidance. We searched relevant domestic and international websites, evidence-based databases, association websites, and primary literature databases via a computerized system. The search period spanned from the inception of each database to December 19, 2025. Two researchers independently assessed the quality of the literature using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) quality assessment tool, and conducted evidence extraction and synthesis for the included studies. A total of 19 studies were ultimately included, comprising 4 guidelines, 6 expert consensus documents, 3 systematic reviews, 1 evidence summary, and 5 randomized controlled trials. A total of 23 pieces of evidence were identified across five areas: core principles, preoperative preparation, key elements of activity management, postoperative activity protocols, and activity support. This study synthesizes the best available evidence regarding early mobilization following laparoscopic radical resection for colorectal cancer. It recommends that nursing staff tailor their approach to individual patients based on clinical circumstances and patient preferences to promote postoperative recovery and enhance the quality of clinical care. http://ebn.nursing.fudan.edu.cn/myRegisterList, identifier ES20259534.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Fecal SDC2 methylation is a promising noninvasive biomarker for colorectal cancer (CRC), whereas serum tumor markers, including carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA), carbohydrate antigen 19-9 (CA19-9), CA242, and CA50, are primarily used for postoperative surveillance and have limited value as standalone early diagnostic markers. This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of combining fecal SDC2 methylation with these four serum markers for CRC detection. A total of 354 participants were enrolled, including 55 with CRC, 188 with adenoma/polyps, 106 with non-tumor/inflammatory conditions, and 5 with other undetermined lesions. Fecal SDC2 methylation was assessed by quantitative methylation-specific PCR, and serum markers were measured via electrochemiluminescence immunoassays. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using multivariable logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. AUCs with 95% confidence intervals were calculated, and sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), and negative predictive value (NPV) were estimated at the Youden-optimal threshold. Fecal SDC2 methylation levels were significantly higher in CRC patients compared to those with adenomas or non-tumor lesions. Fecal SDC2 Ct value alone yielded an AUC of 0.814 (95% CI, 0.751-0.876). The AUC increased to 0.866 (95% CI, 0.814-0.918) after addition of CEA and to 0.872 (95% CI, 0.818-0.926) for the full model incorporating CEA, CA19-9, CA242, and CA50. At the Youden-optimal threshold, the full model achieved a sensitivity of 87.3% (95% CI, 76.0%-93.7%), specificity of 78.6% (95% CI, 73.6%-82.9%), PPV of 42.9% (95% CI, 34.1%-52.1%), and NPV of 97.1% (95% CI, 94.2%-98.6%). In contrast, individual serum markers showed limited diagnostic performance, with AUC values of 0.709 (CEA), 0.666 (CA19-9), 0.495 (CA242), and 0.567 (CA50). Integration of fecal SDC2 Ct values with serum tumor markers showed a modest improvement in the noninvasive discrimination of CRC compared with SDC2 alone. Prospective external and stage-specific validation is required before clinical screening implementation.

The clinical efficacy of PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors combined with chemotherapy (± targeted agents) in patients with proficient mismatch repair (pMMR) metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) remains unclear. This study systematically evaluated the efficacy of this regimen. We searched PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and ClinicalTrials.gov for relevant randomized controlled trials (RCTs) published up to May 2026. The primary outcomes were progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS); effect sizes were estimated as hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (95%CIs). These subgroup findings are exploratory, and interaction tests were not performed. PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors combined with chemotherapy (with or without targeted agents) may improve the prognosis of patients with pMMR mCRC and represent a potential first-line treatment option. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD420261330186.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
This study aimed to identify distinct postoperative weight loss trajectories and develop a machine learning-based model for predicting malnutrition risk at 6 months after curative resection for colorectal cancer (CRC). This prospective observational study enrolled 205 CRC patients who underwent curative resection. Weight loss percentages were measured at four postoperative time points relative to preoperative baseline: T1 (postoperative day 7 or hospital discharge), T2 (1 month), T3 (3 months), and T4 (6 months). Latent class growth modeling (LCGM) was employed to identify distinct weight change trajectory patterns. Malnutrition was assessed using the Global Leadership Initiative on Malnutrition (GLIM) criteria at 6 months post-surgery. Core predictors for 6-month malnutrition were screened by taking the intersection of Lasso regression and the Boruta algorithm. Ten machine learning models were constructed and systematically compared, with the optimal model interpreted using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). LCGM identified three distinct weight change trajectories: persistent weight loss (28.3%), gradual recovery (38.5%), and rapid recovery (33.2%). Multinomial logistic regression (reference category: persistent weight loss group) showed that age > 65 years and ASA III-IV were associated with lower odds of gradual recovery, whereas colon cancer (right or left) was associated with higher odds. For rapid recovery, female, age > 65 years, ASA III-IV, and adjuvant chemotherapy were associated with lower odds, whereas colon cancer (right or left) was associated with higher odds. The overall incidence of GLIM-defined malnutrition at 6 months was 33.2%. Among the ten machine learning models, XGBoost achieved the best comprehensive performance, with an AUC of 0.836 (95% CI: 0.779-0.894). Calibration curves demonstrated good agreement between predicted and observed probabilities, and decision curve analysis confirmed net clinical benefit across a 9-91% threshold range. SHAP analysis revealed that lower preoperative BMI, receipt of adjuvant chemotherapy, older age, and rectal tumor location were associated with increased malnutrition risk. This study revealed three distinct postoperative weight loss trajectories in CRC patients. The developed XGBoost model, incorporating four readily available clinical variables, demonstrated favorable predictive performance and clinical utility for early identification of patients at high risk of long-term malnutrition, pending further external validation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
ObjectivesOrganized, population-based cancer screening is recommended by European Union guidelines. Employer-provided screening within Workplace Health Promotion (WHP) programs may differ from evidence-based guidelines. This study aimed to evaluate the alignment between international cancer screening recommendations and screening services offered by companies participating in the Lombardy WHP Program.MethodsA cross-sectional survey was conducted between April and September 2024 among companies participating in the Lombardy WHP Program. Screening practices for breast, cervical, colorectal, prostate, and lung cancer were compared with the most recent international guidelines. Company characteristics were analyzed using descriptive statistics and univariate logistic regression models.ResultsOf the 308 companies participating in the survey, 95 reported the inclusion of preventive medicine services in their corporate welfare offer. Among these, breast cancer screening was the most frequently offered service (67.4%), followed by cervical cancer screening (57.9%). Both the majority of mammography offers (51%) and Pap test offers (92.6%) were not guideline-adherent, thus resulting in overscreening. Colorectal cancer (41.1%) and lung cancer (33.7%) screening were even less commonly provided by the participating companies. Prostate cancer screening with PSA testing was available in 63.2% of participating companies. Large companies had significantly lower odds of inappropriate mammography intervals (OR 0.11; 95% CI 0.02-0.58).ConclusionCancer screening services offered by companies, compliant with the Lombardy WHP Program, are frequently not aligned with current evidence-based recommendations, with overscreening emerging as a predominant issue. Strengthening coordination between occupational health services and public health authorities is essential to ensure appropriate, equitable, and sustainable integration of workplace-based screening initiatives into organized regional cancer prevention strategies.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Myeloid cells regulate immune exclusion, T-cell dysfunction, angiogenesis, stromal remodeling, and resistance to immune checkpoint blockade in solid tumors. Pharmacological development has moved from nonspecific depletion toward recruitment or survival blockade, intracellular state reprogramming, restoration of antigen presentation, and tumor-selective phagocytosis. Clinical experience nevertheless shows a recurrent gap between biological activity and attributable therapeutic immune conversion. We introduce the Myeloid Immune Conversion Audit Trail (MICAT), a fixed four-level extension of the pharmacological audit trail that grades intratumoral target engagement, conversion of the intended myeloid state, propagation through the immune ecosystem, and randomized clinical attribution. Each level is scored as not demonstrated, partial, or demonstrated. Applying MICAT across representative trials shows that most programs stop at systemic pharmacodynamics or partial lineage effects; few establish ecosystem propagation, and none yet completes the entire causal chain for an immunological switch in a solid-tumor carcinoma. The analysis identifies compensation and redundancy as the central biological obstacle: CCR2 blockade can recruit CXCR2-positive neutrophils, CSF1R inhibition can spare resistant SPP1-high macrophages, and CD40 or PI3Kγ activation can induce interferon-linked PD-L1 feedback. We therefore prioritize lineage-resolved paired tissue, preservation of cDC1 and cDC2 function, absolute cell quantification, orthogonal functional and spatial readouts, and randomized component-controlled trials. Disease context is decisive: tenosynovial giant-cell tumor establishes CSF1R dependence without proving immune conversion; macrophage-rich triple-negative breast cancer is a rational PI3Kγ test-bed; pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma permits sequence-aware CD40 and stromal studies; and microsatellite-stable colorectal cancer is a stringent failure benchmark. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
While minimally invasive surgery and traditional open surgery are generally equivalent in terms of oncological outcomes for rectal cancer, maintaining postoperative quality of life is increasingly important. Low anterior resection syndrome is a distressing complication following sphincter-preserving surgery that severely impacts a patient's normal life. This study aims to systematically compare the short-term clinical efficacies of laparoscopic total mesorectal excision and open radical surgery, using LARS scoring system to objectively evaluate postoperative anal function. A retrospective, single-center analysis was conducted on clinical data from patients who underwent radical resection for mid-low rectal cancer at Nanjing Drum Tower Hospital Group Suqian Hospital from January 2020 to March 2023. Following strict inclusion and exclusion criteria, 361 patients were initially selected. To mitigate baseline imbalances, a 1:2 propensity score matching was utilized, yielding a final matched cohort of 160 patients in the LaTME (laparoscopic total mesorectal excision) group and 80 patients in the OsTME (open total mesorectal excision) group. Both groups demonstrated highly comparable oncological efficacy, achieving negative circumferential resection margins in 97.50% of cases and complete total mesorectal excision in over 96.00% of cases. Additionally, 1-year and 3-year disease-free survival and overall survival profiles showed no statistically significant differences between the two modalities. While systemic postoperative complications were similar between groups, the LaTME cohort experienced a significantly lower rate of postoperative urinary retention (1.90%) compared to the OsTME cohort (8.80%, Laparoscopic total mesorectal excision provides equivalent oncological outcomes to traditional open surgery for mid-low rectal cancer. LaTME offers superior short-term functional benefits by reducing postoperative urinary retention and substantially decreasing the severity of early Low Anterior Resection Syndrome. These minimally invasive advantages support prioritizing LaTME to maximize functional preservation and patient quality of life.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) screening based on fecal occult blood testing (FOBT) has demonstrated effectiveness in multiple studies. To estimate the potential demand for colonoscopy generated by a single-sample qualitative fecal immunochemical test (FIT) in the FONASA beneficiaries aged 50-75 years using data from the 2016-2017 Chilean National Health Survey (ENS). A prevalence study was conducted in a representative subsample of FONASA beneficiaries aged 50-75 years. Participants underwent a single-sample qualitative FIT. The prevalence of positive FIT results was compared across different groups, and multivariable models were constructed adjusting for sex, age, urban/rural residence, health insurance status, body mass index (BMI), alcohol consumption, tobacco use, and family history of CRC. A total of 892 individuals were included (97.8% test return rate), mean age of 60.52 years (SD 0.40); 53.71% were women, and 3.22% reported a family history of CRC. The prevalence of lower gastrointestinal bleeding during the previous three months was 10.22%, while 36.86% reported a change in bowel movements. FIT positivity was 17.46% (95% CI: 14.07-21.29), with no significant differences according to sex, family history of CRC, or reported symptoms. The estimated colonoscopy demand corresponds to 440,443 individuals. Implementation of a FIT-based CRC screening strategy would require a substantial increase in colonoscopy capacity in Chile to meet the additional demand generated within the target age group, with heterogeneous distribution across regions.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
IntroductionLocally advanced rectal cancer receives neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (nCRT) as standard clinical management. Reliable non-invasive biomarkers for predicting pathological complete response (pCR) after nCRT remain urgently needed. This study aimed to explore correlations between peripheral blood lymphocyte subsets and pCR rate in rectal cancer patients receiving nCRT, and screen predictive immune markers for individualized therapeutic decision-making.MethodsThis was a retrospective cohort study. A total of 143 rectal cancer patients receiving nCRT in our center between June 2021 and December 2022 were consecutively enrolled. Tumor regression grade (TRG) was applied to evaluate pathological treatment response. Kolmogorov-Smirnov test, Mann-Whitney U test, chi-squared test, binary logistic regression and ROC curve analyses were performed to investigate associations between lymphocyte subsets and pCR.ResultsA total of 48 patients (33.6%) achieved pCR after nCRT. Absolute counts of all detected peripheral blood lymphocytes after nCRT. Gender and age were correlated with lymphocyte subsets: males had higher absolute counts and percentages of NK cells than females (P<0.05); patients younger than 65 years had higher percentages of CD3+T cells and CD3+CD4+T cells, and lower NK cells (P<0.05). Multivariate logistic regression demonstrated that age <65 years (P=0.038), TNM stage I (P=0.026), longer interval between radiotherapy and surgery (P=0.003), and higher percentage of CD3+T cells (P=0.043) were independent predictive factors for pCR. ROC analysis revealed that CD3+T-cell percentage yielded an AUC of 0.673 (95% CI:0.581-0.764) for pCR prediction, with optimal cutoff value 68.155, sensitivity 0.563 and specificity 0.726.ConclusionThe percentage of peripheral blood CD3+ T cells may serve as a non-invasive predictive marker for the efficacy of neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (nCRT) in rectal cancer (RC) patients. Combined with age, tumor stage, and treatment interval, it may help optimize individualized treatment regimens.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) metastasizes to the ovary in approximately 0.8-7.4% of cases, typically indicating aggressive biology and poor prognosis. Metachronous bilateral ovarian involvement with spontaneous rupture is exceptionally rare, and the distinction between signet-ring cell (Krukenberg) and non-signet-ring cell metastases carries prognostic significance. We present a 54-year-old female who underwent laparoscopic right hemicolectomy for pT4aN0M0 ascending colon adenocarcinoma, followed by eight cycles of adjuvant XELOX chemotherapy. Nineteen months later, imaging revealed huge pelvic cystic-solid masses with diffuse peritoneal thickening. Intraoperatively, spontaneous rupture of the mass (~14 cm) with active bleeding and hemorrhagic ascites was found, along with extensive miliary peritoneal seeding. The patient underwent bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, omentectomy, and HIPEC catheter placement. Pathology confirmed bilateral ovarian metastatic adenocarcinoma of colorectal origin with no signet-ring cells, excluding a true Krukenberg tumor. Genetic testing revealed NRAS p.G12D mutation and high tumor mutational burden (TMB-H). She subsequently received six cycles of XELOX chemotherapy with bevacizumab and serplulimab (anti-PD-1), achieving stable disease. This case demonstrates that non-signet-ring cell ovarian metastases can be equally aggressive, manifesting as spontaneous rupture after standardized therapy. For T4a CRC patients with serosal invasion, vigilant surveillance for ovarian and peritoneal metastasis is warranted. The multimodal strategy of cytoreductive surgery, HIPEC, and genotype-directed immunotherapy may offer a promising salvage approach in this challenging setting.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Stimulator of interferon genes (STING) agonists are intended to convert cytosolic DNA sensing into productive antitumor immunity, yet their biological effects vary substantially among tumors. Outcomes depend on the cellular compartment engaged, the amplitude and duration of signaling, tumor genotype, the immune architecture of the tumor microenvironment, and drug distribution. A critical distinction must therefore be made between chronic endogenous, tumor-cell-intrinsic cyclic GMP-AMP synthase-stimulator of interferon genes (cGAS-STING) signaling, as may occur in chromosomally unstable tumors, and controlled pharmacological STING agonism. The former can sustain maladaptive inflammatory programs in selected experimental settings, whereas the latter can be delivered transiently and may preferentially activate dendritic cells and other host immune compartments. This narrative review examines canonical STING-TBK1-IRF3/type I interferon signaling and alternative chronic outputs; relates these mechanisms to chromosomal instability, mismatch-repair status, immune surveillance, and immune checkpoint blockade; and evaluates early clinical experience with intratumoral STING agonists. Available trials demonstrate target engagement and generally manageable toxicity, but efficacy has been limited or heterogeneous. Mismatch-repair status, tumor mutational burden, chromosomal instability, baseline interferon activity, STING pathway competence, immune-cell topology, and delivery feasibility should therefore be considered components of a candidate composite biomarker strategy rather than validated predictors. By contrast, STING inhibition in chromosomal-instability-high tumors remains a promising preclinical hypothesis, not an established treatment. Prospective, compartment-resolved biomarker studies are needed to match agonists, delivery systems, combination regimens, or inhibitory approaches to the appropriate tumor state.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Immune checkpoint blockade has reshaped cancer therapy, but durable responses remain limited by insufficient antigen release, poor T-cell infiltration, immunosuppressive tumor microenvironments, and systemic immune-related toxicity. Ultrasound-responsive nanoplatforms provide a spatiotemporally controllable strategy to overcome these barriers by exploiting deep tissue penetration, focal activation, and repeatable external triggering. In this review, we summarize recent experimental advances in sonosensitizer-based and ultrasound-triggered nanoplatforms for cancer immunotherapy. These systems integrate sonodynamic immunogenic cell death, pyroptosis, ferroptosis, necroptosis, cGAS-STING activation, immune checkpoint blockade, mRNA delivery, gas therapy, and tumor microenvironment remodeling to convert immune-cold tumors into immune-responsive lesions. We further discuss cancer type-specific applications in hepatocellular carcinoma, pancreatic cancer, glioblastoma, triple-negative breast cancer, colorectal cancer, bladder cancer, and other solid tumors, emphasizing how ultrasound-responsive designs can be matched to distinct anatomical and immunological barriers. Finally, we highlight key translational challenges, including long-term biosafety, controllable immune activation, ultrasound parameter standardization, scalable manufacturing, and clinically compatible combination strategies. Ultrasound-responsive nanoplatforms are emerging not merely as drug carriers, but as programmable immune-engineering systems capable of coordinating when, where, and how antitumor immunity is activated within the tumor microenvironment.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Enterotoxigenic Bacteroides fragilis (ETBF) weakens the intestinal epithelial barrier and promotes inflammatory signaling through secretion of B. fragilis toxin (BFT), a metalloprotease associated with chronic intestinal inflammation. By triggering the breakdown of the E-cadherin glycoprotein in cellular junctions, BFT compromises tissue integrity and affects pathways involved in tumor suppression and signal transduction. Despite growing evidence implicating BFT in colorectal carcinogenesis, its role remains ambiguous, in part due to limited availability of suitable tools for its detection and neutralization. Selective binding molecules targeting BFT are, therefore, critical for understanding the role of ETBF in these clinical pathologies. Here, we used phage display screening to develop hagfish VLRB-derived consensus scaffold, termed ccombodies, as alternative non-immunoglobulin molecules targeting BFT. Three candidate binders (B8-1, C2-6, and G8-5) were expressed and purified for characterization. Specificity analyses against a range of bacterial virulence factors confirmed the selective recognition of BFT. Binding affinity was determined by ELISA titration and biolayer interferometry (BLI) yielding apparent KD values in the nanomolar range. The ccombodies detected BFT at low nanogram levels by Western blot and exhibited high specificity and sensitivity in toxin recognition. Furthermore, treatment with ccombody attenuated BFT-induced cytotoxicity in Caco-2 and HT-29 epithelial cells. These findings establish ccombodies as a novel class of BFT-targeting molecules with potential applications in selective toxin detection, passive immunoprophylaxis, and antivirulence intervention.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Early-onset colorectal cancer (EOCRC) exhibits distinct clinical and biological features compared with late-onset CRC (LOCRC), yet its genomic architecture and immune microenvironmental determinants remain incompletely characterized. Here, we integrated multiomics discovery analyses of 69 EOCRC and 461 LOCRC patients from the TCGA cohort, complemented by independent validation, single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and systems-level network analysis. We identified 10 genes significantly enriched for mutations in EOCRC, including ANXA7, ZNF267, and POLQ, which displayed distinct domain-specific clustering and were validated in an external cohort. Mutational signature decomposition showed that EOCRC was associated with an SBS87-like signature, whereas LOCRC was dominated by SBS1; because TCGA lacks detailed treatment history, this SBS87-like inference should not be interpreted as direct evidence of prior thiopurine exposure. Immunologically, EOCRC displayed an immunosuppressive microenvironment characterized by elevated regulatory T cells, resting NK cells, and tighter immune-stromal coupling, as further supported by spatial transcriptomic analysis. Single-cell atlas analysis identified M2-polarized, SPP1-expressing macrophage subsets in EOCRC. Weighted gene coexpression network analysis identified a mitochondrial-ribosomal biogenesis module as the transcriptional hallmark of EOCRC. Finally, random forest analysis identified FAT3 mutations as a genomic correlate of a hot-like, immune-activated phenotype in EOCRC. Integrative single-cell analysis localized FAT3 predominantly to cancer-associated fibroblasts, especially myofibroblasts, and an in silico FAT3 perturbation analysis suggested potential downstream programs involving extracellular matrix remodeling, inflammatory signaling, chemokine response, and mitotic spindle regulation. These findings delineate age-stratified genomic and microenvironmental features of EOCRC and generate testable hypotheses for future functional and clinical validation.

Staged introduction of a first-in-human concomitant robotic liver resection and cone-beam CT-guided percutaneous liver ablation in a hybrid operating room (HARMONY): an IDEAL stage 0/1 study.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
To perform the first-in-human concomitant robotic liver resection and cone-beam CT (CBCT)-guided ablation in a hybrid operating room (HARMONY). IDEAL stage 0/1 study outlining the preparatory steps and outcomes of the first-in-human HARMONY procedure. IDEAL stage 0 involved conceptualisation, team training and dry runs. The first HARMONY procedure was performed and the procedural technique is described in detail. All procedures took place at a single academic medical centre. Patients eligible for the HARMONY procedure are any adults eligible for combined ablation and resection of colorectal liver metastases. The HARMONY procedure was performed in a first patient. Outcomes of patients who underwent sequential robotic liver resection and CT hepatic arteriography-guided liver ablation in the preparatory phase are also reported. Concomitant robotic liver resection and CBCT-guided ablation in a hybrid operating room. The primary outcome was technical feasibility of the HARMONY procedure defined as the technical success of both the robotic surgical resection and CBCT-guided ablation within the hybrid operating room. Between 2018 and 2024, 19 patients underwent sequential robotic liver resection and CT-guided ablation. Median interval between procedures was 4 days, with 36.8% treated during one admission. Intraoperative incidents occurred in three (15.8%) patients and two (10.5%) patients experienced severe complications requiring reintervention. The first-in-human HARMONY procedure was successfully completed without intraoperative complications. The concomitant performance of robotic liver resection and CBCT-guided ablation is technically feasible in a hybrid operating room. Future studies should evaluate its reproducibility, safety and long-term outcomes. CCMO Research with human participants (NL-009169).

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Combination therapy with encorafenib, binimetinib, and cetuximab for BRAF V600E-mutated colorectal cancer is associated with early adverse ocular events, including serous retinal detachment. Therefore, careful monitoring of patients during outpatient treatment is essential. A 56-year-old woman with stage IV BRAF V600E-mutated colorectal cancer was treated with encorafenib, binimetinib, and cetuximab. Given the risk of adverse ocular events, hospital pharmacists requested that a community pharmacy provide intensive monitoring. On day 5, during a telephone follow-up by a community pharmacist, the patient reported visual symptoms but did not recognize their clinical significance. Suspecting a serious adverse ocular event, the community pharmacist advised immediate medical evaluation and submitted a tracing report to a hospital pharmacist. Both encorafenib and binimetinib were discontinued immediately, and ophthalmological examination confirmed a grade 2 serous retinal detachment. After the event was resolved, encorafenib and binimetinib were resumed at reduced doses on day 71. Continued follow-up after dose reduction enabled the detection of recurrent visual symptoms. The community pharmacist contacted the hospital pharmacist and submitted a tracing report. Because serous retinal detachment was confirmed as grade 1, the therapy was continued at reduced doses without interruption. Therapy continued until disease progression was observed on day 260. This case highlights the role of community pharmacists in monitoring adverse events during outpatient oral anticancer therapy. Scheduled telephone follow-ups, combined with hospital-community pharmacy collaboration, may facilitate the detection of adverse events, prevent progression to severe outcomes, and support continued treatment.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a major health concern. Adenoma Detection Rate (ADR) is a key quality indicator in colonoscopy and has been primarily studied in screening populations. Objectives: To report the ADR among symptomatic patients aged ≥50 years undergoing diagnostic colono-scopy, determine the overall adenoma prevalence, and describe the characteristics and associations of adenomatous polyps. Data from 235 consecutive symptomatic patients undergoing colonoscopy by a single endoscopist at a single centre over three years were analysed retrospectively. Demographic information, endoscopic findings and histopathological reports were collected. The chi-square and Fisher's exact test were used to compare the adenoma prevalence across the different age groups and genders, taking a p-value of 0.05 as statistically significant. The majority of patients were males (56%), with a median age of 60 years (IQR:42-69). The ADR among symptomatic patients aged ≥50 years was 22% (95%CI:16.2-27.7), while the overall adenoma prevalence was 19.6% (95%CI:14.9-25.1). Polyps and histologically confirmed malignancies were detected in 52 patients (22.1%), with 46 (19.6%) having adenomas. Most adenomas were sessile (77%, n=57) and located in the descending or sigmoid (39.2%) and transverse colon (35.1%). Multiple adenomas were detected in 34.8%. There was an age-related rise in adenoma prevalence, with those aged ≥60 years having the highest ADR (25.4%, p<0.05). Conclusion: The observed ADR of 22% in patients aged ≥50 years serves as preliminary evidence for a regional ADR benchmark for diagnostic colonoscopy in symptomatic patients, outside of screening programmes, particularly in resource-limited settings.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Lynch syndrome, historically known as hereditary nonpolyposis colorectal cancer, is caused by germline mutations in the DNA mismatch repair (MMR) genes, MLH1, MSH2 (EPCAM), MSH6, and PMS2. While the genetic changes associated with Lynch syndrome have previously been characterized, there have not been studies of the associated proteomic alterations, in part because of the limited availability of primary samples and the absence of in vitro model systems. In this study, the first large-scale tissue proteomic assessment of Lynch syndrome samples as well as three other subtypes of colorectal cancer was completed with specimens from the Ohio Colorectal Cancer Prevention Initiative. The cohort contained three groups of microsatellite unstable (MSI-high) colorectal cancer (CRC) patients (Lynch syndrome, double somatic MMR mutation, and MLH1 hypermethylation) and a group of microsatellite stable (MSS) CRC patients. A total of 122 tumor and complimentary normal mucosa samples from 61 patients were evaluated using label-free bottom-up proteomic analysis identifying 7,352 proteins. Hierarchical clustering analysis of the global proteome showed that the MSS group was significantly different than the three MSI-high groups. Of the 1,607 proteins found to be dysregulated within CRC patients, 648 proteins were specific to Lynch syndrome and 260 proteins were dysregulated across all four subtypes studied. Further examination of dysregulated proteins in response to age of diagnosis and patient's sex assigned at birth were also evaluated. This study fills a critical gap as the first proteomic characterization of Lynch syndrome samples to date. Data are available via ProteomeXchange with identifier PXD073693.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Introduction: Treatment strategies for colorectal cancer liver metastases (CRLM) are increasingly complex, driving interest in advanced prognostic tools. Externally validated benchmarks based on established clinical risk scores are needed to contextualise emerging models. However, existing scores remain difficult to apply and compare, because they provide categorical risk strata rather than individualised probabilities, and because model parameters are rarely published. Here, we validate and recalibrate seven established risk scores to derive individualised recurrence probabilities for future score benchmarking. Method: Patients undergoing index CRLM resection from two tertiary centres were included: Karolinska University Hospital (retrospective KaroLiver cohort [2013-2021, follow-up to 2025, n=709]) and Oslo University Hospital (OSLO-COMET trial cohort [2012-2016, follow-up to 2022, n=198]). Performance of the GAME, m-CS, Fong, Nordlinger, Nagashima, Konopke and Helsinki scores was assessed using recurrence-free survival as the primary outcome. Results: Among 709 patients in KaroLiver (median age 67 years [IQR 59-74]; 434 men [61%]), 422 (60%) had synchronous metastases and 444 (63%) received neoadjuvant chemotherapy. All scores significantly stratified recurrence risk (log-rank P<0.001; time-dependent AUC 0.63-0.74 at 3 years), albeit with performance differences across time points. Recalibrated models showed good agreement between predicted and observed recurrence and were externally validated in OSLO-COMET with broadly comparable net benefit. Models were implemented in the online tool PLATO (Personalised Liver metastases risk AssessmenT in Oncology). Conclusion: Established CRLM risk scores can be translated into individualised probabilistic recurrence estimates at clinically relevant time points, supporting patient communication, risk-adapted surveillance and transparent benchmarking of next-generation prognostic models.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Most population colorectal cancer (CRC) screening programs use the faecal immunochemical test (FIT), which quantifies occult haemoglobin in faeces and has proven to be effective in detecting and reducing CRC incidence and mortality. Sessile serrated lesions (SSLs) account for up to 30% of sporadic CRC, yet FIT has low sensitivity to detect them. Faecal microbial biomarkers may improve their detection, but FIT samples have not previously been used to study the SSL microbiome. We asked whether FIT samples preserve the faecal microbiome as accurately as fresh collection, and whether they can reveal a microbial signature of SSL. We first reanalysed a published dataset of paired FIT and fresh faecal samples from the same participants. Donor identity explained 63.5% of compositional variance compared with 16.7% for collection method, indicating that FIT preserves the donor-specific signature on which biomarker discovery depends. We then generated shotgun metagenomes from FIT samples of 24 adults scheduled for diagnostic colonoscopy, twelve with at least one clinically significant SSL and twelve with no neoplasia (NN) and compared each group with a published fresh faeces cohort matched on colonoscopy outcome. Collection method explained 6.3% to 7.6% of variance, and no individual species was significantly differentially abundant between methods. Between SSL and NN FIT samples, community structure did not significantly differ, and conservative differential abundance analysis returned no results. More permissive count-based models suggested a depletion of fermentative commensals in SSL. Functionally, SSL samples encoded significantly fewer KEGG orthologs and less polyamine biosynthesis capacity, while orthologs carried by several Bifidobacterium species were more abundant. Many depleted functions reflected Enterobacteriaceae gene content concentrated in a few control samples. No single feature was diagnostic on its own. A multi-feature signature, confirmed in larger cohorts and applied to samples that screening programs already collect, may increase the detection rate of SSLs.

Targeting REV1 Exposes Context-Dependent Therapeutic Responses in Colorectal Cancer
bioRxiv (预印本) · 2026-11-06 · Gupta, V.; Guyette, M.; Bhattacharya, S.; Victor, J.; Kothandaraman, N.; Boyle, K. A.; Girard, J. P.; Hong, J.; Ramsey, J.; Zhou, P.; CHATTERJEE, N.
意义与启示：REV1抑制剂JH-RE-06在肠癌中增敏化疗呈背景依赖，并抑制患者来源类器官生长，提示REV1靶向需精准分层且可能拓展至TLS之外机制。
展开英文原题摘要与原文链接
ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Translesion synthesis (TLS) promotes DNA damage tolerance and contributes to chemotherapy resistance by enabling replication across damaged DNA templates. REV1, a central TLS regulator, is a potential therapeutic target to enhance the efficacy of genotoxic chemotherapy. Here, we investigated the therapeutic consequences of pharmacologic and genetic REV1 targeting in colorectal cancer (CRC) and evaluated the sensitivity of patient-derived CRC organoids to the REV1 inhibitor JH-RE-06. JH-RE-06 enhanced oxaliplatin sensitivity in HCT116 cells and 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) sensitivity in HT-29 cells, whereas reciprocal combinations produced limited sensitization, indicating treatment- and cellular context-dependent responses. siRNA-mediated REV1 depletion similarly enhanced chemotherapy sensitivity, supporting REV1 involvement in these responses. MNNG sensitivity assays and MLH1 expression analyses did not reveal consistent treatment-associated changes in mismatch repair function, while targeted HPRT1 sequencing identified no detectable sequence alterations in the region examined. Chemosensitization was not accompanied by consistent increases in caspase-3/7 activation under the conditions tested. REV1 inhibition also caused LC3-II accumulation and, after prolonged inhibitor exposure, reduced beta-tubulin abundance, indicating additional autophagy-associated and cytoskeletal responses. In two patient-derived CRC organoid models, JH-RE-06 exhibited single-agent growth-inhibitory activity, with mean IC50 values of 2.01 micromolar and 1.4 micromolar, respectively. Together, these findings demonstrate context-dependent chemosensitization and organoid growth inhibition following REV1 targeting, suggesting that its therapeutic consequences may extend beyond canonical TLS-mediated DNA damage tolerance.

意义与启示：MintCNA通过整合单细胞多组学数据提升拷贝数变异检测精度，在结直肠癌中揭示转移过程中17号染色体进行性缺失，为肠癌肝转移克隆演化研究提供新工具。
展开英文原题摘要与原文链接
ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Chromosomal copy number alterations (CNAs) are key drivers of tumor evolution, disease progression and therapeutic resistance, and their identification is critical for delineating tumor clonal structure. However, accurately detecting CNAs from single-cell data remains challenging as most existing CNA callers still analyze a single omics layer and are susceptible to assay-specific noise. Recently, single-cell multi-omics techniques have enabled joint sequencing of multiple molecular layers (e.g., genomics and transcriptomics) simultaneously in the same cells, yet computational methods that fully exploit such complementary multi-omics data for CNA analysis remain limited. Here, we present MintCNA, a unified framework for CNA detection from paired single-cell multi-omics data. MintCNA integrates deep-learning based denoising with a missingness-adjusted multivariate change-point detection procedure to enhance CNA profiling across omics layers. In simulations, MintCNA outperformed existing single-cell CNA callers across all evaluated scenarios. MintCNA showed the highest correlation with bulk whole-genome sequencing in a colorectal cancer dataset and revealed progressive loss of chromosome 17 during metastasis. In an IDH-mutant glioma cohort, MintCNA generalized to paired single-cell ATAC-seq and RNA-seq data and identified copy number subclones corresponding to distinct malignant cell states. MintCNA provides an advanced multi-omics integrative single-cell CNA analysis tool for better delineating the mechanisms underlying disease progression and tumor evolution.

First-trimester nocturnal cardiorespiratory coupling during home sleep testing and later pregnancy complications: a secondary analysis of the nuMoM2b cohort
medRxiv (预印本) · 2026-11-05 · Wu, Y.; Asvadi, S.; van der Ven, M.; van der Hout-van der Jagt, M. B.; Peri, E.; Vullings, R.; OEH van Laar, J.; Fonseca, P.; Overeem, S.; Mischi, M.; Long, X.
意义与启示：该研究揭示孕早期心肺耦合异常可预测妊娠糖尿病与巨大儿，与肠癌无直接关联，但提示心肺耦合等生理节律标志物或可拓展至肿瘤预后研究。
展开英文原题摘要与原文链接
ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
We tested whether direction-specific nocturnal cardiorespiratory coupling (CRC) in the first trimester differed in pregnancies that later developed obstetric complications. The analysis included 2504 nulliparous women from the nuMoM2b cohort with valid level 3 home sleep recordings at 6-13 weeks' gestation. Bidirectional CRC between RR intervals and abdominal respiratory effort was quantified using bivariate phase-rectified signal averaging in consecutive 5-min segments. Coupling strength, local transition dynamics, and waveform irregularity were summarized by nightly mean and standard deviation. Associations with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM; n = 111), preeclampsia (n = 149), preterm birth (n = 192), and fetal macrosomia (n = 186) were examined using proportional-odds models with CRC feature quintile as the ordered outcome. Models included all four complications simultaneously and adjusted for maternal age, pre-pregnancy body mass index, race and ethnicity, gestational age at recording, relevant medical and family history, medication use, and apnea-hypopnea index >5 events/h. Holm correction was applied across outcomes. GDM was associated with lower respiration-to-heart rate coupling strength (cumulative odds ratio, 0.45; 95% CI, 0.31-0.64; P < 0.001) and shallower slope at the anchor point (0.63; 0.45-0.89; P = 0.03). Fetal macrosomia was associated with lower within-night variability in heart rate-to-respiration waveform irregularity (0.59; 0.45-0.77; P < 0.001). No associations with preeclampsia or preterm birth remained significant after correction. Direction-specific differences in nocturnal CRC were detectable in the first trimester in pregnancies that later developed GDM or resulted in fetal macrosomia.

意义与启示：揭示APOLD1/ELF5启动子低甲基化驱动CIMP阴性肠癌干细胞样可塑性，且ELF5转移灶对PI3K/mTOR抑制敏感，为肝转移分层治疗提供表观遗传靶点。
展开英文原题摘要与原文链接
ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) has high phenotypic plasticity, but regulatory mechanisms of aberrant cell states are not well described. We investigated DNA methylation-based regulation of cancer cell-intrinsic transcriptomic heterogeneity in 1,183 multiregional primary tumor samples, liver metastases and tumor organoids. Most genes with strong methylation-transcriptomic association reflected canonical promoter hypermethylation and expression repression related to the CpG island methylator phenotype (CIMP). However, promoter hypomethylation and overexpression of APOLD1 and ELF5 identified two largely non-overlapping subgroups of canonical CIMP-negative CRCs enriched with stem-like and transit-amplifying cell states. APOLD1 tumors were further highly proliferative while ELF5 tumors were slow-cycling and associated with good survival in early-stage disease. Target genes showed patient-specific expression changes in matched primary-metastasis samples, and ELF5 aberrant metastases showed ex vivo sensitivity to putative targeting of stem cells by PI3K/mTOR inhibition, fetal de-differentiation and transition into non-canonical intestinal states. This implicates focal promoter hypomethylation in phenotypic plasticity in CRC metastasis.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Spatial transcriptomics (ST) is increasingly used to map clonal architecture within tumors, yet methods for analyzing cancer ST data are difficult to evaluate because real tumors lack ground truth for copy-number alterations (CNAs), subclonal identity, and malignant cell fraction. Existing ST simulators model normal tissue and do not represent tumor evolution, CNA-driven expression, or the spatial organization of malignant subclones. We present OncoSpot, a cancer-aware simulator of Visium-like spot-based ST data. OncoSpot combines a spatial evolutionary scaffold from DEMON, CNAs generated along the resulting clonal phylogeny with CNAsim, cancer-type-specific malignant transcriptional programs, and spatially clustered nonmalignant cell types, and aggregates cells into spots with known malignant fraction, subclone, and copy-number profiles. We demonstrate OncoSpot on high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma, colorectal cancer, and hepatocellular carcinoma, which represent three distinct modes of tumor evolution. Simulated subclones were spatially clustered and showed stronger phylogeny-space concordance than those generated by scCube under matched subclone populations. Benchmarking CopyKAT, CancerFinder, Clonalscope, and RCTD revealed cancer-dependent performance: Clonalscope recovered copy-number signals more accurately in ovarian and colorectal cancer, whereas CopyKAT performed better in hepatocellular carcinoma, reflecting both the assumptions of each method and the copy-number landscapes of the three cancers. OncoSpot's ground truth also exposed a failure mode in Clonalscope's malignant spot identification, in which tumor and normal labels were inverted, and allowed us to trace its cause. These method-dependent behaviors would be difficult to detect in real data. OncoSpot provides a framework for benchmarking CNA inference, subclone detection, malignant spot identification, and normal spot deconvolution, and its modular design and guidelines allow extension to additional cancer types. OncoSpot is freely available at https://github.com/compbio-mallory/OncoSpot.

A post hoc closest-10% matching sensitivity gave P=0.571. In 23 independent GSE132465 patients, the tumour-wide correlation was 0.735 (permutation P=0.00060) and the epithelial correlation was 0.376 (P=0.0892). The difference in absolute correlations was 0.359, with a 95% confidence interval of -0.041 to 0.759, leaving attenuation uncertain. These results identify the comparison conditions needed to interpret the tested RNA readouts. Linking them to membrane transfer requires event-resolved protein measurements.

In particular, KDM6A has been implicated in a variety of malignancies and is frequently mutated in cancers including those in kidney, bladder, colorectal, and breast. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Background: In rectal cancer (RC), tumor deposits (TDs) are clinically important as they are associated with a negative impact on prognosis and affect risk stratification as well as management plans. MRI radiomics combined with artificial intelligence (AI) has been explored for non-invasive preoperative TDs detection. However, results vary across studies; therefore, we performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to pool their diagnostic test accuracy (DTA). Methods: This systematic review and DTA meta-analysis were conducted in accordance with the Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Diagnostic Test Accuracy and reported in adherence to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses of Diagnostic Test Accuracy Studies (PRISMA-DTA). Databases were screened for DTA studies of MRI-based radiomics predicting TDs in adult RC patients with histopathology as reference. Results: Nine studies (2589 patients) were identified. Across included studies, the bivariate meta-analysis showed pooled sensitivity of 0.765 (95% CI 0.714 - 0.809) and specificity of 0.790 (95% CI 0.750 - 0.825), with overall AUC of 0.845 and very low heterogeneity (I2 = 7.3%). In validation datasets, diagnostic performance remained consistent (AUC 0.806), with pooled sensitivity 0.751 (95% CI 0.681 - 0.809) and specificity 0.751 (95% CI 0.681 - 0.809). For MRI modality, T2 weighted image (T2WI) showed higher sensitivity (0.745) than T2WI plus diffusion weighted image (DWI) (0.697), while T2WI+DWI had higher specificity (0.809 vs 0.737) and AUC (0.829 vs 0.796), with no significant subgroup differences (p[≥]0.192). Models combining radiomics with clinical/radiological variables achieved significantly higher sensitivity (0.842 vs 0.657, p<0.001) and higher AUC (0.827 vs 0.752), with comparable specificity. Conclusion: MRI-based radiomics demonstrates good accuracy for preoperative detection of tumor deposits in RC. The integration of radiomics with clinical or imaging features increases the accuracy of identification. Amongst the MRI modalities, models that utilize the combination of T2WI plus DWI are more accurate than those using T2WI or DWI only.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Chromosome replication initiation in bacterial genomes typically occurs at a single origin, called oriC, through the binding of the DnaA initiator protein to specific chromosomal repeats known as DnaA-boxes. Here, relying on comparative genomics, we show that the family Fusobacteriaceae, which belongs to the order Fusobacteriales alongside the family Leptotrichiaceae, deviates from this paradigm. Our analysis revealed a stark contrast between the two lineages: while dnaA flanks oriC in Leptotrichiaceae, it is notably missing from Fusobacteriaceae genomes. Adjacent to oriC in Fusobacteriaceae, we identified a gene encoding replication initiator protein A (RPA). We characterized RPA as a Rep-type initiator involved in plasmid replication that likely originated from an iteron-containing plasmid, iterons being the plasmid analogues of DnaA-boxes. Phylogenetic reconstruction indicates that the gene encoding RPA was acquired together with its associated iterons and subsequently domesticated by the Fusobacteriaceae ancestor, successfully displacing the ancestral chromosomal dnaA gene at the origin of replication. This shift to a plasmid-derived replication system may represent an adaptive trait of the Fusobacteriaceae, potentially offering new insights into the biology of Fusobacterium nucleatum, a member of this family known to be a major driver of colorectal cancer progression within the tumor microenvironment.

Liver metastases are a major cause of mortality in colorectal cancer (CRC) and pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), yet the oncogenic signals that shape tumor metabolism in the hepatic niche remain poorly understood. Here, we show that HER3 activation drives a liver metastasis-specific glycolytic program in both cancer types. Genetic or pharmacological HER3 inhibition suppresses cancer glycolysis while increasing dependence on oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS), rendering liver metastases vulnerable to OXPHOS inhibition. Combining the HER3 inhibitor sapitinib with distinct OXPHOS inhibitors led to in vitro synergy and durable tumor-free survival in orthotopic CRC and PDAC liver metastases models, with further validation in patient-derived xenografts. Mechanistically, HER3 promotes glycolysis through activating PFK2 and reduces OXPHOS through activating DRP1-mediated mitochondrial remodeling, both pathways were activated in liver metastases compared to matched primary tumors. Together, our findings identify the HER3-AKT/RSK-PFK2 axis as a driver of glycolysis and metastatic growth and reveal an OXPHOS dependency induced by HER3 inhibition that may be exploited through combined HER3 and OXPHOS targeting in metastatic CRC and PDAC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
During development, the blood vasculature expands by sprouting angiogenesis, but the programs that guide this process can become dysregulated in the pathological angiogenesis of neovascular diseases leading to excessive disorganized blood vessels. We previously reported that in endothelial cells, the pro-mesenchymal transcription factor Slug critically regulates angiogenesis through a partial and reversible endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition (pEndoMT); however, the upstream regulators that activate Slug and may contribute to pathological activation of the pEndoMT pathway in disease are still poorly understood. Here, we show that endothelial cells express an unusual low molecular weight variant of Ovol1 - a zinc-finger transcription factor that regulates mesenchymal transition in epithelial cells. Ovol1 and Slug are co-expressed in angiogenic endothelial cells, and using ChIP, we confirm direct Ovol1 binding to the endogenous Slug gene at a species-conserved binding motif. Whereas Ovol1 is typically a transcriptional repressor in epithelial cells, we find using a combination of silencing RNA and lentiviral overexpression constructs that the endothelial Ovol1 variant upregulates Slug, and is sufficient to drive pEndoMT marker expression and enhance endothelial cell migratory capacity. Silencing of Ovol1 abolished sprouting angiogenesis in a 3D in vitro sprouting angiogenesis assay, whereas constitutive overexpression of Ovol1 produced overaggressive and disorganized hypersprouting that depends upon Slug. We generated Ovol1 or Slug endothelial-specific knockout mice (Ovol1ECKO and SlugECKO) and found that healthy developmental angiogenesis of the neonatal mouse retina proceeds relatively normally in knockout animals. By contrast, Ovol1 was reduced in established post-natal blood vessels but became strongly re-expressed in tumor endothelial cells, and we found that colorectal cancer syngraft growth was significantly reduced in both Ovol1ECKO and SlugECKO mice alongside a failure of tumor angiogenesis. Lastly, neovascularization in the oxygen-induced retinopathy (OIR) model was also reduced in SlugECKO mice. In conclusion, we report that an endothelial Ovol1 variant upregulates Slug and drives a mesenchymal-like state, and that this Ovol1-Slug pEndoMT signaling axis is essential for pathological angiogenesis in neovascular disease models.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Introduction: Sexually transmitted infections (STIs) and colorectal cancer (CRC) are rising in the United States, yet their shared mucosal environment remains underexplored. Rectal douching, a common practice among individuals engaging in receptive anal intercourse, has been epidemiologically linked to increased STI and HPV risk, but biological mechanisms are unclear. Methods: Using a human colorectal epithelial co-culture model (Caco-2/HT29-MTX-E12), we compared the effects of common douching products on cell viability, barrier integrity, and cytokine response. Results: Hyperosmolar or surfactant-containing solutions, including saline enemas, detergents, and soaps, caused rapid declines in metabolic activity and transepithelial electrical resistance, coupled with IL-6 and TNF- upregulation. In contrast, isotonic formulations maintained epithelial viability and barrier function comparable to buffered controls while reducing inflammatory signaling. Discussion: These findings provide mechanistic evidence that many consumer douching products compromise mucosal health and highlight the feasibility of harm-reduction designs for safer anal hygiene and sexual preparation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Selectively eliminating cancer cells based on their oncogenic drivers holds great promise but remains challenging for targeted cancer therapy. Here, we present ORCA (Oncogenic RNA-triggered Cancer Ablation), a programmable and modular platform that couples RADAR-based detection of oncogenic RNA with conditional expression of therapeutic payloads in cancer cells. We identify RADAR sensors targeting the transcripts of endogenously amplified oncogenes, including MYC, FGFR2 and wild-type KRAS in colorectal and gastric cancer cells. Focusing on colorectal cancer (CRC) driven by extrachromosomal DNA-amplified MYC, we demonstrate targeted ablation of high-MYC cancer cells using two orthogonal strategies: anti-CD19 CAR-T therapy and enzyme-prodrug therapy. In vivo delivery of ORCA using adeno-associated virus (AAV) suppresses tumor growth in a subcutaneous xenograft model and prolongs survival in a CRC liver metastasis model. ORCA establishes oncogenic RNAs as actionable inputs for targeted cancer therapy via programmable RNA sensing, thus offering a strategy to target tumors through the transcripts of otherwise difficult-to-drug oncogenes such as MYC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
DNA Polymerase Delta (Pol {delta}) acts in DNA synthesis and in DNA repair, both important factors in the proliferative nature, longevity, and mutability of cancer cells. The chromosomal region containing POLD3, the third subunit of Pol {delta}, has recently been identified by genome wide-association studies as containing single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) that increase the risk of colorectal cancer (CRC). To explore the effects of changing POLD3 levels that may underly these statistical associations in CRC, we first carried out survival analyses in the Cancer Genome Atlas colon adenocarcinoma cohort. Cox proportional hazards modelling showed higher POLD3 expression to be associated with moderately improved overall survival in the full cohort. This association with survival was clearest in the microsatellite stable (MSS) subgroup. In order to investigate the mechanisms by which lower POLD3 expression may be associated with poorer outcome, we generated CRC cell line models with reduced POLD3 expression levels. Knockdown of POLD3 resulted in reduced proliferative ability and stalling of the cell cycle in S phase, with some apoptosis of CRC cells. Importantly, POLD3 knockdown cells exhibited DNA damage, manifested by double-stranded breaks (DSBs), and upregulation of DSB repair pathways. Reduced POLD3 also correlated with shortened telomeres with disruption of, specifically, the ALT telomeric maintenance pathway. Taken together these observations suggest that lower POLD3 expression can increase genetic instability in CRC cells in the form of DSBs and shortened telomeres and that this might underly the functional effect of CRC risk SNPs in the POLD3 locus in 11q13.4. Simple SummaryDNA variants associated with an increased risk of colorectal cancer (CRC) are found near the gene POLD3. This study investigated the role of POLD3, a DNA replication and repair protein, in CRC. Analysis of patient data suggested that lower POLD3 expression was associated with reduced overall survival, particularly in patients with microsatellite stable tumours. To understand the biological basis of this association, CRC cell lines with reduced POLD3 expression were generated. Lower POLD3 levels slowed cell growth, stalled DNA replication, and increased cell death. Importantly though, reduced POLD3 expression led to greater DNA damage, including double-strand breaks, and activated DNA repair pathways. Cells with lower POLD3 also had shorter telomeres, probably due to disruption of the alternative lengthening of telomeres (ALT) maintenance pathway. These findings suggest that reduced POLD3 expression promotes genetic instability in CRC cells, which may contribute to poorer clinical outcomes, and provide a possible functional explanation for the risk variants in the POLD3 genomic region.

Gastrointestinal diagnosis and monitoring rely on colonoscopy, which requires anesthesia and a long wait, and non-invasive alternatives are lacking. Here we show that whole-transcriptome sequencing of stool host RNA, recovering a median of 6,300 protein-coding genes across 285 libraries spanning colorectal cancer (CRC) and inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), precancerous lesions (APL), and normal samples, reads a census of the cells shed into the lumen. In normal samples, epithelium supplies 81% and immune cells supply 11% of stool host mRNA transcripts; the immune cells share rises in CRC and IBD, and B- and T-cell receptor clonotypes rise with it. In this work, we show that CRC, IBD, and normal samples carry distinct transcriptome profiles, which a three-class model separates with an area under the curve of 0.94-0.96, and that within inflammatory bowel disease a 15-gene neutrophil score tracks endoscopic activity better than fecal calprotectin in the same stool.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Spatial transcriptomics (ST) has become a central tool in tissue biology, with multiple technologies addressing the issue from a different angle. Each platform imposes its own raw data format conventions, and few workflows address reproducible, scalable, cohort-level analyses while integrating expert-supervised decisions to strengthen computational and biological provenance. In this work, we present SpaceBlocks, a Snakemake workflow for reproducible cohort-level analysis of single-cell resolution-ST data that prioritizes expert supervision over full automation. SpaceBlocks homogenizes heterogeneous platform outputs into a common data format, whose structure is validated to ensure downstream processing. Comprehensive expert supervision is facilitated through per sample quality control and cell type annotation diagnostic visualizations, after which downstream analyses automatically follow. SpaceBlocks also allows the ingestion of technology-agnostic externally formatted data and provides interoperability with existing tools and technologies. We demonstrate the use of SpaceBlocks through the reanalysis of 37 samples from public Visium HD, Xenium 5K and MERSCOPE datasets. SpaceBlocks exhibited processing scalability across the three platforms. This reanalysis identified previously missed cell types in Visium HD and heterogeneous marker gene expression in MERSCOPE, highlighting the need for expert-supervised annotations. Moreover, SpaceBlocks facilitated the identification of differentially expressed genes associated with previously defined multiple sclerosis (MS) spatial domains in MERSCOPE, and transcriptional differences between healthy and malignant colorectal tissues in Visium HD. Together, these findings establish SpaceBlocks as a flexible and reproducible workflow for expert-supervised spatial transcriptomics analysis across technologies and biological cohorts.

C.; Meier, C.; Heim, T.; Neumann, C.; Attaran, S.; Brown, L.; Hooda, J.; Miller, L.; Kota, K.; Liu, T.; Puhalla, S. L.; Gurda, G.; Rigatti, L. H.; Sflomos, G.; Brisken, C.; Lucas, P. C.; McAuliffe, P. F.; Atkinson, J. M.; Lee, A. V.; Oesterreich, S.
意义与启示：该文献建立了罕见ILC细胞系并揭示PI3K/AKT通路脆弱性，对肠癌研究启示有限，但提示罕见亚型模型构建与通路靶向验证思路可借鉴。
展开英文原题摘要与原文链接
ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Breast cancer is broadly divided histologically into no special type (NST) and special subtypes, of which invasive lobular carcinoma (ILC) is the most common. ILC is distinguished by discohesive, single-file growth from loss of E-cadherin (CDH1). Few ILC cell lines exist, limiting mechanistic study of this understudied disease. Here we describe WCRC-25, a novel ILC cell line established from a pleural effusion of a patient with metastatic ILC. While WCRC-25 lacks ER expression, it is molecularly defined as luminal with Her2-like features, and shows anchorage-independent growth and haptotactic migration toward Collagen I. Sequencing identified a CDH1 Q706* truncating mutation alongside FOXA1, CTCF, BRCA2 and TP53 mutations shared with the patient's metastases, while copy-number and optical genome mapping revealed structural rearrangements typical of ILC. Transcriptomic AKT-pathway signatures predicted, and cell-based assays confirmed, sensitivity to PI3K/AKT inhibition. WCRC-25 also engrafted and spontaneously metastasized in vivo. WCRC-25 is a valuable new tool for dissecting ILC biology and therapeutic vulnerabilities.
