Prediction of Tubulin Inhibitor Sensitivity in Colon Cancer
bioRxiv (预印本) · 2026-11-02 · Linares-Blanco, J.; Lemler, L.; Chicote, I.; Ros, J.; Alcantara, A. M.; Martinez-Quintanilla, J.; Elez, E.; Palmer, H. G.; Fernandez-Lozano, C.; Seoane, J. A.
意义与启示：基于37基因预后签名构建ColoTubIn，可预测结肠癌对紫杉醇等微管蛋白抑制剂的敏感性，为药物重定位和个体化治疗提供新策略。
展开英文原题摘要与原文链接
ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer is the second most common cause of cancer death worldwide. Despite advances in molecular strategies for stratifying patients with colorectal cancer, their clinical implementation remains limited. Previous efforts have mainly focused on the development of prognostic gene expression signatures; however predictive biomarkers remain essential for translating molecular insights into effective therapies and ultimately enhancing patient outcomes. This study advances the translation of a molecular signature identified in colon cancer toward new therapeutic options for clinical applications. We leveraged public gene expression datasets to develop a prognostic 37-gene signature in colon cancer and validated its prognostic value across six clinical cohorts. We subsequently investigated the biological processes associated with the signature and its predictive potential for therapeutic response. We further evaluated its predictive capability for tubulin inhibitor response using paclitaxel in vitro and in vivo in patient-derived preclinical models. The signature showed prognostic performance comparable to published gene expression signatures across six independent cohorts without clinical covariates. The signature was associated with the mitotic phase of the cell cycle and identified a population of patient-derived colon cancer models sensitive to tubulin inhibitor drugs, subsequently referred to as the Colon Tubulin-Inhibitor Expression Signature (ColoTubIn). Low ColoTubIn scores were associated with increased paclitaxel sensitivity. Hence, ColoTubIn performs comparably to existing prognostic signatures while additionally identifying a molecularly defined subgroup of colon cancers with therapeutic potential. ColoTubIn is of particular interest since it can serve as a basis for drug repurposing strategies leveraging existing safety data to accelerate translation into the clinic.

Journal of Clinical Oncology : Official Journal of the American Society of Clinical Oncology · 2026-11 · Lafarge MW, Harkin A, Iveson T, Saunders M, Adams DJ, Oien K, et al.
要点与启示：imCMS基于常规病理图像实现结直肠癌分子分型，可改善II/III期预后分层且易于临床推广，为肝转移风险识别提供新工具。
展开英文原题摘要与原文链接
ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Risk stratification in localized colorectal cancer (CRC) remains inadequate. Transcriptome-based classifiers such as consensus molecular subtyping (CMS) improve this, but are challenging to implement. We determined the performance of a novel image-based method for CRC CMS subtyping (imCMS) using routine pathology images from the SCOT trial and investigated association of imCMS subtypes with clinicopathologic and tumor molecular and immune factors, treatment benefit, and survival. We applied a novel imCMS classifier to stage II/III CRCs from the SCOT trial (ISRCTN59757862) which examined 3 versus 6 months of adjuvant oxaliplatin-based chemotherapy following curative-intent surgery. We determined correlates of imCMS subgroups and investigated imCMS prognostic and predictive value for CRC recurrence-free interval, overall survival (OS), and survival after CRC recurrence (SAR) by univariable and multivariable Cox regression. A total of 2,816 cases were informative for imCMS classification, of which 664 (24%) were imCMS1 (immune), 987 (35%) imCMS2 (canonical), 433 (15%) imCMS3 (metabolic), 653 (23%) imCMS4 (mesenchymal), and 79 (3%) of mixed subtype. Analysis confirmed expected associations of imCMS1 with deficient DNA mismatch repair (dMMR) and imCMS3 with imCMS classification improves CRC prognostication beyond existing tumor factors and is potentially deliverable in clinical practice. imCMS prediction of therapeutic benefit requires further study.

展开英文原题摘要与原文链接
ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The goal of this project was to develop a joint European clinical practice guideline for the diagnosis and treatment of obstructed defecation syndrome (ODS), based on the best available evidence. These guidelines are intended to support all healthcare professionals involved in the care of patients with ODS, such as general practitioners, colorectal surgeons, gastroenterologists, gynecologists, radiologists, physiotherapists, and psychologists, as well as to provide accessible information for patients themselves. A multidisciplinary Guideline Development Group representing seven European scientific societies and including patient representatives formulated PICO-based clinical questions. Evidence was identified through a systematic literature review and assessed using the GRADE approach. Recommendations were formulated according to the available evidence and, where evidence was insufficient, as expert opinions. The final guideline includes 28 statements (1 moderate grade evidence, 2 low grade evidence, 3 very low grade evidence, 22 expert opinion) covering the diagnosis, conservative and surgical management of ODS, including indications for various imaging modalities, functional tests, and both transanal and transabdominal surgical approaches. Multidisciplinary assessment is recommended throughout the diagnostic and therapeutic pathway. Conservative treatment represents the initial management strategy, with biofeedback recommended before surgery in patients with ODS and dyssynergic defecation who fail dietary and laxative treatment. Surgery should be reserved for selected patients with persistent symptoms after conservative treatment and considered following multidisciplinary pelvic floor evaluation. These multidisciplinary European guidelines offer a comprehensive and evidence-based framework for the diagnosis and management of ODS. They are intended to promote standardized, high-quality care across Europe and to improve outcomes and quality of life for individuals affected by this complex condition. Given the limited quality of evidence supporting many interventions, individualized decision-making within a multidisciplinary setting remains central to ODS management.

本周热点与趋势总结

由本期文献提炼的课题组可执行信号
  1. 治疗策略：pMMR/MSS型mCRC免疫联合化疗的获益边界进一步明确。一项纳入截至2026年5月RCT的荟萃分析（Frontiers in Oncology）系统评估PD-1/PD-L1抑制剂联合化疗（±靶向）在pMMR mCRC中的疗效，以PFS与OS为主要终点、以HR及95%CI为效应量，提示该人群整体免疫获益有限，联合策略的适用需依赖更精细的生物标志物分层而非普适性推广。
  2. 生物标志物：CLDN18.2被定位为结直肠黏液腺癌（CMA）的谱系相关标志物与新兴转化靶点（Frontiers in Pharmacology）。CMA富集近端结肠、dMMR/MSI-H、BRAF V600E、CIMP-high及锯齿状通路特征，CLDN18.2在该组织学亚型中的表达为靶向药物（如CLDN18.2 ADC/双抗）在CRC中的患者选择提供了组织学—分子双重富集路径，值得在肝转移队列中前瞻验证。
  3. 机制发现：早发性结直肠癌（EOCRC）的侵袭性由多谱系重编程与NOTCH相关信号重塑所刻画。一项整合7个单细胞RNA测序队列、共473,939个高质量细胞（174例CRC，含39例EOCRC与135例平均发病年龄CRC）的研究（Frontiers in Oncology）构建了全面细胞图谱，提示EOCRC的 aggressive 生物学源于上皮谱系可塑性与微环境NOTCH信号重塑，为年轻患者肝转移高风险的机制解释与靶向干预提供线索。
  4. 机制发现：ANKRD22下调经脂质代谢重编程激活Notch/Hes1通路，驱动结直肠癌免疫抑制性巨噬细胞极化（Immunotargets and Therapy）。该研究结合非靶向代谢组学与细胞因子微阵列，识别CRC细胞上清中抑制巨噬细胞ANKRD22的代谢物与细胞因子，将肿瘤代谢—Notch轴—髓系免疫抑制串联为可干预节点，与上述EOCRC的NOTCH重塑形成呼应。
  5. 手术与局部治疗相关生物学：神经周围侵犯（PNI）与侵袭性表型及卡培他滨敏感性降低相关。一项724例组织学确诊CRC的双队列回顾研究（Frontiers in Oncology）显示PNI与复发、远处转移及化疗耐药相关，并首次提供PNI与特定细胞毒药物敏感性关联的患者层面证据；鉴于PNI是肝转移与局部复发的风险标志，其病理判读的采样局限与观察者间差异亟需标准化。
  6. 微环境与免疫治疗转化：髓系抑制的药理学重编程与超声响应纳米平台成为本周免疫转化两条并行主线。Frontiers in Pharmacology提出“髓系免疫转换审计轨迹（MICAT）”四层证据标准，以弥合生物学活性与可归因治疗性免疫转换之间的鸿沟；Frontiers in Immunology综述超声响应纳米平台利用深部穿透与可重复聚焦激活实现时空可控的抗原释放与T细胞浸润，二者共同指向肝转移免疫抑制微环境的可工程化改造。
